- 2026-10-25 (the writer that was in 4.3BSD) — SUMacC's tohex and fromhex were in 4.3BSD all along: tohex wrote the wild file, and the format's own readers compare the sum on 32 bits, so this does too
- 2026-10-25 (the two that said nothing) — a MIME multipart past the walk's depth and a Finder info GateKeeper vetoes are report lines, not silence: UNC_ERR_NESTED, and "name: Finder info refused"
- 2026-10-25 (the envelopes that left) — the encryption check joins the sniffer's image and the MacBinary and AppleDouble readers BinHex's: 2,464 B back on every budget but an envelope's
- 2026-10-25 (the archive Symantec shipped) — a DDAR record is the stored file's catalog entry: +78 is its resource fork, a creator other than DDAP is stored raw, and +100.. is the Finder's position; read off DD Expand 3.7.7
- 2026-10-25 (the review before the release) — the 38 commits since v0.43.0 read before tagging: a DiskDoubler walk that could step backward for ever, and four smaller faults
- 2026-10-25 (the archives that drew as the application) — the documents MacExtract's bundle claims draw the archive icon, not the application's: MacStamp writes our creator, so the Finder shows them
- 2026-10-31 (the helper list Expander asks for) — StuffIt Expander 5.5's installer offers to become Internet Config's helper for downloaded files; it claims no Finder creator, so nothing in it replaces a stub

---

## M0

- **License LGPL-2.1-or-later** — forced by transcribing XADMaster
  (LGPL) algorithms; see NOTICE.
- **`reference/` is gitignored**, repopulated by
  `tools/fetch_references.sh`: it holds a full LGPL repo clone plus wiki
  text of unclear licensing. The fetch script *is* the provenance record.
- **Listing = extraction minus writes.** No `unc_list` API:
  `UncOptions.list_only` drives the same streaming walk and reports entries
  via `begin_entry`/`end_entry` (`begin_entry` returning >0 means "skip
  data"). One code path, no arrays to size, progress-capable listing free.
- **CRC tables are compile-time constants** from the documented polynomials
  (0x1021 XMODEM for MacBinary II/BinHex, reflected 0xEDB88320 for
  Arsenic/zip/gzip), check values asserted in unit tests. XADMaster's
  reflected-table + unreverse XMODEM (`XADCRCReverseTable_1021` +
  `XADUnReverseCRC16`) is mathematically identical to plain MSB-first;
  pinned by check value 0x31C3 and every MacBinary/BinHex fixture.
- **Engine emits raw archive-encoding names** (MacRoman for Mac formats);
  MacRoman→UTF-8 is CLI-side (`--raw-names` opts out). Mac containers →
  MacRoman, zip/tar/gzip → pass-through.
- **Oracle manifests are built with `unar -nr` (no recursion)**: one
  manifest per container layer. Nesting is tested by chaining layers, not by
  replicating unar's name-based recursion (XADMacArchiveParser recurses into
  MacBinary members only when the *name* matches /\.(sea|sit|cpt)$/ — a
  quirk, not a spec).
- **Manifest dates are not compared** (v1): the oracle's timestamps pass
  through XADMaster's timezone interpretation, and matching them validates
  no decompression code. The engine still surfaces raw 1904-epoch seconds.
- **Allocator budget lives in the frontend callback**: the engine sees NULL
  and fails per-entry. Budget policy (CLI `--budget`, Mac `FreeMem()`) stays
  out of the engine and over-budget behaviour is mechanically testable.
- **`unc_skip` rejects offset wraparound** (`pos + len < pos`) as corrupt:
  all offsets are 32-bit by design (HFS caps files at 2 GB).

## M1

- **Oracle output is not blindly trusted:** GNUstep `unar` mishandles
  resource forks when it cannot append `.rsrc` (leading `~`, seen with
  `lipservice.bin`); `make_manifests.py` refuses a manifest when unar prints
  `cannot append extension`. **Narrowed 2026-08-08:** a `-k visible` bug;
  manifests are now built with `-k hidden`, under which `lipservice.bin` is
  ground truth. The refusal stays as a guard.
- **MacBinary II/III CRC fallback:** XADMaster also accepts a CRC-16/USB-style
  checksum (reflected 0xA001, init/xor 0xFFFF) from buggy encoders;
  transcribed as a bitwise loop (124 bytes, speed irrelevant).
- **Envelope fixtures are "derived" corpus entries:** each BinHex/MacBinary
  payload is extracted with the oracle and registered as its own fixture
  (`derived-*`, provenance `derived:unar-nr:<parent>`), giving per-layer
  ground truth without replicating unar's recursion.

## M2

- **BinHex sniffing reads beyond the 512-byte head:** real Info-Mac .hqx
  files bury the banner after mail headers (observed at offset 1270). The
  probe streams up to 8 KB (XADMaster's window) with a rolling 40-byte
  comparison.
- **Filename sanitization differences are normalized in the harness, not
  imitated:** for '/' in Mac names unar-on-Linux emits '_', MacExtract ':'.
  `run_diff.py` maps [:/] → '_' on both sides per component; the engine
  still emits raw bytes.

## M3

- **PackIt trailing fork CRC is big-endian in both modes.** macutils pit.c
  reads it little-endian for Huffman entries, XADMaster big-endian;
  arbitrated by unpit 0.3.1 (`getcrc()` = `(byte1 << 8) | byte2`) and the
  nocash PSX-SPX PackIt page, both big-endian. macutils' LE read is its own
  bug, so `macunpack` cross-checks only stored entries.
- **PackIt date fields:** creation @84, modification @88 (macutils pit.h
  H_CTIMOFF/H_MTIMOFF + nocash); XADMaster reads them swapped. **Settled
  2026-10-12**: every entry PackIt wrote in `derived-PackIt.pit` has
  @84 ≤ @88 (`PackIt.doc` 1985-10-23 / 1988-01-28) and the LC 475's Finder
  shows them as created/modified, so `lsar` reports the two swapped.
- **No real PMa4 fixtures exist** on the surviving mirrors (Info-Mac, funet,
  macgdn: every .pit is stored-mode). Coverage comes from
  `tools/synth_pit.py` (provenance `synthetic:tools/synth_pit.py --seed N`,
  regenerated by `harvest.py --restore`), validated against unar.
- **Encrypted PMa5/PMa6 entries are reported and skipped** with macutils'
  resync (scan for the next block magic): without the password the entry
  length is unknowable. Decryption out of scope (v1). (superseded:
  DECISIONS.md 2026-08-23 (decryption), *five schemes in, and the one with
  no second reader*)
- **lsar JSON is parsed with `strict=False`:** it can embed raw control
  bytes (binary `XADNextSolidEntry` values in PackIt archives).
- **Manifest builder synthesizes entries for orphan sidecars**
  (resource-only entries: unar writes nothing for a 0-byte data fork, so
  only the sidecar — `._<name>` since 2026-08-08, `<name>.rsrc` before —
  exists).

## M4

- **Path model:** `UncEntryInfo.name` is a '/'-separated path. Mac name
  components get the reversible '/'→':' swap in the engine (':' cannot occur
  in an HFS name), zip/tar paths pass through. The CLI treats '/' strictly
  as a separator and defuses '.'/'..' components.
- **CPT probe verifies the full index CRC** (as XADMaster's recognizer
  does): the 1-byte magic 0x01 is far too weak. Extraction then trusts the
  index and per-file CRCs, avoiding a second pass.
- **Index parsed via per-entry `unc_read_at`, no preload:** peak stays
  ~17 KB (io + staging + 8 KB window) regardless of entry count.
- **LZH block padding transcribed from XADMaster**, not macutils: macutils'
  eager 16-bit refill implicitly skips 2–3 padding bytes at each
  0x1FFF0-cost block boundary; XADCompactProLZHHandle states it explicitly
  (align; skip 3 if odd bytes consumed since the previous trees, else 2),
  which fits our lazy bit reader.
- **RLE quirks preserved bit-for-bit** from macutils cpt_outch: an 0x81
  that would be the final output byte is a literal; 0x81 0x81 emits a
  literal 0x81 while staying escaped; 0x81 0x82 0x00 is a literal
  "0x81 0x82". The 106-fixture corpus exercises all of them.
- **~~Oracle output can be structurally undecidable~~ — WITHDRAWN
  2026-08-08.** Claimed: archives holding both "X" and "X.rsrc" (THINK C
  projects) cannot be represented, so `derived-BootTime.cpt` and
  `derived-GNU_Chess_3.0.cpt` stayed corpus-only. It was the chosen
  `.rsrc`-suffix convention, not the archives: `unar -k hidden` and
  `macextract --forks hidden` name the sidecar `._X`. Both now have
  manifests. BLOCKERS.md *Withdrawn claims*; DECISIONS.md 2026-08-08.
- **`UncBufIn.limit`** bounds every compressed fork substream so corrupt
  streams cannot read into unrelated bytes (XADMaster's bounded sub-handles).

## M5+M6 (committed together)

- **One commit:** almost every classic .sit carries method 13 beside
  methods 0/2/3, so an M5-only build cannot pass the StuffIt suite and CI
  must be green at every commit. Methods 0/1/2/3 were still validated first
  (211-fixture suite + unit tests), then 13/5/8 added.
- **CRC-16/ARC** (reflected 0xA001, init 0) for StuffIt header and fork
  CRCs; pinned against an independent bitwise implementation and check
  value 0xBB3D.
- **LZW lives in unc_lzw.c** (compress(1)-compatible, LSB-first codes):
  method 2 is compress with 14-bit codes + block mode (XADStuffItParser
  passes flags 0x8e); M8's .Z reuses it. Quirks preserved: width grows at
  power-of-two table sizes; a clear code discards the rest of its 8-code
  group.
- **Method 13 fixed tables are machine-transcribed**
  (tools/gen_sit13_tables.py -> src/sit13_tables.h) from
  XADStuffIt13Handle.m — 3,270 entries, too many to hand-copy safely. The
  generated header is committed so the build does not need reference/.
- **Method 13 is the one little-endian-bit-order format** in the family;
  UncBitIn grew an LE mode. UncCanon.first[] must be 32-bit: 17-bit
  canonical codes overflow uint16 (dynamic codes reach 17+, fixed tables 18).
- **Method 5 ("LZAH") transcribed from XADLZHDynamicHandle** — the handle
  the oracle runs — including its LHarc-style window preload, not from the
  disabled libxad SIT_lzah in the same file. XADMaster's TODO doubts the
  preload; our fixtures decode byte-exact against the oracle either way.
- **Method 1 (RLE90) has no corpus fixture**; pinned by unit tests incl. the
  0x90 0x01 illegal-count case (XADRLE90Handle). (superseded: DECISIONS.md
  2026-08-01, *what the corpus actually contains, measured rather than
  recalled*)
- **StuffIt entry-header CRC failures abort the walk** (UNC_ERR_CORRUPT):
  headers chain by compressed lengths, so a bad header leaves no way to the
  next entry (XADStuffItParser raises at the same point).
- **`~`-name oracle bug generalized:** GNUstep unar can silently write the
  AppleDouble container INTO the data-fork filename (derived-020_Simulator.sit);
  five more fixtures were dropped as .rsrc-collision undecidable (BitMap11,
  The_Journal, TogSndVol, Unzip101, unshar_1.11). **All six recovered
  2026-08-08** with `-k hidden`. The guard's stronger form: every `._`
  sidecar must parse as AppleDouble, or the fixture is refused.

## M7

- **SIT5 entry-header CRC is not verified** (XADStuffIt5Parser reads and
  ignores it; the 0xA5A5A5A5 id re-syncs every header and fork CRCs guard
  the data).
- **Second-block prefix is 14 bytes** (u16 flags, u16 ?, u32 type, u32
  creator, u16 finderflags) then a 22-byte (entry v1) or 18-byte (v2+) skip
  — not 16, found the hard way.
- **SIT5 "mystery entries"** (datalen 0xFFFFFFFF after every directory) are
  skipped without consuming an entry slot, as XADStuffIt5Parser does;
  parentage is tracked by header offset (bounded map, 256 dirs / 16 KB path
  pool; overflow degrades to root-relative paths, not failure).
- **Arsenic transform vector is sized to the actual block fill**, not the
  declared block size. Every real SIT5 fixture declares 512 KB blocks
  (blockbits 19) even for 3 KB payloads; 4 x blocksize up front would pin
  every extraction at ~2.6 MB. Lazily sized, the corpus measures min
  0.63 MB, median 0.97 MB, mean 1.23 MB, max 2.53 MB. A 1 MB Mac Plus
  expands small Arsenic archives and refuses large ones per entry
  (UNC_ERR_MEM), by design.
  **RE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-01** against the M10 entry that contradicted it:
  instrumenting `sit_arsenic.c`'s block-size read shows all 484 Arsenic
  streams across the 31-fixture corpus — one per compressed fork —
  declaring 512 KB, without exception.
- **Arsenic CRC-32 is internal to the stream** (final block's end marker vs
  ~crc of output); the SIT5 header CRC-16 is meaningless for method 15 and
  skipped, as in XADMaster.
- **No synthetic Arsenic unit fixture:** it would need an arithmetic
  *encoder*; coverage is 31 real SIT5 fixtures plus their 310 corruption
  variants.

## M8

- **zlib 1.3.1 vendored unmodified** (inflate subset) into third_party/zlib;
  allocation routed through UncAlloc via zalloc/zfree, so the no-libc rule
  holds. Raw mode (-15): gzip/zip framing, CRCs and trailers are our code.
- **Synthetic exogenous fixtures are encoded by independent reference
  implementations** — Info-ZIP zip, GNU gzip, GNU tar, ncompress
  (tools/synth_exo.py; deterministic via TZ=UTC, fixed mtimes, gzip -n,
  tar --sort/--owner/--group/--mtime, zip -X) — plus era files
  PCCTS.tar.gz, popper-1.7.tar.Z, a2ps.V4.3.tar.Z from funet.
- **4acalc.zip / 4alnch11.zip (PKZIP 1.x, Implode) exercise the clean
  per-entry "unsupported method" path.** "Even unar fails on them" was
  wrong: unar fails on ONE entry of each, and since per-entry manifests
  (2026-08-08) both carry ground truth for 5 of 7 entries. Corrected
  2026-08-08 with the harness that skipped them whole (TESTING.md, "When our
  engine declines an entry").
- **gzip/.Z carry no entry name; unar derives it from the archive filename
  minus extension, ignoring even an embedded FNAME.** `UncOptions.name_hint`
  lets frontends supply the same convention.
- **Zip is parsed from the central directory** (EOCD scanned in the last
  66,000 bytes), data offsets from each local header (its name/extra sizes
  can differ). Other methods and encrypted entries are per-entry errors;
  zip64 out of scope.
- **tar acceptance requires a valid header checksum** (unsigned, or signed
  for old GNU tars); link/device/GNU-extension entries are per-entry
  "unsupported", not silently skipped.

## M9

- **Auto-unwrap lives in the CLI, not the engine.** The CLI re-sniffs the
  single output of an envelope format (MacBinary, BinHex,
  AppleSingle/Double, gzip, .Z), extracts in place (depth ≤ 8) and deletes
  the intermediate (+ sidecar) only after the inner layer succeeds. `-nr`
  disables; the diff harness uses it.
- **Detect-only probes completed** from XADMaster recognizers: StuffIt X,
  DiskDoubler (all three magics incl. 'DDA2', with header CRCs), Now
  Compress (byte-sum checksum), LZH/LArc. DiskCopy 4.2 NOT detected: no
  reference in the cloned sources.
  **[SUPERSEDED 2026-07-25 — the DiskCopy 4.2 half only.]** A reference was
  obtained (`reference/notes/DiskCopy42.md`, DiscFerret wiki) and
  `unc_diskcopy_probe` matched a synthetic and a real 800K GCR image, 0
  false positives across the corpus; retired 2026-08-26 (see the M10
  DiskCopy bullet below).
- **The fuzzer treats exit codes 0 and 1 as success** — the contract is
  "clean error, no crash/hang/sanitizer trip", as in the robustness suite,
  extended to wild inputs (archive splices, magic-prefixed garbage).

## M10

- **Built with Retro68's Multiversal Interfaces** (toolchain at
  /opt/Retro68-build; m68k half built with `build-toolchain.bash --no-ppc`).
  Differences from Apple's Universal Interfaces: trap types are
  kToolboxTrapType/kOSTrapType, `DirCreate` exists only as PBDirCreateSync,
  `GetApplLimit` glue is absent (LMGetApplLimit used), `ioDirMask` defined
  locally (ioFlAttrib bit 4, Inside Macintosh: Files).
- **`MacExtract.dsk` is a mountable HFS image, not a bootable one:** a System
  file cannot be redistributed; drag the app onto any System 6..9 boot disk.
- **Compile-only means compile-only** (MANUAL_TESTS.md held the runtime
  checklist). **[SUPERSEDED by the M10 runtime sections below]:** the app
  runs on System 6.0.8 / Mac Plus under Mini vMac byte-exact (44/44 sampled
  fixtures at 4 MB, 39/44 at 1 MB) and its UI has been driven end to end
  (`tools/vmac/interactive.py`); the `SFReply` working-directory item was
  tested on 2026-08-01, below.
- **The engine compiled for m68k without a single change** — the M0
  discipline held from the first decoder to the last.

## M9 follow-up (real-tar coverage)

- **The tar gap:** the only oracle-verified tar was synthetic. Deriving the
  real tars as fixtures exposed two bugs: (1) the probe demanded "ustar",
  rejecting every pre-POSIX v7 tar — XADTarParser recognizes v7 only by
  *filename*, which our content-only rule forbids, so our v7 probe demands
  structure (checksum + octal field syntax + printable NUL-terminated name);
  (2) v7 marks directories only by a trailing '/' and "./" prefixes are
  routine. Both handled; both 1990 tars (popper-1.7, PCCTS) extract
  byte-exact.
- Remaining corpus gaps, for lack of real files: PackIt PMa4 (synthetic
  only) and StuffIt method 1 (unit tests only). (superseded for method 1:
  DECISIONS.md 2026-08-01, *what the corpus actually contains*)

## M10 runtime verification (Mini vMac / System 6.0.8 / Mac Plus, 4 MB)

Mini vMac 36.04, System 6.0.8, 4 MB, driven via Xvfb + xdotool, output read
back with hfsutils.

- **Verified on genuine 68000:** launch, the Toolbox UI (SFGetFile, volume
  navigation, dialogs, Cancel), `unc_sniff`, and the decoders: test-only
  mode (full decode + in-engine CRC, no writes) on a real `.sit` reports
  "Extraction complete". File creation and `PBSetCatInfo` metadata work.
- **[SUPERSEDED — the whole bisection was confounded: every File Manager
  open was silently failing (BLOCKERS.md, "Earlier 'root causes' that turned
  out to be confounded"). The write path works byte-exact on-Mac.]**
  Recorded then: enabling `FSWrite` gave a layout-sensitive heap corruption
  (Sad Mac dsMemFullErr=25 on 4 MB, F-line bomb, or a spurious error);
  ruled out engine overrun (guard-byte allocator), stack (256 KB
  SetApplLimit bump), FSWrite signature, floppy-specific (5 MB HD image
  identical); any NoteAlert or padding change masked it.
- **`FlushVol` after extraction** — a genuine durability fix (writes were
  lost on non-clean exit).
- **Conclusion then:** engine verified on Mac Plus; shell "compile-only +
  engine-verified". **[SUPERSEDED — the shell is verified byte-exact
  on-Mac; see below.]**

## M10 deep debugging (max-effort session)

- **Engine proven correct on big-endian 68000:** engine+CLI cross-compiled
  with `m68k-linux-gnu-gcc`, the full 769-fixture differential suite under
  `qemu-m68k` is byte-exact (`-m32` already covered LE 32-bit).
- **The Mac sink is a testable unit.** `mac/macextract_mac.c` guards its
  Toolbox code behind `UNC_SINK_TEST`; `mac/mac_mocks.h` +
  `tests/mac_sink_test.c` run the ACTUAL sink/allocator/io code against the
  engine under ASan+UBSan and `qemu-m68k`; `tests/run_mac_sink.sh` (in
  `ci.sh`) checks it byte-exact. The Linux CLI's own sink never exercises
  this code.
- **[SUPERSEDED — the cause was MacExtract's own File Manager calls, fixed by
  the param-block rewrite (below).]** Claimed then: the write crash is
  environmental, needing MacsBug.
- Streaming (not staging) sink kept: more memory-efficient for the 1 MB
  floor, equally proven off-Mac.

## M10 write path — resolved (single-fork) + characterized (two-fork)

The "disk-write crash" was a stack of bugs (BLOCKERS.md). Decisions:

- **`mio_seek` tolerates `eofErr`:** `SetFPos` to/past EOF returns `eofErr`
  on a real Mac while positioning at EOF; treating it as an error gave
  spurious `UNC_ERR_IO`. The mock's `SetFPos` now reproduces it.
- **[SUPERSEDED 2026-08-02 — the archive is read straight off the file; see
  "the archive is no longer slurped into RAM" below. The interleaving claim
  does NOT reproduce: `UNC_AT_INTERLEAVE` reads a file three ways with 67
  file creations in between and gets the same CRC every time.]**
  ~~Slurp the whole archive into RAM (`MemIO`/`xio_*`), because interleaved
  File Manager reads and writes on one volume return zeros.~~
- **[SUPERSEDED — streaming is the shipped sink; see "The Mac sink writes
  each chunk straight to the File Manager" below. The volume corruption is
  from the confounded period.]** ~~Staging, not streaming, because deep
  writes corrupt the volume.~~
- **[SUPERSEDED — "three blocks bomb the Memory Manager" is FALSE; with the
  opens fixed, `UNC_AT_SEPARATE_BLOCKS` extracts a two-fork file byte-exact
  with three blocks (BLOCKERS.md).]** Two-fork staging uses ONE shared block
  (`sharedBuf`, data region then resource region; proven off-Mac via
  `UNC_MAC_FORCE_SHAREBUF` in `tests/run_mac_sink.sh`). It is harmless and
  marginally more heap-friendly; the block-count justification is not why.
- **Reserved-header diff is expected:** resource forks come out byte-exact
  except offsets 16–127, which the Resource Manager stamps per session; the
  autotest treats an all-in-16..127 diff as a pass (see the mask bullet in
  the next section).

## M10 (real Mini vMac) — the decisions that actually made it run

- **[WITHDRAWN 2026-07-25 — explanation only; the fix ships.]**
  ~~Retro68's HOpen glue is broken on System 6.~~ Observed: `HOpen()` gave
  `noErr` but the refNum was garbage, so the archive slurped as 0 bytes and
  extraction failed silently as `UNC_ERR_FORMAT`; `HOpenDF` gave `paramErr`.
  Invisible off-Mac (the mock never touches the glue). **Fix:** explicit HFS
  param blocks (`PBHOpenSync`/`PBHOpenRFSync`/`PBHCreateSync`/
  `PBHDeleteSync` via `MyOpenFork`/`MyHCreate`/`MyHDelete`), reading
  `pb.ioParam.ioRefNum` ourselves. This unblocked everything; the "two-fork
  crash" investigation was confounded by it (BLOCKERS.md).
- **On-screen result channel.** [Justification WITHDRAWN 2026-08-02 — see
  "the Out volume can be read after all"; the channel ships.] The app
  CRC-32s both forks on-Mac (resource header 16..127 masked) and paints an
  8-value aggregate to the framebuffer (`qd.screenBits`, `at_report`),
  decoded host-side by `tools/decode_grid.py` + `tools/vmac_check.py`
  against `macextract x -nr`. ~~QuickDraw bombs after File Manager
  activity~~ — **WITHDRAWN 2026-08-01** (`tools/quickdraw-repro/`, twelve
  configurations, every call clean with `MemError()==0`). Kept because it
  needs no allocation, cannot fail, and still reports when the Toolbox
  cannot be trusted. `HideCursor()` first so the cursor's saved background
  cannot stamp over the grid.
- **[WITHDRAWN 2026-08-01]** ~~Arsenic blocks are 128 KB (dominant) / 256 KB
  / 512 KB, from `--stats` peak heap: 14 / 9 / 8 of 31; peak ≈ 5× block =
  0.64–2.6 MB.~~ All 484 Arsenic streams declare **512 KB**; the M7 entry
  was right. Peak is `~35 KB parser state + 512 KB block + 4 × actual block
  fill`, not `5 × block`, so dividing by five reads a small payload as a
  small block (0.64 MB is a 512 KB block holding ~24 KB). Peak heap cannot
  recover the declared size; the field must be read where `sit_arsenic.c`
  reads it. What survives: every Arsenic entry exceeds 400 KB, so Arsenic is
  a ≥4 MB tier, and on a 1 MB Plus the boundary was the *archive's* size
  (slurped into RAM first).
- **'SIZE' resource: 4 MB preferred / 400 KB minimum.** The engine budget
  comes from `FreeMem()` at runtime, so one binary adapts from a 1 MB Plus
  to a G3; System 6 without MultiFinder ignores SIZE.
- **Cancel/error removes the partial file:** `sink_end` `MyHDelete`s the
  file created in `sink_begin` on Cmd-. or per-entry failure.
- **DiskCopy 4.2 stays detect-not-implemented** (no reference offline; rule
  #3 forbids inventing the header). **[SUPERSEDED 2026-07-25]:** with
  `reference/notes/DiskCopy42.md` the probe became real, matching a
  synthetic and a real 800K GCR image, 0 false positives across 803
  fixtures. **[RETIRED 2026-08-26]** with the other disk-image probes, to
  `attic/` (`UNC_FORMAT_DISKCOPY_RETIRED`; DECISIONS.md 2026-08-26, *a name
  is only worth something inside the frame the user came with*).
- **The "broken Retro68 `HOpen` glue" root cause is WITHDRAWN.** The minimal
  reproduction meant for upstream (`tools/retro68-hopen-repro/`) disproved
  it: on the same System 6.0.8 / Mac Plus / Mini vMac / Retro68 `335fa54f6d`
  setup, ten cases pass — `HOpen` writes the refNum every time and matches a
  hand-filled `PBHOpenSync`, with a poisoned stack, real vRefNum and
  non-zero dirID, `fsWrPerm`, `HOpenRF`, and across volumes. Poisoning
  `ioMisc` with `0xA3A3A3A2` still opened correctly. **Corrected
  2026-10-13:** that address is outside a Mac Plus's RAM; one inside it is
  written through (*the bug was the footnote*), so this disproof does not
  hold. The param-block rewrite is kept because it works ("it zeroes the
  whole param block"). **The true root cause was left unestablished
  [corrected 2026-10-13: it is `ioMisc` — *the bug was the footnote*].**
  Rule: a root cause never reduced to a minimal reproduction is a
  hypothesis, not a finding.
- **No upstream issue was filed:** the headline finding was false, and this
  environment had no `gh` or credentials. What survived — **both `OpenDF`
  and `HOpenDF`** return `paramErr` on System 6 (the `_OpenDF` trap is
  System 7 and neither falls back as `FSOpen` does), plus the uninitialised
  `ioMisc` in the three H-variants — was written up in
  `tools/retro68-hopen-repro/ISSUE.md`. **Corrected 2026-08-01**: the
  write-up first named only `HOpenDF`; settled by running it (case 11), not
  re-reading `glue.c`. **Corrected 2026-10-13:** the `paramErr` is Apple's
  documented contract; the `ioMisc` point is the bug (*the bug was the
  footnote*).
- **The on-Mac resource-fork mask is bytes 16..127, and it is header
  padding, not a fudge:** exactly the 112-byte "reserved for system use"
  area of the 256-byte resource FILE header (Inside Macintosh: More
  Macintosh Toolbox), which System 6 stamps with session scratch. Verified
  on `AT View.rsrc` (dataOffset=256, mapOffset=16805, do+dl==mo,
  mo+ml==filesize: bytes 16..255 are padding, 112 system / 128
  application). Not the resource *map* header (22 reserved bytes at
  mapOffset, reference/XADMaster/XADResourceFork.m). Two limits keep it
  honest: bytes 128..255 are NOT masked (THINK C writes its copyright
  there), and `mask_reserved()` refuses unless dataOffset and mapOffset are
  both >= 128. Corpus sweep: 1545/1545 resource forks standard.
- **The on-Mac harness is committed and fetches its copyrighted inputs.**
  Every "runs on System 6" claim used to rest on an uncommitted, vanished
  working directory, so nothing could be re-run — two of three BLOCKERS.md
  open items were unreproducible for that reason. `tools/vmac/` scripts it
  all; the Mac Plus ROM and System 6.0.8 image are fetched by URL and
  verified by SHA-256, never committed. The 44-fixture sample is
  `tools/vmac/sample.txt`, so runs months apart compare like for like.
- **The emulator runs "all out", so the harness measures correctness
  only.** No timing claim about a 7 MHz 68000 can come from it; the old
  "185 s for XferIt" was struck, its 1x setup gone.
- **The autotest always reports what it is doing:** a grid with
  `ret = -1000` before work, `-1001`/`-1002` when In/Out is missing — far
  outside `UNC_ERR_*`. Without it a missing grid was ambiguous between
  "never launched", "bombed" and "still decoding"; a broken disk set once
  looked like a slow decoder.
- **The Mac sink writes each chunk straight to the File Manager; it no
  longer stages whole forks.** Staging cost `archive + engine peak + largest
  output fork`, which stopped a 1 MB Plus extracting the two largest-output
  sample fixtures. The "deep writes corrupt HFS" comment dated from the
  confounded period, so it was re-tested: streaming is byte-exact through
  the mock (ASan/UBSan, qemu-m68k) and on System 6.0.8, 44/44 at 4 MB and
  39/44 at 1 MB (remaining failures: StuffIt 5 budget refusals).
  `UNC_MAC_STAGE_WRITES` keeps staging buildable; CI proves both.

- **"QuickDraw bombs after any File Manager activity" is FALSE**
  (`tools/quickdraw-repro/`). Filed under "test-harness lessons (not app

## 2026-08-01 — testing a working directory without a Finder

`SFReply.vRefNum` with `dirID` 0 had been untested since M10; two attempts
through System 7's Finder produced only mis-aimed double-clicks.

**`UNC_AT_WD`**: the autotest opens its own working directory over a
subfolder with `PBOpenWD`, calls `RunExtract` with `(vRefNum = that WD,
dirID = 0)` — the call `ExtractOne()` makes with Standard File's reply — and
counts files in the folder vs the volume root. Five seconds a run, same on
System 6 and 7. Passes on both: 3 entries, 3 files in the folder, 0 in the
root, wdRefNums -32717 and -32701 (genuine WD references, not volume
refNums).

**When a UI test is hard to drive, ask what the UI hands the code, and hand
it that directly.** The empty-root assertion is the whole test: every earlier
harness extracted into a volume ROOT, where WD and root coincide, so none
could have caught a mistake here.

## 2026-08-01 — the cancel test only covered the path where no fork was open

The mock File Manager's `--cancel` aborted before any `sink_write`, so the
existing test only ever exercised "no fork opened"; cleaning up a
half-written fork was never reached. The mock now aborts mid-fork on both
write paths. **A test named after a feature is not a test of that
feature.**

## 2026-08-01 — a tag freezes the documentation, not just the code

`v0.1` pointed 10 commits behind `main`, publishing status files already
corrected on `main`. This repository's errors have been in the documentation
rather than the engine, so the frozen docs are what matter. Push the docs,
then tag.

## 2026-08-02 — driving the Mac OS 9 Finder with the keyboard, not the mouse

Launching on Mac OS 9 took six boots, five spent on the mouse. Three real
defects were fixed and published as root causes (a 0.9 s double click, an
ADB pointer fed absolute coordinates, the Setup Assistant holding the
foreground); the volume still did not open.

`tools/vmac/os9probe.py` measured primitives instead of outcomes: eleven
probes, one boot. Every mouse probe changed 0.0000 of its watched rectangle,
every keyboard probe worked, and the pointer was only ever found in screen
corners. **Decision: the Finder is driven from the keyboard** (type-select,
Cmd-Down, Cmd-Q; `launch_by_keyboard()`). It worked first try.

- **Measure the primitive before theorising about the compound.** An outcome
  that did not happen names no link in the chain (same mistake as the
  `macburger-helper.hqx` timeout, written up three times before the byte
  counter was instrumented).
- **A fix that is real is not thereby sufficient.** Call nothing a root
  cause until the symptom is gone.

## 2026-08-02 — checking Mac OS 9 output through the disk image, not the screen

The framebuffer grid exists to work around Mini vMac's awkward disk
retrieval, a constraint OS 9 under QEMU does not have. `verify_output()`
waits for the emulator to exit, lifts the Apple_HFS partition out at
`mkapmdisk.py`'s offset, and `hcopy -m` pulls each file as MacBinary (both
forks in one file); forks are compared byte for byte with `macextract x
-nr`. Strictly stronger than the grid: bytes not CRCs, no pixel decoding,
names which file and fork differed, and an unflushed volume fails to mount
rather than passing. **When the environment changes, re-ask what the
workaround was working around.**

**It found a real bug in its first run.** The grid sums `nfiles`, CRCs and
lengths and has never compared a NAME. `synth-exo-Z.Z` and
`synth-exo-gz.gz` — passing on Mini vMac for weeks — wrote `archive.sit~1`
where Linux wrote `archive`: `RunExtract()` passed the whole Pascal string as
`name_hint` instead of the name minus its last extension (as `macextract.h`
documents and `cli/main.c` does), so `foo.gz` collided with itself. Fixed in
`mac/macextract_mac.c` with the CLI's rule, including "a leading dot is not
an extension". **An aggregate check cannot fail on a property it never
aggregates.**

**The new checker's own first verdict was wrong**: 7/11, all four failures
its blind spots — it listed only the volume ROOT (`synth-exo-tar.tar`'s
`bin/` and `docs/` looked MISSING); it read HFS names as UTF-8 not MacRoman
(`Appé` unequal to itself; `run_diff.py` has NFC-normalized for months); and
it failed "the Mac wrote nothing" for `derived-DandStoQIF2.sea`, where
nothing is correct (DiskDoubler was then detect-only; Linux writes nothing
either). Re-reading the SAME volumes gave 11/11 (13/13 after two more
fixtures). A FAIL from a young harness is a claim about the harness until
shown to be about the target.

## 2026-08-02 — the reporting channel, not the volume, was what blocked HFS+

"Extraction has never touched an HFS+ volume" (MANUAL_TESTS.md since M10)
read like a missing capability. The autotest finds volumes **by name**, so
renaming the OS 9 HFS+ boot volume `Out` points the binary at HFS+ with no
code change. The obstacle was the answer channel: `at_report()` writes 1bpp
pixels, invisible on OS 9's 32-bit screen. `at_report_file()` writes the
same values, plus every output NAME, to a file on the plain-HFS INPUT volume
the harness built.

- **Wait for the artifact, not a sign of it.** Two screen-based completion
  detectors ("screen changes", "screen goes black") each ran their full
  240 s timeout on runs that had already succeeded; polling the transfer
  image for the report FILE finds it in ~20 s.
- **"It landed on HFS+" was checked, not inferred.** The File Manager
  answers `'BD'` for HFS+ volumes for compatibility, so a signature proves
  nothing (a fixed-offset signature read produced the withdrawn "the boot
  volume is plain HFS" claim). hfsutils sees only the HFS wrapper, which
  still holds its single placeholder file, so the output is not on plain
  HFS.

## 2026-08-02 — the archive is no longer slurped into RAM

`RunExtract()` used to `NewPtr(fileSize)` and read the whole archive first:
on a 1 MB Plus a 278 KB archive took 278 KB from the engine. The M10
justification — interleaved reads and writes on one volume return zeros —
was never reproduced, and sat in the same bullet list as "deep writes
corrupt the volume", already withdrawn as confounded.

`UNC_AT_INTERLEAVE` reads one file three ways on one volume (undisturbed;
in chunks with a fresh file created and written between each; seeking with
`SetFPos` before every read): **identical every time** — 278,294 B / CRC
05746998 over 67 rounds, and 286,720 B / CRC 8f448a65, at 4 MB and 1 MB.
Withdrawn. The default is now a `FileIO` that seeks and reads on demand with
the input held open; `UNC_MAC_SLURP_ARCHIVE` keeps the old path buildable.

Measured on System 6.0.8 / Mac Plus:

| run | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 44-fixture sample, 4 MB | 44/44 | 44/44 |
| 44-fixture sample, **1 MB** | 39/44 | **40/44** |
| same sample, 4 MB, **output on the archive's own volume** | never run | **44/44** |

Three of the four remaining 1 MB failures went from refusing everything to
extracting most: `derived-Library_ISBN_Barcoder.sit` 0 → **31 of 34**,
`derived-Troi-ClipSave-Plug-in1.1.sit` 0 → **6 of 13**,
`derived-PuzzleGetter_0.8.sit` 11 → **25 of 26**.

- **The same-volume case had never been tested**, though the interactive
  app writes next to the archive. `UNC_AT_SAMEVOL` covers it: 44/44. A
  harness can be thorough and never once assume the shape the shipped
  program uses.
- **A claim's neighbours are evidence about it.** Sitting beside a withdrawn
  claim from the same week was reason enough to re-test it.

## 2026-08-02 — the Out volume can be read after all, so names are checkable

BLOCKERS.md said Mini vMac's write-back is "lazy and PARTIAL — it can commit
one fork of a file but not the other", so System 6/7 tiers verified through
the grid, which cannot check a NAME — how the `foo.gz~1` defect survived for
weeks. It does not reproduce: `run.py --keep-disks` keeps each run's images
and `tools/vmac/checkdisk.py` reads them, **44/44 byte-exact, both forks,
names and folders included** — decisively `derived-RWAsm_Folder.sit`, 38
files and **73 forks**, dozens with both forks non-empty; `spinning brain ƒ`,
`Appé` and `.DS_Store` survive too. The grid is kept (liveness and setup
failures); `checkdisk.py` is an addition.

Its first verdict, 38/44, was again the checker's: `hls` hides dot-names
without `-a`; hfsutils path arguments must be MacRoman bytes; `<X>.rsrc` is a
sidecar only when `<X>` exists beside it. 44/44 on the SAME images.

**A workaround outlives the claim that justified it, and takes the
capability it displaced with it.**

## 2026-08-02 — the claim audit, finished

Every assertion about Mac or emulator behaviour made without a reproduction
has been tested:

| claim | outcome |
|---|---|
| QuickDraw bombs after File Manager activity | withdrawn 2026-08-01 |
| deep writes from the decode callback corrupt the volume | withdrawn earlier |
| three non-relocatable staging blocks bomb the Memory Manager | withdrawn earlier |
| interleaved reads/writes on one volume return zeros | withdrawn — `UNC_AT_INTERLEAVE` |
| Mini vMac's write-back is lazy and partial | withdrawn — `checkdisk.py`, 44/44 |
| `HideCursor()` before drawing the grid | **CONFIRMED**, with a reproduction |
| `pkill -9` never flushes; boot+kill corrupts the image | withdrawn — 11 cycles |

**Not everything was wrong.** Built without `HideCursor()`, with the pointer
dragged through the grid's cell centres, one cell is stamped over and the
decoded value comes back with one flipped bit.

**The test passed twice before it meant anything**: first with the pointer
parked outside the emulator window ((144,129) on the 800x600 Xvfb), then
dragged *between* cell rows. Only aimed at cell centres did the bit flip. A
green result from a test whose reach is unestablished says nothing.

**An unreproduced claim is a liability proportional to what it forces.** The
write-back claim cost most because it displaced a capability (reading names
off the volume). Ask first "what does it stop us doing?".

## 2026-08-02 — "DECISIONS.md is truncated" — it was not

A session reported this file cut off mid-entry; it was intact. "Restoring"
it would have overwritten correct history with a reconstruction, invisibly.
`git diff HEAD` settles "has this file been damaged?" in seconds — run it
before deciding what a document should have said.

## 2026-08-03 — the Arsenic block is grown, not assumed

At 1 MB, 2 of 6 sampled StuffIt 5 fixtures extracted fully, three
partially, one not at all, and the floor was described as hard (512 KB
block vs ~700 KB free heap). Wrong number: **512 KB is what the block
DECLARES, not what it holds** — the fixture peaking at 643.2 KB held **24 KB**
in its 512 KB block. The transform vector was already fill-sized; the block
was still allocated at the declared size in `ars_decode_init`.

`ars_block_reserve()` grows it on demand, doubling from 8 KB, capped at the
declared size. Peak becomes `~35 KB parser + capacity + 4x fill`:

| fixture | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `derived-RWAsm_Folder.sit` | 643 KB | **163 KB** |
| `derived-KeyGraphics.sit` | 656 KB | **176 KB** |
| `derived-PuzzleGetter_0.8.sit` | 710 KB | **262 KB** |
| `derived-Troi-ClipSave-Plug-in1.1.sit` | 1034 KB | **650 KB** |
| `derived-a2basic.dmg.sit` | 1319 KB | 1063 KB |
| `derived-Library_ISBN_Barcoder.sit` | 1810 KB | 1810 KB |

The last row's blocks really hold ~316 KB; the win is proportional to unused
declared space.

- **Growing never sets the high-water mark:** the transient is
  `old + new = 1.5x new`, and 1.5x capacity < 5x fill for any fill worth
  having, so the saving is real rather than moved.
- **The declared size is still enforced:** `blockbits` can declare as little
  as 512 bytes and the reserve clamps to it; corruption checks against
  `blocksize` are untouched. Capacity is an allocation strategy, never a
  format bound.

**A number that comes from the data is not a number you have to budget
for.**

## 2026-08-03 — the LZW table is sized from the input, once

`unc_lzw_init` allocated `(1 << maxbits) * 4`, the **declared** ceiling;
`compress(1)` writes `maxbits=16` by default, so `.Z` cost a flat
**274,432 B** for every input (a 488-byte fixture allocated 256 KB). It was
the only peak in the matrix that did not vary with its input, which made it
worth suspecting.

**Growth on demand was tried first and was wrong:**

    synth-exo-Z.Z          274,432 -> 18,432 B
    synth-exo-tar-Z.tar.Z  274,432 -> 61,440 B
    a2ps.V4.3.tar.Z        274,432 -> 208,896 B
    popper-1.7.tar.Z       274,432 -> 405,504 B      <- WORSE than doing nothing

Copy-based growth has an `old + new` transient, and **where the table IS the
whole allocation, the transient becomes the peak**. Arsenic escaped only
because its 4x-fill transform vector dominates later. *Growth pays off only
when something larger than the grown buffer is allocated after it.*

**What works is a bound from the input.** Each code defines at most one new
symbol and codes are at least 9 bits, so

    symbols <= 256 + reserved + insize * 8 / 9

One allocation, no transient. `fmt_exo.c` passes the stream size less the
3-byte header; StuffIt method 2 the entry's compressed length. The bound is
**strict** (entry `256 + reserved + k` takes `k + 1` codes), which keeps the
decode bit-identical: `maxsymbols` also decides where code width stops
growing and the table is full — choices the encoder made — so lowering it
would desync silently. `maxsymbols` keeps its declared value; a new
`capsymbols` carries the allocation and chain-buffer bound.

`lzw_grow` widens to the ceiling if the bound under-estimates. Verified both
ways: growth hard-disabled, 769/769 (the bound never under-estimates in the
corpus); `-D UNC_LZW_TINY_TABLE` (initial capacity 258, growth on every
stream), also 769/769 under ASan/UBSan/alignment; and starving the table
without the net gives **675/769**, establishing that 94 fixtures can fail on
this code.

Result: 50 fixtures improved, none regressed, `.Z` from a flat 268 KB to
15–219 KB; the 1 MB floor sweep unchanged at 41/44. Numbers in FORMATS.md,
footnote §.

## 2026-08-06 — method 13's LZSS window is sized from the entry

Same shape, but the ceiling is a format constant: `SIT13_WINDOW` is 64 KB,
the window the format PERMITS, not what a stream can REACH. A well-formed
encoder never emits `moff > pos`, so a fork whose output is 6 KB addresses
6 KB of window; the other 58 KB was allocated, zeroed per fork, never read.

The window is the fork's uncompressed size rounded up to a power of two,
capped at 64 KB. The power of two keeps it exact: with `win >= outlen`,
`pos & (win-1) == pos` and `from & (win-1) == from` for every reachable
offset — the same indices the 64 KB window computes.

- **Measured, not argued:** an instrumented run counted `moff > pos` across
  the corpus: **0** (the suite alone would pass even if such references read
  zeros either way).
- **Sensitivity:** forcing the window to its 256-byte minimum gives
  **654/769**, so 115 fixtures can fail on this code. ASan stayed clean at
  that size: the masking keeps accesses in bounds, so a bad bound corrupts
  output, not memory.

Result: 34 fixtures improved, none regressed, `derived-MacGzip.sit`
76,944 → 13,456 B; the corpus maximum stays 76,944 B (some forks exceed
64 KB).

**The estimate was wrong, instructively.** ~115 fixtures looked improvable
(175 of 225 StuffIt fixtures at the 64 KB peak, about two thirds with
largest fork under 64 KB); 34 did. One fork over 64 KB pins the whole
archive's peak. **A per-archive maximum cannot be predicted from a per-fork
distribution** — the Arsenic block-size error (FORMATS.md, † footnote) from
the opposite direction.

## 2026-08-06 — the Arsenic block's first allocation is sized from the entry

Fourth in the "size it from the data" series, but about the SHAPE left
behind rather than how much was allocated.

`ars_block_reserve` grew from 8 KB by doubling: for a 128 KB block it
allocated 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 KB, freeing each. **A geometric trail can
never satisfy the step that follows it** — the earlier steps sum to one step
short — so the freed 8+16+32+64 KB sat under the final block as 122,880 B of
unusable holes; measured on the 1 MB floor, 125,614 B stranded. That refused
an entry in `derived-Troi-ClipSave-Plug-in1.1.sit`: its transform vector
asked for 498,548 B with 678 KB of budget left and `MaxBlock` at 468,126 B.
It needed 666,004 B against a 678,392 B budget — never short of memory, only
of a contiguous run.

The fix: the first allocation is `min(outlen, blocksize)`, both bounds the
data gives, so normally there is no second allocation and no trail. Growth
stays as a safety net.

**It is a bound, not an exact size, and that cost 4 small regressions.** An
encoder may split a fork into several blocks even when `outlen < blocksize`:
`derived-Berkeley_Packet_Monitor.sit` 338,964 → 362,236 B, three others by
2 KB or less. Against that, 24 fixtures improved (`Library_ISBN`
1,854,208 → 1,682,080 B) and the floor went 41/44 → 42/44. Taken
deliberately: none crosses the 400 KB threshold or the ~700 KB a 1 MB Mac
has, and every alternative sizing reintroduces a trail. A weaker standard
than the LZW change (any regression disqualifying), because this one buys a
capability, not an efficiency.

**How it was found.** Four configurations had moved `MaxBlock` by under
500 B — `NewPtr`, `MaxMem()` retry, handles with `MoveHHi`, handles with the
move confirmed by address. `MoveHHi` demonstrably worked (205,828 →
803,634 B free below the moved blocks) and changed nothing at the refusal:
each assumed LIVE blocks stranded the space, and the trail is DEAD ones,
which nothing in the probe reported. 8+16+32+64 = 120 KB sat suspiciously
close to the 125,614 B measured; setting the initial capacity to 128 KB
passed the fixture in one run.

## 2026-08-07 — the inverse BWT falls back to a sampled occurrence index

Fifth and last in the series, and the first that reduces the requirement
itself.

`ars_inverse_bwt`'s transform vector costs **4 bytes per block byte**, the
decoder's dominant allocation: `Library_ISBN` needed 1,854,208 B against the
678,392 B a 1 MB Plus was then thought to leave the engine (597,036 B as
re-measured on 2026-08-24, which only widens the gap), 1,293,536 B of it
that one vector. No placement or defragmentation closes that gap.

`ars_index_build` answers the same query from **samples**: the position of
every `1 << shift[c]`-th occurrence of each byte value, `shift[c]` chosen so
no value exceeds `target` samples. A query binary-searches the value owning
the sorted index, jumps to the nearest sample and scans forward. Memory
`~4 * sum_c min(counts[c], target)`, time `~blocklen/target` positions per
output byte — a pure time-for-memory dial.

- **Samples are per byte VALUE, not per sorted index:** per index, the scan
  covers `target` occurrences of `c`, which for a rare `c` is most of the
  block.
- **Adaptive, fast path first at every block;** the choice is made by an
  allocation failing, the only thing that knows the budget. Cost on a
  machine that never needs it: peak heap over all 31 StuffIt 5 fixtures is
  **HEAD + 8 bytes, exactly** (one pointer in `struct Arsenic`), corpus
  byte-exact.
- **The dial is greedy:** `target` halves only until the allocator accepts,
  so peak-under-budget is roughly the budget, not the requirement —
  `Library_ISBN` peaks at 614,080 B under a 678,392 B cap but extracts down
  to **393,028 B** (bisected). Bisect for the requirement.

| fixture | needed before | predicted | measured minimum |
|---|---|---|---|
| `derived-a2basic.dmg.sit` | 1,088,588 | ~245,699 | **245,897** |
| `derived-Library_ISBN_Barcoder.sit` | 1,854,208 | ~379,435 | **393,028** |

**Within 200 bytes and 3.6%**, where the method-13 estimate was wrong,
because this estimated a SINGLE allocation — the quantity the change
controls — not a per-archive maximum. **Estimate the thing you are
changing, not an aggregate over things you are not.**

**Time is the price, and uneven.** At the 1 MB budget, x86 -O2: `a2basic`
20→50 ms, `Library_ISBN` 36→124 ms; `derived-Domino_v1.4.sit` 33x (tighter
squeeze, smaller `target`). At `target=1` the walk is quadratic: the
StuffIt 5 set takes 8.4 minutes instead of one second.

**On the target, 1.65x to 2.47x, not predicted by x86.** At authentic
7 MHz: `a2basic` 587 s fast / 966 s sampled (1.65x), `Library_ISBN` 768 s /
1,898 s (2.47x); the ratio widens with block fill as the model says. x86's
`a2basic` ratio is 2.5x — relatively *cheaper* on a 68000, most likely
(hypothesis) because the arithmetic decoder dominates more there. It needed
a 1 MB 1x emulator (`build_mv mv-1M-1x 1M z`); no all-out build answers a
timing question. Scaling `a2basic` by output size called `Library_ISBN`
"near an hour"; it took 31.6 minutes — **per-byte cost tracks block fill.**

**Degradation is bounded by an accident:** below ~350 KB the BLOCK BUFFER is
refused first (it is allocated before the index is planned), so the entry
fails cleanly before `target` turns pathological. Probed 678,392 B →
200,000 B on `Library_ISBN`: clean `rc=0` to 450,000, 5 s at 400,000, clean
refusal at and below 350,000, no hang.

**The sampled walk silences progress:** it spends minutes turning
already-consumed input into output. `unc_progress_poll` fires the tick
without moving the byte count, every `UNC_PROGRESS_STEP` output bytes, on
the sampled path only.

## 2026-08-07 — the progress dialog gets a bar, a percentage and a time left

A 15-minute Arsenic extraction wants a time estimate, and the text
percentage was wrong for most of it.

**The fix is in the engine.** Progress counts archive INPUT consumed;
Arsenic decodes a whole block, then walks it to output, so on a one-block
fork the input position runs to the end and stops. `derived-a2basic.dmg.sit`
under a 1 MB budget: 41 ticks, the last **23 identical** — 100% for the ~42%
of the run the walk takes, about seven minutes on a Plus. Now
`UncProgressState.hold` suppresses the input-side tick for the fork and
Arsenic reports `pbase + span * produced / outlen` (`span` = the fork's
compressed length, `UncBufIn.limit`): same unit, monotonic, interpolated by
OUTPUT. After: 801 ticks, evenly spread.

- **Tick interval 256 output bytes, not 8192:** at 8 KB the run reports
  every 37 seconds (4% jumps, Cancel taking half a minute); 256 gives
  ~1.2 s. The Mac shell rate-limits to 10 Hz; the 769-fixture suite time is
  unchanged.
- **The bar is a DITL userItem with a real draw proc**, surviving update
  events. ETA `elapsed * (100 - pct) / pct`, held back for two seconds and
  below 1%; redrawn only when the reading changes (`SetDialogItemText` at
  10 Hz flickers).
- **Moving the button broke the harness silently.** The dialog grew 80 →
  110 points and Cancel moved down 30; `interactive.py`'s hard-coded click
  hit inert background, the extraction completed, and the run still
  produced `3-cancelled.png` — of the progress dialog. **A UI harness that
  drives by coordinate cannot fail on a moved control; it can only
  photograph the wrong thing.** The constant now carries its derivation from
  the DLOG and DITL rects.

## 2026-08-07 — the progress rewrite costs ~9% on a 68000, and why is UNKNOWN

An observation, not a finding: no reproduction of the mechanism, three
explanations measured and killed.

**Measured, reproducible.** `derived-a2basic.dmg.sit`, Mac Plus at
authentic 7 MHz, extraction only:

| build | 4 MB (fast table) | 1 MB (sampled index) |
|---|---|---|
| b4b5429 (before the progress rewrite) | 536 s, 537 s | 927 s |
| 8248ab8 (after) | 583 s, 587 s, 582 s | 966 s, 966 s |
| delta | **+47 s** | **+39 s** |

Host idle (load 0.18). The deltas are close in ABSOLUTE terms for the same
205,019 bytes of output, so "9%" misdescribes it: ~40 s attached to this
fixture.

**What it is NOT** (each a stated hypothesis, tested):

- *The autotest grid* (21,888-byte framebuffer erased byte-wise, 272 cells,
  41 → 801 reports): rate-limiting to one repaint per 5 s (~117) changed
  nothing, 587 s. The rate limit is kept anyway.
- *Anything per tick:* `ARS_PROGRESS_STEP` back to 8192 (26 calls instead of
  801): 582 s. A 30x cut in callbacks bought zero; also rules out
  `ars_scale`'s 32-bit divisions.
- *x86 cost:* `macextract t` 19 ms before and after, ten runs.

**What it IS, as far as evidence goes:** the four changed `src/` files
copied into the b4b5429 worktree with its Mac shell reproduce it, 582 s —
the engine diff, on a 68000. Its only per-output-byte addition, one
`produced >= nexttick` compare over 205,019 iterations, would need ~1,900
cycles a byte at 7.83 MHz. The arithmetic is irreconcilable with the
measurement, hence unexplained rather than attributed.

**Kept regardless, as a judgement:** it buys a moving bar and a Cancel that
answers in about a second instead of thirty-seven on quarter-hour
extractions.

**Next discriminators, cheapest first** (do not re-test the killed ones):
(1) fixed or proportional? two runs of `derived-KeyGraphics.sit` (33 KB
output), old and new, four minutes; (2) the compare itself? delete only the
`produced >= nexttick` test and tick from `ars_read_block`, one 10-minute
run. The arithmetic says it cannot be the compare; it also said it could not
be the reporting. Measure before believing either.

## 2026-08-07 — releases are published by Actions, not by a token here

This machine authenticates with a **deploy key** (git over SSH), which
cannot reach the Releases REST API, so v0.5 first shipped with no release
page.

**A workflow with the runner's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`, not a PAT stored here:**
a stored token persists across sessions and grants its scope to anything
that runs, including a confused or compromised agent session; the workflow's
credential lives for one run, is scoped to one repository, and leaves an
Actions audit trail.

`.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes what is committed in `dist/`
rather than building (building twice adds a way for the two to disagree),
refuses a missing or empty asset, and uses the runner's preinstalled `gh`
(no third-party action pinned).

**Cost then: nobody here could confirm a release exists** (private repo,
deploy key cannot read the API, unauthenticated calls 404). (superseded:
public since 2026-10-19, the releases API answers; CLAUDE.md, *Cutting a
release*.)

**Confirmed by v0.5:** a deploy-key push may add files under
`.github/workflows/` (the workflow-scope restriction applies to PATs over
HTTPS), and a deploy-key tag push triggers a workflow (the no-recursion rule
applies to `GITHUB_TOKEN`-driven events).

## 2026-08-08 — the undecidability was the oracle's fork convention, not the archives

Nine fixtures had no manifest, both reasons properties of `unar -k
visible`: seven held `X` and `X.rsrc` (THINK C projects), so one entry's
sidecar is another's name; two had a leading `~`, which GNUstep's
`stringByAppendingPathExtension:` refuses, so unar writes the AppleDouble
container into the *data*-fork filename, sometimes without the warning the
builder guarded on.

`unar -k hidden` names the container `._NAME`: prefixing never calls the
failing path code, and `._` is disjoint from real names. All nine build; the
suite goes 769 → 778. **The manifest never encoded the convention** (names
and per-fork hashes): rebuilding all 774 pre-existing manifests gave
identical entries, only the `oracle` string differing.

The CLI gained `--forks hidden` for the same reason: comparing two trees in
the same ambiguous encoding lets a mistake cancel out. The default stays
`visible`, matching unar; the harnesses pass the flag.

**"Structurally undecidable" was a claim about the tool's output format,
applied to the data.** TESTING.md quoted the `unar --help` line naming the
remedy, one paragraph from the limitation, from M1 (2026-07-23) until now.
Before recording something impossible, check whether it is impossible
*under a flag you chose*.

Not reached then: the Mac tiers still read `<X>.rsrc` sidecars (closed the
same day, next entry but one), and a CLI user without `--forks hidden` still
got the silent clobber on a THINK C archive (closed the same day, next
entry).

**The trap:** under `-k hidden` a resource-only entry yields only `._X`,
which reads exactly like a dropped data fork — and one `~` fixture has that
shape. It is an empty data fork: `lsar` shows one entry with
`XADIsResourceFork: 1`, the container holds ids 9 and 2 only. Checked on all
nine.

## 2026-08-08 — the CLI refuses to write over its own output

Under the `.rsrc` convention entry `X`'s sidecar and entry `X.rsrc`'s data
fork are one path, opened `"wb"`: on `derived-Unzip101.sit`,
`Source/UnZip.π`'s 7,048 B resource fork became 0 bytes, exit 0, nothing on
stderr.

Every output open now `stat()`s first and fails the entry when the path
exists, naming both remedies (`--forks hidden`, `--overwrite` for the old
behaviour). Per-entry error, nonzero exit.

**Refusing beats switching the default to `._NAME`:** the suffix form is
what unar writes and the docs show, an error can carry its own remedy and a
changed default cannot, and it also covers identical names and
re-extraction into a populated directory.

Exempt: the envelope being unwrapped (it exists while the inner layer
writes, and an inner entry may carry its name); the sink allows that path
and its sidecar. The five unwrap chains in `ci.sh` would catch this being
wrong.

**Fixing the harness can hide the defect it was hiding:** with `run_diff.py`
on `--forks hidden` the corpus no longer exercises the shipped default.
`tests/run_collide.sh` extracts with the DEFAULT and asserts the refusal;
it fails against the pre-fix binary.

**What that test cannot see:** one shape (`X` plus a real `X.rsrc`). No
fixture holds byte-identical names, so that branch is exercised only by
re-extraction, and a collision with an unrelated pre-existing file is not
distinguished from one of our own (both refuse).

## 2026-08-08 — the Mac-side checkers stopped guessing at sidecars

The host-side readers called `<X>.rsrc` a sidecar when `<X>` existed beside
it — wrong precisely for the nine fixtures just recovered. All reference
extractions now use `--forks hidden` and pair `._X`; `aggregate_dir`,
`checkdisk.py` and `check_mac_sink.py` infer nothing. On HFS the resource
fork is inside the file, so there was never an ambiguity on the Mac; the
mock in `tests/mac_sink_test.c` now writes `._X` too, since a `.rsrc` suffix
made it *less* faithful to the File Manager.

Measured on the enlarged 53-fixture sample: **53/53 at 4 MB on System
6.0.8, 53/53 at the 1 MB floor, 53/53 on System 7.0.1**, and **53/53 read
back off the Out volumes with names and folders** (`--keep-disks` +
`checkdisk.py`). Two of the nine also run through the qemu-m68k mock in
`ci.sh`.

**One fixture of a new SHAPE found three harness defects**, all unfailable
rather than passing:

- `check_mac_sink.py` compared UTF-8 manifest names with raw MacRoman on
  disk; every listed fixture was ASCII until `UnZip.π`.
- It gated each comparison on fork size, so an empty data fork was never
  looked for. It now asserts presence whatever the size.
- `checkdisk.py` joined Mac components with `/`, legal in an HFS name
  (`derived-unshar_1.11_folder.sit` holds `mw/68k•unshar π`; two entries
  could not be copied off). Paths are now tuples, joined with `:` only when
  a Mac path is needed.

**The list a harness runs on is part of the harness.**

**The heuristic was in four readers** (`vmac_check.py`, `checkdisk.py`,
`os9.py`, `check_mac_sink.py`), one comment saying so. Fixing three left the
fourth (the OS 9 pair, no CI job) comparing against a tree that no longer
used the convention; found by grepping for `.rsrc`. **One home per finding
applies to code too** — the copy nobody tests is the one that survives.

## 2026-08-08 — "the oracle cannot read it" was the harness throwing evidence away

**Claim.** StuffIt method 1 had no oracle coverage because `unar` fails on
`derived-New_Python.sit`, so no manifest.

**Evidence.** `unar` reads the method-1 fork perfectly — the 470-byte
resource fork of `I Want To Buy Some Cheese` (`rmeth=1`, 470 → 389),
byte-identical to ours. It fails on the *data* fork of `It's A Bit Runny
Sir`, method **3**. Nine of ten forks were ground truth, discarded to avoid
recording the tenth.

**Consequence.** Manifests are built per entry: a fork the oracle failed is
recorded as `"unadjudicated": {fork: reason}` with no hash. 19 fixtures now
contribute; the suite goes 778 → 793 and method 1 is adjudicated. Sabotaging
`sit_rle90`'s run length fails exactly `derived-New_Python.sit`.

- **The all-or-nothing rule was invisible because it never failed:**
  `oracle FAILED on X` read as a property of the fixture, not the builder.
- **A true fact about the archive was applied to the wrong fork** — the
  Arsenic 512 KB shape again.
- **A failed extraction leaves three shapes on disk** (19 fixtures): 0-byte
  file (most), 114,644 B partial output (`guysmaccontacts.sea`), a sidecar
  padded with garbage to the DECLARED length (`appledraw51.cpt`, 13,121 B vs
  our 13,036). "Failed forks must be empty" would have admitted two shapes
  and made the padded sidecar ground truth; the parse is checked instead
  against unar's own failure count and `lsar`'s entry list.
- **An excuse must be anchored to the other implementation:** a per-entry
  error from `macextract` is tolerated only where the oracle failed that
  entry. Tolerating "recognized but unsupported" generally would excuse
  every StuffIt fixture the day the dispatch table broke.

**A fixture for what one real fork cannot reach:** `tools/synth_sit1.py`
generates `synth-sit-rle90.sit` (layout from the XADStuffItParser.m offsets
the parser cites, RLE90 as the inverse of XADRLE90Handle.m, self-tested).
The real fork has 25 run escapes and one literal `0x90`; the synthetic adds
runs *of* `0x90`, the maximum 255-byte token, multi-token runs, output
ending inside a run and the shortest legal token, on both forks. Breaking
only `c == 255` fails `synth-sit-rle90.sit` and **nothing else among the 225
StuffIt fixtures**.

## 2026-08-08 — a second oracle: `macunpack` adjudicates what `unar` cannot

**Claim.** "There is no oracle for method 6." **Evidence against.**
`reference/macutils/macunpack/sit.c` has decoded StuffIt fixed Huffman since
1991 and was already in `reference/`. **Consequence.**
`tools/build_macunpack.sh` builds it from a copy of the read-only tree and
`make_manifests.py` offers it every fork `unar` left unadjudicated: 23 forks
across 9 fixtures gained ground truth, the suite went 793 → 795, and the only
unadjudicated forks left are ones our engine also declines. Only 1 of the 23
is method 6.

- **"No oracle exists" is a statement about one tool** — it sat in three
  status files for a week.
- **A build flag can delete the branch under test:** macunpack must be built
  `-m32` — `util.c`'s `get4()` returns `unsigned long` assigned to a `long`,
  so the sign test selecting a *stored* method-6 segment is unreachable on
  LP64, which dies "Premature EOF" exactly on the branch the synthetic
  fixture exists for.
- **A predicted output filename becomes ground truth:** macunpack names via
  `transname.c` (many-to-one) and writes nothing for an empty fork, so a
  mispredicted name looks like two empty forks. The builder requires the
  `.info` file macunpack writes per extracted entry, and refuses names two
  entries share.

## 2026-08-08 — StuffIt method 6: the tree is generated, not built

Method 6's Huffman tree SHAPE is a format constant: macunpack derives it per
fork from a fixed weight table (`code6[258]`) by recursively splitting the
leaf range at half the remaining weight (`sit_dosplit`); only each leaf's
byte is declared per segment. `tools/gen_sit6_tables.py` computed it once
into `src/sit6_tables.h`: 514 nodes, depth 13, two `uint16_t` tables with
leaf rows dropped.

**The generated table is gone since 2026-09-21** — 26 bytes and a
builder state the same code book, and `tools/check_sit6_tree.py`
is what that generator became: *2026-09-21, (the table that was
twenty-six bytes)*.

Generating it bought no recursion, no per-fork 68000 cycles, and a generator
that checks itself (a tree, all 258 leaves reachable once, no dangling
node) — *a tree that agrees only with itself proves nothing*.

The segment buffer is freed and reallocated when a segment needs more, never
grown by copying: the old contents are dead at a boundary. Same shape as the
LZW table (2026-08-03), opposite answer, same reason — whether the old bytes
are still needed.

**A fixture for what one real fork cannot reach:** the corpus's one method-6
fork (34,818 B, `derived-INITLoader.sit`) is two Huffman segments — no
*stored* branch, no `0x80` PackBits filler, no shortest run, no third
segment. `tools/synth_sit6.py` generates `synth-sit-fixhuf.sit` (five
entries, ten method-6 forks): the stored branch, both segment orders, every
PackBits control-byte edge, a one-byte and a 254-byte alphabet, twelve
segments in one fork. It reads the tree from the generated header and
self-tests by decoding its own output. All ten forks are byte-exact against
macunpack, including the stored branch an LP64 oracle cannot see.

## 2026-08-08 — an excuse must be anchored outside our own output

A review of the per-entry oracle work found no hardcoded fixture names but
two excuses that could not fail — found by asking *what evidence does this
tolerance rest on?*

**The first rested on our own error message:** `run_diff.py` skipped a
fixture when every entry failed "recognized but unsupported", so the thing
graded decided whether it was graded. Costs: `4acalc.zip` and
`4alnch11.zip` carry adjudicated hashes for 5 of 7 entries (unar implements
Implode), so ten forks plus names and counts went uncompared, the M8 reason
("even unar fails on them") false since that morning — **two files
disagreeing**, the third finding by that mechanism; and a regression making a
SUPPORTED method report "unsupported" for a whole archive became a skip,
guarded only by a printed count vs a TESTING.md number that went 3 → 2 the
same day.

The excuse is now anchored in the ORACLE: manifests record `lsar`'s
`oracle_methods`, and "recognized but unsupported" is excused only where the
oracle's method is out of scope (`ORACLE_OUT_OF_SCOPE`, then just
`Implode`). Nothing is skipped for what our binary says; an out-of-scope
entry is still graded on its name, count and anything written. The set lists
only methods the corpus contains: an unlisted one fails loudly.

**The second rested on the oracle too coarsely:** one failed fork excused
the whole entry, so an adjudicated sibling fork was never required (six
fixtures). Absence is now excused only for out-of-scope entries.

**Both demonstrated failing first**, with stub binaries: one writing nothing
for `•Draw 5.1.cpt` (78,123 B adjudicated data fork), one calling every entry
of `derived-Export.sit` unsupported. Real results unchanged; 795 → 797 graded
(the two zips).

**Also guarded:** `matchkey()` flattens `:` and `/` to `_`, so two names can
share a key and a failure be attributed to the wrong entry — leaving the real
one holding hashes of whatever unar dropped. No fixture collides; the builder
now refuses one that does, as the macunpack matcher already did. **Two
matchers in one file disagreeing about one hazard is a bug even when neither
has fired.**

## 2026-08-08 — Multi-segment archives: one scheme, chosen for its header

Multi-segment moved from out of scope to in; one scheme implemented, the rest
filed in OPEN_ITEMS.md. Parts may be anywhere and named anything, which is
decidable only where a part says what it is:

| scheme | what identifies a part | oracle here |
|---|---|---|
| StuffIt segments | 100-byte header: part number, original name, 26 fingerprint bytes | `unar` |
| Compact Pro segmented | a volume byte per archive and per entry; segment 2+ layout undocumented | **none** — neither `unar` nor `macunpack` extracts them |
| spanned Zip | the filename extension* | `unar` |
| `.001` split | the filename, and nothing else | `unar`, only when part 1 is not itself a recognizable archive |

\* Too coarse, corrected 2026-08-09 when the scheme was implemented:
its first and last parts DO identify themselves, and the last is the
only place the part count is written. See the entry of that date.

StuffIt segments is the cheapest and strongest, and its join touches no
decoder (the payload is a byte concatenation, an envelope like MacBinary).
Compact Pro has no reference implementation, so it needs a genuine sample
first. (superseded: all four schemes were built — DECISIONS.md 2026-08-09,
2026-08-10 and 2026-08-14 below.)

- **The engine sequences, the host opens:** parts arrive through an
  `UncVolumeSource` callback; the joiner is caller-provided (no allocation);
  "where is part 2?" is a directory scan in the CLI, an alert on the Mac.
  **One part open at a time:** a one-drive Plus cannot mount two, and
  System 6 counts its FCBs.
- **The header gives away two things:** `rsrclen + datalen` is the exact
  payload total, so completeness needs no part count (none is stored, which
  is why XADMaster stops at the first gap); and a one-part set extracts with
  no volume source.
- **A missing part is the archive's verdict:** reported as EOF, the entry
  ends `UNC_ERR_TRUNCATED` with partial output kept, and the call returns
  `UNC_ERR_SEGMENTED` — declared in `macextract.h` since M0, first produced
  here.
- **Backward crossings are measured:** `unc_segment_stats()` / `--stats`
  count part re-opens (on removable media, a disk swap): **0 on both the
  3-part and 12-part cases.** Reported per run, since it is a property of the
  container inside the join.

### The oracle's discovery is name-gated; ours is not

`unar` matches parts by content but only among files whose name starts with
the opened part's basename, so a renamed set vanishes from it. Ours reads
every file in the folder. The `misnamed` case is therefore adjudicated on a
renamed copy of the same bytes.

**The trap:** `unar Part.1` joins nothing and extracts part 1 alone,
looking successful, while `unar ./Part.1` works — `[name
stringByDeletingLastPathComponent]` returns `@""` and the `if(!dirname)
dirname=@"."` guard tests nil, not emptiness. A manifest built that way would
be truncated and our correct output would "fail". Recorded in TESTING.md.

## 2026-08-09 — Driving the segment dialog: a UI harness cannot tell its own bugs from the application's

The emulated join used the autotest build, which does not compile
`SegAskUser`. `tools/vmac/interactive.py --segments` leaves part 1 on the
boot volume and the rest on a second floppy, forcing the alert. It works;
both bugs found were the harness's, **and both photographed like application
bugs**:

- *"Part 1 of derived-Cal.sit has not been found"*: Standard File opens on
  the LAST-INSERTED volume, so the click opened part **2**, and asking for
  part 1 was correct. The phase now clicks Drive first and photographs the
  volume before touching a row.
- NOT FOUND for a working run: `Mac()` boots a private *copy*, and the
  read-back opened the pristine template.

The phase ends on a **byte comparison** of the joined file read off the
volume the Mac wrote to, and on a miss prints the volume listing ("not
found" cannot distinguish a wrong name from a failed extraction).

Locating one part rescans its folder, so supplying part 2 also picks up part
3 beside it — one line in `SegAskUser`, one interruption instead of one per
disk.

## 2026-08-09 — Asking where the output goes, on a system with no folder picker

Output beside the archive is wrong on floppies: that volume must be ejected
for the next part.

**There is no folder picker:** `CustomGetFile` is System 7, the floor is
System 6.0.x, so the classic idiom is `SFPutFile` with the name ignored,
now called between `SFGetFile` and extraction. Standard File keeps ONE
current folder across both, so Return means "beside the archive" — the old
behaviour.

**Traps, photographed:**

- The prompt is one ~200-point static text item that does not wrap:
  "Extract the files into this folder:" rendered on System 6 as "Extract the
  files into this". Now "Extract into this folder:".
- Seeding the name with `reply.fName` raised **"Replace existing
  "archive.sit"?"** on the DEFAULT path (nothing is written under that name;
  the default button No returns to the dialog). The default name is a
  constant now.
- The two dialogs look alike; the second was reported as the first redrawn.
  **`SFGetFile`'s `prompt` is documented "Ignored"** (Inside Macintosh:
  Files) — confirmed first by photograph, 0 of 175,104 pixels differing.
- **`DITL` -4000** (read from the System file's resource fork; the parser
  cross-checked by reproducing our `DITL` 128 against `mac/macextract.r`):
  item 10 is an *enabled* empty `statText` at t=1044 l=20 b=1145 r=116, a
  thousand points below a 348x200 dialog; item 2 is parked at t=1152.
  Apple's route is `SFPGetFile` with a *customized* template, so dragging it
  into view under the standard one is undocumented — not built on.
- **The white band is layout:** the open dialog's first item starts at t=39,
  the save dialog's at t=29 — the 21-against-11 measured on screen.

So the cue is POSITION: the destination dialog opens 30 points down and
right (open 366x216, destination 322x200, both whole on 512x342).

**The bug was reachable only where nothing looked:** `--dest` switched to an
EMPTY floppy where nothing collides, so it passed twice while the default
path was broken; the default interactive phase sat in the alert and printed
"extraction settled after ~134s" (photograph-only by design,
tools/vmac/README.md). Found by looking at the frames. A test aimed at a new
path can leave the default less covered than before.

### A "the screen stopped changing" oracle is a "the screen is changing slowly" oracle

`--dest` asserts on the volumes, and its first run reported output on the
WRONG volume: `Mac.settle` (two identical consecutive frames) returned at 33%,
because the dialog repaints once per 8–16 KB of *input*. `quiet=EXTRACT_QUIET`
now demands SECONDS of stillness exceeding the worst repaint gap, on every
settle waiting for an extraction.

- **The unsound wait had been in every interactive phase since M10** and
  never failed, since they judged by eye; the first assertion that could
  fail accused the application — the third harness defect in two days
  dressed as an application bug.
- **The readback re-derived a solved problem:** `hls -1` split on
  whitespace, so "Demo Manual V1.6" was three names; `checkdisk.walk` (since
  2026-08-08) is imported now. A harness that re-derives a name rule gets the
  old version.
