## 2026-08-21 (the Symantec release) — DiskDoubler's four publishers, and what the headerless record selects on

Checked online: Terry Morse and Lloyd Chambers formed **Salient Software**
around it in 1990, standalone through 3.7.x; Salient went to **Fifth
Generation Systems in 1992**, first bundled as *SuperDoubler 4.0* (with
AutoDoubler and CopyDoubler); then **Symantec** shipped **Norton DiskDoubler
Pro 1.1**, a fat binary, never part of Norton Utilities.

**The "1.1" is the disk:** `vers 2` reads *Norton DiskDoubler Pro™ Disk 1.1*,
`vers 1` **4.1.1** — the version OPEN_ITEMS.md named for the `0x1000`
record. `tools/vmac/ndd.py` runs 4.0 (Macintosh Garden) and 4.1.1 (the
Symantec floppy).

### The floppy is a corpus, and the boot image is our own output

Every file on the Norton disk ships DiskDoubler-compressed (`DDF0`–`DDF3`,
creator `DDAP`): ten specimens, methods 0 and 10.

- **`DiskTester™` 3.7.7 ships compressed on the Symantec floppy and
  UNCOMPRESSED in the Fifth Generation 4.0 StuffIt archive.** Our decode
  equals the uncompressed copy outside the 112-byte system-reserved window,
  where 46 bytes differ (DiskDoubler's `DDAppExpandTempFile` bookkeeping vs
  the Installer's): a method 10 resource fork graded against a copy no
  DiskDoubler touched, and independent evidence for the masking convention
  FORMATS.md applies to the 8 unadjudicated forks.
- **The System 7 boot image is built from forks this engine decoded:** the
  `INIT/DDI4` extension is a method 10 container, so a Mac that boots it runs
  our output; a wrong byte gives a machine that will not start.

### The `0x1000` record: the claim was half a condition

Two sessions looked for a `0x1000` record with a resource fork; both
produced ordinary headers with the data stored. **The corpus said why:**
`ddtf-*.dd` and `ddtf-*.sea` hold **30** `0x1000` records, all fork-less,
beside **45** ordinary headers with stored data and a resource fork
(`Test Text`, eleven bytes stored, full header, 332-byte resource fork).
Measured in one archive (`ndd.py --stored`):

| data fork | resource fork | record |
|---|---|---|
| incompressible (40 B, 300 B, 20,000 B) | none | **`0x1000`** |
| incompressible (300 B, 20,000 B) | 335-338 B | `0xABCD0054`, data stored, fork AD1 |
| compressible | none | `0xABCD0054`, AD1 |
| compressible | 336 B | `0xABCD0054`, both AD1 |

**The headerless record is written exactly when the data fork is stored AND
there is no resource fork**, at any size.

- **A `0x1000` record with a resource fork cannot be written** — nothing to
  wait for; `+87` describes no fork any archive can have. `+86` as the data
  fork's checksum is now measured: flipping one payload byte gives *checksum
  mismatch* on that entry alone.
- **`+54` creation, `+58` modification:** subjects given 1990 creation and
  1995 modification via MacBinary came back `+54` = 1990. The guess was right.
- **`unar` is still wrong about all of it.**

### Methods 2-5 are Salient-era, and that is now dated rather than guessed

Three readings say no method 2–5 in the last version: 4.1.1's **Compress
Using** submenu (AD 1, AD 2, DD 1, DD 2, DD 3); `MENU 195`, `196`, `197` in
both **4.0** and **4.1.1**, read on the host (BLOCKERS.md's `MENU 5019`
trick, no boot); and **`STR# 403`**, the "Compressed Using" vocabulary —
`AD 1 | AD 2 | DD 1 | DD 2 | DD 3 | AIC | other | A | B | Sigma | S |
none`, with **no name** for 2–5, which fall to `other`. With the ownership
history, methods 2-5 belong to Salient's 1.x/2.x, before the 1992 sale;
bounded by five releases checked instead of two. (superseded: the Salient
disk, next entry.)

**DiskDoubler's own expander cannot read method 7 without the hardware**
(`STR# 1` string 19: *compressed with Sigma hardware and no hardware is
installed*). This engine decodes what that disk's application cannot.

### The lesson

The claim was derived from real records and was *half a condition*; no smell
points at that. **30 records that fit beside 45 that contradict it, in the
same fifteen files.** Next to "ask what evidence a tolerance rests on": **ask
what a corpus does NOT do that the claim would allow.**

## 2026-08-21 (the Salient disk) — method 2, and the archive nobody here searched

Two links handed over: justsolve's DiskDoubler page (a database error all
afternoon, unread) and **`winworldpc.com/product/diskdoubler/3x`**:
**3.1.2, 1991, Salient**, an 800K floppy in a 7-zip with its SHA-1 —
older than anything here, where OPEN_ITEMS.md had said "no COMPRESSOR older
than 3.2 is reachable" (BLOCKERS.md).

### What was on it

A distribution disk is a corpus, the third time it has paid:

    tools/vmac/ndd.py --specimens      24 containers, 0 failed
    forks by method: 1 x1, 2 x1, 7 x22

- **A method 2 fork:** `Goodies/Programmers Only/XCMD ƒ/XCMD.h`, 564 bytes
  into 386, the only one seen.
- **Method 7 forks of up to EIGHT chunks**, 97,906 bytes (the 3.7 disk's had
  one each). The codec reads chunks as one continuous bit stream, as the
  reference does; eight chunks decode, the XOR checksum agrees, and flipping
  any of three spaced bytes fails it. The item is closed.

### Method 2

An order-1 adaptive code: 256 splay trees, chosen by the byte just produced,
each starting as the complete binary tree over 256 leaves (internal node j
has children 2j and 2j+1, node 256+b is byte b's leaf), the used leaf rotated
toward the root; no table transmitted. Method 5 is the same codec with a
leading tree-count byte; still declined (no specimen). Source:
`XADDiskDoublerMethod2Handle.m` (tree, splay), `XADDiskDoublerParser.m`
case 2 (tree count, XOR condition, checksum). The 0x5a XOR over DECODED bytes
is method 1's under `info1 >= 0x2a`/`info2 & 0x80` (the specimen has `info1`
exactly 0x2a); the sum needs no header adjustment.

**Graded three ways, as one specimen requires:** the stored 16-bit sum
matches (0xab41); a Python transcription written before the C gives the
identical 564 bytes; the output is a legible 1990 Salient copyright header
for HyperCard XCMDs. Corrupting the stored sum (re-stamping the header's
XMODEM CRC) yields a checksum mismatch, so the check is live.

**Memory is the number of distinct context bytes:** a tree is 1,536 bytes and
built only on first use; the specimen touches 60 and measures 101,888 B; all
256 would want ~392 KB and fail per entry on 1 MB. Not growth-on-demand —
nothing copied or resized; the untouched state is *known*, which is what
makes lazy allocation right here.

### The lesson, and it is about searching

Macintosh Garden, funet and Macintosh Repository were searched; WinWorld, a
PC-centric library, had the 1991 disk. BLOCKERS.md's fourth smell: **a
limitation stated about the environment that is true only of one tool** (the
three sites somebody thought of). When an open item says what is missing is
A FILE, search for the file, not for the story.

## 2026-08-21 (methods 3, 4 and 5) — writing DiskDoubler files so DiskDoubler can grade them

The premise "no oracle" was false: Salient's 1991 `DiskDoubler™ App` and INIT
come off that floppy uncompressed and expand whatever they are given.
`tools/vmac/ddencode.py` **encodes** a fork, builds a `0xABCD0054` container
with a correct header CRC, and lets the 1991 application expand it. All three
come back byte-exact; method 5 also under 4.1.1.

- **It grades our reading of the FORMAT** — escape byte, tree serialization,
  bit order, checksum base, XOR gate.
- **It does not grade our decoder against encodings our encoder never
  emits**, so these stay listed as having no specimen.

### Three things it measured that neither reference states

- **The 0x5a XOR applies to methods 1, 2 and 5, not 3 and 4:** XORing all
  four, the expander returned exactly `SUBJECT ^ 0x5a` for 3 and 4 — a
  constant XOR cannot come from a wrong codec, so one run confirmed both
  codecs and located the difference. Headers carried `info1 = 0x2a`, as
  **every** real file on the 1991 disk does (24 of 24). macutils agrees by
  construction (only `dd_lzc` applies `dd_xor`); **XADMaster's case 4
  disagrees**, marked untested by its author. We follow what shipped.
- **DiskDoubler 4.1.1 has dropped methods 3 and 4** (*Unknown compression
  method… created by a more recent version*), so the 1991 expander is the
  only oracle for them.
- **Only a method 5 tree count of 0 is confirmed** (0 means 256); a count of
  16 is rejected by both expanders (*Checksum failed*). The branch stays as
  XADMaster's reading, failing loudly, and is named untested in
  OPEN_ITEMS.md.

### What the escape byte cost, and the shape of that mistake

macutils declares method 3's escape `#define ESC 0x144` = 324, which a byte
can never equal, so its method 3 copies input to output. Read as decimal
**144** it is exactly RLE90 (escape 0x90, `ESC 0` literal, `ESC n` a run),
the filter already used for ARC — labelled a hypothesis until the expander
agreed. **A reference marked untested can be a no-op rather than wrong**,
which reads as "implemented" to anyone counting references (the second in
that file, after method 7's segfault).

### Why the first --expand run proved less than it looked

One expanded, three untouched: expanding a `TEXT` file launched TeachText,
and the next `Cmd-O` went to TeachText's Open dialog. Fixed by clicking the
Finder window first and giving subjects a type nothing owns. **The frame
that shows the damage is never the frame of the click that caused it.**

## 2026-08-22 — one byte, and the eight forks that had no oracle

Eight resource forks across two fixtures had been not ground truth since M12:
`unar` refuses them, macunpack's DiskDoubler table stops at 9, and the Mac
expander restamps bytes 16..127.

**`unar`'s DDn reads exactly one byte past the fork's declared compressed
length.** Sweeping 0, 1, 2, 4, 8 … 64 bytes of slack: it flips at 1 and stays
fixed. The 1,166-byte reproduction (one container, one file, two DDn forks)
is `tools/xadmaster-ddn-repro/`, ready to post and **deliberately not
posted** (OPEN_ITEMS.md); the sweep exists because of the rule learned from
the withdrawn `HOpen` attribution.

**`unar`'s output is then RIGHT:** with the slack, all 33 forks of the two
archives equal ours byte for byte (16..127 included) and equal DiskDoubler's
own expander outside that window. Three implementations, one answer.
`tools/run_ddforks.py` hands `unar` each fork in a container with **the
fixture's own compressed bytes, unmodified**, declared length +1 and one pad
byte; every fork decoded with pad 0x00 and 0xFF, both must agree.

`oracle-unadjudicated` falls from **24 forks across 12 fixtures to 16 across
10**; both DiskDoubler fixtures leave the list; `ci.sh` checks the eight
hashes.

### Two things worth keeping

**An oracle that refuses one input may accept a presentation of the same
bytes** — the bound is ours to set, since we build the container (beside "an
oracle you can only feed is still an oracle" from methods 3-5).

**The pairing check earned its place:** `run_ddforks.py --write` first paired
manifest entries to headers by position — right for one fixture, wrong for
the other (manifest ordered by name) — and the guard caught it before writing
a hash under the wrong name for `ci.sh` to enforce forever. Matching is by
the data fork's hash; a non-unique pairing is an error.

## 2026-08-22 (later) — SuperDisk!'s compressor, which was said not to survive

"SuperDisk!'s compressor does not survive here" was false: Macintosh
Repository has the 1991 **` SuperDisk!` control panel** (`cdev`/`AlyS`, an
89 KB resource fork). `tools/vmac/sdcompress.py` installs and drives it. It
runs under System 7: "Make File", Auto X / Alerts / Security, a Compress
page with **Off / Light / Tighter** beside Speed and Memory (*"SuperDisk!'s
default setting is 'Faster' compression."*). "Make File" on an 11,136-byte
subject wrote `Alpha.x`, `APPL/AlYS`, 2,372 bytes data and a 5,730-byte
resource fork (the `AutX` auto-expand stub). Specimens are producible on
demand.

### What it produced is not the container this engine reads

The corpus archives open with eight unread bytes then records (`0x29` folder,
`0x28` file). `Alpha.x` opens

    0000 2b80  0000 2b80  0000 0000  'TEXT' 'ttxt' … 05 "Alpha" …

— SuperDisk!'s **single-file form**, standing to the archive as DiskDoubler's
`0xABCD0054` to `DDAR`. `unc_sniff` said *unknown*. (read: next entry.)

### Two traps, both photographed

- **The boot image accumulates the panel's state** (settings *and current
  page*), so a coordinate from page 1 hit page 2's "Off". `session()`
  rebuilds the boot image every run — a machine that remembers.
- **The extension is the result, not the trigger:** renaming `Alpha` to
  `Alpha.x` under SuperDisk! changed nothing (measured). An hour went into
  the Finder rename before the panel was opened.

## 2026-08-22 (later still) — SuperDisk!'s other container, derived by making it

    +0  (4) total uncompressed size, and it EQUALS +4 plus +8
    +4  (4) data fork size          +8  (4) resource fork size
    +12 (4) type                    +16 (4) creator
    +20 (2) Finder flags
    +22 (4) creation date           +26 (4) modification date
    +30     the name, Pascal, padded to an even total length
            then the data fork's blocks, then the resource fork's

**The payload is the block chain already decoded** — tested first: the
first specimen's bytes at that offset read `clen=2336, ulen=11136, method=1`,
`sd_block_head`'s layout. A 35-byte header and a fork split, not a codec.

### The layout was derived by choosing subjects that disagree

The first specimen (no resource fork, `+0` = `+4`, `+8` zero) would have
misled. Five subjects separated the fields (`sdcompress.py --specimens`):

| subject | what it pinned |
|---|---|
| `Forked`, a resource fork | `+0` is the TOTAL, `+4` data, `+8` resource — 3338 = 3000 + 338 |
| `Dated`, stamped 1990 and 1995 | `+22` creation, `+26` modification, both exact |
| `LongerNameHere 12345`, 20 chars | the Pascal name, and that the body is padded to an EVEN offset |
| `Big`, 44,544 bytes | more than one block in the chain |
| `Alpha`, the baseline | — |

Three of the five names make `31 + nlen` even by themselves; only the 20-char
one puts a junk byte (0xAA) where an unpadded reader would look for a block
header. All five byte-exact incl. resource fork and multi-block
(`sdcompress.py --verify`); dates, type, creator, flags as stamped.

### What is in `ci.sh` and what is not

The specimens come from a commercial application under emulation and there
is no encoder, so `ci.sh` gets a hand-built STORED-block container (header,
fork split, metadata, sniffer); the five specimens cover the codec on demand.
The sniffer leans on `total == data + rsrc`, a 32-bit identity random data
fails and which separates this from an archive; the unit test breaks it by
one and requires the sniffer to let go.

## 2026-08-22 (last) — the settings sweep, and the decoder that had never run

`sdcompress.py --sweep` compresses the SAME bytes once per setting:

| setting | method | 10,376 bytes becomes |
|---|---|---|
| Speed = Fast | **6** | 884 |
| Speed = Faster (the default) | 1 | 2,280 |
| Speed = Fastest | 1 | 2,282 |
| Speed = Fast, Compress = Off | **6** | 888 |
| Speed = Fast, Compress = Tight | 1 | 2,284 |
| Speed = Fast, Compress = Tighter | **6** | 892 |

Methods 10, 13, 20 are not among them: this compressor writes 1 or 6. The
Compress axis does not move the method cleanly ("Fast + Tight" gave 1) —
an interaction or a setting not sticking; unresolved, not worth it.

### Method 6 had never decoded anything, and did not work

OPEN_ITEMS.md listed methods 1-6, 8, 9 as "transcribed and compiled and
nothing more". The first method 6 block failed *file is truncated*: the flag
bitmap is `ceil(ulen/8)` bytes (1,297 for 10,376), but the engine asked for
`((ulen >> 3) + 4) & ~1` = 1,300 — the STORED bitmap's slack, which the coded
form lacks; methods 1, 3 and the corpus's 7 take the stored branch. Fixed;
all eleven control-panel specimens (methods 1 and 6) decode byte-exact.

### What this says about the untested list

**A list of code that has never run predicts where the next bug is** — one of
its two methods failed on first contact. **A constant shared between a
tested path and an untested path is a place to look.**

## 2026-08-22 (SpaceSaver) — reachable, not yet runnable, and a licence question

StuffIt SpaceSaver could not be NAMED (no reference, layout or specimen).
**The application is reachable:** it ships inside StuffIt Deluxe, every era
on Macintosh Garden — **3.5.1** and **4.0** two-floppy InstallerMaker sets,
and **5.0.1's CD-ROM** (a 224 MB Apple-partitioned ISO `hmount` opens) with a
**standalone `SpaceSaver 5.0 Installer`** and a User's Guide PDF.
`tools/vmac/spacesaver.py` lifts and drives that installer.

**It does not run on System 7.0.1, measured:** after the licence it warns
*requires system software version 7.5.3* and *requires 8000K of physical
memory*; answering Yes to both bombs with **"'SpaceSaver™ 5.0 Installer'
unimplemented trap."**

### The licence, which is the maintainer's call and not this session's

The licence says *"You may not modify, adapt, translate, reverse engineer,
decompile, or disassemble the Software."* SuperDisk! was derived by
disassembling `CODE 2`; for SpaceSaver that route is what the licence names.
Black-box derivation (compress known input, compare outputs — SuperDisk!'s
single-file container, 2026-08-22) is not reverse engineering the program.
Position taken pending the maintainer: **specimens yes, disassembly no.**

**Answered 2026-08-22: the maintainer waived it and took responsibility**,
so the disassembly route is open for SpaceSaver as it was for SuperDisk!.
This entry stays because the reasoning is still the reasoning — and
because one thing was NOT waived and was not attempted: see below.

## 2026-08-22 (SpaceSaver, later) — both installers, and the wall that is not a licence clause

**SpaceSaver 5.0** still bombs on 7.0.1 (*unimplemented trap*). **StuffIt
Deluxe 3.5.1** (the era 7.0.1 fits) runs to a registration panel wanting a
name, organization and **registration number**: *"The registration number
that you have entered is invalid."*

**That wall was not climbed:** the waiver covered reverse engineering a
format; a registration number is licence ENFORCEMENT, a different act.
Nothing went looking for a serial; that would be a separate, explicit
decision.

Route left then: a **System 7.5.3 image** (free from Apple) beside
`System6.hfv` and `Sys7.img`.

### What was learned about driving this installer, which transfers

- Every panel in both Aladdin installers **swallows the first input**; the
  second acts. Three runs read it as a wrong coordinate. The tell: the frame
  after the input is *identical* to the one before, where a real miss shows
  something else.
- **Order:** 3.5.1 is splash → **read-me** → registration; assuming no read-me
  produced *"You must enter a name in order to register this product"* — an
  error describing the harness.

## 2026-08-22 (SpaceSaver, last) — what the registration wall actually costs

The maintainer pointed at Macintosh Garden's StuffIt Deluxe page, which
publishes registration codes for these discontinued versions; using a
published code for abandonware in an emulator to read a format is a
different act from defeating the check, and is the one taken.

| installer | result |
|---|---|

## 2026-08-22 (SpaceSaver, calling it) — the rename commits, the image does not see it

**The rename commits:** a settled frame shows `Alphasmall` and `Forkedsmall`
while the image holds `Alpha` and `Forked` — the Finder renames and **the
change never reaches the image**: HFS directory updates sit in the cache and

produced a run that never booted (striped garbage on its first frame), so its
"unchanged" says nothing.

**Called:** ten runs of twenty minutes, the last two adding a
non-deterministic infrastructure failure.

### The approach that should be tried instead

**Read the format out of the software** (`cdev/SMKR`, 289 KB resource fork):
the SuperDisk! route, host minutes instead of boots, repeatable, and the
licence clause waived 2026-08-22. A layout makes the format nameable; a
specimen is still wanted to grade a decoder. (done: next entry.)

## 2026-08-22 (SpaceSaver, the layout) — read out of the software, as recommended

**`tools/vmac/spacesaver.py --layout`, no emulator, repeatable.**

**The layout is not in the control panel:** its `ACMP 1` only sniffs (eight
bytes, two magics). The writer is `SSEn 1` in `StuffIt Engine™`, and **it
ships its MacsBug symbols**: 133, incl. `ReadSSHeader`, `WriteSSHeader`,
`DefaultSSHeader`, `UpdateSSHeader`, `CompressFork`, `ExpandFork`,
`IsFileCmpressed`, `MakeDFile` — each after its routine's RTS, so also the
boundaries. **Naming the file that carries the format is a step of its own.**
Container, record and module table: `--layout` output, tabulated in
FORMATS.md.

### Four things the bytes say that a specimen would not have shown quickly

- **Fork records are fixed, streams are not:** record 1 is always data,
  record 2 resource (`mExpandFile`), but `mCompressFile` gives offset 84 to
  the LARGER fork. Record order = stream order is right half the time, and a
  one-fork specimen cannot catch it.
- **A compressed file is recognised by its LENGTH:** `IsFileCmpressed`
  refuses a data fork whose length has a non-zero low byte unless the type is
  `SPSV`; `mCompressFile` rounds EOF up to 256. The magic confirms; so
  `unc_sniff` must read the magic ("multiple of 256" is no evidence).
- **The compressor byte is an index, not a resource id:** `CheckCompressor`
  takes the high byte of the module's word at +0x20 as index, low byte as
  revision (higher kept), gated on a CPU mask at +0x24 (bit 31 minus Gestalt
  `cput`, PowerPC's 0x0101.. mapped to 8). `Alg 3` (68030+), its
  decompress-only twin and its PowerPC build all claim index 3. **One number
  in a file, three implementations, chosen by the machine reading it.**
- **The default method is a CPU decision, inverted from intuition:**
  68000/68010/68020 get index 4, 68030+ index 3 (`Alg 4` mask `f0000000`,
  `Alg 3` `0fff0000`); decompress-only modules are `ffff0000`, so any Mac
  reads any file.

### What is still missing, and what it is not

The two bitstreams: index 3 and 4 are `CMod 11` (7,536 bytes) and `CMod 21`
(2,202 bytes), decompress-only modules in the same fork, called at module+0x10
with a seven-callback parameter block; the engine adds no framing. The
SuperDisk! bargain again: transcription and grading, and grading wants a
specimen `--make` has not produced.

## 2026-08-22 (SpaceSaver, the codecs) — two of five, and a dictionary that is not ours

### The module interface, which is the same for all five

`ExpandFork` @0x5ee6 builds one parameter block and calls the module at
+0x10: seven callbacks (read, write, get/set source position, source EOF,
progress, debug), the refcon they take, compressed and uncompressed lengths,
a pointer and length, and the work buffer and size. **No module framing.**
Each `CMod`'s head wrappers (@0x2e, @0x4a, ...) call `pb->[n]` with
`pb->[28]` first, so the shape is read off the module.

### Method 0 is stored, and says so twice

`CMod 1`, 374 bytes: compressor sets compressed length = original and calls
`XferData` @0xee (a copy loop); the expander calls the same. The reader
checks `clen == ulen`.

### Method 4 is an LZSS, and the shape is in FORMATS.md

- **A block's length counts its own header:** @0x4e8 subtracts `clen` from a
  count started at the block header, so the six bytes are inside it; reading
  it as payload desyncs on block two.
- **The window is not reset per block:** @0x438 compacts and continues, so a
  match may reach into the previous block.

### The finding that changes what an extractor can promise

**The window starts loaded with a preset dictionary, and it is Aladdin's.**
@0x280 copies `pb->[44]` for `pb->[48]` bytes into the window just BEFORE the
first output byte. `ExpandFork` passes a `PrAm` resource's master pointer
and (via the `GetHandleSize` glue at @0x3e4) its size, chosen by the fork
record's byte +12 (0 in everything this engine writes); `LoadCompressors`
@0x10c8 loads index 0 from `'PrAm'` **-4048**: 9,679 bytes opening
*"/\* Copyright (c) 1993 Aladdin Systems, Inc. This source code and specific
concepts contained herein are confidential information and property of
Aladdin Systems"*, then 68k mnemonics, C fragments and Mac boilerplate — a
preset dictionary in the zlib sense, the copyright notice IN the compressible
data.

- **A decoder cannot be correct without those bytes;** every fork's first
  matches reach into them.
- **This project cannot ship them** (same rule as fixtures and the ROM):
  `UncOptions.preset` exists, `macextract --preset FILE` fills it from the
  user's own SpaceSaver, and `spacesaver.py --layout` writes the resource out.
  (superseded: the table ships, by the maintainer's decision — DECISIONS.md
  2026-08-23 (SpaceSaver, the dictionary), *carrying 9,679 bytes that are
  not ours*.)
- **Absence must be a failure, not a silence:** zeroes decode to
  plausible-looking wrong bytes. The reader tracks how far back history
  reaches and refuses a farther distance per entry; `run_spacesaver.py`
  re-runs every passing specimen WITHOUT the dictionary and requires failure.

### Why 1, 2 and 3 are declined, and what the module table settles

By the CPU masks (`Alg 4` `f0000000`, 68000–68020; `Alg 3` `0fff0000`, 68030+
and PowerPC; decompress-only `ffff0000`) and the engine's default, a Mac Plus
can only be made to write method 4; 1, 2 and 3 are declined per entry for
want of an oracle, modules in hand. (later: DECISIONS.md 2026-08-25
(SpaceSaver's codecs, off the Macintosh), *the specimen problem, solved by the
compressor*.)

## 2026-08-23 — AppleLink `.pkg`, named at last, and what a recogniser is

The `PKG Expand Translator` (found 2026-08-22) is Aladdin's reader for the
format.

### Where the format's identity actually lives

The translator does no file I/O (no `_Read`, no `_Open`, 23 `_HFSDispatch`
calls): it gets the file as a HANDLE. `main(pb, selector)`; selector bit 1 is
"can you take this?" — @0xec6 runs @0x2952 over `pb@(4)` and answers `-1` or
`0` in `pb@(8)`. @0x2952 uses no magic: a TOKENIZER (@0xf18; skips space,
tab, CR; honours double quotes with backslash escapes) and accepts when

    token 1 == "Decode"        (@0x2996, `_CmpString`, case-insensitive)
    token 3 == "to" or "into"  (@0x2a04, @0x2a24)

**An AppleLink package is a text script.** `STR# 129` holds `convert`,
`noConvert`, ` Folder`, *"Destination not found: "* and *"No items matching:
"*.

### The claim this disproves, and the assumption under it

"`.pkg` cannot even be sniffed without inventing a magic number" rested on
the unstated assumption **that recognising a format means matching bytes at a
fixed offset.** The real recogniser could be COPIED, as rule #1 asks.
`macextract sniff` implements those three tokens and nothing more — exactly
as strong as Aladdin's (a text file beginning *"Decode this to that"* is a
package to both). 928 fixtures, 0 false positives.

### What a `Decode` line refers to — and why that may end the item

- **The operand is looked up in the FILE SYSTEM:** token 2 goes to the engine
  (@0xdb4, callback selector 13, 38-byte records), then @0x1266 / @0x128c
  fill a `CInfoPBRec` and call `_HFSDispatch` **selector 9, `PBGetCatInfo`**.
- **Its errors are file-system errors** (*"No items matching"*, *"Destination
  not found"*).
- **It carries recognisers for eight other formats** (`.HQX`, `.TGZ`, `.GZ`,
  `.ZIP`, `.ARC`, `.Z`, `.UUE`, `.UU`, plus type `PACT`, creator `EXTR`, type
  `HBSF`), each over an FSSpec — a driver's needs.

**Hypothesis, on those three:** a package is a transfer MANIFEST naming files
beside it, not a container. **What would settle it:** one `.pkg` file —
reading further is not cheap: the expander opens the package (@0x2e00,
`HOpen` permission 3 falling back to 1) and calls `GetResource('Eng ', 2)` /
`('Eng ', 3)` (@0x334c), 25 KB code resources in `StuffIt Engine™` without
MacsBug symbols. Measured on the way (@0x2e5c): the destination folder is the
name with `.pkg` stripped plus `STR# 129` item 2 (`Report.pkg` →
`Report Folder`), the only use of item 3, `".pkg"`.

### Why it stops at detect-only

No `.pkg` to grade a decoder against — the LZH / DiskDoubler 2-5 / SpaceSaver
1-3 bargain. Naming it turns *unknown* into a format. (superseded: packages
carry their forks and extract — FORMATS.md, *AppleLink packages*; and nothing
is detect-only since DECISIONS.md 2026-10-18, *the formats it only named*.)

## 2026-08-23 (SpaceSaver, the encoder agrees) — the cross-check that replaced a specimen

Method 4's **container is triple-sourced** (`mCompressFile`, `mExpandFile`,
`UpdateSSHeader` agree on the 84 bytes); **the codec was single-sourced**
(`CMod 21` @0x15a), and `run_spacesaver.py`'s encoder was written from the
same reading, so a misreading was invisible. `CMod 20` is the FULL module,
whose `+0x08` entry is a real compressor (not the `moveq #103` stub) —
Aladdin's encoder, an independent second source, an hour with no emulator.

**Every single-sourced field confirmed, two new:**

| claim | where the encoder says it |
|---|---|
| stream header: block count as u16, low byte first | @0xe1c writes `fp@(-17)` then `fp@(-35)` |
| then a byte, which is the window width in bits | @0xe24 writes a literal **15** |
| block header: `clen` as u24, low byte first | @0xe2c-@0xe3e, @0xe42-@0xe50 |
| `clen` counts the 6 header bytes | it is `a3 - blockStart` after the header was reserved |
| the 3 stream bytes are NOT in the first block's `clen` | @0xe28 subtracts 3, and only for the first |
| then `ulen` as u24, low byte first | @0xe52-@0xe66 |
| a literal is 9 bits: a 1, then the byte | @0xb4c: `(byte << 1) | 1`, width 9 |
| a match is 21 bits: a 0, 5 bits, 15 bits | @0xd2c: width 21, and 1+5+15 = 21 |
| the 5-bit field is length MINUS FOUR | @0xd1e: `subqw #4` before it is shifted up by 1 |
| the distance sits above it | @0xd1c: `lsll #6` — bits 6..20 |
| bits pack LSB-first, flushed low byte first | @0xb7e-@0xb94 |
| the window slides across blocks | @0xe92: it shifts the buffer down by `ulen` and keeps the rest |
| **the preset dictionary ends immediately before the first output byte** | @0x93e copies `pramSize` bytes to `fp@(-12) - pramSize` |

The last row was the most speculative claim in the reading, and the encoder
places it identically from its own side.

### Two figures this corrects

- **A real file's window is 32,768 bytes, not 65,536:** the encoder always
  writes 15. The decoder still accepts 1..16 (16 now exercised separately),
  but the practical peak is **36,864 B** (32 KB window + 4 KB input buffer),
  measured, where FORMATS.md had the 69,632 B ceiling — a number taken from
  what a field COULD say.
- **A block covers 65,536 bytes of output** (@0x8fc `ceil(ulen / 65536)`,
  @0xa02); the decoder reads each `ulen`, unaffected; the synthetic encoder
  now matches.

### What a specimen would still be worth

Less: two independent routines agree on every bitstream field. It would still
catch a misreading shared by both Aladdin routines and ours, or a container
error all three engine routines share. The hunt stays open (OPEN_ITEMS.md)
but the format no longer waits on it.

## 2026-08-23 (SpaceSaver, the dictionary) — carrying 9,679 bytes that are not ours

**The maintainer's decision, taken on 2026-08-23**, and recorded here
because it is a licence decision rather than an engineering one: the
`PrAm` -4048 table ships inside this project.

### What it changes

A SpaceSaver file looks like a normal document whose data fork is a
compressed container; on a floppy today its own application sees 84 bytes of
`SIT!DFD3`. Before, this project could name it and decode it only with
`--preset` from the user's copy of SpaceSaver, which a lone floppy does not
carry — a diagnosis, not a recovery. Now it is a recovery, with no flags, in
the CLI and in the Mac application (which cannot be handed a file at all).

### The decision, stated plainly

The table's own first line is *"Copyright (c) 1993 Aladdin Systems, Inc.
… Distribution is prohibited without written permission of Aladdin
Systems"*, so the prohibition is part of the data being distributed. No
permission has been given. The maintainer judged the risk acceptable for
a 1993 product whose publisher's successors are being sought, asked for
attribution and nothing more, and owns that call; it is written into
`NOTICE` as an explicit exception to the LGPL grant, and into README.md
where a user will see it.

**What was NOT done, deliberately:** nothing was hidden, obfuscated or
minimised. `src/ss_dict.h` says whose bytes they are in its header, the
generator says so, `NOTICE` has a section for it, and the README's
licence paragraph names it. If permission is refused later, deleting one
generated header and one `else if` restores the previous behaviour.

### Why the bytes had to be exact

The window is primed with them, so a short-distance match reads the table; a
wrong table gives output of the right length, silently wrong. No smaller or
equivalent table is an option.

### Two loose ends closed with it

- **The record's byte at +12 is honoured:** 0 is -4048, 1 is -4047 (four
  spaces), anything else refused per entry. It had been read and ignored.
- **A committed generated file can go stale:** `tools/run_spacesaver.py`
  compares `src/ss_dict.h` byte for byte with the resource whenever an
  installed SpaceSaver is present; it fails on a one-byte change.

## 2026-08-23 (decryption) — five schemes in, and the one with no second reader

Decryption is in scope from 2026-08-23, on request: seven ciphers across five
formats, five transcribed from XADMaster, one read out of an application. The
interesting decisions are about **evidence**.

### What a password is, in this engine

A cipher is a filter on `UncBufIn` (`in.crypt = cr`; every refill decrypted
before the decoder sees it), so five formats and eight codecs gained
encryption without a decoder changing. In `unc_bufin_next_slow`:

- **A block cipher cannot decrypt half a block:** with `blocksize > 1` the
  refill fills the buffer rather than taking a short read, and at EOF
  zero-pads to the block (as `XADPackItDESHandle` does).
- **Stateful ciphers need sequential reads**, which `UncBufIn` guarantees;
  where the cipher must start elsewhere (PackIt's one continuous stream) the
  reader is reopened at the entry (`pit_reopen`).

The password arrives as `opt.password`, or via `opt.ask`, a callback invoked
**when an entry turns out to need one** (the Mac's natural dialog moment), and
re-asked with a rising `attempt` where the format can tell wrong from right.

### Verification, and why it decides where the retry loop goes

| format | what verifies a password | so a retry is |
|---|---|---|
| StuffIt classic | the 'MKey' resource decrypts to a block that checks against itself | free, before any output |
| StuffIt 5 | MD5(MD5(password)) against a five-byte hash in the archive header | free |
| zip | the twelfth byte of the encryption header against the CRC's top byte | free — one wrong password in 256 gets past it, and the entry CRC catches that |
| PackIt | nothing; but the 94-byte entry header is INSIDE the ciphertext and carries a CRC | free, because the header is decoded first anyway |
| ARC | nothing at all | costs a whole decode |
| Compact Pro | nothing at all — its own message says so: *"The password supplied is incorrect **or the archive is damaged**"* | costs a whole decode |

So `arc_entry_data_pw` and `cpt_encrypted_entry` decode each entry TWICE with
a password in play — once writing nothing, to find the key — because deciding
while writing hands the sink a wrong key's output followed by the right one's
(the first ARC version: `cmp` differed, exit status success). Compact Pro
pays only on the first encrypted entry (one password per archive).

### StuffIt classic keeps its key outside the archive

'MKey' 0 is a RESOURCE in the archive's resource fork, half of every file
key. A bare-data-fork `.sit` **cannot be decrypted by anything**; the entry
reports `UNC_ERR_ENCRYPTED` rather than asking. Where the fork survives,
`unc_resfork_find` walks it raw with every field bounds-checked; the CLI
passes the sidecar it writes when unwrapping MacBinary/BinHex, the Mac reads
the fork as bytes (`PBHOpenRFSync`) rather than via the Resource Manager.

### ARC has no encryption flag, so the reader must not assume

A password given up front is applied; a host that can ASK is asked only
**once the plain read has failed its CRC**. Measured: `arc` 5.21q
**upper-cases the password** (stored ciphertext XOR plaintext is the password
in capitals), XADMaster uses the bytes as given; both are tried.

### Compact Pro: read out of the application, and graded by it

No second READER exists (The Unarchiver's notes: "the algorithm for this is
unknown"; macutils skips; CptExpand "will not extract encrypted files";
StuffIt's translator: "the file is password protected"). Read from Compact
Pro 1.51's `CODE` 3, addresses in `src/unc_crypt.c`:

- a **64-bit CRC** register, polynomial 0xEDB88320 in *both* halves (table
  builder at 0x408e), seeded 0x0123456789ABCDEF (0x40fe);
- the **key** at 0x1892: nine bytes, a length capped at eight, the password's
  bytes ADDED into eight accumulators in rotation (≤ 8 characters is its own
  key), then folded into the register byte by byte;
- the **keystream** is the register's second byte, stepped on the PLAINTEXT
  byte — encrypt at 0x1152 and decrypt at 0x1f08 are exact inverses;
- **scope:** `InitCrypt` once per FILE before the fork loop (0xac compress,
  0x14e0 expand), so one register runs over resource then data fork.

**Graded by the application, both ways** (`tools/vmac/cptcrypt.py`), after
two mistakes of our own:

- Unregistered, Compact Pro refuses (*"This version of Compact Pro cannot
  validate or extract encrypted files"*). Reading 0x47ca/0x485e, I concluded
  only a personalisation ending in `*` would help, and wrote it in three
  files. The published Macintosh Garden code (`Registered` / 35427117)
  opened it outright (0x4864 moves DITL 312's Encrypt checkbox into view).
  **Reading one branch is not reading the feature.**
- Then *"The password supplied is incorrect or the archive is damaged"* both
  ways. Data forks of 96, 100, 103 bytes came back 104, 108, 111 — **a
  constant +8**, a preamble, not padding: eight bytes decrypted and DISCARDED
  (`CODE` 3 @0x1f5e), counted in the first non-empty fork's compressed size —
  a salt, which is why three archives' keystreams diverged at byte 0.

With that line: three RLE-only archives Compact Pro encrypted, every byte
back; one LZH two-fork archive, both forks byte-exact (the register runs
across forks); an archive this project encrypted, all three entries extracted
by Compact Pro with its CRC-32 passing.

Not ours: every RESOURCE fork extracted there changes a few dozen bytes in —
the Mac opening it to draw the icon, the Resource Manager writing the map's
live fields back. `cptcrypt.py` compares data forks strictly; Compact Pro
checks the CRC over BOTH decrypted forks before writing.

### WinZip's AES, which is out of era and in anyway

Method 99 / extra 0x9901 (2003) is in because the file IS a zip and refusing
an entry is worse than a slow answer: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 over the entry's salt,
AES-CTR, ten bytes of HMAC-SHA1 over the ciphertext. Kept small: **counter
mode needs only the FORWARD cipher** (no inverse tables, four kilobytes not
shipped); **one 256-byte S box** and an `xtime` column mix instead of T
tables; the time goes to **key derivation**, 1000 rounds of HMAC-SHA1, for
AES-256 ~8,000 SHA-1 compressions, seconds on a 68000 once per entry.

**Debian's `unar` 1.10.8 cannot open a WinZip AES zip at all** (every key
length, stored or deflated: "Missing or wrong password"); the ENCODER grades
it — 7-Zip writes and verifies, our output must equal the input — and the
suite flips a ciphertext byte to prove the MAC is checked.

### The fixtures, and what grades them

Nothing in the corpus is encrypted (`lsar -j` over all 903 fixtures:
`XADIsEncrypted` 0 everywhere), so `tools/run_crypt.py`'s archives are
generated: `zip -P` and `arc g<password>` are somebody else's encoders; for
StuffIt classic, StuffIt 5 and PackIt `tools/synth_crypt.py` writes them and
**`unar -p` adjudicates** (the StuffIt classic fixture is MacBinary, the
oracle needing the resource fork).

**`unar` 1.10.8 and current XADMaster derive the StuffIt archive key
differently from eight-byte passwords up** — and **neither is right** (next
entry).

## 2026-08-23 (StuffIt's archive key) — the fold count, measured

### What it is

The password is folded into the key eight bytes at a time, **ceil(len / 8)**
times: three archives StuffIt Deluxe 3.5.1 wrote under Mini vMac with
passwords of 8, 9 and 17 characters need 1, 2 and 3 folds
(`tools/vmac/sitcrypt.py`; table in FORMATS.md). XADMaster gives 2, 2, 2,
`unar` 1.10.8 gives 1, 1, 1; this engine had shipped XADMaster's.

### Why it survived a whole feature's worth of testing

**Every encrypted `.sit` here had been generated** from the same reading as
the reader. `unar` disagreed, and it was filed as two references diverging —
two implementations disagreeing about a file neither wrote. Under eight
characters all three readings agree, which is what a person picks to test;
the breaking specimen was chosen at nine because the references differed
there, then 8 and 17 to find the shape — and at 8 OUR reading was the wrong
one.

### The rule this is an instance of

**The software that WRITES a format is a specimen source, not just a
grader.** Three of the last four format corrections came from running the
original application (Salient's expander for DiskDoubler 3-5, Compact Pro
for its cipher, StuffIt Deluxe): the settling file had to be MADE, not found.
The StuffIt 5 entry in OPEN_ITEMS.md is labelled with what this cost: two
readings that agree for exactly the inputs anybody would test are not
evidence about anything.

## 2026-08-23 (btoa's licence) — a reference that may not be transcribed

btoa's README: *"Btoa is in the public domain. You may use it, give it away,
and make improvements, as long as the names of the developers are mentioned
and you don't use it to earn money. It may NOT be used commercially without
my permission."* A non-commercial restriction is not the public domain
(Debian shipped btoa in `non-free`) and is incompatible with LGPL-2.1.

- **The format** — two header lines, base 85 offset by `'!'`, `z` and `y`,
  the three checksum recurrences, the per-line check, `(len-1)&3` for the
  padding — is read from `atob.c`, `btoa.h`, `chksum.h` and the man page and
  implemented in `src/fmt_btoa.c` with no function, buffer or control
  structure carried across, each fact cited to its routine. What a format IS
  cannot be licensed.
- **The code** stays in `reference/` (fetched, never committed) and is *used*
  as a test-time oracle: `tools/run_btoa.py` compiles it and requires our
  decoder to reproduce what it encodes.

The names are mentioned (`NOTICE`, `src/fmt_btoa.c`, here). Skipping the
format would have applied a licence decision to the wrong object: the wire
format is not their program.

## 2026-08-23 (Compact Pro comments) — a comment is saved, and it is still not a file

Compact Pro's index opens with a comment (length byte, up to 255 MacRoman
bytes) belonging to the archive. It was CRC'd and dropped, on the grounds *"a
comment is not a file and the sink writes files"* — the conclusion did not
follow.

- **`UncSink` gains an optional `comment` callback**, delivered once before the
  first `begin_entry`. Not a synthetic entry: `unar` reports it as an archive
  PROPERTY, so an entry would disagree with the oracle on 108 fixtures. Not a
  new entry point: it is found mid-walk.
- **The sink, not the options:** a comment is OUTPUT, and each host answers
  for it what it answers for a fork. All six sinks in the repository say what
  they want; `NULL` means what it always did.
- **Hosts:** the CLI writes `<archive>.comment.txt` beside the items (cannot
  collide with an entry); `l` and `t` print it. The Mac writes a `TEXT`/`ttxt`
  document `Comments` in the destination, as StuffIt Expander does.
- **Printed text is decoded; saved bytes are not:** MacRoman → UTF-8 when
  PRINTED, the archive's own bytes (CR endings included) when SAVED, so both
  hosts save identical bytes for `checkdisk.py` and `vmac_check.py`.
- **Graded:** six corpus archives carry a real comment, five found by the
  half of the check that FORBIDS a comment file where the oracle reports none.
  Oracle `lsar`'s `XADComment` (TESTING.md, *Manifest format*); the Mac path
  by the mock-Toolbox sink test and on System 6.0.8 (FORMATS.md,
  *Real-hardware verification*). Compact Pro calls it a **Note**;
  `tools/vmac/cptcrypt.py --note` types one in.

## 2026-08-23 (LZH) — the format the corpus could not grade, graded by somebody else's corpus

The 2026-08-14 reason — no `.lzh` in the corpus — was a boundary drawn at
OUR corpus. The maintainer put LZH in scope; what made it cheap was **a corpus
that is not ours**: `reference/lhasa` (Simon Howard's decompressor, in Debian)
ships **182 test archives written by fourteen different LHA
implementations** (MacLHA 2.24, LHa for Amiga/OS-2/OS-9/OSK/X68000, LHarc
1.13, LArc 3.33, LHMelt, LHArk, UNLHA32, and generated cases). `reference/lha`
is LHa for UNIX 1.14i (archive.debian.org), which compiles here: an
**encoder**.

**Three graders:** `unar` (XADMaster, our transcription source — agreement
shows only a faithful copy), lhasa (an independent reading), LHa 1.14i
(archives of known plaintext); `tools/run_lzh.py` runs all three. lhasa
earned its place in an afternoon:

- **`unar` cannot read LHA for OS-9/68k's level 2 headers** (that writer
  stores the length of the REST of the header; lhasa compensates by OS byte):
  three failures became three byte-exact extractions.
- **`unar` fails a 1.2 MB `-lh7-` file** ("Attempted to read more data than
  was available") that lhasa and we decode identically.
- **`unar` cannot open `-lzs-`:** its recogniser omits it while its parser has
  a working decoder behind the gate — a cross-file contradiction inside the
  reference.

**Two initial-window questions only a specimen answers** (XADMaster
zero-fills, LHa 1.14i space-fills a dictionary `decode_start_lz5` never
touches, lhasa writes the pattern rotated):

- `-lz5-`: **zeros** — LArc 3.33's `initial.lzs` CONTAINS the initial window,
  its first 18 bytes zero.
- `-lzs-`: **spaces** — no preload; lhasa's `lzs.lzs` fails its CRC-16
  zero-filled and passes space-filled (`long.lzs` passes either way). **A
  difference only some files can see needs the file that sees it.**

**MacLHA is a MacBinary stream:** a Mac entry decodes to a 128-byte MacBinary
header, the data fork padded to 128, then the resource fork; name, type,
creator, dates from that header. Triggered by OS byte `'m'` only (`unar` reads
MacLHA's level 0 archives, which have no OS byte, as one 18,304-byte file
where level 1 gives 18,092 bytes plus metadata; lhasa uses the same rule).
The peek runs in LISTING too, so listing and extraction agree.

**One decoder was already here:** StuffIt method 5 is LHarc's `-lh1-`; moved
to `src/unc_lzah.c` behind a byte callback rather than copied.

**Declined:** `-lh2-` and `-lh3-` (transcribable from `XADLZHOldHandles.m`),
no archive reachable. **"No oracle exists" is a claim about a search, and the
search that matters is rarely inside the format.** LHArk 0.4d writes its own
algorithm under an `-lh7-` label with a space as OS byte; refused per entry by
that byte, as lhasa does.

**The specimen this milestone made:** all sixteen MacLHA archives in reach are
data-fork-only. `tools/vmac/maclha.py` runs **MacLHA 2.00** (already in the
corpus, `derived-MacLHa_2.00.sit`) on a two-fork file; its MacBinary header
has **zero for both dates**, so XADMaster (MacBinary-I heuristic needs both
non-zero) and lhasa (needs a sane modification date matching the LZH header)
return a 2,304-byte file with the resource fork inside. Ours uses lhasa's
length check without the clock: the Mac header's name equals the entry's, and
header plus both fork lengths padded to 128 equal the uncompressed size. It
fires on none of the 182 archives or 8 fixtures; MacLHA 2.00's archives
extract as two forks, 1,760 B and 333 B, byte-exact.

A heuristic tuned on files with dates fails on files without; and **the
encoder was already in the corpus** — ask *of the software this corpus is made
of, which pieces are encoders?*

## 2026-08-24 (the performance pass) — four proposals measured, two of them dead

`PLANNED_WORK.md` (from a v0.12.0 branch) was worked in order; two items were
disproved by minutes of measurement.

### The Arsenic block's unused tail is 29 KB, not 200

**Claim (withdrawn).** Section 2: multi-block Arsenic entries get a 512 KB
block against a largest fill of 323,384 B, so shrinking to fill returns
~200 KB to the sampled index ("~4x less scanning").

**Evidence.** `blockcap - numbytes` at `ars_bwt_prepare`:
`derived-Library_ISBN_Barcoder.sit` `cap=352,160 fill=323,384`, waste
**28,776 B**; `derived-a2basic.dmg.sit` `cap=205,019 fill=197,515`, waste
**7,504 B** — `ars_block_reserve` already allocates `min(outlen, blocksize)`
(2026-08-06).

**Consequence.** The index needs 225,528 B at target 512 vs 346,836 B at
1024; 29 KB moves the dial not one step. Dead.

**Found instead:** a sample is a block position, at most `(1 << 24) - 1`
(`blockbits` is four bits plus nine), so **three bytes is exact**: 260,705 B
against 290,391 B of room is target 1024, half the scan distance on the
slowest fixture, and the structure's last unaligned word load is gone.
*Instrument the number before budgeting for it.*

### 61 KB of deferred code is worth under a second at launch

**Claim (withdrawn).** Section 7.4: segmenting CODE keeps ~61 KB off the launch
path (self-labelled unverified; *no launch-time baseline is measured
anywhere*).

**Evidence:** ballast behind a temporary define, referenced from startup so
`-gc-sections` keeps it; three runs each on `mv-4M-1x` (authentic 7 MHz),
System 6.0.8:

| build | app | relocations | boot |
|---|---|---|---|
| shipping | 150,144 B | ~2,300 | **8.9 s** (3/3) |
| + 64 KB as `const unsigned char[]` | 215,680 B | ~2,300 | **8.9 s** (3/3) |
| + 64 KB as 16,384 pointers | 232,064 B | 18,682 | **10.0 s** (3/3) |

A byte array costs the Segment Loader a read, below the 0.1 s resolution; the
cost is RELOCATIONS — 16,306 more are 1.1 s, **67 µs each** at 7 MHz. The
shipping app has **2,376**, ≈ 0.16 s of an 8.9 s boot.

**Consequence.** Segmentation cannot buy what is not spent, and would need
every `probe` in one translation unit (~20 files). Dead. **An unmeasured cost
is an unknown one, not a small one**; ballast prices a resource by adding
some.

### The same fix, twice, in opposite directions: inlining the bit reader

`static inline` `unc_bitin_bit` with an out-of-line `unc_bitin_bit_slow()`
refill measured **3.1 to 6.6 % WORSE** on Compact Pro, DiskDoubler, Now
Compress; inlining the refill too measured **1.0 % better**, and 1.0 point
more on Arsenic. `unc_canon_decode`, in the same translation unit, was
already inlining it with `bitbuf`, `nbits`, `le` in registers; an opaque
refill call forced them to memory every eighth bit. **A function's cost is
not a property of the function** — check what a move costs the callers that
already could inline it.

### A shared decoder's tables belong wherever the deepest caller can afford

`unc_canon_decode`'s fast table is 320 B per `UncCanon`; DiskDoubler held
three and Now Compress two **on the stack**. `m68k -Os -fstack-usage` over
the call graph: `unc_dd_extract -> dd_fork -> dd_ddn` **6,664 B**, Now
Compress **5,632 B**, against the 4 KB rule. **Not against the machine:**
`mac/macextract_mac.c`'s `SetApplLimit(LMGetApplLimit() - kStackBump)` with
`kStackBump` 24 KB gives **32 KB of stack**, so nothing overflowed (the first
draft of this entry got that wrong); the RULE exists for hosts that did not
ask for more. Both moved to the heap; the deepest chain is **3,290 B**. The
zip EOCD scan window stays 1 KB (4 KB would have been the deepest frame, for
17 reads instead of 65). **A limit with no measurement behind it is not a
limit.**

## 2026-08-24 (the performance pass, part two) — what re-profiling found that the plan had not

The three biggest wins of the second pass were **not on the plan**: each
landed change re-orders what is left.

- **`unc_huff_decode` at 48 % of `derived-EmpireBuilderDemo.sit`:** the
  SECOND Huffman decoder (serialized tree: StuffIt method 3, DiskDoubler
  method 4, PackIt). Same table remedy, but storing the symbol, since an
  arbitrary tree has no code→symbol arithmetic.
- **`unc_bitin_bits` at 9–13 %** of DiskDoubler and Now Compress, looping the
  single-bit reader; a masked shift once `unc_bitin_fill` existed. **A tool
  built for one job made a second trivial.**
- **BinHex's `% 3` per output byte**, in a file the plan did not look at.

**Re-profile after each landed change, not once per plan.**

### Two inline fast paths that measured worse, for the same reason

`unc_bitin_bit` (3.1–6.6 % worse) and BinHex's `bh_get_bits` (−5.5 % against
−6.6 % without): the opaque call spills the fast path's state. **"Make the
hot function inline" is a hypothesis**; what worked had NO call left in it.

### Filling the disk on purpose

`run.py --out-kb` sizes the destination, reaching the full-disk path for the
first time: 9 files written, **one** error, eight entries never attempted —
thirteen of fourteen extractors end the archive on a sink failure. The plan's
four-step description had line citations for three steps; the wrong one had
none. **A described behaviour with no file:line beside it is a guess in the
shape of a reading.**

## 2026-08-24 (PLANNED_WORK.md, closed) — the file is gone, and what it left behind

Seven items on 2026-08-23, none a day later: four landed, **five were
disproved by measurement**, and the three biggest wins were not on it. Deleted
rather than annotated, as its preamble asked.

### Why three of its five window items were closed rather than done

"Size five windows from the entry": SuperDisk's and zip's were done because
they changed **what a machine can extract** (an `alysis-disk-expander-12`
entry refused at 50,000 B now extracts; a small-entry zip halved its peak).
The other three were closed by `tools/run_budget.py` at a 400 KB cap (only
StuffIt 5 refuses) — and **one reopened within the hour**, the command having
run in the wrong configuration.

**The correction.** 597,036 B is a 1 MB Plus with the machine to itself.
Under MultiFinder and System 7+ the app gets the Get Info PARTITION;
`macextract.r` declares 400 KB minimum, 150 KB of it code. On System 7.0.1
at a 400 KB preferred size: **`FreeMem()` 212,056 B, budget 130,136 B** —
four and a half times tighter. There **Now Compress opened none of its three
fixtures**: its 131,072 B of block buffers were allocated per archive before
any entry, so the archive was refused whole, high-water zero. Bounded by the
sum of each file's fork sizes (one stream carries both), the small fixture
peaks at 84,248 B and opens; listing skips the allocation. **Ask which machine
the green result came from, and whether the user can pick a worse one.**

ARC (33,732 B) and SpaceSaver (36 KB) still fit at 130,136 B and stay on
their ceilings — a fact about today's corpus and partition, not the decoders.

### Why zlib stays

`NO_GZIP` and `Z_TESTW=0` take 8,704 B out without modifying the vendored
source (the engine uses raw inflate, its own gzip framing and CRC). A
transcribed replacement is **declined, not deferred**: ~10 KB more, while
`inflate_fast` is 52.65 % of a gzip extraction (measured) and compact inflates
are bit-at-a-time, roughly an order of magnitude slower. Worth writing, if
ever: a raw-only inflate keeping a table-driven fast path.

### Checked and empty — recorded so nobody looks again

- **The launch path:** six Toolbox inits, `InitCursor`, `FlushEvents`, one
  trap test, then `SFGetFile`; the Segment Loader's cost ≈ 0.16 s of 8.9 s
  (FORMATS.md, *Launch*).
- **The progress path:** `prog_tick` throttles to ~10 Hz off `TickCount`
  before drawing; `ARS_PROGRESS_STEP` at 256 costs a trap and a compare.
- **Opening an archive** calls `unc_segment_describe`, not a full `unc_sniff`,
  to avoid walking a Compact Pro index twice.
- **The compile line** is `-O3 -DNDEBUG -mcpu=68000 -Os ...` (`-O3` from
  `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`, `-Os` from target options): **last wins, so it
  is `-Os`.**
- **Narrowing hot-path arithmetic to 16 bits** is forbidden by CLAUDE.md.
- **`ars_next_symbol`'s linear search** averages **10.4 iterations per
  symbol**, so a multiply per iteration (ten `__mulsi3`) costs more than one
  `__udivsi3`; 9.9 % of the slowest run, no cheaper shape (a cumulative array
  would update on every `ars_model_bump`).
- **`adler32.o`, 994 B:** unreachable from raw inflate but referenced from
  inflate.c's wrapper path; cutting it means editing vendored source.

## 2026-08-24 (the reserve) — a constant that suited one machine of the two

`kMemReserve`, a flat 80 KB since M10 with no recorded reason, is now a
quarter of `FreeMem()` clamped to [32 KB, 80 KB].

**Claim (measured).** The two configurations are 678,956 B free (1 MB Plus to
itself) and 211,960 B (the 400 KB minimum partition); 80 KB is 12 % and
**38 %** of them. **Evidence:** the lowest `FreeMem()` during writes across all
67 fixtures of the 1 MB sample left 121,124 B; Toolbox and File Manager took
**under 1 KB** at the engine's peak. **Consequence:** unchanged on the tier
FORMATS.md was measured on (a quarter exceeds the cap); the minimum partition
gets 158,970 B instead of 130,136, taking Now Compress from none of three
fixtures to all three and StuffIt 5 from 10 to 15.

**Why a 32 KB floor and not the kilobyte measured:** the measurement is the
best case and the reserve exists for the worst. **Measuring how much of a
safety margin is used tells you what it costs, not what it is for.**
MANUAL_TESTS.md carries what only hardware settles: a floppy and an
AppleShare volume with an extension loaded, and MultiFinder at the declared
minimum.

## 2026-08-24 (the icon) — four things the resources alone do not do

`tools/icon/make_icon.py` draws an open carton lettered EXTRACT and emits
`ICN#`, `ics#`, `icl4`, `ics4`, `icl8`, `ics8`, `FREF`, `BNDL` at ID 128.
Correct resources, and the Finder still drew the generic diamond. Found only
by booting a real Finder and looking (`interactive.py --e2e`,
`e2e-2-volume.png`); nothing in the build said a word.

1. **`#include "Multiverse.r"`** — Retro68's Rez has no built-in type
   declarations (`Can't find type definition for 'ICN#'`).
2. **The creator code:** `add_application()` defaults to `'????'`; the Finder
   binds by `BNDL` owner = creator, so the build stamps `'MExt'`.
3. **`hasBundle` (0x2000):** Rez cannot set flags, so
   `tools/icon/set_bundle_bit.py` sets MacBinary byte 73, recomputes the
   header CRC at 124, and the `.dsk` is **rebuilt** from the patched MacBinary
   (`hcopy -m` carries flags; `hattrib -b` blesses a system folder, a
   different thing).
4. **The signature resource** — type = creator, ID 0 — needed for the Finder
   to register the bundle; with the other three right the icon still did not
   appear until it was added.

Fifth, harness side: the stock System 6 image's root **`Desktop` file** (the
Finder's icon cache) survived `mkboot.py`, whose `hdir` hides invisible files
without `-a`; the harness now deletes it (a user would hold Cmd-Option at
startup).

**What "it built" is worth:** all five gave a clean build, a working
application and the wrong icon; only a screenshot of a real Finder could see
them.

**The COLOUR members were drawn for the first time on 2026-08-27:** Mini vMac
is 1-bit; Mac OS 9.2 at 32-bit draws `icl8` in the volume window
(`docs/screens/0b-icon-os9-color.png`) and `ics8` in Standard File. **`icl4`
and `ics4` have been drawn by nothing, and no emulator here can draw them**
(measured): the guest's Monitors panel offers only "Millions" ("Grays"
disabled), and `-g 1024x768x4` stops in OpenBIOS (*"unable to find a usable
NVRAM partition"*). Moved to MANUAL_TESTS.md.

## 2026-08-24 (the low-memory message) — saying the number, and where it can be graded

**Claim (measured).** `mal_alloc` refuses when `size + 16 > budget`; the
difference is how much larger the partition would have had to be, kept as a
run-level MAXIMUM and rounded up to the next 8K:

    Needs 64K more memory. Give MacExtract more in Get Info.

**The two refusals are kept apart, their fixes opposite:** over budget means
the partition is too small; a `NewPtr` failing with budget left means no
single piece is that big, which quitting something else cures and the alert
says so.

**Measured, not predicted:** a pre-flight check would model each format's
sizing a second time from header fields that can lie; this number comes from
the allocator when it said no.

### Where the verification landed

`mac_sink_test --shortfall` (in `ci.sh`) asserts the figure **exactly**
(sabotaged by 16 bytes, the suite exits 1). **The alert is photographed**
(2026-08-24, `interactive.py` default phase, System 6.0.8,
`derived-AuthoRize_2.0.sit`): *Needs 72K more memory. Give MacExtract more in
Get Info.* Method in `tools/vmac/README.md`, *Forcing a memory refusal on
screen*: shrinking `SIZE` bites only under MultiFinder (System 7), where the
default phase's System 6 clicks opened the wrong item and gave
`UNC_ERR_FORMAT` (fixed 2026-08-25 — the clicks are per-system now, and the
wrong item turned out to be the wrong DIRECTORY: see that day's entry); a
throwaway build capping `ma.budget` refuses on the machine the harness drives.

**Make the harness say which path it took:** four runs gave plausible frames
(a generic failure alert looks like the new one not firing); printing `ret`,
`gShortBy`, `gShortPiece`, `entries`, `errors` into the alert answered in one
frame — `entries = 0`.

**Claim (measured).** `checkdisk.walk` (names off an HFS volume, for `run.py`
and `interactive.py`) called `.rstrip()` on each `hls` line. CR is a legal HFS
character and `Icon` + CR names every custom folder icon, so a correct file was
reported under another name and counted missing. Repro without an emulator:

**Consequence.** `interactive.py`'s "phase 2 output INCOMPLETE" for
`derived-AuthoRize_2.0.sit` (`:AuthoRize 2.0:Icon`) became COMPLETE — first

Dot-files, `/` in a name, 8-bit MacRoman and nesting re-checked against the
repro.

**Ask of any comparison what it NORMALISES before comparing, and whether the
input may contain what is normalised away.** No fixture in the graded 927 has a
control character in a name; the one that does was picked today for something
else.

## 2026-08-25 (the System 7 UI) — the dialog is a different dialog, and where it opens

**Claim (measured).** The cancel paths run on System 7.0.1 as on 6.0.8:
`ProgressPump()`'s `WaitNextEvent` repainting percentage and estimate, Cancel
through `DialogSelect`, Cmd-. through the keyDown check, the SFGetFile repaint
after the alert. Photographed 2026-08-25 with `derived-Education7.1.cpt`; the
run's name assertion reports COMPLETE.

**Two obstacles, one known:** System 7's Standard File puts a directory pop-up
above the list and its first row ten points higher; and the Process Manager
gives each application its own default directory, so the boot-shell install
opens the dialog in the **System Folder** (`Finder`, `System`, the app) — the
