## 2026-08-30 (the flag that was never measured on these files) — 70.4 s to 52.6 s, and a kilobyte

Asked to match StuffIt Expander 4.0.2 on the archive it wins. Level now — 56 s
each — with no decoder line changed; what changed is what the optimiser may
work on.

**The probe first.** `UNC_AT_TIMING` bills File Manager time on the Mac:
reads 0.6 s, writes 0.3 s, create/`SetEOF`/close/`FlushVol`/catalog 0.2 s,
**engine 69.4 s of 70.4** (FORMATS.md, *What -O3 is worth, and where*). Every
I/O idea was worth 1.1 s in total, including dropping per-fork `FlushVol`.

**Then the flag.** `mac/CMakeLists.txt` built everything `-Os` on one sound
measurement: `-O2` on `sit_arsenic.c` cost 1,536 B and was SLOWER, 1,304 s
against 1,284 s. Applied to forty files, with a note that it could not be
re-asked without a harness resolving better than 20 s — which the tick probe
now is. On the four files a StuffIt run lives in, `-O3` is **−25.4 %**. **A
rule proved on one file is a rule about that file.**

**The knee argued for a list.** `-O2` on the whole engine bar Arsenic: 56.0 s
for +40,192 B, against 56.2 s for +5,504 B on four files. The maintainer asked
whether this argued for assembly; it argued for aiming:
`__attribute__((optimize("O3")))` on six functions is **52.6 s for +1,024 B**,
against 52.5 s for +8,320 B (the file flag paid +2,428 B for
`unc_huff_read_tree`, 0.44 % of the run).

- **Marking functions puts them under the oracle.** `UNC_HOT` lives in `src/`,
  so the 932-fixture differential suite decodes through the optimised code;
  a flag in `mac/CMakeLists.txt` it never saw.
- **The attribute made a function smaller**: `unc_sit_decode_fork` is 226 B
  under its `-Os` size, as GCC will not inline across differing attributes.
- **Assembly would now have to beat `-O3`** and would cost that coverage; the
  `qemu-m68k` module harnesses are the shape a graded asm routine needs, built
  before the first instruction.

**Not claimed**: that `UNC_HOT` is the right list (one archive's measurement
plus two shared primitives), or that `sit_arsenic.c` should join (its own
measurement says otherwise and was not re-taken).

## 2026-08-30 (the shell name System 3.0 does not read) — the oldest system a Mac Plus boots, and a NOGRID that meant nothing

**Claim: the application runs unchanged on System 3.0 / Finder 5.1, the system
the Macintosh Plus shipped with in January 1986.** 69/69 byte-exact at 4 MB and
69/69 at 1 MB, plus the interactive application driven end to end
(FORMATS.md, *System 3.0 tier*). Same binary.

**A harness assumption, inherited by every tier.** The first run reported
`NOGRID`. Every harness installs the app as boot shell via the boot blocks'
`bbShellName` (`mkboot.py`, offset 0x1A), which works on 6.0.8 and 7.0.1.
Disproof in one boot: shell name `NoSuchApp` gave a framebuffer with the same
MD5, as did the app at the volume root. System 3.0 does not act on that field;
the result was evidence about `mkboot.py` only.

**Consequence: it is launched the way a person launches it** — Finder,
volume, double-click (`tools/vmac/sys30.py`). *(This entry first said the
Finder therefore stays resident while the engine works. It does not: launching
an application unloads it. The claim and what it cost are in BLOCKERS.md, `the
Finder that was never there`.)*

**Cmd-. does not cancel Standard File on System 3.0.** Since an undelivered
chord looks identical (`interactive.py`, `command_key`), the discriminator was
our own code: the same chord in the same run cancelled an extraction
(*"Extraction cancelled."*). The Cancel button quits normally.

**Not claimed**: that System 3.0 is the oldest that could work — only the
oldest a Plus boots. Older means a 64K ROM: no HFS, no `NGetTrapAddress`.

## 2026-08-30 (512 KB, and the machine that cannot be reached) — the RAM was never the boundary

**Claim: 512 KB of RAM is enough, and a 64 KB ROM is not.** A Macintosh 512Ke
runs the application under System 3.0, 65/69 of the sample byte-exact, the rest
refused per entry (FORMATS.md, *512 KB machines*). A true 512K never reaches
the application.

**The interesting number is which SYSTEM.** Same machine: System 3.0 passes 65,
System 6.0.8 passes 58 (a strict superset of failures). Free heap at start is
218,208 B against 122,808 B, a 95,400 B gap, against System files of 181,913 B
and 1,221,287 B. **The floor was set by the system, not by the machine**, and
nobody had varied the system.

**The negative was attributed before it was reported.** The 512K gives Sad Mac
`0F0064` on our System 3.0 floppy. A/Bs: same ROM, no disk → blinking floppy,
framebuffer identical to the Mac Plus control (machine healthy); 128K ROM
(`28BA61CE`) and 512K ROM (`28BA4E50`) fail identically (not the revision); a
blank 800 KB HFS volume without boot blocks gives the no-disk frame (added
2026-08-31), so the boot code dies — and that ROM predates HFS.

**Which codecs survive is decided by adaptivity, not appetite.**
`derived-PuzzleGetter_0.8.sit` asks 270,043 B and fits by renegotiating its
block; `derived-a2basic.dmg.sit` asks 247,687 B and does not, having reached
37,372 B (2026-08-03's finding, on a smaller machine). *(First made with
`popper-1.7.tar.Z`, refused at 224,264 B; no longer refused — next entry.)*

**Not claimed**: that the Sad Mac's cause is reduced to a minimal repro; the
trap-level explanation is a hypothesis in FORMATS.md. It does not change the
outcome: `TrapAvailable` calls `NGetTrapAddress` and every file operation uses
an HFS parameter block, neither present in a 64K ROM.

## 2026-08-30 (a byte buys fewer symbols the further in it sits) — a third off the LZW table, and a fixture back

**Claim: the Unix compress table was a third larger than the input justifies,
and `popper-1.7.tar.Z` now extracts on a 512 KB Macintosh.** 225,170 B of
budget before, 148,408 B after (binary search on Linux); on the machine
224,232 B became 147,796 B, taking that tier from 64/69 to 65/69 (FORMATS.md,
*Unix compress: the `.Z` peak*, *512 KB machines*).

**The old bound assumed every code is minimum width**:
`256 + reserved + insize * 8 / 9`. Codes are 9 bits only under 512 entries, 10
under 1024, and so on, so a late byte buys a sixteenth of a symbol. Walking
the schedule is the exact bound: 59,323 B of input → 33,870 entries, not
52,988.

**Still strict**: creating the symbol that takes the table to k costs one code
at the current width; the first code creates nothing; a block-mode clear
resets table and width, and one generation holding every bit dominates any
split.

**Cheap to attempt** because `lzw_grow` nets an under-estimate and `ci.sh`'s
`UNC_LZW_TINY_TABLE` variant runs that net on every stream: an error would be
slow, not wrong, and the 932-fixture suite adjudicates.

**Not claimed**: help for the three fixtures still refused at 512 KB — StuffIt
5, limited by a BWT block size their compressor chose. Small `.Z` streams were
already exact.

## 2026-08-30 (the Desktop file the password phase needed) — a harness reported a working feature as broken, and a bisect agreed with it

**Claim: encrypted StuffIt archives extract on the Macintosh, and always did.
What broke on 2026-08-24 was the harness.** `interactive.py --password`
failed once `mkboot.py` deleted the boot volume's invisible `Desktop` file
(`d3907fc`). Under the boot-shell arrangement, with no Finder running, that
stops the encrypted archive's resource-only entry reaching the volume. Fixed
by dropping the file only when a Finder will run.

***The mechanism is not understood, and that is written into `mkboot.py`.***
The fix rests on the bisect, not a causal story.

**Always ask which side of the instrument moved.** Holding the application at
the bad commit and reverting `mkboot.py` alone turned "an advertised
capability is broken" into "the test is", in one run.

**The bisect before it was worthless.** `git bisect start <bad> <good>` takes
the GOOD end **on trust**; mine came from an entry recording the password path
working on **Mac OS 9**, while testing **System 6**. Five emulator runs
converged on a docs-only commit; with both ends measured, the real commit was
108 revisions earlier. **A bisect is only as good as its good end, and the
good end is the one thing bisect will never check for you.**

**Why it hid for six releases**: no emulator phase runs in `ci.sh`, and
`run.py`'s 69-fixture sample has no encrypted archive (none in the corpus;
FORMATS.md, *Encryption*), so only a hand-run phase covers it, and nobody ran
it between 2026-08-24 and 2026-08-30.

## 2026-08-31 (the overlay that works and is not worth it) — a lifetime argument, and a 6 KB prize

**Claim: loading part of the engine on demand works, and buys about one
archive.** Two branches, both run on a 1 MB Mac Plus: `selective-loading`
makes the ciphers an overlay fetched when a format wants them; `overlay-eager`
loads it at launch. **Parked, neither merged**, kept as a working mechanism.

**Its prize figure, its "StuffIt can never be one of the formats it helps"
and its "neither branch OPENS anything new" are superseded — 2026-09-25, *the
parked decision that outlived its numbers*.** What follows is the reasoning of
2026-08-31 and the cipher-only measurements it rested on, both correct for the
overlay that existed that day. The three later entries that cite 5,988 B as a
scale are left alone; the number is corrected here, where it lives.

- **The prize is 5,988 B**, for six formats, not StuffIt — about one archive
  in 922 at roughly one archive per 6–7 KB of budget, and not
  `derived-EasyFind.dmg.sit`. For scale, re-pricing one memory-reserve
  constant the same week was worth 49 KB (FORMATS.md, *Budget*).
- **It stood at 6,140 B for a day, from two builds that were not the same
  build**; one build at one commit gives 5,988 B, or 5,720 B for two autotest
  builds (corrected 2026-08-31). **A figure that cannot change the conclusion
  is a figure nothing checks.**
- **The download grows**: the `OVLY` ships inside the application, so
  `MacExtract.bin` is 191,104 B against 188,800 B — **2,304 B bigger**, not
  "7,016 B off". Resident heap is bought with disk.
- **StuffIt cannot be one of the six**: a format is disqualified if it may
  carry an encrypted entry (StuffIt's is per entry, signalled only by
  `UNC_ERR_PASSWORD`, too late) or is an envelope with unknown contents (a
  `.sit.hqx` sniffs as BinHex).
- **The disk dependency can only be moved.** A lazy `GetResource` touches the
  application's floppy after the archive is chosen, when a one-drive Plus may
  have swapped it; loading at launch still reloads per later archive.
  `selective-loading` pays on the first encrypted archive, `overlay-eager` on
  the second.

**Consequence: a disk swap or stall for one archive's worth of memory** — the
wrong side of this project's trade (FORMATS.md, *Size flags, priced in both
currencies*), since neither branch OPENS anything new. Scope status:
OPEN_ITEMS.md, Part 1.

### The transferable part: a release lifetime is an argument about scope, and it can be wrong silently

`overlay-eager` shipped a bug for one commit: the release ran after each
sniff while the "already tried" flag was session-global, so after an LZH an
encrypted `.sit` in the same session found no ciphers — **a capability lost
because of what was opened before it**. *"If it was released the format
cannot want it"* is true within one archive, false across a session.

**If something later needs tens of kilobytes, the loader exists**: `-mpcrel`,
`.bss`/`.data`, the three dispatch tables and the `--gc-sections` correction
are in the code, indexed by FORMATS.md, *Where the traps are written down*.
(Written when both were branches; they merged on 2026-09-25 and the notes
went with them.)

## 2026-08-31 (the message that failed a successful extraction) — the allocator cannot know which refusals matter

**Claim: a memory shortfall is not a failure, and the shell treated it as
one.** `derived-Troi-ClipSave-Plug-in1.1.sit` extracts **completely** on a
1 MB Mac Plus and ended with *"Needs 48K more memory."* (measured through
`interactive.py`, *phase 2 output COMPLETE* in the same run).

`mal_alloc` sets `gShortBy` on any over-budget request. StuffIt 5's inverse
BWT asks for `numbytes * 4` **expecting** refusal on a small machine and falls
back to a sampled occurrence index, byte-identical — the reason the format
fits at 1 MB (2026-08-07). So exactly the archives exercising the designed
fallback were told they had failed. **The fix is where the knowledge is**: the
message is now gated on `errors > 0 || ret != UNC_OK`. The shortfall was
reported by the component that could measure it, not the one that could
interpret it.

### How it was found, which is not how it was looked for

OPEN_ITEMS.md carried *"joining a segmented set costs far more memory than
the same archive whole"*: 472,137 B whole against a refusal 64 KB over budget
joined. **Those came from different instruments** — peak heap used (autotest)
against `gShortBy` asked (alert).

- **On Linux, join and whole are identical**: `macextract x --stats` on a
  three-part set prints **8,192 B** (join) and **661,173 B** (inner); whole
  prints **661,173 B**.
- **The sizes name their source**: `derived-Library_ISBN_Barcoder.sit` peaks
  at 1,683,101 B; 1,683,101 − 615,348 is the "over a megabyte more", the
  transform vector, present on both paths.

One emulator run of the archive whole printed the same message. **The variable
was never the join.** When two figures disagree, check they are the same
measurement first. The withdrawn claim hid a defect on the path almost every
StuffIt 5 user on a small Mac takes (BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn claims*).

### `gHasWNE` does not mean MultiFinder, and the first fix used it

The advice *"Give MacExtract more in Get Info"* names a control that does not
exist without a partition. Choosing the wording on `gHasWNE` failed: on System
6.0.8 with no MultiFinder, `TrapAvailable(_WaitNextEvent)` is TRUE — the same
screenshot showed it. What answers it is the heap's SHAPE: a zone reaching
most of RAM versus one far smaller than RAM (~700 KB of a 1 MB MemTop against
~400 KB of 4 MB; a 512 KB Mac, ~220 KB of 512 KB, is on the correct side).

## 2026-08-31 (the joined archive that was never meant to survive) — a harness expectation, three hours old and already documented

**Claim: the Macintosh segment join is fine; the check asked for a file the
application is supposed to consume.** `interactive.py --segments` ended on
*"Extraction complete."* then failed `NOT FOUND (50205 B expected)`,
reproducing at the session's starting commit, and sat for a few hours in
OPEN_ITEMS.md as *"completes and writes nothing where it is checked"*.

The volume held the joined archive's CONTENTS:

    f  DFIL/DMOV     27545         0  Cal 3.02
    f  TEXT/MACA         0      2739  Cal.Intro
    f  APPL/C0tl     39884         0  Calendar Tools

**The application has unwrapped envelope chains since 2026-08-14**, so a
joined `.sit` never reaches the disk. `expected_names()`'s docstring
(2026-08-27) already described exactly this failure; every phase but this one
had been converted to it. `phase_segments` now uses it.

### What it cost, and the part worth transferring

**Cost**: an hour, a worktree bisect against `bba32c5`, and a false
OPEN_ITEMS.md entry — the second phantom defect filed from an instrument in
one session (BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn claims*, the segmented-join memory row).
**Both were a check written before a behaviour changed, failing in the
direction that looks like an application bug.** An unrun harness starts LYING:
this phase last ran 2026-08-09; the behaviour changed 2026-08-14.

## 2026-08-31 (the drop the Finder does not make, and the version it does show) — a gesture measured on three Finders

Two questions answered from memory were put on the machine:
`tools/vmac/interactive.py --drop` drags an archive onto the application's
icon, photographs the result, then reads Get Info.

**The drop is a System 7 gesture, and an `FREF` is what enables it.** Six runs,
one variable at a time, on `derived-ScrollbarPattern.sit` under `mv-4M`:

| system | `FREF` for the type | the file's type | what happened |
|---|---|---|---|
| System 3.0 / Finder 5.1 | yes | `SIT!` | icon moved, nothing launched |
| System 6.0.8 | yes | `SIT!` | icon moved, nothing launched |
| System 7.0.1 | no | hfsutils' default | icon moved, nothing launched |
| System 7.0.1 | no | `SIT!` | icon moved, nothing launched |
| System 7.0.1 | yes | hfsutils' default | icon moved, nothing launched |
| System 7.0.1 | **yes** | **`SIT!`** | **the application launched** |

On System 7 the `FREF` is necessary and sufficient, and costs only a resource.

**`'****'` is a wildcard**: one `FREF` of that type launched the application
for an archive typed `'????'`. This program's users hold files that arrived as
`TEXT` or `'????'`; enumerating `SIT!`, `CPT!`… would refuse exactly the files
the program is FOR. A single `'*'` compiles silently to `\0\0\0*` (checked in
the built `FREF`) and matches nothing. Below System 7 the Finder has no such
gesture, so the ~344 B of code reading `AppParmHandle` (measured by building
and reverting) buys nothing on the floor target, and `FREF` and code are worth
adding only together.

**Neither is committed**; the harness is.

### The control is the whole experiment

"Icon moved, nothing else" is also what an undelivered drag looks like
(BLOCKERS.md, *a coordinate in a vmac harness is right if the run
completes*), so each run first drags to empty space and photographs it.
The first System 7 run was a false negative: `mkboot.py --data` leaves
hfsutils' default type, so the `FREF` could not match; the phase now sets it
with `hattrib`. **The subject of the experiment has to be the thing the
experiment is about.**

### And the version

`vers` 1 and 2 shipped earlier the same day unseen. Get Info shows them
**twice on System 6.0.8 and on System 7.0.1** (under the name and on
`Version:`); **System 3.0's "Information about MacExtract" has no version
line at all**. On System 7 the archive beside it says `Version: n/a`, so the
field reads `vers`. Both boxes first read *"MacExtract 0.29.0"*, naming the
application twice; the strings are now the version alone, re-photographed on
System 6.0.8 (`MacExtract`, `0.29.0`, `Version: 0.29.0`).

## 2026-08-31 (the drop, taken) — 128 bytes, one Rez line, and a partition that stopped asking

What was done with the entry above's measurement.

**The wildcard is documented, not just observed.** Inside Macintosh: Macintosh
Toolbox Essentials, Finder Interface: a `FREF` of `'****'` lets users *"drag
all file types ... but not including disks or folders"* to the application,
and the Finder reads `FREF`s *"in system software versions 7.0 and later"*.
`'****'` rather than a list of archive types, because the files this program
is FOR are the ones whose type is wrong — a `.hqx` is `TEXT`, a raw download
`'????'` — and an enumeration would refuse exactly those. `fType` is thrown
away: what the file holds is `unc_sniff`'s business.

**128 bytes, and the alternative cost 344.** `AppParmHandle` is read where it
lives; `CountAppFiles`/`GetAppFiles`/`ClrAppFiles` are glue in the Multiversal
libraries, cost 216 B more, and `GetAppFiles` spins forever at index ≥ 2
(`glue.c`, `while(index)` with no decrement). Every document is taken, one per
pass of the existing loop, falling back to Standard File when the list runs
out. The `tools/build_mac.sh` ratchet moved 147,296 → 147,424. Driven end to
end on System 7.0.1: a `'????'` file dropped on the icon, no Open dialog,
*"Extraction complete."*, both entries of `derived-ScrollbarPattern.sit` out.

### The partition that had been asking all along

`SIZE` asked for 4 MB, so a 4 MB Macintosh met *"MacExtract prefers 4,096K of
memory. 3,089K is available."* on every launch. Nothing here had seen it,
because every harness installs the application as the BOOT SHELL, which gets
all of memory; it turned up in the first Finder launch on System 7. Preferred
is now 2 MB, clearing the alert with about a megabyte of margin.

**The baseline is the part worth keeping.** "This costs
`derived-EasyFind.dmg.sit`, which needs 2,658,721 B" was the obvious sentence,
and false: measured at 4 MB preferred on the same machine, EasyFind is refused
there too — the partition was never 4 MB. The real cost is archives needing
~1.9–~3.8 MB on a machine with more than 2 MB free (an 8 MB Macintosh, which
no emulator here boots). `derived-Library_ISBN_Barcoder.sit` passes byte-exact
at a peak of 1,683,101 B inside the 2 MB partition. **A cost you cannot
measure is not a cost you may assert**; one run against the OLD value turned a
regression note into "unreachable from here".


## 2026-08-31 (the medium, not the machine) — the Macintosh 512K boots, and both reasons it could not were wrong

**Claim: "a true Macintosh 512K cannot be reached at all" was a claim about
HFS.** The machine boots Apple's 400K MFS System 1.1 floppy, and System 3.0 /
Finder 5.1 off an MFS volume built here; it then launches this application and
bombs, `ID = 03` (FORMATS.md, *A true Macintosh 512K*).

**The negative was one A/B short, on the axis the conclusion named.** The
previous day's three A/Bs varied ROM revision, RAM and disk presence and
concluded "it is the volume" without ever varying the volume. A negative whose
evidence never touches the variable it blames is worth one more experiment.

**A sentence stopped the experiment, not the work.** The same entry said the
application was "out on the ROM regardless", naming `NGetTrapAddress` and HFS
parameter blocks — written from the code's shape, not a run, and false in both
halves: `tools/vmac/traptest` returns from `NGetTrapAddress` twice and from
`PBHGetVInfoSync` on a 64K ROM, and bombs at `PBGetCatInfoSync` (`ID = 12`).
The verdict survives — `PBGetCatInfo` is how the application walks a
directory — but **treat "regardless" as the most suspicious word in an
entry**: it claims something need not be measured.

**Retro68 cannot write the volume** (`--cc name.dsk` always emits 800K HFS),
so `tools/vmac/mkmfs.py` builds, lists and extracts 400K MFS volumes:
structure from Inside Macintosh II, "Data Organization on Volumes"; geometry
read off an Apple-initialized volume. Validated by listing Apple's System 1.1
disk (ten files, every fork chain terminating), then rebuilding it from its
own files and booting the rebuild.

**Hold the screen.** The first `traptest` painted its marks and returned; at
emulator speed the System repaints before a frame is taken, so a probe that
exits erases its own evidence. `for (;;)` is the fix.


## 2026-09-01 (the second Toolbox call) — what bombs a 64K ROM, and three instruments that lied on the way to it

**Claim: `MaxApplZone` bombs a true Macintosh 512K, and Apple says so.**
Inside Macintosh II-30 marks it `[Not in ROM]`; the trap arrived with the 128K
ROM and Retro68 emits it unconditionally. Measured with `tools/vmac/traptest`
and by bisecting the real application: `SetApplLimit` returns, `MaxApplZone`
does not (FORMATS.md, *A true Macintosh 512K*).

Three instruments misled on the way:

- **The bomb ID.** `ID = 03` from the application, `10` from the probe, `28`
  from an instrumented build: a missing trap dispatches into whatever is at
  that address, which moves with the binary. **An error code is evidence about
  the aftermath; the call before the first missing mark is the evidence.**
- **A mark nobody could see.** The marks sat mid-screen, under the system
  error dialog, so the run that "proved" `SetApplLimit` fatal had painted its
  survival mark beneath the bomb box. The grid is now eight to a row in the
  top 75 points.
- **`--gc-sections`, again.** A `for (;;)` after a readout made the rest dead
  code; 188,928 B became 10,368 B — a different memory map. The fix is a
  condition the compiler cannot fold (`while (LMGetScrnBase() != (Ptr)-1L)`);
  check the binary's size after any change meant to freeze it (BLOCKERS.md
  records the same trap eating three of four ballast runs).

**Writing to screen memory made the bisect possible**: marks before `InitGraf`
need nothing initialised. The same trick painted 24-bit values as bars to read
the trap addresses in FORMATS.md, with `ScrnBase` painted alongside as a known
value; the decode drifted twice and was caught.

**A guard built on `TrapAvailable` does not fire.** On a 64K ROM it reports
`MaxApplZone` PRESENT: the table entry is neither `_Unimplemented` nor a
routine. **A trap-availability test cannot see a `[Not in ROM]` routine**;
these machines need a machine test. Skipping the call in a throwaway build
reached the whole UI, a file sniffed, and an extraction stopping at `ID = 12`
on an HFS call.

**No change to the application.** A 64K-ROM Macintosh is out of scope
(OPEN_ITEMS.md); `MaxApplZone` is correct on every machine the project claims.


## 2026-09-01 (two byte reads) — the guard that lets a 64K-ROM Macintosh start, and why it is not a trap test

**Superseded 2026-10-15** by `GrowApplZone()`, which runs on every ROM
alike and is on `main` since 2026-10-16 (*the purge MaxApplZone never did*).

**Claim: one guard makes the application start on a 64K ROM at no cost
elsewhere.** Kept on branch `rom64k`, not `main`: neutral on every claimed
tier, but no real machine had run what it enables, and an unexercised
capability does not belong in the download. `Has128KROM()` reads the ROM
version word at `ROMBase+8` and skips `MaxApplZone` when it positively reads
as a 64K ROM. Measured: the build reaches Standard File on the emulated 512K
under MFS System 3.0; **69/69 at 1 MB on System 6.0.8** and **66/69 on System
3.0 at 512 KB** unchanged.

**Not `TrapAvailable`**, for the reason in the entry above.

**Sources, both Apple's.** Inside Macintosh II, `Environs`: the ROM version is
the word at `ROMBase+8`, "$00xx for the Macintosh 128K or 512K"; Inside
Macintosh IV, Preface: version ≥ 117 ($75) is safe for that volume's routines.
`Environs` is itself `[Not in ROM]` glue, hence the low-memory route: a test
must not depend on what it tests for.

**Written as a negative on purpose**: `!(rom[8] == 0 && rom[9] < 0x75)`, so
any unsurveyed version word (a Macintosh XL reads `$xxFF`) leaves behaviour as
before. The first draft asked "is this a 128K ROM?" and would have skipped
`MaxApplZone` on every non-`$00xx` machine — a regression the two 128K-ROM
tiers run would not have shown.

**The size ceiling did its job**: 8 B over `UNC_MAC_MAX_CODE`; comparing the
low byte instead of composing the word saved exactly those 8 B, so **0 B of
the engine's budget** (FORMATS.md, *What the application costs the engine*).

**Not claimed**: that the application works on a 64K-ROM machine. Extraction
needs HFS, which those machines only have with a `Hard Disk 20` Mini vMac does
not emulate. The rest is MANUAL_TESTS.md §6, askable because the branch's
download does it — a test that needs the tester to own Retro68 is one nobody
runs.


## 2026-09-01 (the package that cannot be handed over) — three routes into Aladdin's AppleLink expander, and the control that made an empty list mean something

OPEN_ITEMS.md filed AppleLink `.pkg` as waiting on a gradeable specimen — an
assumption: the grammar was transcribed out of `PKG Expand Translator` on
2026-08-23, so a package can be WRITTEN here, and that translator is a second
reader on the same disk image (the technique of `tools/sdmodule/`,
`tools/ssmodule/`). Seven boots say Aladdin's software will not take one.

### Three routes, three controls

| route | what it did with a package | its control, same boot |
|---|---|---|
| `Translate ▸ PKG Expand…`, StuffIt Deluxe 3.5.1 | Standard File lists **only folders** | `CPT Expand…` lists the type-`PACT` files |
| StuffIt Expander 4.0.2, `Expand… ⌘E` | lists every package, expands **nothing**, no error | `Payload.hqx` → `Widget`, byte-exact, 1,256 B |
| `DropConvert™`, `Convert… ⌘C` | `Convert` produces **nothing** | `Payload.hqx` → `Widget.sit`, 532 B, `SITD/SIT!` |

Two boots of empty lists, and four Finder typings (`TEXT/ttxt`, `PACT/EXTR`,
`PACT/ttxt`, `TEXT/EXTR`), read as a fact about the packages; one Compact Pro
archive in the same dialog made it a fact about the command.

### What that dialog is actually asking for

A folder. The filter proc `PKG Expand` hands `_SFPGetFile` tests `ioFlAttrib`
bit 4 (*is a directory*) (`Othe` 0 @0x215e), where the CompactPro
translator's tests type `PACT` (@0x2e1c). `DITL 2051` reads **"Expand into
selected folder"**, `DITL 2052` is *"Name of new folder:"*, and its `Help`
says it extracts "archives created by AppleLink ... usually [with] a suffix
'.pkg'". That fits 2026-08-23's manifest hypothesis without settling it: this
build puts up `DLOG 2050`, which has no such button, and Open on a folder
descends into it, so nothing here can complete the command.

### What this cannot see, and the lesson

**A null result from somebody's user interface is not a fact about a
format**: nothing separates "will not take this input" from "this is not a
package"; one real `.pkg` settles both. The open item is unchanged, its cost
recorded — **seven boots**. **An empty list is evidence about nothing until
something has filled the same list**; the control cost four minutes and
arrived two boots late.


## 2026-09-01 (the tier that needed no Macintosh) — a budget sweep, a ceiling, and a number that was an artefact

The 512 KB tier stood at 66/69 and read like a target.

### The sweep

The Mac allocator is a running total against a cap, refused per entry;
`macextract --budget N` is the same rule. `tools/run_tiers.py` sweeps the
69-fixture sample at a tier's measured budget in **five seconds** against one
emulator boot per fixture, and reproduces System 3.0 / 512 KB **exactly** —
66/69, the same three — and the 1 MB floor's 69/69; `ci.sh` asserts both.
What it cannot see is in TESTING.md, first item: System 6.0.8 / 512 KB comes
out 59/69 against the machine's 58, because the Memory Manager must also find
one PIECE that big.

### The ceiling

Bisected minimum budgets **246,734 B**, **393,869 B**, **401,408 B** against
197,728 B. Two ask for more in a SINGLE allocation than the machine has —
205,020 B and 352,161 B, each one resident BWT block; the third wants 1,536 B
per context byte across all 256, adaptive state that cannot be dropped.
**66/69 is the machine's ceiling, not an engine gap** (FORMATS.md has the
numbers).

### The number that was an artefact

`synth-dd-m5.dd  short by 928`, on a fixture needing 405,520 B: **a shortfall
is the FIRST refused request's, not the entry's demand** — method 5 asks
1,536 B at a time, so the figure understates by 220x here and 3,000x at
300,000. It was printed to users as *"Needs 8K more memory. Give MacExtract
more in Get Info"*, and following it yields the same message. Both front ends
now say **at least**. The old wording called itself "round enough to type and
never short" — a claim about a number by the code computing it, already wrong
once (M46: firing after a successful extraction). A message is the only claim
the user reads, and no byte-comparison suite can fail on it.

## 2026-09-01 (the search, not the reference) — Apple Archive, and what rewriting a probe actually buys

**Superseded 2026-10-18** (*the formats it only named*): Apple Archive is
not recognised any more; libNeoAppleArchive writes the specimens that must
not be.

**The claim was about a search.** OPEN_ITEMS.md said Apple Archive was unnamed
"for want of a reference". One query found `0xilis/libNeoAppleArchive` (MIT, a
from-scratch reading of the format: `AAR_MAGIC`/`YAA_MAGIC`, the `pbz*` set,
the six-byte prologue, sixteen field subtypes). Withdrawn in BLOCKERS.md with
its cost.

**It is an oracle, not just a spec.** `tools/build_neoaa.sh` compiles the three
core sources with `gcc` and `EXCLUDE_AEA_SUPPORT=1` (its Makefile wants
`clang`, Homebrew OpenSSL and an install step); `tools/neoaa_write.c` writes
each of the four shapes the probe recognises and reads it back. That moves
Apple Archive from RAR's "signature only" grade to bzip2's and 7z's.

**Two sources disagree usefully.** The library defines codecs `e` LZFSE, `z`
zlib, `b` LZBITMAP; the archiveteam wiki (`reference/notes/Apple_Archive.md`)
adds lzma `x` and lz4 `4`, and the library's own `docs/NeoAAArchiveGeneric.md`
says both belong to the format, "not yet added". All five are claimed; the two
nothing here can write are marked untestable in TESTING.md. `pbzx` is also the
payload inside an Apple flat package, so those now name as Apple Archive.

**The Macintosh ratchet refused it — the useful part.** 196 B over a ceiling
with 20 B headroom. Two rewrites (subtypes as a string walked by `in_set()`,
since on a 68000 data is free and comparisons are code; three length tests
made one) bought 52 B — **12 %**. Code shape is worth little; what the code
*is* is worth everything (same as *Size flags, priced in both currencies*,
where a day of flags bought 780 B). The remaining 164 B was paid on the
named-only set's existing terms (OPEN_ITEMS.md, part 1): 1.2 % of the
13,602 B by which `derived-Domino_v1.4.sit` clears the 1 MB Mac Plus budget
(FORMATS.md, *Budget*) — paid in the open, unlike the 31,860 B that quietly
moved the budget on 2026-08-24.

## 2026-09-01 (the reader was in the sentence) — feeding SuperDisk!'s own extractor a stream we wrote, and one hypothesis that did not survive it

OPEN_ITEMS.md carried SuperDisk!'s path cap as untested for five days under a
sentence saying a generated stream could not be graded because nothing off
the Mac reads the container — followed by "the one second reader that exists
is an archive's own self-extractor ... never handed a stream this project
wrote". The second sentence disproves the first. **"There is no oracle" was a
claim about what had been TRIED** (withdrawal in BLOCKERS.md).

### The method, which generalises past this format

`SD! Utilities.x` is an APPL whose data fork IS the archive and whose resource
fork is the extractor. `tools/vmac/superdisk.py` MacBinaries it back together
around a stream `tools/synth_sd.py` wrote, and `CODE 2` walks it. **Any
self-extracting archive is an implementation you can feed.** Ten folders of 31
characters, eleven files, declared paths 43 to 331 bytes: every one built,
all eleven byte-identical. The extractor creates each component through the
File Manager and never assembles a path, so **what it makes IS the uncut
path** — and for the three files and two folders past 255 bytes,
`unc_path_leaf` reports exactly it.

### What was built rather than invented, and why the difference showed up

Every byte this project does not decode is COPIED from a corpus archive (the
eight head bytes, a folder record's twenty, four unread bytes of a file's
thirty): a wrong guess there is indistinguishable from the failure sought. The
first run broke that rule — invented file records and STORED blocks — and
bombed, *unimplemented trap*, writing nothing. It also exposed a coverage
fact: **no stored block exists in either fixture** (all seven are methods 7
and 11), so `sd_block_head`'s bit-15 branch had never run on real data and the
116 corrupted variants only flip bytes inside coded blocks.

### The hypothesis, and the discipline that killed it

"The stored branch is wrong" was wrong: the same 4,796-byte fork written coded
and stored, otherwise byte-identical, **both came back byte-exact** — so the
reading off `CODE 2` @0x614 on 2026-08-20 (bit-15 length counting its own two
header bytes, except 0x8002) is confirmed. Two more single-variable runs
cleared a stream opening with a file record and a guessed file record. **Four
causes cleared, the bomb still unexplained**; the untried combination is a
root file FOLLOWED by a folder, written up as a one-boot task and labelled a
hypothesis (`tools/vmac/README.md`).

Had the first run used borrowed blocks it would have passed, closed the item,
and left the stored branch untested. **The broken run was worth more than the
clean one**, because the difference was reduced one variable at a time.

## 2026-09-01 (the machine that is too small) — a 128K Macintosh, and a status row measured on the other machine

**Claim: the guarded build's interface works on 64K-ROM Macintoshes, the 128K
among them.** Measured on a 512K only; false for the 128K: the `rom64k`
`dist/` bombs `ID = 03` there from the same volume, `Mac128K.ROM` and System
3.0 (FORMATS.md, *A Macintosh 128K*). `mv-128K` is `-m 128K -mem 128K`,
`mv-512K` is `-m 128K -mem 512K` — the fourth variable was carried in the
machine's NAME rather than in a run, one notch along from the withdrawn
file-system claim (BLOCKERS.md).

**This negative is arithmetic, so stable.** `ApplLimit − ApplZone` is
78,568 B on a 128K; `CODE` totals 148,780 B, one segment 142,152 B placed
whole; the largest grantable block is 63,744 B, measured. No volume, System or
build flag moves RAM under the screen buffer; only a different program would.

**`FreeMem` reports both machines identical**, 4,846 B, because the zone
starts small and grows on demand. The Segment Loader wants one contiguous
block, so the probe bisects `NewPtr`. **Ask what the failing code requests,
then measure that.**

## 2026-09-01 (no hotspot, twenty-three decoders) — where the application's code is, and two instruments that said otherwise

**The application is not large because of one thing.** 147,568 B of `CODE`,
**59.3 % in twenty-three decoders**, the largest 8,860 B; the largest file is
the shell at 17,358 B, the two largest functions ~5.1 KB each (FORMATS.md,
*Where the code is*). Nothing is worth more than about 6 %.

**Both cheap instruments lie high.** Summing `m68k-apple-macos-size` gives
178,696 B (21 % high: `--gc-sections` drops the uncalled); counting `.text`
and `.rodata` in the map gives 179,561 B, because **Retro68 places `.rodata`
in the A5 world**. Only sections under a `.code*` output section answer the
budget's question; `tools/code_map.py` checks its total against `size`.

**That puts 32,077 B of tables outside `CODE` already** — the SpaceSaver
dictionary at 9,701 B, cipher S-boxes, fixed inflate tables — which is WHY
data is free (*What the application costs the engine*); no large table hides
in the code figure. **It prices the parked overlay work**: `selective-loading`'s
5,988 B is the ciphers, 7,480 B of code, 5.1 % of the binary; every other
candidate is a 2.5–8.9 KB decoder with the same eligibility problem. **A bigger
prize needs segmenting the decoders as a set**, a different question.

### The transferable part: an assertion that fires is not an assertion that protects

`code_map.py` exited 1 on a wrong `--expect` — and still printed **the entire
table** to stdout, disowning it on stderr, so `> numbers.txt` kept the numbers
and dropped the disowning. **Ask also what a check DOES once it has fired**:
decide before printing, and print nothing on stdout when the answer is no.
Every harness here that prints results and then grades them is exposed.

## 2026-09-03 (the binary nothing builds, twice more) — three UI failures that were one unfinished fix, and an explanation that fit six cases out of nine

`segcheck.py`'s `zip-named`, `split-named` and `wrapped` were recorded failing
on `main` across eight runs, the application blamed. All three pass:
`phase_wrapped` and `phase_named` graded against `build/dev/macextract`, which
nothing builds and `make clean` removes; `R.sh` reaches it unguarded, so the
phase raised `FileNotFoundError` before comparing. With `phase_chain`'s guard
and `CD.CLI`: ~155 s, ~134 s, MATCH. **The same defect was fixed on 2026-08-27
in one of three places**, under "One CLI per file now"; one `grep` settles a
claim about every line of a file.

### The transferable part: an explanation that fits the cases you looked at

The offered account — passes are schemes found by HEADER, failures by NAME —
explained six of nine and was cheaply wrong on three: `wrapped` stages parts
under names that share no stem ("under names that say nothing", its own
docstring); `chain` is interactive and passes; and FORMATS.md said all three
joined byte-exact on the Mac, a cross-file contradiction live throughout.
**When a hypothesis partitions a set, check the members on each side, not the
ones that suggested it.** The true partition (which phase had its reference
CLI repaired) is one `git log -S`.

### And a correction to what would have closed it

The item said a Linux run through `unc_segment_describe` would settle it. It
would not: **name-based sibling search is host code, written twice** —
`cli/main.c` and `mac/macextract_mac.c` (`ZipFamPartOf`, `SplitPartOf`,
`SegScanFamily`) — so a Linux run is blind to a Mac-side naming fault. Both
are correct (Linux: `Aset.z01` → `payload.bin`, 278,294 B; `Ablob.001` →
`Downerƒ`; `Apart.sit.1.hqx` → `Downerƒ`; and on the Mac), but the proposed
command could not have shown it.

## 2026-09-03 (the struct that grew after it was measured) — 296 was the offset of the last field

`UncEntryInfo` was quoted at **296 bytes** on the 68000 target in FORMATS.md
(*Name limits*), *the name cap* and a `src/fmt_lzh.c` comment. The target
compiler says **298** (`m68k-apple-macos-gcc -Os`; `m68k-linux-gnu-gcc`
agrees; x86-64 is 304).

**296 is the offset of `name_full_len`.** `name_truncated` closed the struct
at 295, padded to 296; the same day's correction added `name_full_len` and
nothing re-measured. Nothing rested on the two bytes (zip's 65,535-byte name
cannot travel on a 4 KB stack either way; the stack, 5,200 B constant on
2026-08-31, was measured directly).

- **A measurement taken mid-change describes a struct that may not exist by
  evening**; re-measure at the END of a change.
- **It hid behind a coincidence**: 296 is also the nine-deep path
  `tools/synth_now.py` writes (*the path builder's own cap*), so a reader
  checking 296 found a 296 that was right.

**`tools/check_docs.py` gained a fifth invariant**: every `"N bytes on the
68000 target"` in the root docs, `src/`, `cli/`, `mac/` and `include/` must
equal `sizeof(UncEntryInfo)` from a one-line Retro68 probe (0.2 s; skips out
loud without an m68k compiler). Mutation-tested: restoring `296` fails one
site; adding a field fails all three at 302. A historical value is written
outside that phrase — *quoted at 296 bytes*.

## 2026-09-03 (a folder is a name too) — numbering folders like files, and the table that made it affordable

**At the maintainer's ask.** The shell numbered a FILE landing on a taken name
(`dup.txt` → `dup~1.txt`) but descended into a FOLDER, so two folders agreeing
for 31 characters merged on disk. Folders are now numbered `~1`..`~99` by the
same `BumpName`.

**What looked impossible was a table size filed as a property of the
formats.** OPEN_ITEMS.md (*Limits of the formats themselves*) said a folder
declared only inside file paths "looks exactly like the first folder being
revisited", and remembering long names costs too much. Neither held:
`RepDirMemo` already recorded every directory the run created, and its cost
was whole NAMES, 68 B a row for 24 folders. A 32-bit hash of the component
answers the only question asked — *is this directory this run's, and this
name's?* — in 8 bytes: **200 folders in the 1,600 B that held 24**.

- **A directory this run did not make is still descended into**, so
  re-extracting an archive does not spray `~1` over the first run's work.
  `tools/run_macnames.py`, *folder_again_case*, holds it.
- **The table never evicts**: a lost row would SPLIT one archive folder across
  two directories, worse than the merge. A full table stops numbering and
  merges as before. **The safe direction for a bounded table is the behaviour
  it replaced.**
- **The merge line takes from the report's failure reserve.** Past `~99` a
  folder says *combined with*; an archive reaching that has a hundred rename
  lines crowding it out. Measured: at 101 folders the line was dropped without
  the reserve.

**Unpredicted: the duplicate report.** Every file in a merged folder rediscovered
it; the merged folder is now memoed under its own name too, so a directory may
hold more than one row.

The old claim's cost is in BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn claims*; disproving it took
one zip and the mock sink in `ci.sh` since 2026-08-28 — a claim about our own
binary, the cheapest to test.

## 2026-09-04 (the field nobody assigned) — a struct filled field by field, and the crash that was shaped like three formats

**Claim.** The Mac OS 9 bomb on every DiskDoubler archive and on SuperDisk!
(BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn claims*) was an uninitialised pointer. `RunExtract`
in `mac/macextract_mac.c` filled `UncOptions` field by field and never set
`long_name`/`long_name_cap` (added 2026-08-27; `git grep long_name mac/`
returned nothing). `unc_path_push` → `path_full_add` (`src/unc_util.c`) writes
every component through that pointer when non-NULL with cap ≥ 2, and only
DiskDoubler, SuperDisk! and Now Compress walk a tree with it. **Measured**:
`tools/longname-repro/` passes a 4-byte block with a 1 MB cap under ASan —
those three die in `path_full_add` on the first component (`WRITE of size 1`,
via `unc_path_leaf` ← `dd_archive`), Compact Pro and StuffIt never touch it,
all five clean with NULL. The fix zeroes the struct before setting fields.

**Why every experiment pointed away, and what that teaches.**

- **A symptom shaped like a format is not evidence about the format.**
  Format-specific plus host-specific means a *host input* the formats consume
  unequally; one `grep` of the option fields against the shell's assignments
  answers it. The host surface is small: `UncIO`, `UncAlloc`, `UncSink`,
  `UncProgress`, `UncOptions`.
- **"The classic Mac shell passes NULL" was a header comment in
  `include/macextract.h` nobody ran** — BLOCKERS.md's tenth smell, in a comment.
- **An uninitialised local defeats every instrument that changes the stack.**
  Tracers, `-D` probes, `kStackBump`, checkpoint files and unrelated commits
  moved the garbage; hence a `git bisect` first-bad commit that would not
  reproduce, a cure by "keeping the probes but never executing them", and two
  shipped versions bombing with different errors at different entries. **A
  defect that moves with layout is a read of state nobody set: search for a
  missing assignment, not a wrong write.**
- **The autotest build and the Mini vMac tiers passed on luck** (a different
  call chain, different garbage). **Inferred, not measured**: no run on
  System 3.0, 6.0.8 or 7.0.1 showed the fault.
- **The lesson was already in the tree.** `unc_extract_as` zeroes the struct
  for a NULL `opt`, with a 2026-08-27 comment about a field list that had
  segfaulted the unit tests the day `long_name` was added; the fix went only
  where that crash was. **Grep the other hosts the same afternoon.** It paid:
  five field-by-field `UncOptions` in `tests/unit_formats.c`, all in
  DiskDoubler and SuperDisk! tests; gdb on the pre-fix binary saw NULL in all
  20 reads. Zeroed now.

**What would have caught it before Mac OS 9 did.** Nothing in `ci.sh`: the
mock Toolbox build (`tests/mac_sink_test.c`) never executes `RunExtract`, and
neither ASan nor valgrind reports an uninitialised STACK read — valgrind was
silent through those 20 reads, since bytes an earlier call wrote count as
initialised. That is MemorySanitizer's job, on a path no host build takes
(TESTING.md, *mac sink*). The rule that catches it: **zero the whole struct,
then set fields.**

**Consequence.** `RunExtract` zeroes `opt`, history in a comment;
`tools/longname-repro/` keeps the host half of the reproduction;
`tools/vmac/os9sample.txt` gains `synth-now-mixed.now`. Mac OS 9.2 comes back
**21/21**, and all six DiskDoubler archives extract there byte-exact.

**A harness defect the fix let the run reach.** `derived-Terrainman_2.0__.sea`
reported ten present files missing: the verifier passed folder paths to `hls`
as a Python `str`, so 8-bit folder names went out UTF-8. Files with such names
had been checked since 2026-08-28; a folder never had. **A harness right about
one shape of a thing is untested on the others** — the encoding rule was
already written two functions away, for `hcopy` (`tools/vmac/README.md`,
*Checking a run off the disk*).

Cost in BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn claims*; numbers in FORMATS.md, *Mac OS 9.2*.

## 2026-09-09 (the disk image that is expanded and not opened) — DART, and an error code for a file with nothing wrong with it

**Asked for**: expand a compressed DART to an uncompressed DART, and say so
plainly when the file is already uncompressed. MacMount mounts an UNCOMPRESSED
DART and refuses a compressed one, because unpacking is this program's job.

**The scope line moved by one method, not by a principle.** Disk images stay
out of scope (a filesystem, not a codec). But DART's third method is *no
compression*, so what a mounter reads is a DART with a 2 in its first byte —
expanding one is a codec with a sink-writable output and no volume involved.

**The refusal needed its own code.** An already-uncompressed DART is neither
`UNC_ERR_FORMAT` (it is valid) nor `UNC_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` (the opposite of the
truth). It is `UNC_ERR_NOTCOMPRESSED`: the shell says "This DART disk image is
already uncompressed.", the CLI "already uncompressed: there is nothing to
expand", where it would have said "This file could not be extracted". **An
error enum is a vocabulary, and a verdict it cannot express becomes the
nearest wrong word.**

**Identification without a signature.** Three weak fields (a byte in {0,1,2},
one of six, a size); what makes the probe safe is that **the chunk-length
table must add up to the rest of the file, to the byte** — the test that
settled the format for MacMount (lengths as bytes leave
`Studio8_Program.dart` 300,951 short; as WORDS, 811,586 exactly). A cut DART
is therefore not recognized at all rather than half-read. The type/size
pairing is **tighter than CiderPress2's** `FormatToKind` (eleven combinations)
— Apple's `DartIntf.h` names a file type for seven; the other four (Lisa 800K,
Apple II 400K, 720K Mac, 1440K MS-DOS low-density) DART could not have
written. **Where two references disagree about what is legal, obey the one
that names a constant.**

**The codec was already here.** DART's "best" is LZHUF, i.e. `-lh1-`, run by
`unc_lzah.c` since M5 (StuffIt method 5) and M28 (LZH). Apple dropped the
leading length word and fills the window with 0x00 instead of 0x20: one mode,
`UNC_LZAH_DART`, eight lines. LZHUF's start position `N - F` versus this
decoder's 0 does not matter: with a UNIFORM fill, a back-reference before the
first byte reads the fill byte either way.

**Graded against the encoder's input.** Neither `unar` nor `macunpack` parses
DART; CiderPress2 publishes two 800K disks DART 1.5.3 compressed under MAME,
both methods, **with the source images**. Four assertions: data halves equal
the source images; tag halves equal the source Disk Copy tags; the methods
agree; and one specimen's resource fork carries DART's own 1993 checksums
('CKSM' 2 = `183F8B19`), checked against a Disk Copy 4.2 checksum of the
output. Each was made to fail first (0x20 window, byte-length reading, dropped
slot rule, off-by-one run count), each on a different assertion.

**A cap from a format's fallback is worth asserting.** The first synthetic
encoded a chunk as all literals — 20,962 bytes for 20,960 — and was refused,
correctly: DART stores such a chunk as 0xFFFF, so "a compressed chunk may not
exceed its expansion" is a format rule and bounds the read buffer. When such a
cap is wrong the failure is "not recognized" and nobody looks.

**The peak that was a constant.** A fixed 20,960-byte chunk buffer made peak
RAM identical for every DART — CLAUDE.md's smell, real here. Sizing it from
the table's longest entry makes it vary (24,582 B vs 25,056 B on the two
"fast" archives); the saving is 0–474 B on all five specimens, since every
real 800K disk has a barely-compressible chunk, kept for mostly-empty 400K
disks on small machines. (It also cost a heap overrun from a stale
`chunk + 20960`, caught on the next suite run.)

**Cost on the Macintosh**: +2,168 B of code, +164 B of A5, both ratchets in
`tools/build_mac.sh` raised with attribution. The A5 figure came from diffing
`.data` symbols: 28 B type table, 20 B format row, 4 B probe pointer, 4 B on
`unc_strerror`'s switch, ~100 B text. Rows hold the DIGIT of the file type,
not the OSType — 8 B of code to save 24 B of data, the second time composing a
constant beat storing one (2026-09-01, *two byte reads*).

**A bug in `tools/fetch_references.sh`**: the wiki block's `cd
reference/notes` never returned, so on a fresh tree the script died at the
zstd fetch under `set -e` and zstd, brotli, lrzip, wimlib, libNeoAppleArchive
and the Apple Archive page never arrived — unseen because each block is
guarded by its own output. `cd` removed; the banner moved to the end. **A
script whose steps are each guarded by their own output is never run end to
end.**

**Not done**: no resource fork in the output, so DART's checksums are not
written; nothing reads them and no reference says what they should be for an
uncompressed DART (OPEN_ITEMS.md, part 2).

**Run on the target**: both methods byte-exact through the shell on an
emulated Mac Plus at 4 MB and at the 1 MB floor, peak matching Linux plus
per-block overhead; the refusal photographed on System 6.0.8. The harness
floppies are 1440 KB, so an 838 KB output fits — the assumption that it could
not was about an 800K floppy.

Numbers and per-specimen results were FORMATS.md, *DART*, and the suite
TESTING.md, *DART*; **both left with the format on 2026-09-25** (*the disk
images that found another home*). What this entry describes is v0.9 through
v0.32.0 and nothing since.

## 2026-09-09 (the oracle that built two times in three) — a timestamp race, and a suite that reported it as a missing reference

**Found by eye in a CI log.** `run_mime.py` printed *"SKIPPED — no
reference/mpack"* and returned 0 with `reference/mpack` present. Two defects,
one symptom.

**The root cause, reduced.** `tools/build_mpack.sh` copied the reference tree
with `cp -r`. mpack 1.6 ships `Makefile.in` ten minutes newer than
`Makefile.am` (2003-07-21 23:49:20 vs 23:39:28), which keeps automake's
`$(srcdir)/Makefile.in: Makefile.am ...` rule from firing; `cp -r` restamps
both, and when `Makefile.am` lands on the later clock tick, `make` runs
**automake 1.17 over a 1994 tree** and dies (`required file './depcomp' not
found`, `Error 63`). Measured: **3 failures in 8 runs** with `cp -r`, **0 in
40** with `cp -pR`. The comment beside `-p` says why.

**Why nobody saw it**: output went to `/dev/null` and `set -e` killed the
script before its own error message, exiting 2 silently. It now keeps
`build/mpack.log` and prints the last twenty lines on failure.

**The second defect is the transferable one.** `run_mime.py`'s `build()`
returned `None` both when `reference/mpack` was never fetched and when the
tree was there and the build FAILED, and the caller called both "no
reference/mpack" and exited 0 — differential coverage silently gone, `ci.sh`
green. **A skip and a failure that look the same in a 200-line log are the
same thing in practice.** The rule now, in all three suites that build an
oracle from `reference/`:

- reference tree **absent** → skip, exit 0 (a fresh clone must still run
  `ci.sh`);
- **present** and the oracle will not build → print the build's output and
  **exit 1**, ending "fix the build, or delete `reference/X` to make this a
  skip".

`run_lzh.py` had the messages right and still returned 0 on a compile
failure; changed to 1. **A right message is not a right verdict.**

What it could have cost: the MIME suite is the only thing holding
`src/fmt_mime.c` against munpack. Found by a **cross-file contradiction** — a
message naming a directory `ls` showed was there. **Hypothesis, labelled**:
that the triggering CI run had this cause (log gone, timing-dependent); the
mechanism itself is reduced and measured.

---

## 2026-09-09 (the merge that deletes the branch) — bringing four parked branches up to date

Four branches merged up to `main` after DART; three routine.

**A branch whose feature was REMOVED from `main` loses it to a clean merge.**
`rom64k` exists to carry `Has128KROM()`, which `main` had briefly and removed
in `2dbe26d`. The branch had not touched `mac/macextract_mac.c` since, so `git
merge main` replays the removal with no conflict. Measured beforehand: `git
merge-tree origin/main rom64k` yields **zero** occurrences of `Has128KROM`
against five on the tip. **A conflict is a question; a clean merge is an
assumption** — dangerous exactly where only one side edited. Check branches
whose purpose `main` decided against; it is one command.

- The branch carried a **withdrawn claim** in three files (the guarded build
  starts on "the 128K and the true 512K"), disproved by M49 (the 128K's
  largest block is 63,744 B against 142,152 B of `CODE`); two doc conflicts
  were resolved AGAINST the branch.
- It needed correcting **four** times: `dist/README.txt` is generated by
  `tools/make_dist.sh`, restored from before M49 along with the guard, so the
  one page an end user reads came back with the claim. **Restoring an old
  commit restores its prose too.**

**Ratchets are set from a build, not arithmetic**: on `selective-extract` the
merged build is **60 B of code and 24 B of A5 MORE** than main's DART increment
plus the branch's own.

## 2026-09-18 (the byte that left through a pointer) — runs out of the window, the CRC the writer already kept, and a model half its size

A speed/size/RAM review, landing only what costs nothing on the other two
axes. Four things qualified; the rest — a three-byte Arsenic transform vector,
`UNC_HOT` on Compact Pro and Now Compress, a second Now Compress block slot,
transient cipher tables — trade one currency for another and were parked.
Graded by the 932-fixture suite, measured with callgrind; no Mac tick taken.

- **Runs, not bytes, through the pointer.** `unc_lzah_decode`,
  `unc_lzdyn_decode`, `unc_lzst0_decode` and `unc_arsenic_decode` took
  `int (*put)(void *, uint8_t)`. The LZ three already write every byte into
  their window, so they now take `UncPutRun` and flush `[flushed, pos)` every
  2 KB (4 KB for 8 KB windows), keeping unflushed span plus longest match
  inside the window. Arsenic, whose only caller is `unc_sit_decode_fork`,
  takes the `UncForkOut` and uses the inline path.
- **Arsenic's per-byte `unc_crc32`** — 641,115 calls on
  `derived-Library_ISBN_Barcoder.sit` — is replaced by the fork writer's CRC
  over its 512-byte flushes (`UNC_CK_CRC32`, seeded `UNC_CRC32_INIT`).
- **The model stored a symbol that was always `first + n`.** Nine `ArsModel`s
  of 128 `(int32, int32)` pairs is 9,360 B in every StuffIt 5 entry's peak;
  frequency-only is 4,788 B. *uint16_t was tried and rejected*: the zero-extend
  cost the hottest loop **+7.8 %** of its instructions on
  `derived-a2basic.dmg.sit`. Thirty-two bits, no symbol: −4,572 B, loop
  unchanged.

**Result, Linux Ir:**

| fixture | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `derived-Library_ISBN_Barcoder.sit` (Arsenic, fast path) | 200,508,178 | 181,691,663 | **−9.4 %** |
| `derived-a2basic.dmg.sit` (Arsenic, fast path) | 151,556,773 | 145,451,251 | −4.0 % |
| `test1-best` (DART, LZHUF) | 156,623,685 | 152,234,748 | −2.8 % |
| `lhasa-maclha-l2_lh1.lzh` (-lh1-) | 3,079,619 | 3,005,236 | −2.4 % |
| `derived-XferIt_1.5b4.sea` (Compact Pro, control) | 76,939,094 | 76,573,429 | −0.5 % |

**StuffIt 5 under a 400 KB budget: 24 of 31, was 23**; the six bisected
minimums in FORMATS.md fell by 3,569 to 3,755 B. The Mac tiers were not
re-run; every earlier on-Mac StuffIt 5 peak is that much high, and FORMATS.md
says so once.

**It was not the zero promised.** Flushing at two sites per coder through one
shared six-argument function cost **+468 B** of 68000 code; one site at the
loop head plus a static flush per file: **+76 B of `CODE`, −12 B of A5**,
against a review that said "roughly 0". A failed entry's partial output is
not flushed further; it was never graded and both hosts discard it.

**Six probes moved ahead of the zip pair.** The spanned-zip probe scans the
last 64 KB backwards in 1 KB reads, so LZH, Now Compress, DiskDoubler,
AppleSingle and both Compact Pro probes waited up to 65 reads. None can take a
zip (every zip head is `PK`; the argument is beside the table in
`unc_engine.c`), and a Compact Pro archive carrying a stored zip part in its
last 64 KB, formerly misclaimed, is now the archive it is. **Unmeasured on a
floppy, labelled so**: the gain is a hypothesis about real hardware; safety is
graded by 932 fixtures, 9,320 variants and the DART specimens.

**"No impact on the other dimensions" was asserted from reading the code and
was wrong twice in a day**, by 468 B and 7.8 %, both caught by per-object
`m68k-apple-macos-size` and per-function callgrind run before the commit. A
cost estimated is a cost unknown.

## 2026-09-18 (the floppy that was full) — a 40-byte gap that was written up as 62 KB, and a refusal that was a full disk

FORMATS.md said the Mac needed 16 KB more budget than the Linux cap on one
fixture and 33 to 62 KB on another, blamed 16 B per block (which cannot make
16 KB with six blocks live), and carried `derived-EasyFind.dmg.sit` as not
extracting on a 1 MB Mac Plus. The review ranked checking it above every code
change.

**The measurement**, both capped at 562,000 B (559 B above their bisected
Linux minimum of 561,441 B) on the 1 MB machine:

| fixture | Linux peak | Mac peak | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `derived-XMenu.dmg.sit` | 561,882 | 561,922 | byte-exact, 704 s |
| `derived-EasyFind.dmg.sit` | 561,879 | 561,919 | byte-exact, 1,427 s |

**40 bytes, twice, and 40 at the shipped budget as well.**

**Two instrument errors made the gap.** The 2026-08-30 figures cited
`gRefusedWhy = 1`, which records a run's FIRST refusal — for StuffIt 5, the
transform vector requested expecting no (M46 found the same in the *Needs 48K
more memory* alert, and nobody revisited this). And EasyFind's "refusal" was
`UNC_ERR_SINK`, `ret` −9: its one entry is 1,851,907 B and `run.py`'s Out
volume has been a 1,440 KB floppy since M10 (`--out-kb 2400` exists). **A
per-entry failure is not a memory refusal until the error code has been
read.** What hid it: at that budget the walks take 12 and 24 minutes against
`run.py`'s 300 s default timeout. Three boots settled it.

**Consequences.** FORMATS.md is rewritten around the 40 B; the caveat on every
`--budget` figure is gone; EasyFind extracts; **the whole corpus fits a 1 MB
Mac Plus, on the machine**; the 2026-08-30 withdrawn-claim row in BLOCKERS.md,
which had recorded a true claim as false, says so; OPEN_ITEMS.md's overlay
note no longer says archives are out of reach.

**Read every "the Mac needs more" for the instrument it is really about.**
Here there were two, neither the Mac; the 33 KB judged worth more than every
code change was worth nothing, against eighteen days of caveats.

## 2026-09-19 (three bytes hold a position) — the transform vector at three bytes an entry, and the price it was allowed to have

**Claim (measured).** Arsenic's inverse-BWT vector — the engine's largest
single allocation, one entry per byte of a block up to 512 KB — is three
bytes an entry instead of four. A block is `1 << (4 stream bits + 9)`, at
most 2^24 bytes, so three bytes hold any position; the sampled index's
`pos[]` made this argument on 2026-08-24. Two byte-wise accessors,
`ars_transform_get` / `ars_transform_put`, hold the width.

**What it buys.** The fast path costs `~30 KB + block + 3 × fill` instead
of `4 × fill`. Over the 31 StuffIt 5 fixtures at the 1 MB budget of
648,100 B: nineteen already on the vector peak 16-20 % lower; two —
`derived-Troi-ClipSave-Plug-in1.1.sit` (531,968 B) and
`derived-AuthoRize_2.0.sit` (612,943 B) — move off the sampled index (whose
walk costs 1.37-1.78× the vector's on a Mac Plus at a low rung); ten stay on
the index, their blocks wanting 1.4-2.1 MB at any width. Corpus peaks: min
0.13 / median 0.47 / mean 0.74 / max 2.03 MB, from 0.15 / 0.58 / 0.92 /
2.53. All 31 verify against their internal CRC-32 at unlimited budget, at
648,100 B and under the 400 KB cap (24 of 31 fully, unchanged). The six
bisected minimums do not move: a minimum is a rung of the index.

**What it costs, more than the review said.** Three byte loads and two
shifts replace one long load per output byte: **+4.4 % of instructions on
`derived-Library_ISBN_Barcoder.sit` and +1.9 % on
`derived-a2basic.dmg.sit`**, Linux, fast path only. The review's 2.4 % was
the read's share of one profile, not the change's whole-run delta. On a
Mac Plus the read is a few tens of cycles against ~20,000 a byte for the
arithmetic decoder (542 s for 205,019 bytes), so well under 1 % is
expected there — unmeasured, no tick run. +36 B of 68000 code, −4 B of A5.

**Why it was taken.** The cost lands only where the vector fits, i.e. with
memory to spare; the gain lands on the 1 MB floor and the 512 KB tier,
where every kilobyte of headroom is an archive. An archive that opens beats
one that opens sooner; the maintainer chose it with the number in front of
them. **Not a speed fix for the large Arsenic archives**: the ten that take
twelve to twenty-four minutes on a 1 MB Mac Plus are limited by the block
size the compressor chose.

---

## 2026-09-19 (the seventh that was measured) — `UNC_HOT` on Compact Pro, priced in ticks before it was bought

**Claim (measured).** `unc_cpt_lzh_fork` and `cpt_rle_push` carry
`UNC_HOT`, and a Compact Pro extraction on a 7 MHz Mac Plus is **14.8 %
shorter**: engine 10,256 → 8,735 ticks over `derived-XferIt_1.5b4.sea`,
whole run 10,409 → 8,884, File Manager unchanged at ~150 ticks. +1,028 B of
68000 code, A5 unchanged. DiskDoubler method 8 runs the same two functions.

**Why these two.** Callgrind (2026-09-18) put 37 % of the run in the LZH
loop and 30 % in the RLE push, an out-of-line call per output byte; the
`UNC_HOT` list had been measured on one StuffIt archive, the limit the
2026-08-30 entry named. First format added since.

**Priced first.** The size flags were kept at 780 B for 0.82 % and the six
original marks bought 25 % for 1,024 B; a kilobyte is about a sixth of an
archive at the corpus's headroom density. The maintainer decided on two
tick counts (baseline and trial, twelve minutes, trial reverted before
asking), not an estimate.

**Not claimed.** That the tiers were re-run (the differential suite covers
the path on Linux at the same optimisation level — the point of marking
functions, not files). Nor that Now Compress should follow: its three hot
functions cost 1,152 B and its history slide is the larger lever.

## 2026-09-19 (the slide that ran every block) — Now Compress's block slots, and the `UNC_HOT` that bought nothing

**Claim (measured).** Now Compress decodes into a buffer of history plus
room for four blocks, each block directly after the last, and slides the
window only when the next block would not fit. It used to slide after
every block — the last 32 KB copied byte by byte, and a block's output is
at most 32 KB, so one byte copied per byte produced: 19 % of
`derived-SyntheticReferences2.0.sea` on Linux (callgrind, 2026-09-18).

| | Linux Ir | Mac Plus engine ticks |
|---|---|---|
| `derived-SyntheticReferences2.0.sea` | −15.2 % | not run: 9.9 MB out, half an hour at 7 MHz |
| `derived-Expand_Now_1.0.1.sea` | −12.7 % | **945 → 793, −16.1 %** |

+32 B of 68000 code. The three Now Compress fixtures are byte-exact and
`tools/run_now.py`'s thirteen generated archives grade the two things this
could break: a block whose history is the previous stream's last 32 KB
(`dict`), and a back-reference into history. The decoder's reach limit is
the block's own history, so a corrupt offset is refused where it was.

**Memory.** The buffer is the only per-archive allocation. Four slots ask
235,568 B; on refusal two ask 170,032 B, then one asks 137,264 B — the old
request — so the set of archives that open is unchanged on every tier; the
512 KB tier's 186 KB budget lands on two slots. The slot count is decided
once per archive. The refused first attempts never reach the shell's "Needs
NK more" (shown only when an entry failed, M46).

**The `UNC_HOT` marks bought nothing (measured).** `now_newlzss`,
`now_next_block`, `now_fork` at -O3: 793 → 795 ticks, +0.3 %, for
+1,152 B. Not taken. The review had ranked them beside Compact Pro's on the
same profile shape; the tick probe separated them in six minutes. A
byte-copy loop is the one thing `-Os` compiles as well as `-O3`, and a copy
that runs once per block is the one thing the optimiser cannot make rarer —
the 2026-08-30 rule (a result on one file is about that file) applied in
the other direction.

## 2026-09-19 (the transient tables) — 6 KB of cipher tables built at key setup, and a bit convention fitted rather than transcribed

*(Corrected later the same day: there is one DES SP table, not two — see
*the DES that was only wearing a disguise*. The A5 figure stands.)*

**Claim (measured).** The two DES SP tables and Compact Pro's CRC-64 table
— 2,048 B each, `const`, so in the A5 world every extraction pays for — are
built when a cipher is keyed, into a 2 KB heap block the host frees with its
buffers. Resident instead: the eight S boxes as 512 B and the inverted P
permutation as 32. Mac build **−5,588 B of A5, +756 B of code, net −4,832 B
of budget**; the heap sees 2 KB more only while a PMa6, encrypted StuffIt
classic or encrypted Compact Pro entry is decoded (none in the corpus;
their peaks sit at 9 to 76 KB). No disk is touched, which separates it from
the parked overlay (2026-08-31). A5 ratchet lowered.

**The estimate was 300 B of code and it is 756** (two S-box conventions, a
CRC loop, an allocate-on-first-use wrapper, six `unc_crypt_init` calls);
the review's "about 5.5 KB back" is 4.8.

**The part that needed proving.** StuffIt's table was XADMaster's
`DES_SPtrans`, verbatim — a little-endian DES whose bit order the reference
never states. Rather than transcribe it, the convention was FITTED: every
permutation of the six index bits against three output-bit rules, over all
512 entries. One fits: E-expansion bits in order, bit 0 first, and output
bit k at word bit (k − 1 + 3) mod 32 — the rotate-by-3 `sitdes_crypt`
undoes at block end. `tools/gen_crypt_tables.py` asserts the derivation
against the verbatim table on every regeneration; the DES known-answer test
and Compact Pro vectors grade the C builders, `tools/run_crypt.py`'s 35
cases the ciphers end to end, and the three StuffIt Deluxe archives (8-, 9-
and 17-character passwords) would fail to open if it were wrong. A
derivation checked against the reference at generation and the format at
test time beats a transcription nobody re-checks.

**Not claimed.** Any speed change (512 word writes per encrypted entry,
nothing in the corpus reaches it). The Mac tiers were not re-run.

## 2026-09-19 (the tree that was Yoshizaki's) — the -lh1- coder rebuilt on the published LZHUF, measured against MacMount's, and what it bought on three axes

**Claim (measured).** `src/unc_lzah.c`'s adaptive Huffman tree follows the
published LZHUF (Yoshizaki 1988, Okumura's comments 1989) rather than
XADMaster's `XADLZHDynamicHandle.m`, and every format on it — StuffIt
method 5, LZH -lh1-, ARC 7.x Trimmed, DART's "best" — is faster, smaller
and lighter. (DART left the engine 2026-09-25: DECISIONS.md 2026-09-25,
*the disk images that found another home*.)

| | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test1-best` on a 7 MHz Mac Plus, engine ticks | 18,585 | 16,700 | **−10.1 %** |
| `test1-best`, Linux Ir | 152,236,871 | 124,321,840 | −18.3 % |
| A/UX 1.4 MB boot disk, Linux Ir | 458,688,059 | 363,420,205 | −20.8 % |
| `lhasa-maclha-l2_lh1.lzh`, Linux Ir | 3,007,375 | 2,683,432 | −10.8 % |
| `derived-DEF.sit` (method 5), Linux Ir | 5,645,125 | 4,749,371 | −15.9 % |
| working state per decode | 15,568 B | 9,000 B | −6,568 B |
| `unc_lzah.c.obj`, 68000 -Os | 1,592 B | 1,478 B | −114 B |
| the application's `CODE` | 151,684 B | 151,572 B | −112 B |

Same output everywhere: 932/932, DART 37/37, ARC 7 4/4, 782 unit checks,
and byte for byte MacMount's raw volumes on four real archives.

**Where it came from.** MacMount's parked DART work: its `src/mm_lzhuf.c`,
written from the published program (MacMount is 0BSD), was 22–24 % fewer
Linux instructions in 9,024 B of state. The difference is structural: LZHUF
keeps three arrays (counts sorted in place, sons, parents) and swaps a node
with the neighbour it overtakes; XADMaster keeps six node arrays plus a rank
list and its inverse, and decodes the offset's high bits through a canonical
table where LZHUF looks up eight bits. Only the tree and lookup were taken;
the three modes, XADMaster's window preload (DECISIONS.md 2026-08-23), the
inline bit reader and the run-based output stay.

**Linux promised 18–24 %, the Plus delivered 10.1 %**: the 68000's bit
reader and window copy, unchanged, are a larger share of a symbol there.
The proxy ranks, the machine prices.

**Provenance.** LZHUF.C has no copyright notice or licence; deark's
`readme-lzhuf.txt` cites Russell Marks's 2001 reconstruction of the authors'
intent — "use, distribute, and modify this program freely" — the basis deark
ships it on and now this engine. NOTICE says exactly that, not MacMount's
firmer "released by its authors". MacExtract's licence does not change
(XADMaster is transcribed in twenty other places).

**The second reader.** MacMount's decoder refuses a match past the block end
and whole leftover bytes in a block's stream, which this one (like
XADMaster) tolerates; 192 blocks never exercised either. It drops sector
tags, so `random_t`'s random tags are checked here, not there.

**Not done then.** MacMount's two A/UX disks expand byte-exact but were not
pinned into `tools/run_dart.py`. *Done 2026-09-20 (the checksums that came
with the disks).*

## 2026-09-19 (the DES that was only wearing a disguise) — StuffItDES folded onto standard DES's round, and the half of the hypothesis that was false

**Claim (measured).** StuffItDES is standard DES's round function with no
IP and no FP, keyed by its own schedule. `src/unc_crypt.c` runs both DES
ciphers through one `des_core` and one SP table kind; `revbits`,
`sitdes_round` and `CRYPT_TAB_SITDES` are gone.

| axis | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tools/run_crypt.py` | 35/35 | 35/35 | 0 problems, and the three archives StuffIt Deluxe 3.5.1 wrote are three of them |
| unit tests | 782 checks | 782 checks | including the `openssl enc -des-ecb` vector, which grades `des_core` from the other side |
| Mac `CODE` | 151,572 B | **151,156 B** | −416 B, all of it `unc_crypt.c.obj` (9,676 → 9,260) |
| Mac A5 | 38,668 B | 38,668 B | unchanged: one 2 KB table was already transient |
| peak heap, encrypted `.sit` | 8,192 B | 8,192 B | `t --stats` on a `synth_crypt.py` archive, both binaries |

**The hypothesis was two claims and one held.** "Standard DES around a
permutation" — the key half is **false, cheaply**: `sitdes_setkey` reads all
64 key bits where PC-1 drops eight, so no key permutation maps one schedule
to the other; counting bits settles it without searching for one. The
nibble schedule stays, graded by the three real archives.

**The block half holds.** Machine-checked by `tools/fit_sitdes.py`:
`DES_SPtrans[b][v]` is `ROL(REV(SP[b][rev6(v)]), 3)` for all 512 entries;
with the state in standard layout the subkeys are plain six-bit groups of
the nibble schedule (group 2g is `s1`'s lane 3−g, 2g+1 is `s0`'s) — what the
bit reversal had been undoing — and the rotate-by-3 at both block ends was
the same relabelling, so both go. The tool also A/Bs both formulations over
20,000 random key/block pairs and every single-bit key × single-bit block,
both directions: no disagreement. `tools/gen_crypt_tables.py` now asserts
the relabelling against XADMaster's verbatim table on every regeneration.
Two redundant key setups also went: `unc_crypt_sit` derived the folded
archive key's schedule four times; once now.

**Shown to fail first.** One nibble index moved by one in `sitdes_setkey`
(`i + 14` → `i + 15`) takes `run_crypt.py` from 0 problems to 24, including
all three Deluxe archives.

**Not claimed.** Any speed change (unmeasured; no corpus fixture is
encrypted). Mac tiers not re-run — no decode path changed, code is smaller.
The licence does not move: `unc_crypt.c` still owes XADMaster the nibble
schedule and key derivation. OPEN_ITEMS.md's row said the variant "can be
standard DES plus a permutation": the first clause is now spent, the second
was the false half.

**Claim (measured).** `src/sit_arsenic.c` is written from Matthew T.
Russotto's description of the format rather than from XADMaster's handle,
and on a 7 MHz Mac Plus `derived-a2basic.dmg.sit` decodes in **315 s where

|---|---|---|---|
| a2basic, Plus engine ticks | 29,885 | 18,922 | **−36.7 %** |
| KeyGraphics, Plus engine ticks | 933 | 902 | −3.3 % |
| a2basic, 68000 instructions (qemu-m68k, shipped flags) | 269.6 M | 162.0 M | −39.9 % |
| ISBN, 68000 instructions | 287.9 M | 243.9 M | −15.3 % |
| KeyGraphics, 68000 instructions | 8.14 M | 7.74 M | −4.9 % |
| a2basic / ISBN / KeyGraphics, Linux Ir | | | −10.9 / +1.6 / +1.6 % |
| corpus peaks, min / median / max | 132,624 / 496,200 / 2,129,848 | 131,356 / 494,932 / 2,128,580 | −1.3 KB |
| fully extracted at 400 KB | 24 of 31 | 24 of 31 | |
| the application's `CODE` | 151,572 B | 152,060 B | +488 B |

31/31 byte-exact at unlimited budget, at 648,100 B and under the 400 KB
cap; `ci.sh` green including the forced-sampled variant.

**The instrument came first, and it is the transferable part.** Every

(`-Os -mcpu=68000 -fno-tree-loop-distribute-patterns
-freorder-blocks-algorithm=simple -fipa-icf`) under `qemu-m68k -d
exec,nochain,in_asm`, the trace summed per function and block by
`tools/m68kprof.py`. Instructions, not cycles — but 68000 instructions,
libgcc helpers and byte loops counted as what they are. Of a2basic:
**34.5 % in the MTF's byte-at-a-time shift** (ranks near 128 on an archive
that barely compresses), **27 % in the linear symbol search**, 5 % in
divisions. Callgrind had shown the MTF as nothing: x86 inlines that shift
into a block move.

**The two structures**, both choices the format leaves free:

- **bzip2's two-level move-to-front**: sixteen lists of sixteen in a 2 KB
  array growing downward, re-spaced every ~1,800 symbols; at most sixteen
  moves plus one per list. From the idea in Seward's `decompress.c`
  (BSD-style); same permutation as a flat table.
- **A grouped symbol search**: a sum per sixteen frequencies; walk the group
  sums, then one group. Bump adds to one sum; halving rebuilds them.

**What the write-up says obliquely and the fixtures said loudly.** 17 of 31
fixtures failed the first build "corrupt": `renorm` is rounded down, so
`frequency = code / renorm` can reach the model's total, and the format's
answer is the LAST symbol. The linear walk fell through to it; the grouped
walk had to stop at the last non-empty group. The write-up notes the
rounding as the difference from MACM but not what a decoder must do.

**Not claimed.** Clean-room (the author had read the XADMaster
transcription). That the 1 MB sampled path was re-timed (a 12-minute run at
1x). That the Mac timing table's two Arsenic rows (screenshot clock) are
current.

**Memory.** The first build's 4 KB MTF array and 128 frequencies per model
wasted 4.6 KB; the peak rose 4.2 KB and one fixture fell out at 400 KB. A
2 KB array and one pool of exactly 267 frequencies put it back, 1.3 KB under
the XADMaster form.
