## 2026-09-19 (the byte that went to two places at once) — Compact Pro's LZH and RLE stages fused, −31.7 % on a Mac Plus for +76 B

**Claim (measured).** Compact Pro's LZ match writes each byte into the
window and the writer's staging buffer from one register instead of a call
per byte, and run-length expansion is written as a run.

| | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| XferIt, Plus engine ticks | 8,735 | 5,970 | **−31.7 %** |
| XferIt, Plus whole run | 8,885 | 6,107 | −31.3 % |
| Guy's Mac Consultants, Plus engine ticks | 3,536 | 2,318 | **−34.4 %** |
| XferIt, 68000 instructions (qemu-m68k, shipped flags) | 82,825,986 | 55,513,387 | −33.0 % |
| Guy's, 68000 instructions | 32,473,326 | 21,638,415 | −33.4 % |
| XferIt / Guy's, Linux `Ir` | 76.6 M / 29.3 M | 52.2 M / 18.9 M | −31.9 / −35.7 % |
| `ddtf-dd377ddb.dd`, DiskDoubler method 8, `Ir` | 4,771,312 | 2,527,660 | **−47.0 %** |
| `derived-Terrainman_2.0__.sea`, DiskDoubler `DDn`, the control | 31,212,483 | 31,212,458 | −0.0 % |
| peak heap, every one of the 245 Compact Pro and DiskDoubler fixtures | | | **identical** |
| the application's `CODE` | 151,644 B | 151,720 B | +76 B |
| A5 world (data + bss) | 38,660 B | 38,648 B | −12 B |

(`derived-Guy_s_Mac_Consultants.cpt`: over half its output comes from the
RLE half.) `ci.sh` green; old and new engines identical in exit code,
message and every byte over 945 fixtures and 560 truncated and bit-flipped
Compact Pro / DiskDoubler variants. One token changed in the new loop
(`CPT_ESC1` → `CPT_ESC2`) gives 82 mismatches. Speed only: `fmt_cpt.c`
still owes XADMaster and macutils (OPEN_ITEMS.md, *What is still
XADMaster's*).

**Where the time was.** `tools/m68kprof.py`: 25.6 % inside `cpt_rle_push`
(the call, its sticky-error test and switch alone 13.8 % of the run) and
20 % in the match's byte loop. The RLE stage is the IDENTITY for every byte
that is neither the escape nor inside an escape sequence, so a match is a
copy that stops at the first 0x81:

    do { b = *s++; *w++ = b; if (b == CPT_ESC1) break; *d++ = b; }
    while (s < send);

with each piece bounded (match, both window ends, output owed, staging
buffer) before the loop rather than inside it.

**Three measurements, each cost a round:**

- **Indexing is not addressing.** One index (`s[i]`, `w[i]`, `d[i]`) is ONE
  instruction shorter and about 45 % dearer: `(An)+` reads in 8 cycles, an
  indexed mode in 14. `m68kprof` prefers it; the tick probe is right. Do not
  let an instruction count arbitrate between addressing modes.
- **Splitting the source run as well LOST**: 6 instructions a byte down to
  5, but the extra clip is per MATCH and the average match is eight bytes.
  +0.6 M instructions, reverted.
- **`cpt_rle_push` had to go out of line.** With the run fill inside it, it
  stopped being inlined and the LZ loop got 4.1 % SLOWER (one more live
  value spills the output cursor; two instructions per byte). Marked
  `UNC_NOINLINE` (new in `unc_internal.h`). On this target an inliner
  decision is a performance decision; take it rather than let it move.

**A bulk-fill threshold is not worth having (measured).** `CPT_RUN_BULK` of
4: 0.1 % either way, 244 B of code; removed. It first went in half-removed
(constant at 1, comment describing a crossover it no longer implemented);
the second commit fixed that, 16 B back.

**A swallowed write error — hardening, labelled as such.** Two arms of
`cpt_rle_push` returned `r->err`, set only by the closing flush, so a failed
write returned UNC_OK. `cpt_rle_emit` now sets it (−8 B code, +8 B A5). No
reachable case changes an outcome: both arms stage another byte, so the
closing flush fails again; only a sink that failed once then succeeded
would have lost it.

**Not claimed.** Tiers re-run (no shell or allocation change). Plain-RLE
forks faster (one-byte fast path only; the corpus's largest is 3,897 B).
Any `--budget` change: the peak is identical on every fixture.

## 2026-09-19 (the buffer that became a length) — LZW from the public compress(1), and the array that was hiding 17.8 %

**Item 5 of the shedding list, predicted neutral** ("the chain walk is
already tight", OPEN_ITEMS.md). The walk was; the array it walked into was
not, and only writing from a description made that visible.

**Source.** `reference/deark/src/fmtutil-lzw.c` (Jason Summers, MIT) fully
describes the compress(1) stream: clear code, width growth, and the padding
rule (codes go eight at a time at one width, so a width change mid-group
discards the rest — `delzw_unixcompress_end_bitgroup`; XADMaster's comment
is "God damn, this is dumb"). Algorithm: Welch's. `LZW.c` and
`XADCompressHandle.m` are no longer sources of `src/unc_lzw.c` (NOTICE).

**What the rewrite found.** A string is stored backwards (`chr[s]` last
byte, `parent[s]` the rest); the old decoder staged it reversed in a
`capsymbols`-byte array and copied it out. On `popper-1.7.tar.Z` that copy
was **1,212,620 of 6,832,171 instructions, 17.8 %**, existing only because
the length is unknown until the walk ends.

**So store the length.** `len[sym]` takes the staging array's byte per
symbol (allocation still `cap * 4`: `parent` 2 + `chr` 1 + `len` 1), and the
walk writes into the caller's buffer from the far end. For that byte to be
free:

- **One byte saturates at 255**; `lzw_strlen` walks UP the parents until one
  did not saturate — length−254 steps.
- **The new entry needs the string's FIRST byte**: the last byte the walk
  stores; for a self-defining code, the previous string's first byte,
  already in hand.
- **A string longer than the caller's buffer** is re-walked skipping what
  was handed over — quadratic in pieces, so measured: ARC reads LZW through
  a 64-byte buffer and splits 46 of `synth-arc-mixed.arc`'s 740 codes
  (still −1.7 % on Linux); popper splits 16 of 33,612.

| | old | new | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `popper-1.7.tar.Z`, Mac Plus engine ticks | 713 | 646 | **−9.4 %** |
| `derived-xmasbeeps.sit`, Mac Plus engine ticks | 2,850 | 2,801 | **−1.7 %** |
| `popper-1.7.tar.Z`, Linux Ir | 6,832,171 | 5,260,173 | −23.0 % |
| `a2ps.V4.3.tar.Z`, Linux Ir | 3,413,007 | 2,767,512 | −18.9 % |
| `ddtf-dd377dda-testfile.TIF` (DiskDoubler 1), Linux Ir | 2,581,333 | 2,133,022 | −17.4 % |
| `derived-xmasbeeps.sit`, Linux Ir | 26,689,757 | 23,452,283 | −12.1 % |
| `derived-EmpireBuilderDemo.sit`, Linux Ir | 28,397,076 | 25,924,370 | −8.7 % |
| `synth-arc-mixed.arc`, Linux Ir | 1,926,042 | 1,893,798 | −1.7 % |
| `CODE` | 151,836 | 151,976 | +140 B |
| A5 | 38,660 | 38,648 | **−12 B** |
| peak heap, all 113 LZW fixtures | — | — | identical, to the byte |

**The Mac got a fraction of what Linux promised — the transferable part.**
−23.0 % of x86 instructions is −9.4 % of Plus ticks; −12.1 % is −1.7 %. The
rewrite removed a byte copy with two pointer increments, about the cheapest
thing a 68000 does; what remains is two indexed loads per byte, about the
dearest. The overstatement was ~2x for `-lh1-`, here 2.4x and 7x: not a
factor to carry in one's head. The Linux count RANKS a change, the tick
probe PRICES it.

**One shape refused, one taken against the Linux number.** One pending
counter instead of two: 40 B code to save 8 B A5 — refused. Folding the two
`lzw_strlen` call sites and turning the continuation loop into an `if` (it
can only run once) gave **128 B back for 1.5 to 3.0 % of Linux
instructions**; on the Plus **−4 ticks on popper and +6 on xmasbeeps, both
inside the ±0.5 % two runs of one build differ by**. Taken: 128 B on a 1 MB
machine is a measurement; 1.5 % of x86 instructions is not.

**A fixture list from what a format CAN use is not what a file DOES use.**
The brief named `arc2pak1.pak` as "ARC's LZW methods"; instrumenting the
decoder shows it never enters it (Crushed and Distilled). The ARC fixture
that reaches LZW is `synth-arc-mixed.arc`.

**Graded.** `ci.sh` green; old vs new over the **113 fixtures that reach
the LZW decoder** (found by instrumenting, not by extension): identical exit
code, messages, bytes and peak heap. Three one-token mutations gave **113,
113 and 111** mismatches.

**The path no archive reaches.** The longest string in the corpus is **223
bytes**, so `lzw_strlen`'s resolving walk never runs in a shipped build.
`ci.sh` builds a variant at `UNC_LZW_LEN_MAX=4`, byte-exact on all 113;
breaking the walk by one token changes **nothing at 255 and 112 of 113 at
4**.

**The canonical Huffman half, and a bug that came with the reference.**
`unc_canon_build_ext` / `unc_canon_decode` now follow RFC 1951 3.2.2 and
puff.c (Mark Adler, zlib licence) rather than `XADPrefixCode.m` and
macutils' `cpt.c`; puff.c states that an INCOMPLETE code set is legal with a
defined meaning, not a Compact Pro quirk. Byte-identical on the corpus,
**0.00 % on Linux** on four users (Compact Pro, `-lh7-`, Now Compress,
StuffIt); −4 B code, −20 B A5 (the over-subscription check carries code
space LEFT as a counter). Transcribed as-is it would have been a defect:
puff.c's signed `int` counter is safe at `MAXBITS` 15 and undefined at this
file's `UNC_CANON_MAX_BITS` of **31** (two length-31 symbols reach
`1 << 31`). The corpus goes no deeper than 18 bits, so 944 agreeing fixtures
said nothing; the boundary is a unit test, shown to fail with the signed
form ("left shift of 1073741824 by 1 places cannot be represented in type
'int'"). Now checked before the subtraction, unsigned. **A reference
implementation's constants are part of what it assumes.**

**Not claimed.** Licence movement; the `.Z` header (`fmt_exo.c`, item 6);
clean-room; a re-measured 1 MB budget figure — 648,100 B is still the
2026-08-31 number, and this row takes 160 B of it.

## 2026-09-19 (the facts that were somebody else's to state) — the container parsers re-cited on their own specifications

**Decision.** Seven files cited `reference/XADMaster/<file>` for facts that
are not XADMaster's — an alphabet, a header offset, an entry table — because
it was the only description on this machine. `tools/fetch_references.sh` now
fetches seven public documents into `reference/notes/`, and the sources cite
them:

| file | now cites | for |
|---|---|---|
| `fmt_binhex.c` | Peter N Lewis, "BinHex 4.0 Definition" (1991); RFC 1741 App. A | the alphabet, the banner, the 0x90 RLE, the CRC |
| `fmt_macbinary.c` | MacBinary II Standard (7/24/87); MacBinary III Proposal (1996) | the 128-byte header, the padding, the CRC, `mBIN`, the version procedure |
| `fmt_applesingle.c` | RFC 1740, App. A and B | magics, version, filler, entry table, entry ids, the 2000 epoch |
| `fmt_exo.c` | RFC 1952; APPNOTE.TXT 6.3.10; POSIX.1-2017 `pax`; deark | the gzip header; zip's records, Zip64 and AES; the ustar header block; the `.Z` three-byte header |
| `fmt_zipseg.c` | APPNOTE.TXT 4.3.12, 4.3.16, 8.5 | the (part, offset) pairs and the spanning marker |

The `.Z` header is the one *the buffer that became a length* handed over.

**MEASURED: no code moved.** Release builds (`-O2 -Werror`) of this commit
and its parent give the same sha256 for `macextract` and `unit_tests`.

**Four findings from reading the documents themselves:**

- *RFC 1741 cannot define BinHex*: its Appendix A alphabet has a stray space
  (65 characters). Lewis's document is right and alone states the CRC and
  the zero-count-means-literal rule.
- *A claim in `fmt_zipseg.c` was made false*: "50 4B 07 08 ... no reference
  in this repository documents them" — they are APPNOTE 8.5.3's spanning
  signature. Behaviour unchanged and better argued: 8.5.4 gives a
  one-segment split a different marker (0x30304b50, yet Info-ZIP was
  measured writing 0x08074b50), and 8.5.5 makes the value a data-descriptor
  signature too. Three meanings, so the displacement stays the test.
- *MacBinary I's heuristics were never XADMaster's.* The II standard gives
  the no-checksum test. Of `mb_version`'s four tests three are the
  standard's, two applied differently on purpose (zero from 99 rather than
  101, as 99 is the Get Info comment length nobody implemented;
  `UNC_MAC_MAX` rather than 0x007FFFFF, a 1987 statement about files); only
  the nonzero-date test has no document. Each difference is written at its
  line.
- *`fmt_stubs.c` was not a dead end.* deark (MIT) recognises the StuffIt X
  magic; macutils' `macunpack/dd.h`, cited here for years for other formats,
  states DiskDoubler's older headers (`MAGIC2 "\253\315\000\124"` =
  0xABCD0054; `C_HDRCRC 82` in 84 bytes, `ARCHHDRCRC 76` in 78). A citation
  is not a search. Only Now Compress is XADMaster's entire; `DDA2` is read
  off the CC0 specimens NOTICE credits.

**Still XADMaster's, marked where made:** the MacBinary CRC-16/0xA001
fallback; the nonzero-date test; the byte-swapped AppleSingle header (the
RFC forbids it); the StuffIt split header in `fmt_sitseg.c` (unpublished,
read by neither deark nor macutils); Now Compress in `fmt_stubs.c`.

**Not claimed.** Licence movement (these files carried facts, not code).
Behaviour change. An exhaustive search — only `reference/` (deark, macutils,
lhasa, LHa, mpack, btoa, CiderPress2, XADMaster).

## 2026-09-20 (the checksums that came with the disks) — the two A/UX DART specimens pinned, a peak-RAM table that had gone stale under them, and the `--only` case a stride never reached

*(Superseded for DART: the format left the engine on 2026-09-25 —
DECISIONS.md 2026-09-25, *the disk images that found another home*; the

**Claim (measured).** The two A/UX 3.0.1 floppies Apple's DART 1.5.3
compressed in 1993 became fixtures graded by `ci.sh`:
`AUX301_ReadMe_MacSE.dart` (381,699 B, 800K, 40 slots) and

72-slot archive this project has held). `tools/run_dart.py` went from 37 to
53 cases; six synthetic cases no longer needed `reference/ciderpress2`.

**The oracle came with the disks.** OPEN_ITEMS.md asked for MacMount's
derived Disk Copy 4.2 checksums; both members carry Apple's own in a
411-byte resource fork ('CKSM' 1 tags, 'CKSM' 2 data, and a 'DART' 0 string:
*"1.5, tag checksum=$AC4AA5C3, data checksum=$E257EF53"*). The data halves
agree with the derived numbers (`E257EF53`, `3DF12BA6`); the addition is the
TAG side, `AC4AA5C3` over 19,200 B of real GCR tags.

**The 72-entry table was checked from the specimen.** Both table lengths
were tried, requiring the one `srcSize` calls for to sum to the file (4 + 2n
+ Σ lengths, 0xFFFF counted as 20,960); a 40-entry reading of the boot disk
falls 407,486 B short. Source: `reference/ciderpress2/DART-notes.md`.

**Unpacked by this engine's own CLI** from a StuffIt on Macintosh Garden's
FTP, graded on the way in against the SHA-256s MacMount pinned from `unar`;
all four members byte-identical. `fixtures/SOURCES.md` names the generator.

**A number that should have moved and did not** (the converse of the
constant-in-a-matrix smell). FORMATS.md's DART table still read
40,301–40,624 B for "best" and 15,568 B for the tree, stale since *the tree
that was Yoshizaki's*. Measured on all seven specimens: 27,967–34,056 B,
each exactly longest chunk + 9,000 + 4,096. The Macintosh row, stale by the
same 6,568 B, was re-run: **PASS at 4 MB and at the 1 MB floor**, 838,484 B
out, peak **33,765 B** (Linux + 32 B allocator overhead). **A format's
numbers live in the format's section, not the coder's**, and nothing checks
that. The new specimens also disproved "between 0 and 474 B" saved by
sizing the input buffer off the block table: the *Read Me* disk's worst
chunk is 14,871 B and saves **6,089**; the hypothesis that mostly empty
disks are where it pays survived.

**A sampling stride shifted.** `tools/run_only.py` sweeps every SIXTEENTH
fixture by name; two new files moved the stride and the sample found
`compact-pro-151.hqx`, whose comment `--only` had never met in three weeks.

absent under `--no-comment`, not selectable — each checked by mutation. The
comment's name is discovered, not guessed (it follows the archive inside
the BinHex). **A sweep of every Nth fixture by name can only meet a
property, never cover one**, and adding a fixture reshuffles what several
suites see.

**Not claimed.** Any `src/` change. That a Macintosh expanded either A/UX

## 2026-09-20 (the character that was touched three times) — BinHex's line read, judged and decoded in one pass, and four characters at once

**Item 1 of CURRENT_WORK.md**, from a 68000 profile of
`macburger-helper.hqx` (`bh_get_bits` 41 %, `bh_next` 29 %); 204 of 946
fixtures are `.hqx`.

**The per-BLOCK profile found the larger half.** `bh_refill_line`, inlined
into `bh_get_bits` and invisible by function, was 8.77 M of 34.6 M
instructions, **25 %**, plus 9.7 % in the inlined `unc_bufin_next`; the
6-bit fetch proper 15.6 %. Each character was touched three times: copied
into `line[]` by a call, scanned to judge the line, looked up again for its
six bits.

**Now.** The line is usually already in the reader's buffer, so one scan
for the terminator takes it (`unc_bufin_span` / `unc_bufin_drop`, used only
here). The judging pass also CONVERTS: `line[]` holds 6-bit values and 0xFE
for ':'. Two touches, no call per character. The trim cannot fuse into the
copy: hexbin trims trailing whitespace before judging, and the alphabet
omitting the space is load-bearing (`fmt_binhex.c`, `bh_refill_line`), so
trim still runs on characters between scan and conversion; rule unchanged.

**The 4:3 group.** Four values on the line, none the terminator (one test on
their OR) → three bytes at once. A line is 64 characters, so all but a
line's last group take it; the rest use the unchanged byte path. Serving the
two extra bytes via a pointer pair (`bp`, `bend`) instead of extending
`phase` costs 24 B more code and is **−4.0 %** of the run (23,126,796 →
22,209,542); taken.

| | old | new | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `macburger-helper.hqx`, Mac Plus engine ticks | 3,771 | **2,386** | **−36.7 %** |
| `macburger-helper.hqx`, 68000 instructions | 34,609,457 | 22,209,542 | −35.8 % |
| `a2basic-09.hqx`, 68000 instructions | 22,963,608 | 14,508,403 | −36.8 % |
| `CODE` | 151,976 | 152,216 | +240 B |
| A5 | 38,648 | 38,664 | +16 B |
| peak heap, `macburger-helper.hqx` on the Mac | 8,208 B | 8,208 B | identical |

**Count and ticks agreed to one point**, where they disagreed 2.4x and 7x on
*the buffer that became a length*: that removed a byte copy, this removes
calls, bounds tests and indexed loads, which both price alike. The rule
stands: the profile RANKS, the probe PRICES. **The A5 growth is not a
table**: `fmt_binhex.c.obj` has no data; the 16 B is rodata alignment, as on
2026-09-19.

**A defect only the old-vs-new diff caught.** The first draft left `n` at
the terminator scan's count when falling through, so a line straddling a
refill was appended after a copy of itself: 203 of 204 `.hqx` fixtures
failed CRC — found because the old binary's output was diffed over every
fixture of the format. The 4 KB buffer fires that path about once per 64
lines; a smaller corpus or exit-status grading would have shipped it.

## 2026-09-20 (the row that was not the archive) — one harness's fix, another harness's silent wrong answer

**Claim (measured).** Since 2026-08-30 the yardstick had been extracting
the Finder's `Desktop` file instead of the archive, for any fixture whose
name sorts after it.

**Evidence.** `expander.py` clicked Standard File's first row and pressed
Return. On 2026-08-30 `mkboot.py` stopped deleting `Desktop` (*the Desktop
file the password phase needed*, BLOCKERS.md); that file is **invisible to
`hdir`** and **visible in our dialog**, which filters nothing, so it took row
one: `macburger-helper.hqx` and `unshar-111.hqx` reported *"This file could
not be extracted"* three seconds in, photographed.

**Consequence.** The file is named by type-ahead, and the frame showing the
selected row is photographed before Return. `unshar-111.hqx`: 3 s and
nothing → 60 s and ten files; `macburger-helper.hqx` → 250 s and 312 files,
19 s under FORMATS.md's 269 s row — what that day's BinHex work takes off the
chain's first layer, measured separately. The two published rows sort
BEFORE `Desktop` ("der" < "Des"), which is why three weeks did not meet this.

**Transferable.** A harness that addresses anything by POSITION measures
whatever is there, and what moved it was a correct, documented change to a
DIFFERENT harness. It was findable only because the failure had a
photograph behind a seconds column that looked like a measurement. **A
harness that prints what it produced can be caught lying; one that prints
only a number cannot.**

**Not claimed.** That the 2026-08-29 figures were wrong (269 s and 312 files
then, the day before `Desktop` came back). Nothing else used this instrument
between the dates. Expander's column is untouched: its dialog lists only

## 2026-09-20 (the window that was already the staging buffer) — method 13's per-byte put, and the call that was never inlined

**Item 2 of CURRENT_WORK.md.** The plan — flush runs through
`unc_fork_write` instead of `unc_fork_put` per byte — nearly died on
reading: `unc_fork_write` **is a byte loop over `unc_fork_put`** (chunking
was measured 100 B bigger on 2026-09-18).

**What makes it pay is where the loop is.** `unc_fork_put` is `static
inline` but calls `unc_fork_flush`, so at `-Os` gcc emits it once, out of
line: 10 instructions plus `jsr`/`rts`, **13.6 % of a method-13 run**.
Inside `unc_fork_write`, in the defining translation unit, it IS inlined.
Profile: `unc_fork_write` 5,505,711 instructions where `unc_fork_put` cost
5,504,604; the saving is all in `unc_sit_decode_fork`, 13,889,602 →
9,206,094.

**The window is the staging buffer**, so a run costs no memory: a second
cursor `flushed`, and one `sit13_flush` at the head of the decode loop when
`pos - flushed` reaches a quarter of the window, plus one at the end. A
quarter because one iteration adds at most 32,832 bytes (the 0x13f escape,
15 bits plus 65): 16,383 + 32,832 = 49,215 worst case, inside 65,536. Below
64 KB the window is at least `outlen` (*sit13_winsize*), so `pos` never
wraps.

| | old | new | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `derived-Ultimate_Copland_1.1.sit.1`, Mac Plus engine ticks | 4,395 | **3,867** | **−12.0 %** |
| the same, 68000 instructions | 40,451,161 | 35,769,616 | −11.6 % |
| `CODE` | 152,216 | 152,356 | +140 B |
| A5 | 38,664 | 38,652 | **−12 B** |
| peak heap, the same fixture on the Mac | 81,226 B | 81,226 B | identical |
| the whole corpus, old binary vs new | — | — | **948 fixtures, 0 differences** |

**The wall clock did not move** (140.4 s → 140.5 s): the autotest build
CRC-reads both forks back afterwards, and that is most of it. Engine ticks
are the measurement; `run.py`'s seconds are not, for this build.

## 2026-09-20 (what a helper call costs that its count does not say) — Arsenic's two products, and a count that understated the clock by 3.6x

**Item 3 of CURRENT_WORK.md; better on every axis.** `renorm * low` and
`renorm * freq[n]`, the arithmetic coder's inner products, went through
libgcc's `__mulsi3` (no 32x32 multiply on a 68000). A model's `total` never
passes its `limit` by more than one increment (`ars_model_bump`), so limits
of 256 and 1,024 make `low` and `freq[n]` **11-bit numbers**; only `renorm`
(`ARS_NUMBITS` wide `range`) needs 32. Two 16x16 `mulu.w` products and a
shift are exact: the true product is at most `range`, under 2^25, so the
bits shifted off are zero; unsigned throughout.

**Seen, not assumed.** `objdump -dr`: `__mulsi3` relocations 3 → 2 (the
remaining two in `ars_model_reset` and model setup, once per entry);
`muluw` 2 → 6. That check is why the cast is on both operands.

| | old | new | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `derived-a2basic.dmg.sit` at 4 MB, Mac Plus engine ticks | 18,916 | **17,002** | **−10.1 %** |
| the same, wall clock for the run | 341 s | 321 s | (±one 20 s poll) |
| the same, 68000 instructions | 161,955,101 | 157,445,238 | **−2.78 %** |
| `derived-KeyGraphics.sit`, 68000 instructions | 7,738,377 | 7,598,077 | −1.8 % |

| A5 | 38,652 | **38,640** | **−12 B** |

**−2.78 % of the count bought −10.1 % of the clock: 3.6x**, the first time
a libgcc helper's understatement was measured — and the OPPOSITE direction
from the LZW rewrite (−23.0 % of x86 count, −9.4 % of ticks). The error is
neither a constant nor a sign: a `jsr` into a shift-and-add loop with stack
traffic is not one instruction's worth of machine.

**Not claimed.** The 1 MB sampled path (not re-timed since 2026-09-19; this
is the 4 MB fast path, FORMATS.md, *StuffIt 5 / Arsenic at 1x*). Other

## 2026-09-20 (the tree that could be measured instead) — the serialized Huffman tree, derived from three formats' output rather than rewritten

**Item 11 of CURRENT_WORK.md's Part B, closed without rewriting the
decoder**: the obstacle was never the code. `unc_huffman.c`'s bit-serialized
tree parse (StuffIt method 3, DiskDoubler method 4, PackIt) cited
`XADStuffItHuffmanHandle.m` and macutils' `de_huffman.c`, and the inventory
said "no spec describes it".

**The spec note was cheap.** Try every plausible serialisation at every
offset of a real archive and keep the one whose decode matches the sha256 an
independent oracle recorded for a whole fork. One fork settles it (3,469
bytes of sha256 do not coincide); thirteen across the three formats confirm:

> bits MSB-first; `1` = a leaf and the next 8 bits are its symbol;
> `0` = an internal node, its zero subtree then its one subtree; and
> per output byte, walk from the root, `0` first subtree, `1` second.

`docs/formats/serialized-huffman-tree.md` states it with its evidence;
`tools/derive_huffman_tree.py --grid` re-derives it in about a minute.

**The rewrite is not worth doing, by the project's rule** ("nothing is
rewritten for the licence alone, and nothing is kept unless it is
measured"): the parse is 0.44 % of a run, so a rewrite is neutral at best.
What blocked the row was the SOURCE of the facts, which the note replaces —
as the 2026-09-19 re-citation did for the container parsers, here by
measurement. Two more facts left XADMaster/`pit.c` the same way: DiskDoubler
method 4 writes StuffIt method 3's tree (measured on a container **Salient's
own 1991 expander reads back**), and a PackIt `PMa4` entry codes its 94-byte
header into the same stream as its forks (each entry's name and fork lengths
found in the first 94 bytes).

**The false positive is the transferable part.** A single-leaf tree is nine
bits found almost anywhere and consumes NO bits per symbol, so it "decodes"
any run of one byte; it matched a 700-byte fork of identical bytes at a
meaningless offset and was reported as confirmation until looked at (the
real entry has a 25-leaf tree). **A search over a space finds its
degenerate member, whose match carries no information**;
`derive_huffman_tree.py` refuses them and says why.

**Not claimed.** That `unc_huffman.c` is an independent expression (it is
unchanged; a replacement can now be written from the note by someone who
has not opened it). Licence movement. Compact Pro's canonical 4-bit lengths,
a different mechanism that left this file on 2026-09-19.

## 2026-09-20 (four forks, and the three rules none of them reach) — StuffIt method 8 derived, and the part a derivation could not take

**Item 7 of Part B, by Item 11's template**: derive from the format's own
output, verify against an oracle's bytes, cite the note, leave a decoder
that measures neutral alone.

**What method 8 is.** An LZ coder whose dictionary entries are the
**concatenation of two earlier entries** (previous match + this one) —
Miller and Wegman's 1985 variation, the "MW" in XADMaster's name for it; a
published algorithm. Codes LSB-first, nine bits growing; the caller's byte
count stops it.

**How it was derived.** A decoder over a family of hypotheses, parameters
scored by bytes of the oracle's output reproduced: **all four method-8 forks
in the corpus** byte for byte against `unar`'s sha256, 17,005 bytes down to
1,301 (`tools/derive_stuffit8.py`). A fifth apparent failure,
`BitMapHelp.index`'s 286-byte resource fork, is **method 5**: the oracle
names one method per ENTRY, StuffIt picks per FORK. Explaining the miss made
the evidence stronger — it accounts for the corpus exactly.

**Three rules stay XADMaster's.** Table restart on a code equal to the next
free one, end on a code greater, width capped at 14 bits / 16,385 entries.
**No specimen reaches any of them**: the largest fork stops at 7,347 entries
and 13 bits. Instrumenting for the widest code used is what moved "maximum
14" from asserted (because the shipped code says 14) to unestablished.

**What would close them:** a fork whose dictionary fills. Synthesising one
settles nothing — ours descends from XADMaster and `unar` IS XADMaster; a
second implementation is not an independent one. The row closes at four
fifths.

**Not claimed:** that `sit_mw_fork` is independent expression (unchanged;
a neutral rewrite is recorded, not taken), or that Miller and Wegman's paper
was consulted — the derivation arrived at the rule.

## 2026-09-20 (the encoder that would answer questions) — ARC's header and three coders, derived from archives ARC wrote to order

**Item 9 of Part B; the first row where the format's own program could be
ASKED.** `tools/get_arc.sh` fetches ARC **5.21q**, Howard Chu's UNIX port of
SEA's own — not descended from XADMaster — so derivation became an
experiment with a control.

**Derived**, each against the bytes handed to the encoder, then `unar`'s
sha256 over the corpus (`tools/derive_arc.py`, with and without `--grid`):

- **the member header** — `0x1a`, method, 13 bytes of name, u32 compressed
  size LE, date, time, CRC-16, u32 original size **except method 1, which
  has none**; walked through a real ARC 5, a real PAK and
  `derived-ARCDOS.arc`, an ARC 7 archive `unar` cannot read;
- **RLE90** (method 3, and behind two others);
- **method 4, squeezed** — `u16` count then that many **pairs of `s16`**,
  negative for a leaf holding `-value-1`, symbol 256 ends, LSB-first from
  pair 0;
- **method 8, crunched** — **first byte is the maximum code width**, then
  LSB-first LZW from 9 bits, 256 clears, 257 first assigned, then RLE90;
- **method 9, squashed** — same LZW to 13 bits, no width byte, no RLE90.

**Remainder.** ARC 5.21q will not write methods **5, 6 or 7**; they stay
`XADARCCrunchHandle.m`'s. PAK's **Crushed** did not fall to the LZW grid
(different dictionary organisation) and stays `XADARCCrushHandle.m`'s, the
only reading anywhere.

**Transferable:** a squeezed member's padding bits run off the end of the
file on the LAST member; the derivation raised EOF. Real decoders stop on the
header's size. **A coder with an end-of-stream symbol may still need the
length**, and a derivation reading only mid-archive members won't find out.

**Not claimed:** `src/fmt_arc.c` rewritten (neutral-rewrite rule, as Items 7
and 11); that 5.21q is the original (its value is not descending from
XADMaster); anything on ARC encryption.

## 2026-09-20 (thirty-two of thirty-four) — DiskDoubler's DD coder from its published description, and the two forks that refuse

**Item 6, half.** **`tools/derive_dd.py` reads 32 of the corpus's 34 DDn
forks** from the wiki page alone, byte for byte against the oracle. It has
**no container parser** (the wiki says "see XADDiskDoublerParser.m"): **every
DD block header ends with the XOR of its first twenty-one bytes**, so
scanning for valid headers locates the blocks — a trick for any format whose
blocks self-check.

Five corrections, in `docs/formats/diskdoubler-dd.md`; the two worth
repeating:

- **streams are in the page's order — offset, literal, run length — not the
  header's**, which lists sizes the other way (fails immediately);
- **the window spans blocks**; per-block buffers get every fork over ~12 KB
  wrong — failing *slowly*, the dangerous kind.

**Two forks refuse:** `derived-Terrainman_2.0__.sea`'s 19,240 B and 16,524 B
data forks — method 10, right length, no error, diverging a few hundred bytes
in, all three code tables Kraft-exact; the neighbouring block is perfect. Not
the XADMaster DDn input-bound defect. So `fmt_dd.c` kept its citation: a
transcription can be 94 % right and nobody can tell.

**`ADn` (methods 6 and 9; LZSS over the block, no Huffman): all five AD forks
read**, with one correction — flag bit 0 is set for an UNcompressed block.
Tally **37 of 39 DD and AD forks**.

**Not claimed:** anything about the containers; code changed (`derive_dd.py`
is a probe).
