## 2026-09-21 (the one that had to be asked) — Now Compress's two coders and its blocks, measured off the application

**Item 5, the one row where nothing could be fetched**: no wiki page, spec or
second implementation — `XADNowCompressHandle.m` is the only account.

**So it was asked.** `tools/vmac/nowcompress.py` drives Now Compress under
the emulator over chosen inputs and keeps input beside output (a corpus made
2026-08-16 for another purpose). Four pairs give shape 1 whole:

> a flag byte, eight tokens, bits most significant first; a 1 is a
> literal byte; a 0 is a match of `length - 2` then distance, one byte
> each — unless the length byte is zero, which is an escape, and then
> the token is zero, distance, `length - 2`.

Payload 164 bytes in, a four-byte trailer, and the caller's byte count stops
it (as StuffIt method 8 and ARC squeeze). *Faster* and *Smaller* give
**byte-identical streams** (mode `0x0010` vs `0x003f`); *Archive* mode
**stores** members and compresses the `.sea` around them (49,000 in, 49,000
out).

**The shape of the search is the transferable part.** Five formats fell to
*reading a document and correcting it*; this one to *choosing an input and
looking at what came back*. The tell is whether anybody wrote the format
down — yes five times where the inventory said no.

**Same day: the second coder and the blocks**, from `half.bin` (8,000 random
bytes then 8,000 `'A'`s):

- a **256-symbol Huffman code**, 256 four-bit lengths, found by **Kraft's
  equality** — exactly 1.000000 at one offset only;
- it codes **shape 1's own stream, flag bytes and all** (why symbol 255 is
  shortest in random data: eight literals' flag is `0xff`);
- a **match is two symbols**, `length = (S & 7) + 2`,
  `distance = ((S >> 3) << 8) | D`, length 2 escaping to a third symbol —
  read off ONE match whose distance had to be 4,237: `0x81 0x8d` gives it
  exactly, and length 3;
- a fork is **32,768-byte blocks, each coded its own way** (`mixed.bin`:
  stored then Huffman).

**All eight specimens read** byte for byte, seven **from the fork's own block
table**: eight-byte records from offset 144, u16 offset + u16 mode, ending on
a record whose offset is the fork's size; stored, shape 1 and shape 2 blocks
begin 0, 2 and 1 bytes past it. The two `runs.bin` forks differ **only in the
mode word** (`0x0010` Faster, `0x001f` Smaller): low bits are the user's
setting, **bit `0x20` is the coder** — four data points, and it predicted the
other two forks.

**Left:** the corpus's two archives are not bare forks (one is
self-extracting), so the fork inside the wrapper. `src/fmt_now.c` still cited
XADMaster for all of it. **Two habits did the work:** choosing the input so
literal and match paths are told apart by eye, and Kraft's equality — one
line, three formats' tables found and one guess refuted.

## 2026-09-21 (the two forks that were never about their literals) — DiskDoubler method 10's second form, and 39 of 39

**Claim.** Method 10 has two forms; in the second the coder produces the
fork's **first difference** — `out[i] = out[i-1] + s[i]`, from zero. With
it, `tools/derive_dd.py` reads **39 of the corpus's 39 DD and AD forks** from
the published pages, and `src/fmt_dd.c` no longer cites XADMaster for either
coder — only for the containers, which the wiki punts to that file.

**Evidence.** The two `derived-Terrainman_2.0__.sea` forks, byte for byte. A
literal-substitution trace (feed the true byte at every literal position,
record what the stream carried): **all 5,443 literals of the 19,240-byte fork
were the difference from the previous output byte**; and only **167 of 3,380
matches** copied the right source bytes, all of them under the delta reading
— so it is the whole stream, not a literal filter.

**Why the 2026-09-20 reading looked right.** Its three measurements all hold;
its conclusion **explained the failures and not the successes** — eleven of
the first thirty literals wrong, nineteen right, and the reading accounted
for the eleven. A right rule gives 5,443 of 5,443; a patch gives 19 of 30.
The one-line instrument — check the part of the decode you ASSUMED good —
went unrun for a day (BLOCKERS.md, *"The DD reader's structure is right"*).

**Which forks use it** is a container fact. The corpus states it twice and
both agree on all 186 forks: bit `0x80` of the method byte, and a `u16` that
is 1 rather than 0 fifty bytes further into the header. No specimen separates
them, so the note names both and claims neither, and the reader tries both
forms.

## 2026-09-21 (the archive that was never a fork) — Now Compress's container, and the third coder's table

**Claim.** A Now Compress archive is a container whose **members each carry
their own fork-shaped header**; the block table belongs to the member. Read
so, `derived-Expand_Now_1.0.1.sea` — the corpus's real 1993 specimen — walks
into **three blocks**: 32,768 + 32,768 + 23,406 = 88,942, its fork's size.

**Evidence.** Member records are 110 bytes from offset 24, data-area bounds
at +98 and +102. The block table sits **ten bytes into the data area in
everything 5.0.1 wrote and two bytes in the 1993 file**, told apart by the
header's first-block-offset field; reading the later layout into the older
file drops the FIRST block, which is why it looked unparseable.

**The near-miss that was not one.** The 2026-09-20 note filed a record at 144
reading `(0x4ad6, 0x20)` as probable coincidence, though 0x4ad6 sat one byte
before the file's only Kraft-1.0 table. It is the **second** block, shape 2;
it failed because its output starts at 32,768 and its matches reach into an
undecoded block. **A structure that matches in two independent ways is
evidence; "probably chance" needs its own test.**

**And FORMATS.md had said so for a month**: its *Now Compress* section
recorded on 2026-08-15, from the engine's block loop, "three blocks, 'new'
LZSS twice and Huffman-only once", while the derivation note said the blocks
could not be located. The container walk's shapes — `0x40`, `0x20`, `0x40` —
are that sentence. Cross-file contradiction, first in BLOCKERS.md's list.

**The third coder (mode bit `0x40`, archive members only).** Header read:
`0x2f`, a sixteen-entry four-bit **code-length code** (Kraft exactly 1 on all
eight known blocks), 24 unaccounted bits, then a main table in that code whose
symbols 0..255 are literals. **Stream not read**; the citation cannot move.

**Technique:** `nowcompress.py --case probe` archives a 4,000-byte run of one
byte, 6,000 bytes over `{A, B}`, 6,000 over `{A, B, C, D}`, and a file that is
its own first half twice. **A table whose literal region must hold exactly two
entries is found by what it must contain.** Independent check from the 1993
file: its third block codes 252 literals, and its 23,406 bytes hold exactly
those 252 distinct values.

## 2026-09-21 (the manual for the other machine) — PackIt is published, in the documentation of a DOS extractor

**Claim.** PackIt's container is documented field for field in appendices B
and C of `UNPACKIT.DOC` (unPACKIT 1.0, 1986 DOS freeware, R. Scott
McGinnis). A reader from those plus the project's tree note reads **all 38
forks of the corpus's four PackIt archives** byte for byte
(`tools/derive_packit.py`, `docs/formats/packit.md`); `src/fmt_packit.c`'s
container is no longer macutils'.

**Given:** the four subfile type words and `PEnd`, the 94-byte entry header,
fork/CRC order, and the boxed note that a compressed subfile's header is
coded with the forks, so "the entire subfile must be uncompressed in order to
get to the next subfile" (what 2026-09-20 spent measuring).

**Four corrections:** the name field is fixed at 63 bytes; there is no
MacBinary header on a `.pit` (four of five specimens begin at the type word);
`PMa5` is listed twice, so the fourth word is unnamed; the compression is
named ("huffman encoded"), not described.

**Lesson.** The inventory's reason — *"PackIt's own format is trivial; the
app is not here"* — is about the APPLICATION. `reference/notes/PackIt.md` had
a *Specifications* section naming this document, macutils'
`doc/README.unpit` (already on disk) and PackIt's source, since the first
fetch: **read as far as the magic numbers.** Same failure as *forty pages
nobody had listed*, one level down: a reference that names references is a
fetch list nobody ran. **"Some program is out of reach" is a claim about
programs, not about documentation.**

**Not closed:** the CRCs' polynomial (CRC-16/XMODEM still macutils'), the
resync rule (macutils'), both ciphers and `PMa6` (XADMaster's). The tool
checks no CRC.

## 2026-09-21 (the window that stopped at the fork) — a Now Compress defect the corpus could not reach, and the four-member archive that found it

**Claim.** `src/fmt_now.c` sized its history from the largest fork, but the
window spans MEMBERS, so an all-small-fork archive refused matches into an
earlier member. The bound is now the SUM of every fork, capped at 32 KB.
**No fixture's peak heap changes** (each has a fork over 32 KB).

**Evidence.** A four-member Now Compress archive of 4–6 KB members
(`nowcompress.py --case probe`): two came back *archive structure is
corrupt*, at offsets **6,228 and 13,000 against a 6,000-byte window**. A
reader from the block's bytes decodes all four only with history carried
across members.

**The refutation was in the same file.** The sizing comment said a
back-reference "cannot reach further back than the fork has produced";
seventy lines earlier `now_next_block` says a stream start "reaches back into
the history the PREVIOUS stream left behind". **An intra-file contradiction
is cheaper to find than the cross-file kind, and no tool looks for either.**

**Why the corpus missed it:** two real fixtures, thirteen synthetic, eight
specimens — every one a single file or unrelated members. The probe was built
to make a code table legible and needed similar members. **An input chosen
for one property tests every other** — the argument for generating inputs.

**Measured, not left open:** the offset table reaches `0xe100` plus thirteen
extra bits — **65,791 bytes** — against `NOW_HISTORY` 32,768.
`nowcompress.py --case reach` (five 16 KB members, the fifth a copy of the
first, a perfect match **64 KB back**): the encoder does not take it; largest
offset **32,766**, and all five extract byte-exact. **The window is 32,768
bytes; the extra reach is capacity nothing writes.** By-product: 6,000-byte
members naming offsets of 11,531 and 15,124 confirm the fix independently.

## 2026-09-21 (the pair that never repeats) — Now Compress's third coder, read off matches planted at a length and a distance chosen here

**Claim.** Shape 3 is described: its token grammar, a 33-symbol length
alphabet with a longest match of **257 bytes**, and a 56-class distance
alphabet reaching **65,791**. A reader from that description alone
(`tools/derive_now.py`, `docs/formats/now-compress.md`) decodes **every
shape-3 block of every specimen and both corpus archives**, byte for byte and
**with nothing searched for**: **81 of 81** harness blocks, **3 of 3** in the
1993 archive, **306 of 306** in the 1995 one — 9.9 MB of real data.

**The transferable part: inputs in which the answer is the only thing that
can be there.** `nowcompress.py --case tokdist` and `--case toklen` build each
member from a **de Bruijn sequence of order 2 over 256 symbols** (every byte
pair once, so no LZ match exists), then append a copy of its first bytes: the
only match is at a distance and length chosen here. Forty distances 2 to
16,384, twenty-four lengths 2 to 255; two emulator runs.

**What the bytes said that extrapolation did not:**

- **the distance table stores code length plus two** — Kraft gives 0.250000
  over stored values on every multi-symbol table, exactly 1.000000 after
  subtracting two;
- **the main table is a fixed 290 entries, trailing zeros and all** —
  BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn claims*, for what "ends where the code completes"
  cost;
- **distance classes are not a uniform ladder**: four per octave to 255, then
  eight classes of 256, then doubling every four. Extrapolating put a
  3,000-byte distance at symbol 41 in a 38-symbol table.

**Independent check:** the last class starts at **57,600 and spans 8,192**,
ending at 65,791 — the number measured off the engine's offset table the same
day (*the window that stopped at the fork*). Two routes, one number.

**`0x20` is Huffman ALONE** — found because two `tokdist` members came back
mode `0x120`: one symbol per output byte, no flags or matches, stream one byte
after the table. The mode word is layers: low five bits LZSS, `0x20` a Huffman
code over it, `0x40` the archive coder, `0x100` inside an archive. Reading
`0x20` as `0x3f` with bits missing is why the 1993 archive's MIDDLE block had
never been read; now both corpus archives decode, 3 of 3 and 306 of 306.

**The block header, from the search's own output.** Over 75 blocks with the
stream start found by trial, header byte 4 was 16 minus "bits past the
tables"; byte 1 the same as a byte offset plus 85; byte 3 the same at the far
end; and the last four bytes are **a 32-bit sum of every byte before them** —
the shape-1 "presumably a checksum", now measured, same in all four shapes.
**The rule fitted to 75 blocks was wrong on 306**: the 1995 archive has twenty
blocks where byte 4 is zero and the stream starts at the tables' end; the rule
is `(16 − byte) mod 16`. Caught because the header states the number twice —
**a redundancy in the format is a free test, if you read both.**

**Where a shape-2 stream begins** ("23 bits after its table in one specimen
and 18 in another"): one zero byte plus **two Huffman symbols, `0x00` and
`0x03`** — exactly what every shape-1 block opens with before its first flag.
Starting at the prefix reads a flag of `0x00` whose first match reaches before
output position nought, failing exactly like a wrong start bit: the symptom
said "where" when the fault was "what". Shape 1's payload was documented as
starting **two bytes** in, and nobody had asked what they were.

**A count from 2026-08-16 reconciles.** FORMATS.md's two "stream-restart
records" in the 1995 archive are one repeated offset inside `SynRef2.0 INFO`
(resource fork ends, data fork begins) and the repeat that OPENS the big
member's table — the same two records under different names.

**Corrections to this note's own claims, from leads in `src/fmt_now.c`
(XADMaster's; the note says so where it states each field):**

- the block record's last four bytes, "zero in every specimen", are **a u16
  padding count** and a zero u16 — the bytes between stream and checksum, 1 on
  four harness shape-1 blocks, the decoder stopping exactly `padding + 4`
  short of the next block;
- a **u32 after every member's header and block table is the sum of every
  byte before it** — true of all 75 members of the seven archives here;
- the shape-1 match rule "a length byte, then a distance byte" is wrong: the
  two bytes hold a 3-bit length and a **13-bit** distance, reaching 8,191 back.
  Shape-1 specimens can't tell (no first byte of 8 or more); shape 2 can —
  1,340 of its 2,162 match tokens are where the readings differ. The note held
  both rules, one per shape, for a day (BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn claims*);
- a shape-3 block's bytes 0..1 are **one u16, `0x2F59` plus the compressed
  header length** — same stream position on all 386 blocks, and it explains
  why byte 1 is odd and the 85 (4 − 0x59). The "24 unaccounted bits" are four
  more zero code lengths and a count byte: the alphabet is **twenty** symbols,
  because a distance entry stores length plus two and 17 must fit. **An
  unexplained gap in a header is usually an unfinished field.**

**Cross-check against the only other reader:** `fmt_now.c`'s `UnpackNewLZSS`
arrays and the derived ones disagree **nowhere** — 33 length and 55 distance
classes, every base and extra-bit count, including the jump from five extra
bits to eight at 256 and the last base `0xe100`; 88 numbers. The derivation
was committed before that file was opened, so it is a check, not a source.

**The container, pinned with a specimen made for it:** entry records give both
fork lengths at +86 and +90, the data area's bounds, and at +106 a u32 sum of
the record's first 106 bytes; a folder record is followed by exactly the
entries its +80 field counts — read off the 1995 fixture alone, then confirmed
by `nowcompress.py --case tree` (two folders, two loose files, seven records,
pre-order, every checksum agreeing).

**Result:** given only an archive, `derive_now.py` decodes every block of both
corpus archives (3 of 3, 306 of 306), three checksums keeping the walk on the
rails.

**The detect-only probe left the inventory.** `unc_nowcompress_probe` tests
the first ENTRY RECORD checking itself (`00 02` header, plausible count,
Pascal name, byte sum of 24..129 at 130), and the 24-byte file header is now
described: a version word separating 1993 from 5.0.1, the count as u32 at +8,
at +20 the sum of the twenty bytes before. Nine archives agree; our synthetic
fixture's generator leaves it zero and nothing noticed. `src/fmt_stubs.c`
cites the note; NOTICE can say none of its three probes is XADMaster's.

**Asked for and refused:** the code-length escape past 15. `--case deep` and
`--case deeparc` (Fibonacci histograms, deepest possible code: 20 bits at 21
symbols): **eight tables 10 to 13 deep, escape count zero.** Structural —
every shape puts LZ under the Huffman coder, which eats the skew. **A negative
from a probe designed to force the thing beats silence**; the cases are kept.

**Left open then:** byte 2 of a shape-3 header (255 on 59 of 75 blocks, 0 on
six), what `00 03` means, and the zero byte between a Huffman table and its
stream — *all three settled the same day by mutation: 2026-09-21, (asking the
program that wrote it).*

## 2026-09-21 (asking the program that wrote it) — Now Compress's last four unknowns, and the coders rewritten from the note

**A reader that ignores a field cannot say whether the FORMAT ignores it.**
Four fields were "nothing here reads it" — a fact about this engine and
XADMaster: shape-3 byte 2, the `00 03` prefix, the byte after a Huffman table,
and the offset delta `src/fmt_now.c` corrects a block table by.

**So the encoder was asked.** `tools/mutate_now.py` changes one field and
recomputes every checksum over it (block trailer, block table, entry record,
file header); `tools/vmac/nowcompress.py --expand` drives Now Compress's
**Decompress**, `--adjudicate` a self-extractor's own decoder. Measured:

- **byte 2 is read by nothing**: all 38 shape-3 blocks set to `0x5a`, the
  self-extractor produced **80 forks of 80 byte for byte**;
- **`00 03` is read by nothing** (`5a a5` in shape 1; two other equal-length
  symbols in shape 2);
- **the byte after a Huffman table IS read**: set to 7, 16,000 bytes of
  something else;
- **the offset delta is the format's**: every stored offset short by 100
  (the shape `tools/synth_now.py` writes) — the self-extractor reads it byte
  for byte; this engine without `now_find_delta` refuses all four members. With
  only the first-block u32 short it reads back too, where this engine refuses:
  one constant added to every record breaks the correct ones. The delta is
  real, the reference's mechanism is not the format's, and no encoder-written
  file needs either.

**Byte 2 was 386 easy questions, not a hard one.** Every hypothesis was a
property of the BLOCK. `--case tokdist`'s forty near-identical members give
191, 224, 240, 248, 252, 254, 255, then 255 thirty-two times — halving the
distance to 255 each step, which no per-block quantity can do. **When a long
list of hypotheses all fail, the list may be the problem.**

### The control that stopped the wrong answer

The escape past 15 has no specimen (Now Compress will not write a code deeper
than 15). A from-scratch file — one block, a 20-deep code over Fibonacci data
— was called **"damaged and cannot be repaired"**, which looked like proof the
escape is the reference's fiction. But the **same file with a 13-deep code**,
on the same volume, was refused too: the encoder dislikes something about
files built here. `--recode 20` instead re-codes the Huffman region of the
encoder's own `half.bin` under a legal non-optimal code (lengths 1, 2, … 20,
20; six symbols at 16 to 20 bits): **Decompress returned all 16,000 bytes**,
as did the control re-coded at 15.

A mutation that FAILS proves only that something changed. A positive specimen
says what a field means, a control beside it that the specimen is fair; the
first draft had neither, and its conclusion was the opposite of the truth.

### What the four answers left, and what was under them

The offset delta and the escape were the last facts in `src/fmt_now.c`
resting on XADMaster; with both measured the coders were rewritten from the
note the same day. **One Huffman-region reader serves all three consumers**
(Huffman-only block, the stream under shape 2, a shape-3 header's two tables),
and the 346-byte staging array moved into the per-archive allocation.
Byte-exact on all 124 Now Compress files and `run_now.py`'s 42 archives;
**−204 B of code**, **−616 B** of deepest-chain frames, **790 → 792 engine
ticks** on a 7 MHz Mac Plus (that instrument's resolution).

**The cleanest draft was 2.7 % slower, and Linux said faster.** Splitting the
region's opening into its own function (572 B less frame) cost **790 → 811
ticks** on `derived-Expand_Now_1.0.1.sea`, reproducibly, while callgrind had
12,000 FEWER x86 instructions and 1.1 % fewer on the 9.9 MB archive. Bound
hoisted to a local (−2), class bases fetched after extra bits (0, reverted),
then one function with every value a local (−19) reached parity. **A 68000
pays for register allocation across a call boundary in a loop run 32,768 times
a block, not what a Linux profile counts**; the tick probe should come first.

**The container is one thing.** A compressed FILE is an archive of one entry —
same 24-byte header and 110-byte record, both checksums agreeing on all
sixteen bare forks — which is why "the fork header" had a table at 144 (134 +
10). The block table has **one layout and one offset width**:
`[mode][padding][end offset]` records from +4 on all 108 members, the two
unnamed words being a leading record's mode and padding. The reading is the
reference's; the 108 members and their checksums make it a measurement, and
`tools/derive_now.py` walks it.

## 2026-09-21 (six copies of one file) — what a block table is anchored on, the record a file written here was missing, and byte 2 computed

**One mutation is a question with two answers.** **Six copies of one file on
one volume**, one block-table field moved in each, checksums recomputed, one
run: five came back byte for byte, one did not; a seventh rung (the LAST
record short) showed **a wrong record damages its own block and no other**.
Together (docs/formats/now-compress.md, *The archive layer*): Now Compress's
correction is a **whole-table constant**, works in either direction, ignores
the stored first-block offset, and does not take the record count from it —
short by 100, that u32 makes `(first − start − 4)` −68 and the file still
read.

**The engine was left as it is, deliberately.** It derives the constant from
that u32 and so refuses three files the format reads; the reading that fits
every rung (try one constant across the records, keep it if the blocks check
out) is a hypothesis, and the files it would buy are ones no encoder writes —
not worth changing a walk 124 files and 42 archives depend on.

**Harness lessons:**

- `--expand` pressed Return twice per run, so a first refusal would have
  stopped every file behind it; one Return per file on the volume made a
  ladder one boot instead of six of eight minutes. A constant that does not
  vary with its input is usually an unquestioned ceiling;
- `--rename` wrote the 32-byte name field whole and would have zeroed the 23
  catalogue-shaped bytes the encoder leaves, contaminating the control; caught
  because the mutation printed *"the 23 bytes after the name zeroed (were zero
  already)"*. A mutation that reports its before-and-after is not decoration;
- **a run that ends early looks exactly like a refusal**: the volume was
  ejected while QuickFiler was still working, and two of four "refusals" were
  files not reached (an icon still highlighted is still selected). The harness
  now waits fifteen seconds per file instead of a flat thirty; re-run, both
  came back byte-exact — Finder flags, dates, the u32 at +94 and the 23 bytes
  after a short name are read by nothing.

**The file this project could not get read was missing one record.**
`synth_now.py`'s compressed files, since M12, were *"damaged and cannot be
repaired"* with every checksum right. It is the **leading record** — eight
bytes producing nothing, end offset repeating the first-block offset. Dropping
it from an encoder file gets that alert word for word; **a file built here
with one added comes back byte for byte**, 16,000 of 16,000. As with the
escape: the failing mutation could have been about anything; the field ADDED
named it, with an encoder-written control beside it.

**Byte 2 is computed, not left over.** Re-running the same case: the two
archives differ in dates and checksums over them and nowhere else, byte 2
included. **Ask whether a value is noise before asking what it means**; a
repeat run is the cheapest experiment. It tracks the encoder's window position
— 41 of the 43 values above 200 in the 1995 archive are in blocks starting in
the low half of its 64 KB window — a correlation, filed as one. *Withdrawn: a
case that CHOOSES a block's offset puts eight full blocks at each quarter of
the window and byte 2 is 0 in all eight — 2026-09-21, (the quarter that
changed nothing).*

## 2026-09-21 (the symbol that was only there once) — where `00 03` is written, and the dimension no Now Compress experiment has varied

**A field nothing reads still has a birthplace.** Four experiments said only
what `00 03` is NOT read by — this reader, XADMaster, Now Compress's
Decompress (`5a a5` returns byte for byte). What the encoder thinks it writes
has no decoder in it.

**So the encoder's other half was asked.** A shape-2 block's 128-byte table is
built from the shape-1 stream's frequencies. If the prefix is in that stream,
it is counted; if prepended afterwards, a symbol occurring nowhere else would
have no code. The corpus was searched for that block: `huffgap/g09.bin` —
**4,517 symbols, `0x03` occurring exactly once, as the prefix, carrying a
12-bit code**; 116 symbols coded and 116 occurring, exact both ways, no
coded-but-unused symbol in any of the fourteen shape-2 blocks. **The prefix is
inside the stream the Huffman pass counts.** That does not separate the LZSS
coder emitting it from a wrapper adding it before coding; it retires every
reading where it is added AFTER (header, framing, alignment). Nothing about
what 3 means.

**Narrower than "every specimen":** only **20** blocks carry the prefix —
nineteen first blocks and `stored/mixed.bin`'s second — and **neither corpus
archive contributes one** (shape 3 and Huffman-only throughout). All 20 came
from one installed program: constant over content, settings, two shapes — and
**one version of Now Compress**. Now Utilities shipped as 3.0.2, 4.0.2, 5.0.1,
6.0.x and 6.5/6.7.x; a second encoder is the only instrument that could show
it move, and bears on **what selects the leading record**. — *Both run the
same day: 2026-09-21, (the other program), where the prefix does not move, two
unread fields beside it do, and 3.0.2/4.0.2 turn out to have no compressor at
all. The leading record turned out not to be one: 2026-09-21, (the record that
was never leading).*

**Lesson:** "nothing reads it" is a claim about readers, and four agreeing is
still four. The encoder had written its answer elsewhere — in a frequency
table it had to build before writing the byte.

## 2026-09-21 (the other program) — a second Now Compress, and the difference between a constant and a leftover

**Three fields are written by the encoder and read by nobody** — the `00 03`
prefix, the padding byte before a block's trailer, the leading record's two
words — and mutation showed only that a decoder ignores them, not whether the
ENCODER means them.

**The instrument is a second encoder.** Now Utilities **6.0** (March 1996;
5.0.1 is 1994), same inputs and settings, writes files of the same LENGTH
across all four coders, identical except the entry record's dates, the leading
record's `0037` → `003a`, one padding byte `ff` → `47`, and checksums over
those. **The coder did not change in four years.**

| field | 5.0.1 | 6.0 | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| the LZSS prefix | `00 03` | `00 03` | a constant the encoder means |
| the padding byte | `ff` | `47` | leftover |
| the leading record's words | `0d4c 0037` | `0d4c 003a` | moves with the program; version stamp and deterministic leftover both fit |

A value constant across 27 files from one program, two months apart, both
settings, files and archives, looks intended until a second program changes
the next field along. **"Deterministic" and "deliberate" are the same
observation until the thing underneath changes** (cf. *six copies of one
file*, nearly calling byte 2 uninitialised memory).

**A third question retired:** whether the 1993 archive lacks a leading record
because of version. 6.0 writes one where 5.0.1 does, and the 1995 archive has
a member with and one without — not the program. *It is the fork lengths, and
there is no leading record: 2026-09-21, (the record that was never leading).*

**Cost:** four emulator runs of about five minutes and two downloads. Now
Utilities **3.0.2 and 4.0.2 contain no compressor** (QuickFiler arrives in 5),
and the 1993 encoder was a separate product not on the mirrors. 6.0's
installer is a StuffIt archive of finished files, so install was a copy:
extension and toolbox into `System Folder:Extensions`, droplets at the root,
**leading spaces in their names kept** (load order). Runs on the harness's
System 7.0.1 image on an emulated Mac Plus.

**Pointed at byte 2, the same instrument said the opposite:** `tokdist` by
6.0 gives the same 46,548 bytes and **all 38 shape-3 headers identical to
5.0.1's**, the six non-`0xff` values included — the computation did not
change, in a file where two leftovers moved.

**Generalisable:** for a constant nobody reads, ask not "what does it mean"
but "constant WITH RESPECT TO what?" — vary what the field belongs to.

## 2026-09-21 (the record that was never leading) — one empty block-table record per member, and where a harness had never varied its input

**Claim.** A member's block table holds **exactly one record that produces no
bytes, the boundary between its resource fork and its data fork**: between
them when both are non-empty, at the head when the resource fork is empty, at
the tail when the data fork is. Measured on **153 of the 153 members Now
Compress has written here**. It replaces "a leading record 5.0.1 writes, plus
a separate fork boundary", whose two exceptions (the 1993 member, data fork
empty; the 1995 archive's first member, the only real specimen with two
non-empty forks) were the rule seen once from each position.

**Why it survived — the transferable half.** Every harness member came off an
HFS volume built with `hcopy -r`, which writes the **data fork alone**: 105 of
107 had an empty resource fork and so a boundary at the head. BLOCKERS.md's
smell — *every input made by one program; ask what the generator never
varies* — and here it never varied what the rule is written in terms of.
**Ask a harness what it cannot produce.** `nowcompress.py --case forks`
produces it: four MacBinary members (`hcopy -m`) — data-only, resource-only,
both small, both with a **three-block** resource fork; one run, each record
where the rule says, the big one at index 3, not 1.

**A second sentence fell, the one that mattered.** The note said the window
carries across a restart unchanged. It does not: the block after a restart
reaches into the **dictionary cache**, the last 32,768 bytes ending where the
previous stream's FIRST block ended — identical whenever that stream is one
block, as every specimen was until `bothbig.bin`; there they differ by 19,909
bytes. `src/fmt_now.c` always reloaded (transcribed before described), but
`fmt_now.c` now cites the note, and `tools/derive_now.py` read 8 of that
archive's 11 blocks. Both fixed; withdrawn sentences and cost in BLOCKERS.md.

**Left open:** what the decoder DOES with the record — where it goes and that
a decoder requires one are measured from both sides.

## 2026-09-21 (the quarter that changed nothing) — byte 2 does not track the window, and the archives this project writes are refused

**Two experiments the last handoff asked for, both negative, and a
negative is what each was for.**

### Where in the window a block starts changes byte 2 by nothing

**Claim withdrawn.** A shape-3 header's byte 2 was said to track which
half of a 65,536-byte window its block begins in, on a correlation in
the 1995 archive: 41 of its 43 values above 200 are in low-half blocks.
`nowcompress.py --case wpos` chooses the offset instead: four 65,536-byte
members, each preceded by a 16,384-byte spacer, put two full blocks at
each quarter of the window. **Eight full blocks, byte 2 = 0 in all
eight.** Only the archive's first block differs, at 236.

**Why the correlation looked real.** The 1995 archive's 306 blocks are
all full and all in one member, so they alternate low/high half by
construction; anything drifting through that file correlates with it.
Every earlier byte-2 experiment varied CONTENT and read the offset off
the result. **Nothing had ever chosen the offset** — and a correlation
you only ever observe is one you have not tested.

**What replaced it (hypothesis).** `tokdist`'s forty mutually
unmatchable members walk byte 2 191 → 224 → 240 → 248 → 252 → 254 →
255, each step exactly `b2 + ((255 − b2) >> 1) + 1` — **101 transitions
take it, 31 more sit at the cap**. `reach`'s five near-identical members
go 224 then 0, 0, 0, 0, and `wpos` does the same. Half of this was
withdrawn the same day: byte 2 falls as more of a block can be matched,
but is computed from its own block, and the climb describes a ladder
ordered one way: *2026-09-21, (the ladder that was walked back down)*.

### The archives this project writes are refused, and not for the reasons listed

**Thirteen archives graded by `unar` since M12, never once put to Now
Compress.** `synth_now.py --ladder` builds rungs, each spliced into a
real self-extractor's data fork by `mutate_now.py` so the decoder Now
Software shipped reads it.

| rung | what it adds | Now Compress |
|---|---|---|
| control | `probe`'s 3,830-byte archive in `tree`'s self-extractor, built around one half that size | **all four members byte-exact** |
| `both` | the header's setting, window and byte sum, every block trailer, and the fork-boundary record | **refused** |
| `arch` | plus the `0x0100` bit every archive mode word carries | **refused** |

The control shows the route works and length is not the obstacle. The
LZSS prefix, the first guess, is not a candidate: every block there is
shape 3 or Huffman-only, and only shapes 1 and 2 carry `00 03`.
TESTING.md had listed five differences; two more (the `0x0100` bit and
the header's window word) were found before running anything. The
remaining list of three suspects was also wrong — the answers are a
16-byte trailer, the 32,768-byte block size and word alignment:
*2026-09-21, (sixteen bytes nobody had read)*.

**The instrument lied twice.** `--adjudicate` printed *"the original
extractor agrees with us on every fork"* for both refused rungs, because
an empty volume compares zero forks. It now fails when it graded
nothing, and `--dearchive` counts only new files. **An aggregate over an
empty set is the purest form of the failure this repository keeps
rediscovering.**

**Cost.** Five emulator runs. One went on `--dearchive`, a new route:
QuickFiler offers Dearchive for a file typed `NCar`/`NCdc` (type read
from Expand Now's `FREF`s), yet it expanded nothing, not even the
control. That route is unexplained and the results above do not rest on
it.

## 2026-09-21 (sixteen bytes nobody had read) — what a Now Compress archive needs, and where the three answers were

**Claim.** An archive Now Compress will open needs three things this
project's generator did not do: a **16-byte trailer** after the last
member, **32,768-byte blocks**, and **every block starting on a word
boundary**. The first two are refusals; the third extracts with one
block silently wrong. A fourth difference did not matter. Ten rungs,
ten emulator boots, one control (TESTING.md, *The rungs*). **The first
archive this project has written that Now Compress reads** is the
`no-tail` rung: two members byte-exact, four forks graded.

**Where the three came from — the whole lesson.** None of the three
answers was on the previous session's suspect list. They came from
diffing an encoder-written archive against ours field by field, with
no hypothesis:

- the trailer is **past the end of everything any reader walks**
  (`unc_sniff`, `src/fmt_now.c`, `derive_now.py`, XADMaster). Found by
  asking every specimen *does the file length equal the last member's
  end?* — no for all ten archives, yes for all sixteen compressed files;
- the block size, by printing block lengths next to fork lengths;
- the alignment, by noticing byte 1 of a shape-3 header is always odd,
  recorded earlier as a tally and not as a cause.

This repeats *the symbol that was only there once*; the fix is the same:
**census a property over every specimen rather than reason about one.**
Three of the four candidates came out of a loop over 34 files printing
one number each.

**Why "refused" was nearly the wrong measurement.** Refusals only say
*something among what is left*. The discriminating rung was `no-word`,
ACCEPTED and still wrong (one member differs) — **a pass/fail
instrument would have called it a pass.** The previous day's
empty-volume guard on `--adjudicate` is what makes today's four
IDENTICAL lines mean something.

**Cost.** Ten boots at about six minutes. Five climbed one rung at a
time from below, which is the wrong direction when several differences
are fatal at once. The useful five were **leave-one-out from a rung that
passed**: reach a working archive first, then subtract.

**What this does NOT change.** `src/fmt_now.c` reads every real and
synthetic archive; these are WRITER requirements and our only writer is
a test tool. The thirteen archives keep their old shape on purpose —
`unar` refuses a bit-coded region leaving fewer than four spare bits,
and a 16-bit flush does not always leave more, so aligning them would
cost the oracle that grades them (TESTING.md). The difference is now
measured, named and behind a flag.

## 2026-09-21 (the ladder that was walked back down) — Now Compress's byte 2 is a property of its own block, and the climb was a description of one ladder

**Claim.** A shape-3 header's byte 2 **falls as more of its block can
be matched** and is computed **from that block**, not carried. Eleven
members varying matchability alone give 255, 255, 127, 127, 127, 127,
63, 63, 31, 31, 8; twenty-one walking the ladder up and back down give
those values then their mirror, **every mirrored pair equal**
(`nowcompress.py --case match`, `--case matchv`).

**Withdrawn.** The running-state reading (climb by `b2 + ((255 − b2) >>
1) + 1`, 101 transitions exact; collapse to 0). A carried value updated
by half the distance to a target lags; there is no hysteresis in the V,
and none of the ten transitions back up takes the step. The 101 describe
ladders ordered by a parameter that only increases.

**Second time in one day in the same field** (*the quarter that changed
nothing*). An exact law over 101 transitions looks like far better
evidence than a correlation over 43 blocks, which is why it survived
longer. **The number of confirmations is not the question; whether
anything ever varied the input the other way is.** Walking a ladder
backwards costs one run.

**Cost.** Three emulator runs, one wasted: the first `match` used an
incompressible keystream, so seven of eleven members came out **stored**
(no header, no byte 2). A probe varying one property of a compressed
block must make sure the encoder compresses it. The rebuild uses de
Bruijn bytes for the unmatchable half and a run of one letter for the
rest.

**Still open, narrower.** Six quantities are ruled out by name over 175
tokenised blocks — literal count, literal-to-output ratio, token counts,
table sizes, longest match distance, block length. `matchv`'s `n09` and
`n11` agree on all of them and differ in byte 2; `n00` and `n01` have
identical code tables and differ by half. So it is something the encoder
knows and the block does not spell (search depth, hash occupancy, cost
estimate — hypothesis), and no instrument outside the encoder's code is
left to ask.

## 2026-09-21 (the oracle that was never asked) — a second implementation of StuffIt method 6, four weeks on the disk

**Claim.** deark implements StuffIt method 6 and agrees with this engine
on all 11 method-6 forks here. It is MIT, in `reference/` since 2026-08-25,
and compiled by every `ci.sh`. This withdraws *"the ONLY reference
implementation the project has for method 6"* (`src/fmt_sit.c`,
FORMATS.md, OPEN_ITEMS.md) and TESTING.md's method-6 blind spot built on
it.

**Why it survived (transferable).** The third oracle was offered a fork
**only when `unar` and `macunpack` both left it open**; macunpack reads
method 6, so deark was never asked. **A check positioned where nothing
can contradict it cannot contradict anything.** Ask "what is this check
never run ON", not "what does the suite cover". A second premise —
*"deark has no notion of a resource fork for these formats"* — was also
false (it writes AppleDouble sidecars), and it excluded the only fork
method 6 occurs in: the corpus's one real method-6 entry has an empty
data fork and a 34,818-byte resource fork.

**What changed.** deark cross-checks the 23 forks macunpack alone had
graded (all agree) and fills resource forks. `oracle-unadjudicated`:
**23 forks across 12 fixtures → 15 across 11**.

**The guard that had to be added.** Lifting the restriction failed seven
fixtures: deark does not fail on a damaged file, it **pads**.
`sitdoc.sit` declares a 286-byte resource fork in a file ending 52 bytes
short; we write 234 and report truncation, deark writes 286 with 52
invented zeros, and for one run the manifest graded us against them.
**An oracle that always produces something is not ground truth about a
file that does not contain it.** deark now fills a gap only for an empty
fork (an assertion of absence) or a method it is the designated oracle
for; otherwise it cross-checks.

**The 2026-08-08 trap one layer up.** `ci.sh`'s `make clean` deletes
`build/macunpack/`; a rebuild without it writes weaker manifests, which
`MISSING_ORACLE` flags. deark closing those gaps made the warning
discard itself. The discard now requires macunpack to be present.

**Beyond the oracle.** `src/sit6_tables.h` is **1,028 bytes** from
macutils; deark states the same code book as **13 (count, length) pairs
— 26 bytes — plus a twenty-line assignment rule**, reproducing **256 of
257 codes**; the 257th, the terminator, has two leaves under one 12-bit
prefix in macunpack and one in deark. Taken next: *the table that was
twenty-six bytes*.

**Not claimed.** deark uses none of macunpack's code but credits it as
documentation: independent implementations, not independent readings. A
transcription error shows up; a shared misreading does not. That half
of TESTING.md's caveat stands.

## 2026-09-21 (the table that was twenty-six bytes) — StuffIt method 6's fixed code book, priced on both axes

**Claim.** The 1,028-byte fixed decode tree in `src/sit6_tables.h` is
**26 bytes of information** — thirteen (count, length) pairs and a
twenty-line assignment rule from `reference/deark/modules/stuffit.c`
(MIT). Built at run time they reproduce macunpack's tree over **all
8,192 bit paths of depth 13** (same leaf, same bit count), and the
synthetic fixture regenerates byte-identical.

**The price, on both axes:**

| | |
|---|---|
| code | **+408 B** |
| A5 (data + bss) | **−1,000 B** |
| net, and `build_mac.sh` counts the two one for one | **−592 B off every extraction's budget on a 1 MB Mac Plus** |
| peak heap, method-6 forks only | 40,982 → **42,010 B** (+1,028, the tree) |
| engine ticks on `derived-INITLoader.sit` | 3 → 3, the instrument's resolution |
| extractions lost | **none** — `run_tiers.py` reads 69/69 at the 1 MB floor and 66/69 at 512 KB, the tallies recorded before the change |

**The table was in A5, not code** — the CODE ceiling failed by 408 B and
only the A5 line showed where the 1,028 had gone. Both in code would
have been a 620 B win; table in code and builder in A5, a loss. **Price
every axis the ratchet measures, not the one the change is about.** A
one-loop zeroing of the two arrays is worth nothing: +4 B code, −4 B A5.

**Exhaustive, not sampled.** All 8,192 paths fit a loop, so equivalence
is proved. It mattered: macunpack spends thirteen bits on the terminator
(two leaves) where the code book gives symbol 256 twelve; a tree from the
code book alone would consume one bit fewer at every segment end.
`sit6_build` reproduces the split deliberately (its first draft re-split
the terminator it had just made; the fixtures caught it).

**What it is for.** `tools/gen_sit6_tables.py` became
`tools/check_sit6_tree.py`, which compares the two trees — shown to fail
on two corruptions of the 26 bytes. `fmt_sit.c` still owed macutils
method 6's **framing** (segment header, stored-segment rule, PackBits
tail): closed in *the framing that needed no rewrite*.

## 2026-09-22 (the framing that needed no rewrite) — StuffIt method 6's last macutils row, closed for nothing, and the three places this engine is stricter than both references

**Claim.** Method 6's **framing** — segment header, stored-segment rule,
PackBits tail — is stated in full by `reference/deark/modules/stuffit.c`
and `reference/deark/src/fmtutil-rle.c` (MIT).
`docs/formats/stuffit-method-6.md` is that description plus three
corrections; `tools/derive_sit6.py`, written from it and the container
page alone, reads **all 11 method-6 forks in the corpus** against the
sha256 two oracles recorded. The OPEN_ITEMS.md row closes: **nothing in
`fmt_sit.c` is XADMaster's or macutils' any more.**

| | |
|---|---|
| code | **0 B** — 152,596, the ceiling |
| A5 | **0 B** — 37,660, the ceiling |
| peak heap | **0 B** |
| engine ticks | **0** |
| extractions lost | **none** |

Zero because **nothing executable changed**: `git diff src/` is
comments only. The engine's framing and deark's agree field for field,
which is what a re-derivation is for (RLE90 closed the same way on
2026-09-21; PackIt needed four corrections).

**The references disagree on where a Huffman segment ends**, and the
engine had taken a third position: deark stops at the declared length
without reading the stop code; macunpack ignores the length and decodes
to the stop code; `fmt_sit.c` reads past the length and **requires** the
stop code. Measured: across the corpus's **13 Huffman segments the
symbol after the declared length is the stop code in 13 of 13**. The
strictest reading refuses a segment the others would disagree on.
`derive_sit6.py` implements deark's rule and reports the measurement
beside it.

The other two corrections: **both** references index their translation
array with an unbounded decoded symbol (a 12-byte segment coding a
thirteenth returns stale data — a wrong fork; no segment here does it);
and deark treats a segment header under 10 bytes as a clean stop where
this engine reports the fork corrupt.

**Transferable.** *The code book was worth 592 bytes and the framing is
worth nothing, and both were worth doing:* a licence row is closed by
the description existing, not by it saving anything. `NOTICE`'s
macutils paragraph no longer names `fmt_sit.c`.

**`dist/` was stale.** Rebuilding it gave a resource fork **591 B
smaller** than the committed one: `0aa9101` (the −592 B code book) had
not rebuilt the only download. Ratchets read the working tree and
`ci.sh` builds `build/mac/`, not `dist/`; a stale binary is the right
size and the wrong bytes. Confirmed on a fresh `git worktree` of `HEAD`
that the staleness predated this change. The check that now catches it:
*the download nothing looked at*.

**Figure corrected.** "All 12 method-6 forks" was written in three
files on 2026-09-21 beside an enumeration adding to eleven (ten in
`synth-sit-fixhuf.sit`, one in `derived-INITLoader.sit`); the corpus has
**11**. A number disagreeing with its own enumeration is the cheapest
smell there is.

## 2026-09-22 (the oracle asked about everything else) — deark over the whole corpus, and two things it does that nothing here had written down

**Claim.** `tools/sweep_deark.py` asks the third oracle about
**everything**, not only where the others are silent: **2,080 graded
forks across 593 of the 932 fixtures, 2,053 agree, zero disagreements**.
*(Day's first figures; correcting two mis-readings below took it to
**4,502 forks and 2,151 agreements**, still zero disagreements — see
2026-09-22, "the decline that read as a naming gap".)* It writes and
adjudicates nothing, comparing deark against every hash the manifests
hold: either it finds nothing (cheap, worth knowing) or something.

**First: deark declining a fork is not deark reading an empty one.**
`make_manifests.py` claimed "a member deark wrote at all has both forks".
False: for `derived-BitMap11.sit` (one method-8 data fork) deark writes
the resource sidecar, prints `Unsupported compression method: 8 (MW)`,
and no data file — which read as "0 bytes", the one thing deark is
trusted to assert alone. No manifest recorded a false empty yet; a
hazard found before it fired. `deark_forks` now returns **None** for
forks deark reported errors on (distinct from `b""`); an error it cannot
attach to a fork makes every absent fork of that archive unknown (9 forks
of coverage in two fixtures).

**Second: every entry in a folder was skipped** — 500 of them — because
deark mangles path separators to `_` and both tools matched raw names.
Modelling `de_char_to_valid_fn_char` took the sweep from 1,641 forks to
2,075 and fixed the manifest builder too. **A matcher that silently
drops what it cannot match reports success on the subset it can.**

**Third, known, not a defect:** deark does not unwrap MacLHA's
MacBinary payload; the sweep reports those `wrapped` after checking the
container's data fork is byte-identical to the graded one.

**What it CANNOT see, printed per format every run** — the day's
statement was 283 entries (150 StuffIt 5, 75 StuffIt, 49 Tar, 9 others)
named in a way no mangling reproduces. **Both halves were wrong the same
day**: 225 were entries deark named and declined, and the 49 Tar were
not an AppleDouble merge. **37** is the number, in four shapes TESTING.md
names; the disproofs are the entry cited above and BLOCKERS.md's
withdrawn claims. The method survives: a denominator printed per format
is a blind spot somebody can pull on.

## 2026-09-22 (the container is the oracle) — eight forks in damaged MacBinary graded by the file's own arithmetic

**Claim.** Eight forks in seven damaged MacBinary fixtures had no second
implementation (`unar` declines, deark pads, ours cannot grade ours).
**They did not need one**: MacBinary is a 128-byte header, the data fork
padded to 128, then the resource fork, all stored — offsets are
arithmetic and a truncated file holds exactly what is physically there.
`oracle-unadjudicated` falls from **15 forks across 11 fixtures to 7
across 4** — and back to 8 the same day, when deark stopped asserting
`arcplus712.zip`'s entry has an empty resource fork on a run where it
failed that entry's CRC (*the oracle asked about everything else*,
above).

**Evidence.** All eight match what `macextract` writes — `sitdoc.sit`'s
234 bytes of a declared 286, `systemidle.sit`'s 235, `sigmaedit.sit`'s
348, `ddarchive.sit`'s 238, `appledraw51.cpt`'s 13,036 of 13,121,
`pcal296.cpt`'s 12,899, and `guysmaccontacts.sea`'s data fork at 114,644
of a declared 137,726 with no resource fork present.

**Why it is not circular.** The engine reads the same header, so "the
layout says so" is not evidence alone. The rule **grades nothing unless
the arithmetic is confirmed on that file**, by either:

- the header's **own CRC-16/CCITT** over its first 124 bytes matching
  +124 (MacBinary II) — `guysmaccontacts.sea`, where neither fork had an
  oracle;
- or the entry's **other fork already adjudicated** and reproduced byte
  for byte by the same arithmetic — the six MacBinary I fixtures, where
  `unar` grades the data fork.

Where an oracle and the arithmetic disagree on a file it grades
**nothing** there. Shown failing first: six cases, including a broken
CRC and a falsified oracle hash. The layout itself reproduces both forks
of **174 undamaged MacBinary fixtures** (every single-entry,
two-adjudicated-fork one) with no mismatch.

**Corroborated after all.** `sweep_deark.py` then returned `padded` on
all six resource forks: deark's prefix is right and only its tail is
invented — readable because of the padding guard.

**Transferable.** *Ask what would settle this if no second
implementation existed at all.* A length forced by the container's
arithmetic is a different kind of ground truth from another decoder's
agreement — here stronger, because there is nothing in it for a second
bug to agree with.

## 2026-09-22 (the premise that stopped being true) — Implode has an implementation and an oracle on this disk, and the scope decision is not taken

**Claim.** PKZIP 1.x's Implode (zip method 6) was declined with no
implementation to write from and nothing to grade against. Both are now
here; **nothing is done about it** — scope is the maintainer's
(OPEN_ITEMS.md, *Out by the brief*, the Implode row).

**Evidence, measured 2026-09-22.** `reference/deark/src/fmtutil-lzh.c`
implements it under MIT (in `src/`, not the `foreign/` tree its licence
carves out). deark decodes all **7** Implode entries of `4acalc.zip`
and `4alnch11.zip`, each matching the **CRC-32 PKZIP stored**;
`CALC.TXT` is 5,284 bytes.

**Unchanged.** Implode is not a Macintosh method, predates deflate, and
both archives are PC software in the corpus to exercise per-entry
refusal — still a reasonable case for declining; only "and we could not
check it anyway" is gone. Adding `"Implode"` to `DEARK_METHODS` (record
ground truth before any decoder) belongs to the same decision.

(superseded: DECISIONS.md 2026-10-07, *the method that was out for a premise with no halves left*)

## 2026-09-22 (the download nothing looked at) — the one artefact this project ships, compared with the build for the first time

**Claim.** `dist/` is the only download, CLAUDE.md has a rule to rebuild
it, and nothing enforced the rule. It had been stale since `0aa9101`.

**Evidence, measured.** `0aa9101`'s tree built in a worktree: committed
`dist/MacExtract.bin` declared **188,154 B** of resource fork against the
build's **187,563 B** — 591 B behind, different bytes. `ci.sh` variant 4
already built the Mac shell every run and was never asked what it made.

**Consequence.** Variant 4 now compares SHA-256 from offset 128 on, both
files, failing and naming `sh tools/make_dist.sh` as the fix. Its shape:

- **Content, not size or timestamp.** `unc_strerror`'s `"ok"` → `"oK"`
  gives a `MacExtract.bin` of **exactly the same 187,776 bytes** as the
  shipped one.
- **Not the whole file.** MacBinary stores creation/modification dates
  (byte 94 differs between identical builds); three builds of the same
  source now agree on the payload.
- **The generated prose is `check_docs.py`'s check 7**, not `ci.sh`'s: a
  docs-only change does not run `ci.sh`, and `dist/README.txt` comes
  from a `make_dist.sh` heredoc expanding only `$VERSION`; check 7
  re-renders it and reports the first differing line.

**General shape.** A rule in CLAUDE.md is not a check; the evidence to
catch this was rebuilt from source on every CI run and thrown away.

## 2026-09-22 (the decline that read as a naming gap) — 2,324 forks the sweep was counting as its own blind spot

**Claim.** Of the **283** entries `sweep_deark.py` reported as named in
a way "no mangling of ours reproduces", 225 were named perfectly well:
deark had declined the method.

**Evidence, measured.** `deark_forks` was built from output FILES, and a
fully declined member writes none — `derived-seasons_greetings.sit`
yields 2 files for 8 members and `Unsupported compression method: 13
(LZ+Huffman)` naming each member and fork of the other 6. All 75 StuffIt
entries in the 283 are method 13; 122 of the 150 StuffIt 5 are Arsenic
(method 15). Carrying those members gives **declined 2,342, up from
18**, `agree` and `DIFFER` untouched.

**Consequence.** The fix is in `deark_forks`, so `make_manifests.py`
sees it too; all **12** deark-touched manifests rebuild byte-identically
in memory. (The first check said 9 of 12 CHANGED — `make clean` had
removed `build/macunpack` in between, the TESTING.md trap, caught by a
comparison.) The genuine naming gap is **37**, its four shapes named in
TESTING.md.

**The 49 Tar entries were mis-explained.** Filed as deark writing an
AppleDouble member as `._NAME` where `unar` merges it. Actually a tar
member stored as `./NAME` is reported by `unar` without `./`, and
deark's sanitiser turns the slash into `_`, so `./READ_ME` reaches disk
as `._READ_ME`. None of the 49 files for `derived-PCCTS.tar` starts with
the AppleDouble magic. Matching that name recovers 49 entries and **98
forks, all agreeing**: the sweep now compares **4,502** forks and agrees
on **2,151**. **A coincidence that corroborates a wrong story is worse
than no evidence**; opening one file — four bytes of reading — settled it.

**A member with no file asserts nothing about forks its errors did not
name**: "no file means empty" holds for a member deark wrote, not one it
gave up on. Those forks are unknown — lost coverage, never a falsehood.

**An error's name is not the raw name.** deark prints it
MAKE_PRINTABLE (`reference/deark/src/deark-ucstring.c`,
`ucstring_to_sz`), so `Icon\r` arrives as `Icon<\r>` and our model made
`Icon__r_` where the file is `Icon_`. **382 declined forks across 35
fixtures** were mis-keyed, **none live** that day (no file written for
those members) — a latent false-empty. `deark_err_name()` reverses the
escapes before sanitising; an undecodable byte is `DE_CODEPOINT_BYTE00 +
b` = 0x10000000 + b, past the 0x10ffff `de_char_to_valid_fn_char` keeps,
so it maps to `_`.

**General shape.** A harness printing the WRONG reason for what it
cannot see is worse than printing nothing, because the number looks
audited: 283 had been read three times as "deark is a weak oracle for
StuffIt" when it meant "deark does not implement method 13".

## 2026-09-22 (the name that was never a fork) — StuffIt 5's names are UTF-8, and the oracle was asked in the one way that hides it

**Claim.** This engine wrote StuffIt 5 entry names as mojibake, on Linux
and the Macintosh, and the 932-fixture corpus was byte-exact against an
oracle making the same mistake.

**Evidence, measured.** `derived-Cool_Tools__.sit` holds `C6 92` for a
folder name — UTF-8 for `ƒ`. deark decodes it as UTF-8
(`d->input_encoding` is UTF-8 for `file_fmt==2`, MacRoman otherwise,
`reference/deark/modules/stuffit.c`); `lsar -nr` unforced prints
`Cool Tools ƒ`; `lsar -nr -e macintosh`, the project's oracle
invocation, prints `Cool Tools ∆í`, as this CLI wrote. In Japanese:
`800-SAY-WHAT 3.0.1J/読んで下さい.rtf` against 25 characters of nothing.
28 entries across 5 fixtures — **corrected the same day to 27 across
4**; the 28th had two empty forks and nothing to do with encoding
(BLOCKERS.md; *a name an HFS volume can hold*, below).

**Consequence.** Filed in OPEN_ITEMS.md (*StuffIt 5 entry names are
UTF-8*); the frontend's per-format encoding, the oracle invocation with
its manifests, and the Macintosh shell's HFS names have to move
together. Done in *a name an HFS volume can hold*.

**Why it survived.** `-e macintosh` forces MacRoman on every format, so
unar produced the mojibake and the manifest recorded it as ground truth
— the tolerance-with-no-independent-evidence smell, in the harness's own
command line. Found by the only check comparing names with an oracle
invoked differently.

**Claim.** `ddtf-ddpro411ad1.dd.ad` and `.sea.ad` are inputs, not
archives to grade, so what their entry should be CALLED need not be
answered.

**Consequence.** `make_manifests.py` gains `NOT_ARCHIVES`: these are the

lack manifests because `unar` cannot produce one.

**Why not commit manifests.** They would record `ddtf-ddpro411ad1.dd.ad`
as the entry name (`unar` keeps the extension), forcing a special case
in the general rule that names a name-less format's single entry after
the file minus its extension (`x.txt.gz` → `x.txt`). `run_segments.py`
already asserts the bytes.

## 2026-09-22 (a name an HFS volume can hold) — StuffIt 5's UTF-8 names, on both hosts, and what the fold costs a Mac Plus

**Claim.** The three things moved together: the engine says which
encoding a name is in, the Linux CLI passes StuffIt 5's UTF-8 through,
the oracle is asked in that encoding with manifests rebuilt, and the Mac
shell folds UTF-8 into MacRoman for HFS. Closes OPEN_ITEMS.md, *StuffIt
5 entry names are UTF-8* (finding: 2026-09-22, *the name that was never
a fork*).

**The engine says it; it does not convert.** `UncEntryInfo.name_utf8`
is one byte, set only by `fmt_sit5.c`. A per-front-end format table
would be wrong where neither can see: a **segmented** StuffIt 5 set is
sniffed as a split and walked by whatever the joined stream is
(`derived-Sniffles_2.0.sit.1`). 0 B of stack — `-Os -fstack-usage` on
the three deepest frames unchanged; alignment padding absorbed it.

**The oracle is one word.** `make_manifests.py` picks per format
(`ORACLE_ENCODING`); the first `lsar` is trusted only for the format,
and a format with its own encoding costs one more call. **31 manifests
rebuilt, 35 names changed across 4 fixtures, 0 hashes changed**;
`run_diff.py` 31/31 on StuffIt 5.

**Two independent checks.** `lsar -nr` unforced prints `Cool Tools ƒ`;
deark reads the names as UTF-8 itself, so `sweep_deark.py` goes from
**4,502 graded forks and 37 entries it could not compare** to **4,556
and 10**, DIFFER 0 either way. The 54 new forks are all `declined`
(Arsenic and method 13), so agreements stay **2,151** and declines go
2,342 → 2,396: no new adjudication, just 27 entries correctly counted
as declines. (A first draft said the 54 agreed; checked, not assumed.)

**The 28 was 27.** `.typeAttributes.dict` in
`derived-PuzzleGetter_0.8.sit` has two empty forks and deark writes no
file for such a member (`do_pre_decompress_fork`, `if(frk->unc_len==0 &&
frk->cmpr_len==0)`); now a named row in the sweep's *what it cannot
see*. The encoding case was **27 entries across 4 fixtures**.

**The Mac fold.** `Utf8ToMacRoman` runs once at the door of
`sink_begin`, on the whole path, in place: UTF-8 never puts `0x2F`
inside a sequence (separators survive) and the fold only shortens.
Everything downstream — folder walk, folder hash, 31-character cut,
`BumpName`, the report — sees one name in one encoding. The cut acting
on the FOLDED name matters: 16 `é` are 32 bytes of UTF-8 and 16 of
MacRoman, and before the fold that name was cut mid-sequence. An
unmappable code point becomes `_`, reported once per path component in
its own line — *"`<name>` was named in characters this Macintosh cannot
write"* — naming what IS on disk.

| | |
|---|---|
| code | **+580 B** — `Utf8ToMacRoman` inlined into `sink_begin` (.text 1,114 → 1,596 B) plus `RepLostChars`; ceiling 152,596 → 153,176 |
| A5 | **+316 B** — MacRoman's 128-entry high half (.rodata 11 → 268 B) and the one report line (.rodata.str1.1 1,862 → 1,915 B); ceiling 37,660 → 37,976 |
| peak heap | **0 B** — the fold is in place, in the shell's own copy of the entry |
| stack | **+12 B** — `sink_begin` 400 → 412 B; `ExtractOne`, the largest frame in the shell, unchanged at 1,484 B |
| engine ticks | **0** — the fold does not run at all unless the format set the flag, and then it is one pass over ≤255 bytes per entry |

**896 B off every extraction's budget on a 1 MB Mac Plus, worth
taking**: 0.14 % of 648,100 B, against 5,988 B for the overlay judged not
worth it, and nothing in the corpus has been out of that machine's reach
since 2026-09-18. It buys real names for 4 of the 31 StuffIt 5 archives
here. No converter reaches System 3.0 (Script Manager's is System 7.1,
the Unicode Converter Mac OS 8.5), so a table is the only route; moving
it to a resource to save 256 B of A5 is the mechanism the overlay
decision declined at twenty times the prize.

**No specimen, stated not measured**: a byte not beginning a valid UTF-8
sequence passes through as itself (MacRoman, as before the fold). All
525 entries of the 31 StuffIt 5 fixtures are valid UTF-8.

**Grading.** The ENGINE flag: `run_diff.py` over the corpus's StuffIt 5
archives, names included. The SHELL fold: `mac_sink_test.c --utf8` via
`tools/run_macnames.py`, straight through `sink_begin` like `--cancel`
(nothing here writes StuffIt 5), on **big-endian m68k under qemu** as
well as natively. Both in `ci.sh`. Made to fail first: fold disabled
gives mojibake on disk, no report lines, and the 32-byte name cut at 31.

## 2026-09-22 (the version that could not have written it) — the DiskDoubler the `0x20` row was waiting for does not exist

**Claim.** The last open row of `fmt_dd.c` — the `DDAR` record's `0x20`
flag, which says the two forks follow raw — was recorded as closable by
"a 1.x or 2.x DiskDoubler, neither of which is reachable from here"
(OPEN_ITEMS.md and `docs/formats/diskdoubler-container.md`, both written
earlier the same day). **A 2.x DiskDoubler could not have written a
`DDAR` record of any flags**, so finding one would have settled nothing.
Withdrawn in BLOCKERS.md.

**The search.** Macintosh Garden (where `diskdoubler.py --setup` fetches
3.7) has two DiskDoubler application pages, 3.7 and 4.0, and the
collection `apps/disk-doubler`: five downloads, four EXPANDERS and one
INIT, no 1.x or 2.x compressor. The thread asking for exactly those two
was posted in 2010 by **balrog, XADMaster's own author** ("DiskDoubler
1.x (I have 1.0) DiskDoubler 2.x", "to generate test cases"). The rule
this row cites is that lineage's, and the lineage did not have the file
either.

**The disproof is in the expanders' `BNDL`, and took no emulator.**

| | declares |
|---|---|
| DDExpand 2.03a, 1990 | `DD01`, `DDDA`, `DD02`, `DDTM`, `DDSP` |
| DDExpand 3.1 | those five, plus `DDAR`, `DDTD`, `DDCR` and `DDF0`–`DDF5` |

`DDAR` does not occur in 2.03a's 65,212-byte resource fork; 3.1 holds it
nine times, six as a `cmpi.l` immediate. **A version's own expander not
knowing the type is that version not writing it** — an inference, labelled
as one, but the only reading under which Salient did not ship an expander
unable to open its own archives. So the flag can only come from 3.x, 4.0
or Pro 4.1, which all run here already, and the five shapes offered to

project had called the oldest, and the first COMPRESSOR older than 3.7.
