`Compress Selection;Expand Selection;(-;About DiskDoubler`, and no `DDAR`
is in the file.

**Mechanism, already on the list:** *a search that names the wrong tool*
(BLOCKERS.md, added 2026-08-25 for PKARC) — the row named a VERSION
rather than a shape, on the strength of which version XADMaster's author
owned. **Cost: nothing yet**; what it would have cost is the next
session's search for a 2.x compressor whose output has no `DDAR` record.

## 2026-09-22 (the fold, on a Macintosh) — the UTF-8 fold's first run on a real Mac, and the name that is not composed

**Claim.** The fold shipped that morning (*a name an HFS volume can hold*)
had never run on a Macintosh: no fixture in `tools/vmac/sample.txt` had a
non-ASCII StuffIt 5 name. Two fixtures put it there:
`derived-Cool_Tools__.sit` (`Cool Tools ƒ`, two UTF-8 bytes folding to
MacRoman `0xC4`) and `derived-800saywhat301j.sit` (three Japanese names,
each code point becoming `_`).

**The first cannot fail the harness.** `checkdisk.py` compares
CHARACTERS, so a name MacRoman can spell matches whether the harness folds
or not: with the fold disabled `derived-Cool_Tools__.sit` passes and only
`derived-800saywhat301j.sit` fails (three MISSING, three UNEXPECTED). A
fixture chosen for a feature is not automatically a test of it.

**`run.py` was never going to catch it, though TESTING.md said it would**:
its verdict is a file count, two summed CRC-32s and two summed lengths,
and a summed CRC cannot carry a name. Withdrawn in BLOCKERS.md; the
harness that needed teaching was `checkdisk.py` (`tools/vmac_check.py`,
`mac_component`).

**The name the archive states is DECOMPOSED.** `ユーザーライセンスの購入.rtf`
is thirteen code points (`ザ` = `サ` + U+3099), so the Macintosh writes
**thirteen** `_`. The oracle manifests hold `lsar`'s composed spelling;
`run_diff.py` normalizes both sides to NFC and never could see the
difference. `checkdisk.py` normalized the reference PATH, so it opened a
file that does not exist and compared a fork against zero bytes. It folds
before it normalizes now. **The engine was right; both harnesses read it
through a filter that removed the evidence.**

**Sweeps.** 71/71 on System 6.0.8 at 4 MB and 1 MB, 71/71 on System 3.0
at 1 MB, 67/71 and 64/71 on a 512 KB 512Ke under System 3.0 and System
6.0.8. **No refusal moved**: the two 512 KB tiers each gained exactly
`derived-Cool_Tools__.sit` (its StuffIt 5 block needs 242,464 B).
`checkdisk.py` read all 73 kept Out volumes byte-exact with names.

**Every budget constant was stale, and the freshest the worst.** Budgets
(`FreeMem() - 20,480`) had not been re-taken since 2026-08-31. Re-taken:
**648,282 B** at the 1 MB floor (668,762 free), **219,394 B** on the
512Ke under System 3.0 (239,874), **123,994 B** under System 6.0.8
(144,474). The small two had drifted 21,666 B each; the floor 182 B, made
worse by subtracting 896 B for the fold from a three-week-old base.
**A constant derived from a measurement is only as current as the
measurement, and subtracting from a stale one looks like maintenance.**
With all three re-taken, `tools/run_tiers.py` reproduces **all three
tiers fixture for fixture**, including System 6.0.8 / 512 KB, which
TESTING.md had filed under fragmentation; it was the budget, and that
tier is asserted now.

**The report line is photographed and asserted** (`interactive.py
--report-utf8`): three *"`_______` was named in characters this Macintosh
cannot write"* lines over *"Extraction complete."*; a control expecting
the composed twelve `_` fails it.

**Worked around, not explained, that day:** a report saved to the BOOT
volume after this extraction cannot be read off the image (a 30 s flush
wait, Control-Q, SIGTERM and `FlushVol` did not help); the phase saves to
a floppy. The recorded hypothesis was reduced the same day and is wrong in
its load-bearing half — the BYTES are on the image, the CATALOG ENTRY is
not (*the file that was on the disk and not in the catalog*, below). A
harness limitation, not the application's: the same fold is graded off
the Out volume by `checkdisk.py` on every sweep.

**A harness bug that cost a sweep.** `sys30.py` called `_origin()` whether
or not the window appeared, so a window that never came up died with a
`TypeError` at fixture 70 of 71, taking the tally with it. It says NOGRID
now.

**The other two harnesses that predict a Mac name, taught the same day;
the ORDER (fold, then normalize) is the whole fix.**

- **`tools/check_mac_sink.py` (the `ci.sh` layer)** knew nothing of the
  fold, and `tests/run_mac_sink.sh` held no UTF-8 fixture.
  `derived-800saywhat301j.sit` joins that list (run **big-endian under
  `qemu-m68k`** and native), and the checker puts the manifest name
  through `vmac_check.mac_component`. Measured over all 31 StuffIt 5
  fixtures: 27 non-ASCII names, and both where NFC and NFD differ are
  stored decomposed. Established that it can fail: fold off, three
  MISSING; NFC instead of NFD, exactly the two decomposed names, 12 `_`
  against 13 and 6 against 7.
- **`tools/vmac/os9.py`**: `mac_leaf`'s docstring had labelled the bug as
  latent. With a fixture it predicts `____________.rtf` where the Mac
  writes `_____________.rtf`, and keeps NFC reference paths that do not
  exist — `checkdisk.py`'s bug exactly. Same fix: fold, normalize the
  KEY, keep the VALUE unnormalized. In `os9sample.txt` now: **19 files,
  23 forks byte-exact, `Icon\r` included**.

**The Mac OS 9 walk also could not SEE two things.** The first run
reported `800-SAY-WHAT 3.0.1J/Icon\r` MISSING while the file (51,781
bytes of resource fork, `icon`/`MACS`, invisible) was on the volume:
`hls` omits invisible files without **`-a`** (four entries without, five
with), and `_walk_volume`'s `rstrip()` removed the CR from `Icon\r`.
`checkdisk.py` has had both rules since it was written. **A harness
written twice means only one copy learns anything.** And **a label is not
a fix**: `mac_leaf`'s docstring named this defect and its one-line fix;
what kept it open was that nothing on that tier could fail.

## 2026-09-22 (the magic that was a length) — DiskDoubler ß05, 1990, and the three things the 84-byte header was hiding

**Claim.** `0xABCD0054` is not a magic number: it is the word `0xABCD`
and a 16-bit **header size**, unknown here because all 195 file headers
in the corpus state 84. `DiskDoubler ß05, Copyright 1990 Salient` states
**48**, laid out field for field like the first 48 of the 84. Measured by
running it: `tools/vmac/diskdoubler.py --beta`.

**Why a boot.** `docs/formats/diskdoubler-container.md` was measured on
3.7, 4.0 and Pro 4.1 — one generation, 1992 and later. ß05 came out of
the same day's search (*the version that could not have written it*).

**What it wrote** (11,428-byte data fork, 340-byte resource fork), against
3.7 on the same subject:

| | ß05, 1990 | 3.7, 1992 |
|---|---|---|
| first long | `ab cd 00 30` | `ab cd 00 54` |
| lengths | 11,428 → 1,697, 340 → 97 | the same four numbers |
| `info1` at +22 | `0x1f` | `0x2a` |
| checksums at +48 | **the header has ended** | `d766` / `116a` |
| the data fork begins | `1f 9d 90` | `45 c7 ca` |
| after the two forks | nothing | a byte-identical copy of the header |
| the file is stamped | `ZIVM`/`LZIV` | `DD01`/`DDAP` |

- **The header trailer is 3.x's, not the format's.** 63 of the corpus's
  66 compressed files end with a header copy (the three that do not are
  our synthetics); 1990 writes none: `48 + 1697 + 97 = 1842`, the file
  size.
- **`DD01` is not what ß05 stamps** (`ZIVM`/`LZIV`; its `BNDL` declares
  only its `INIT`), so `DD01`/`DD02` are 3.x's, where `DDExpand 2.03a`
  and 3.1 list them.
- **`info1` is a version byte, and XOR garbling is gated on it.** ß05's
  `0x1f` leaves `compress(1)`'s `1f 9d 90` in clear where 3.7's is XORed
  with `0x5a`. `>=` is still not distinguished from `==` (0x1f fails
  both).
- **The 1990 validator reads the size as a size** (its `CCOD`): word
  `0xABCD`, value at +2 **≥ 48**, `info1` **≤ 31** — a program expecting
  its header to grow.

**Graded against the bytes DiskDoubler was given**: neither this engine
nor `unar` opened a 48-byte header, so `--beta-verify` sets the size to
84, computes each fork's checksum from the input, and hands that to the
engine. Both forks byte-exact, and the computed sums `0xd766` and
`0x116a` are the two 3.7 itself stored. Established that it can fail: a
flipped payload byte and a header read as 84 bytes both fail the entry.

**Not done, as a decision:** the engine still refused a 1990 file
(OPEN_ITEMS.md, *A DiskDoubler header this engine does not read*).
(superseded: DECISIONS.md 2026-09-22, *the header that was a length*.)

**Doc defect found on the way.** The `DDAR` record table gave Finder flags
at **+94** and no creator; `src/fmt_dd.c` reads them at +98 and the
creator at +94, as do `derive_ddc.py` (`R_CREATOR, R_FLAGS = 94, 98`) and
macutils' `dd.h` (`D_FNDRFLAGS 98`). Corrected in place. **A field nothing
reads is where a document rots.**

**Cost: two emulator boots** (one to measure `BETA_MENU_X`), no source
change.

## 2026-09-22 (the right flag with the wrong reason) — what `hls -a` is actually for, and the four walks that believed the explanation

**Claim.** `hls` hides a file whose Finder **INVISIBLE** bit is set unless
given `-a`. It does not hide dot-names, which `checkdisk.py`'s comment and
`tools/vmac/README.md` had both said. Withdrawn in BLOCKERS.md.

**Measured as a 2×2:**

| | leading dot | invisible bit | `hls -1` | `hls -a -1` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.quiet` | yes | no | shown | shown |
| `.loud` | yes | **yes** | **HIDDEN** | shown |
| `Open` | no | no | shown | shown |
| `Shut` | no | **yes** | **HIDDEN** | shown |

`.DS_Store` needed `-a` because a Macintosh writes it invisible: the flag
was right, only the reason was wrong.

**The reason is what propagates.** "hfsutils hides dotfiles" reads as
*irrelevant unless your archive has a `.DS_Store`*, and four later walks
skipped the flag on that reasoning; `os9.py`, the fifth, failed (*the
fold, on a Macintosh*). New smell: *a correct workaround with the wrong
reason attached* — every symptom is in some other harness that read the
comment.

**`tools/vmac/walkprobe.py` makes it executable**: one volume with plain,
invisible, dotted-bit-clear and `Icon\r` subjects, every walk run against
it, no emulator, seconds. `checkdisk.walk` 4/4, `os9._walk_volume` 4/4,
`arcmac.read_volume`, `nowcompress.read_volume`,
`diskdoubler.volume_files` and `superdisk.read_forks` **2/4 each**.
`--check` fails in both directions (established both ways). Corrected the
same day to five of EIGHT (*the column that was already on the volume*,
below).

**Two `os9.py` listings fixed on the spot** because `-a` can only make
them harder to pass: `wrapper_names` (a NEGATIVE) and `report_present` (a
poll, where a miss is a timeout).

**The other four left, as a measurement:** `superdisk.read_forks` had
about thirty callers across nine harnesses, and `-a` also surfaces the
Finder's `Desktop`, `Desktop DB`, `Desktop DF`, which a fork-set
comparison would fail on. (Done later: *the last walk, and the exit code
nobody could get*, below.)

**The same fact had been observed FOUR times and generalised none:**
`checkdisk.py`'s `-a` (explained as dotfiles); `arcmac.macbinary`'s
"bit 0x40 … `invisible`" (actually `fHasBundle`, withdrawn below); the
yardstick's Standard File row taken on the wrong file for three weeks
because the Finder's `Desktop` "is invisible to `hdir`"; and
`mkboot.strip_system_folder` stating the rule exactly right one function
above a comment blaming leftover folders on valence — the two survivors
were `Icon\r`. `hdir` behaves exactly as `hls`: both hide the bit, both
take `-a`.

**The check guarding the boot image could not fail.** `verify_stripped()`
(System Folder holds only System and Finder) listed WITHOUT `-a`, so the
files the strip cannot delete were exactly the ones it could not see.
Demonstrated: an invisible `Ghost INIT` leaves `ls(invisible=False)`
returning `['Finder', 'System']`; with `-a` the check raises. None of the
four boot images holds an invisible file, so this GAINED the ability to
fail rather than uncovered a failure. `ls()` takes the flag as a
parameter, because `strip_system_folder` deletes what it returns and
`Desktop` is sometimes kept on purpose (`drop_desktop`, BLOCKERS.md).
Verified: `run.py` 1/1 PASS.

## 2026-09-22 (the header that was a length) — a DiskDoubler file neither reader could open, for 64 bytes

**Claim.** The engine reads a 1990 DiskDoubler file: the parser takes the
header size off +2 instead of matching a 32-bit constant, and fields past
the stated size are read as absent. Graded against the bytes DiskDoubler
was given: **both forks byte-exact**, listed as `TEXT`/`ttxt` with both
lengths right. `unar` still answers *"format not recognized"*.

**Fields past +47 do nothing**: a short header is zero-filled to the
84-byte struct, and every consumer already handles zero — a zero checksum
is the *"very old file"* case the sniffer has accepted since M12
(macutils' comment says so), zero delta distances mean no delta, and
`info1` `0x1f` with `info2` 0 leaves `dd_xorval()` at 0. **No branch
elsewhere in the format changed.**

**Two sizes, not a range.** ß05's validator accepts ≥ 48, but only 48 and
84 have a specimen; taking exactly two makes each a **whole 32-bit
constant**, and is cheaper:

| | code | A5 | budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| word + range + length pairs | +144 B | +16 B | 160 B |
| two 32-bit magics | **+48 B** | +16 B | **64 B** |

`fmt_dd.c` 8,888 → 8,918 text, `fmt_stubs.c` 1,057 → 1,073, zero data
both times: the 16 B of A5 is rodata alignment (as on 2026-09-19 and
2026-09-20). Both ratchets raised in `tools/build_mac.sh` with that
attribution. **Third time a constant was cheaper constrained than stored**
(2026-09-01 *two byte reads*, 2026-09-09 DART's type table): on a 68000
an immediate is free, so *narrowing* what you accept often costs less than
*generalising*.

**What grades it.** No corpus fixture has a 48-byte header and none can
(the only specimen is `diskdoubler.py --beta`'s), so `--beta-verify` is
the whole byte-level grade. `ci.sh` carries the CONTAINER as a unit test
with stored forks and two negative controls — size 47 (below ß05's floor)
and 60 (accepted by ß05, layout unknown), both must sniff UNKNOWN. The
test fails 7 of its checks against the unchanged engine.

**The budget moved 32 B, not 64.** All three re-taken with `-D
UNC_AT_BUDGET`: 648,282 → 648,250 at the 1 MB floor, 219,394 → 219,362
and 123,994 → 123,962 on the 512Ke. The gap is recorded, not explained
(a `CODE` handle and a rounded A5 world can absorb tens of bytes). **The
measurement is the number; the arithmetic only says when to take one.**
`run_tiers.py` reproduces 71/71, 67/71, 64/71 unchanged, and the
Macintosh agrees: **71/71 at 4 MB and 71/71 at the 1 MB floor** on System
6.0.8.

## 2026-09-22 (the file that was on the disk and not in the catalog) — a hypothesis about flushing, reduced to a reproduction

**Claim.** The hypothesis *"300 KB across a seven-deep tree grows the
catalog, and what is written after that does not reach the image"* is
wrong in its load-bearing half: **the bytes reach the image; the catalog
entry does not.** Measured by `--utf8-to-boot` (this phase without the
volume switch, image read twice):

| reading | answer |
|---|---|
| the extraction's 300 KB of output, in the volume's catalog | **YES** — `800-SAY-WHAT 3.0.1J`, five entries, `Icon\r` included |
| the report, in the volume's catalog | **NO** |
| the report's TEXT, in the image's blocks | **YES** — the three `_` lines and `Extraction complete.`, in order, complete |

The File Manager lays a fork's blocks down, then records the entry, and
the run ends between the two — which is why four remedies aimed at the
write (30 s wait, Control-Q, SIGTERM, `FlushVol`) did nothing.

**The needle was its own trap.** `Extraction Report` is `SFPutFile`'s
default name and so is in the application's resources on the same volume:
a raw search answers YES regardless, and the first probe reported a pass
that way. The working reading searches blocks for a string only the SAVED
document holds (`_______ was named in characters`, one hit) and the
CATALOG for the name. **A search for a name finds every copy of that
name.**

The floppy workaround stays, as a sidestep of a known thing. Which layer
holds the lost update: *the entry a second write placed*, below.

## 2026-09-22 (the entry a second write placed) — the lost catalog update was unflushed, not lost

**Claim.** The missing catalog entry is not destroyed. **One more write to
the same volume places it**: `--utf8-second` saves the report again as
`Second`, and both entries are in the catalog (`utf8-3b`/`utf8-3c`
photograph `Extraction Report` in Standard File's listing), where the
identical run without it reads NO.

**Rules out a fixed tail** (Mini vMac's buffered stdio losing the last N
bytes): both entries share a catalog leaf, so both should then be missing.
Not elapsed time either — this run's `FLUSH_WAIT` is the same 30 s already
measured useless.

**Labelled.** MEASURED: a second B*-tree operation suffices to place the
first entry. HYPOTHESIS: the File Manager holds the dirty catalog block in
the guest's volume cache and the next tree operation writes it. Nothing
depends on which; `--utf8-second` would notice a change.

**Transferable.** "The last thing is lost" and "the last thing is not yet
written" look identical from outside and are fixed by opposite things.
Discriminator: do the thing again and see whether the earlier one appears.

## 2026-09-23 (hardware decoding) — an FPU cannot help a bit shuffler, and the formats answered the CPU question themselves

**Claim.** Hardware acceleration — FPU, coprocessor, NuBus codec card — is
out of scope: there is no measured work for one to take. OPEN_ITEMS.md
Part 1.

**The one FP-shaped operation is priced at 0.72 %.** No float in `src/`;
Arsenic's range coder does two 32÷32 divides per symbol, measured at
**0.72 %** of the ISBN run against **9.9 %** for the linear symbol search
beside them (FORMATS.md, *What is still hot*).

**Ask whether the hardware offering the shortcut is the hardware that
needs it.** A 68881 implies a 68020+, which has native `DIVU.L`; the
68000, where the software divide costs, has no FPU. PowerPC Macs run this
binary through the **68LC040** emulator (FORMATS.md, *Mac OS 9 tier*),
which has none either. And no tier here could execute an FPU path (Mini
vMac is a 68000; the OS 9 tier's CPU has no FPU).

**The formats already solved CPU dispatch in the direction that leaves a
decoder alone.** SpaceSaver and DiskDoubler gate COMPRESSORS on a `CMod`
mask at +0x24 (index 4 for 68000–68020, 3 for 68030+, 15 for PowerPC) and
give each a **decompress-only twin that accepts every CPU** (FORMATS.md,
the SpaceSaver module table). All of those are implemented.

**Unverified, from memory, not load-bearing:** classic-Mac "hardware
codec" meant media codecs (C-Cube CL550 NuBus cards as a QuickTime
`'jpeg'` component), and the AV Quadras' DSP3210 is a floating-point DSP,
a poor fit for serial Huffman.

**Adjacent trade, not open:** a second `-mcpu=68020` build would drop
libgcc's `__mulsi3`/`__divsi3` (~4 % of an Arsenic run per
`sit_arsenic.c`), but it is a second binary the floor machine cannot run,
against a `CODE` size load-bearing at 142,152 B then (54,340 B resident
since the overlays; 2026-10-06, *the wall the overlays had already moved*),
and **this machine cannot price it** — the tick probe is an emulated Mac
Plus.

## 2026-09-23 (the block that was bigger than its fork) — a Now Compress stored block read past its output buffer, and the check that was one clause

**Claim.** A crafted Now Compress archive overran the heap in
`now_next_block` (`src/fmt_now.c`). Found reviewing the XADMaster-shedding
work, not introduced by it.

**Evidence, under ASan.** A 20,158-byte file — one entry declaring a
40-byte data fork, one 20,000-byte stored block, block-table checksum
matching (built from `tools/synth_now.py`'s `build_table`/`entry_record`)
— gives `heap-buffer-overflow ... WRITE of size 20000` at the stored
path's `unc_read_full`.

**Root cause.** A block's compressed length was checked only against
`incap` (`NOW_INBLOCK`, 32 KB), right for the three shapes staging input
in `st->inblock`. The STORED and Huffman-then-LZSS (`0x20|0x1f`) shapes
stage it in `outstart`, whose room `blkcap` is sized from the DECLARED
fork (`min(maxout, 0x8000)`): 19,960 bytes past the allocation.

**Fix, one clause per path:** `if (length > st->blkcap) return
UNC_ERR_CORRUPT;`. A valid stored block's output IS its length, so no
valid file is refused: the 946 fixtures extract byte-identically, and the
three real Now archives pass under ASan.

**Why the fuzzer never found it.** `now_check_table`'s byte-sum checksum
refuses every byte-flipped mutant before the read. The regression test is
CONSTRUCTED: `run_now.py`'s `check_refusals` builds oversized stored and
hufflzss blocks and asserts refusal, under the ASan build in `ci.sh`
variant 1.

**Transferable.** *A bound that is right for most callers is not a
bound* — the shared check was sufficient three times out of five. And
"the robustness suite is green" measured the checksum guard, not the
buffer bound.

## 2026-09-23 (the tables that were the standard's) — DES's constants came from a file with no licence, and the standard itself was one fetch away

**The claim that failed.** OPEN_ITEMS.md's `unc_crypt.c` row called its
five `Crypto/` files "public-domain or permissive". Four are (`md5.c`
Solar Designer, public domain; `sha.c` and `hmac_sha1.c` Aaron Gifford,
BSD-3; `aeskey.c` Gladman). **`des.c` states nothing** — 482 lines, only
"Stuart Levy, Minnesota Supercomputer Center, April 1988" — and so takes
the tree's LGPL.

**What was taken from it was not code**: six tables (PC-1 as
`bK_C`/`bK_D`, PC-2 as `bCD_KS`, `preshift`, `S`, `P`) plus IP from its
prose — all published constants of FIPS 46-3.

**The standard is one fetch**: `csrc.nist.gov` serves FIPS 46-3 (the
1999-10-25 reaffirmation, 468 KB PDF). No `pdftotext`/`pypdf` needed: the
streams are Flate, so `zlib` plus a regex yields all thirteen tables.

**The method worth keeping.** PDF text has no inter-glyph kerning, so
entries arrive split (PC-1's `43` as `4 3`). **Each table is a
permutation of a known set over a known span** (whole table, or each row
of sixteen for the S boxes), so re-segmenting under that constraint has
one solution, and the generator asserts uniqueness. Two limits:

- **The shift schedule** repeats values, so it is checked by its
  ITERATION column (1..16 in order) with shifts asserted in {1, 2}.
- **A table may stop before its digit run does**: S4's run ends with a
  stray page number `18`. Leftovers are allowed, but **no leftover may be
  a legal value of the table**.

**Price.** The regenerated `src/crypt_tables.h` is **byte for byte
identical** (all 1,712 values), so `CODE`, A5, peak RAM and ticks cannot
move — identity, no build needed. `tools/gen_crypt_tables.py` 325 → 388
lines and 0.035 s → 0.060 s; the header gains six lines of provenance.

**Two new checks**: published IP^-1 equals the inverse of IP, and
published IP equals the one reconstructed from des.c's prose (previously
resting only on the DES known-answer test in `tests/unit_formats.c`).

**The first cut was 50 % bigger and made fewer checks** (115 lines,
0.172 s, a widening-retry loop). Scoping distinctness per row deleted the
loop. *A special case that exists to absorb junk is usually a missing
constraint.*

**The licence does not move.** `src/unc_crypt.c` named twelve XADMaster
files; eleven remain, including the StuffItDES nibble key schedule and
derivation (in no published document) and PackIt's keytr1.
`XADStuffItDESHandle.m` is read only to CHECK that `DES_SPtrans` is the
standard SP table relabelled.

## 2026-09-23 (the third statement of the same constants) — MD5's tables were RFC 1321's all along, and the AES S box was already ours

**MD5.** The generator pulled 192 numbers (message-word index, rotation,
constant) from XADMaster's `Crypto/md5.c`; every one is in RFC 1321's
reference implementation (64 `FF/GG/HH/II` calls, `#define S11 7`-style
macros). Plain text: +24 lines, `src/crypt_tables.h` byte-identical. The
RFC states T[i] twice — as 4294967296 × abs(sin(i)) and as 64 literals —
and the generator asserts the literals reproduce the sines. `md5.c` is
still read, only to agree.

**The AES S box needed no source.** `aes_sbox()` extracted `sb_data` from
`Crypto/aestab.c`, BUILT the same 256 bytes from FIPS-197 (GF(2^8)
inverse, affine map), asserted equality, and returned the extracted copy.
Returning `built` changes no byte.

**Together:** `src/crypt_tables.h` contains **nothing derived from
XADMaster** (DES from FIPS 46-3, MD5 from RFC 1321, AES S box from
FIPS-197, Compact Pro's CRC-64 from the application, 2026-08-23). The
LICENCE does not move — `src/unc_crypt.c` still names ten XADMaster
files, the StuffItDES key schedule and PackIt's keytr1 among them.

**Transferable.** *A check that has been promoted to a source is
invisible, because it passes.* Found by reading the function for another
question, as `des.c`'s missing licence was.

## 2026-09-23 (the ciphers nothing had ever fuzzed) — two instruments lied about coverage, and a planted fault settled it

**The gap.** `tools/fuzz.py` ran `macextract t` with no password, refused
at `unc_password` before any key schedule: **no mutation could reach
`src/unc_crypt.c`** — 9,320 robustness variants and 4,000 fuzz cases had
never executed the eight ciphers.

**Two cheap instruments lied.** Scoring "exit 0 or printed *password*"
gave `sit-des` 31/40; truth is 0 (`t` exits 0 having decrypted nothing).
Ground truth: PLANT a fault (a four-byte stack array written at index 4)
in each key setup and count UBSan trips. The first planted fault was a
no-op (`fault[pwlen & 7]` with a nine-character password writes index 1):
*a fault injection is a test too, and has to be shown to fire.*

**Result.** `t` never descends into a StuffIt's MacBinary, so crypt cases
EXTRACT. Under `x`, out of 30 each: StuffIt classic DES 19, StuffIt 5 RC4
21, PackIt XOR and DES 0 (stated cause: header CRC fails before a key —
withdrawn 2026-09-26, *the guard that was on the other side*).

**One to four bit flips**, measured over 80 cases per setting: reaching
key setup 9 at 1..64 edits, 24 at 1..8, **35 at 1..4**, 25 at 1..2. The
crypt generator is its own mutator and takes a quarter of the run (four
encrypted seeds in ~950 fixtures would be drawn about half a time in 150
cases).

**Transferable.** *A coverage claim needs an instrument that can tell
"ran and passed" from "never ran".* Third instance: the result grid that
could not fail on a name, the Now checksum that kept mutants from the
buggy read, a password prompt keeping mutants from the ciphers — a GUARD
in front of the code. Get past it deliberately, then prove you did.

## 2026-09-23 (the ten kilobytes nothing watched) — the application grew 5.7 % in a month, and the only reason it cost nothing is luck

**Observation.** The SHIPPED binary went 178,560 B (2026-08-28) to
188,672 B — **+10,112 B, +5.7 %** (per-object sums, 116,432 B against a
documented 92,580, overstate it: `--gc-sections`).

**Where it went** (2026-08-24 tree rebuilt, same flags): six new files
16,926 B — `fmt_mime` 7,128, `unc_lzdyn` 3,216, `fmt_b64` 2,040,
`fmt_dart` 2,006, `fmt_mimeseg` 1,344, `fmt_foreign` 1,192 — plus
existing decoders gaining methods (`fmt_spacesaver` +3,906, `fmt_arc`
+3,092, `unc_util` +1,904, `fmt_exo` +1,190). Capability, not drift.

**Cost, measured by moving the BUDGET in `run_tiers.py`.** At budgets
10,112 B larger, tallies unchanged (71, 67, 64): **the month cost no
fixture.** At budgets 10,112 B smaller, System 6.0.8 / 512 KB drops 64 to
63; `derived-LHA_Expander_1.0.3.sea` flips between 116,694 and 117,010
against that tier's 123,962: **6,952 B of headroom**. Hence
`tools/check_app_size.py`'s 2,048 B tolerance — three deliberate
acknowledgements before a tier loses a fixture.

**The heap did not grow with the code**: peak heap is per ENTRY. The
month's formats peak at 5 KB (base64), 8 KB (MIME), 24.6–34.1 KB (DART),
against an existing 396 KB maximum.

**Transferable.** *A budget derived from the binary goes stale every time
the binary does, silently.* What was missing was a TRIPWIRE; the docs'
own figure had been wrong for four days. A number nothing compares is a
number nothing defends.

## 2026-09-23 (the 3,504 bytes that stay) — `-lh2-`/`-lh3-` were settled on 2026-08-25, and an inventory re-opened them on one axis

**Not an open decision, and treating it as one is the finding.** `-lh2-`
and `-lh3-` were settled on **2026-08-25** by building what grades them (a
patched LHa writing `-lh2-`, an `-lh3-` encoder, 21 entries in `ci.sh`).
`src/unc_lzdyn.c` stays. The 2026-09-20 shedding inventory (OPEN_ITEMS.md,
*What is still XADMaster's*) priced its removal and wrote **"the decision
is the maintainer's; nothing here will take it"**, re-opening it on one
axis.

**Cost, re-measured 2026-09-23:** 3,476 B `CODE` + 28 B A5 = **3,504 B**
(153,256/37,960 against 149,780/37,932, `m68k-apple-macos-size`) — the
2026-09-20 total to the byte, split moved 4 B (rodata alignment). Half
the 6,952 B tightest-tier headroom (*the ten kilobytes nothing watched*).

**What buys it back is that the file is reachable.** "No corpus archive
uses them" is not "nobody can hand you one": `tools/build_lha_lh2.sh`
makes LHa for UNIX write `-lh2-`, `tools/run_lzh.py` writes `-lh3-`, and
`ci.sh` grades 15 and 6 entries every run. A `.lzh` on a classic Mac
travelled from a PC, Amiga or Japanese desktop — the case an unarchiver
exists for.

**Consequence.** That row can never close on its own terms: the other
reference is LHa for UNIX's own licence and lhasa implements neither
method, so the LGPL stays for this file. Keeping the code is also deciding
the licence is not reachable by shedding alone.

**Transferable.** *An inventory built for one axis will re-open decisions
settled on another without knowing it.* **A row that ends "the decision is
X's" has converted a measurement into an open item, and should say what
changed since the decision was last taken.** Here nothing had; the row
quoted the corpus and never `ci.sh`.

**Swept the other rows the same day.** One repeat: *What WinZip's AES
costs a Macintosh Plus* (2,150 B, "the maintainer's call"), settled
2026-08-23 by the commit adding it; `ci.sh` grades four AES configurations
on **7-Zip**-written fixtures. Fixed in place. Three pass: **PKZIP Implode
is the model** (names what changed: an MIT implementation and a
stored-CRC oracle for all 7 entries arrived 2026-09-22); `fmt_arc.c`'s
Crunch 5/6/7 is a decision taken and dated (2026-09-22); the
`selective-extract` branch was genuinely open, never shipped.

## 2026-09-25 (the parked decision that outlived its numbers) — a scope answer re-read as settled while its evidence grew seventeenfold

**Claim: the overlay decision of 2026-08-31 still landed the same way,
and none of its three premises survived.** Asked because somebody proposed
making `overlay-eager` the default; answered by reading the branch.
(superseded the same day: DECISIONS.md 2026-09-25, *two branches that
were one file apart*.)

- **The prize was 5,988 B and is 84–103 KB.** That was the ciphers as one
  image; the branch had **fifteen** since 2026-09-24. At 1 MB on System
  6.0.8 it grants 734,656 B for a StuffIt 5, 752,898 B for an LZH and
  746,682 B for a Compact Pro, against 650,692 B all-resident; the
  resident column does not move with the archive.
- **"Neither branch OPENS anything new" is withdrawn.** System 3.0 at
  512 KB is **69/71 against main's 67/71**: `derived-a2basic.dmg.sit` and
  `derived-Cool_Tools__.sit` (needing `MoveHHi` and twelve more images).
- **"StuffIt can never be one of the formats it helps"** was a fact about
  the CIPHER image: a StuffIt 5 gains 84 KB too; what it cannot release is
  the ciphers, **10,702 B** (down from 15,748 B after 2026-09-19, the
  transient tables).
- **The download grows more than recorded**: `MacExtract.bin` **189,312 B
  against 214,528 B, +25,216 B** (not +2,304 B).

**Consequence then:** answer unchanged for new reasons — nothing in the
corpus had been out of a 1 MB Mac Plus's reach since 2026-09-18, no tier
above a 68000 had run the configuration, no Linux suite exercised the
loader, and it cost 13 % of the download. OPEN_ITEMS.md, Part 1,
*Overlays*.

### The transferable part: parking a decision does not park the work it was about

The 2026-08-31 entry's own line — *"a figure that cannot change the
conclusion is a figure nothing checks"* — held for three weeks as the
prize grew seventeenfold. **A decision parks and a BRANCH does not**:
sessions wrote findings to the branch's `BRANCH_NOTES.md`, correctly, and
nothing reached `main`, whose status file kept quoting the parking number.

**Caught by the cheapest smell: three files, three numbers** — BRANCHES.md
18,116 B, OPEN_ITEMS.md 5,988 B, the branch neither; readable on `main`
since 2026-09-02. **A parked decision needs its re-read trigger where the
NUMBER lives**: BRANCHES.md rows now carry the figure and its date.

## 2026-09-25 (the skip that could not fire, again) — `./ci.sh` deleted what its first check needs, and the guard for that was a tuple

**Claim: a second `./ci.sh` on an untouched tree failed its first check.**
`make clean` (`rm -rf build/`) takes `build/btoa`; `check_docs.py` then
regenerates the `synth-os9-btoa` row of `fixtures/SOURCES.md` via
`tools/synth_os9.py --kind btoa`, which needs it.

**Cause.** `run_btoa.build()` returns `(ok, why)` (split 2026-09-09). Both
callers tested the TUPLE — `if not run_btoa.build():` in
`tools/synth_os9.py`, `if RB.build():` in `tools/vmac/sitcrypt.py` — and
a 2-tuple is never falsy. The result was a `FileNotFoundError` reported as
*"cannot be restored"* instead of *"generator unavailable here — row not
checked"*.

**Consequence.** Both test the first element: with `build/btoa` deleted
the reference recompiles; with no `reference/btoa`, exit 3 and the row is
reported unchecked.

**Transferable.** **A return type that grows needs its callers re-read,
because widening one is not a change the language reports.** So
`tools/check_tuple_truth.py` fails the build when a function whose every
`return` is a tuple is tested for truthiness; it found these two and no
third, and carries the pre-fix pair as a selftest (TESTING.md, check 0b).

## 2026-09-25 (the flush nobody wrote, and the alarm nobody could read) — the documented rule was not the toolchain's, and a diagnostic that fires when nothing is wrong

**Claim: `overlay-eager` relocated executable bytes at two sites and
flushed no cache; whether it mattered was carried as a hypothesis waiting
for hardware when it was waiting for a document.** Both fixes are in
`mac/ovl_reloc.c` (FORMATS.md, *Overlays*).

**Inside Macintosh: Memory, ch. 4, *Stale Instructions***: "you must flush
the instruction cache every time you modify executable instructions in
memory"; `_BlockMove`, `_Read`, `_LoadSeg`, `_UnloadSeg` do it for you —
`BlockMoveData`, which the shim used, does not.

**The toolchain's answer was not the documented one.** Retro68's
relocator calls `FlushCodeCache` (0xA0BD). Inside Macintosh documents
`FlushInstructionCache` as `_HWPriv` (0xA198) selector 1, which on a
copy-back data cache (the 68040) flushes the DATA cache first — exactly
what copying an image as data needs. **A working implementation in the
toolchain you link is evidence about what runs, not about what the
documentation requires.**

**No tier here can fail for want of the flush**: the 68LC040 Emulator
ignores invalidation requests (Inside Macintosh: PowerPC System Software,
*The 68LC040 Emulator*), and Mini vMac's 68000 has no cache. So the probe
reports the OCCURRENCE: `fc=0 fn=0` on System 6.0.8, **`fc=1 fn=3` on
System 7.0.1** (bundle fixup plus one per kept image). **When the
environment cannot test the effect, test the occurrence.**

### The alarm that fired on a healthy archive

The probe reported `wa=128` (an image wanted after release) on a Compact
Pro archive that extracted completely: three readers free the cipher table
unconditionally at cleanup, the resident implementation is a no-op on
NULL, so a released cipher image was asked for again. Benign — but `wa`
had found the preload bug that flattered every interactive measurement for
a week, and had become always-on. The one path ALLOWED to find the image
gone now asks quietly. **Before trusting a signal, find the healthy paths
that trip it.**

## 2026-09-25 (two branches that were one file apart) — the overlays become the build, and the lifetime becomes a flag

**Claim: `overlay-eager` and `selective-loading` were never two
mechanisms.** Decided by the maintainer after the two tiers above System 6
came back at parity: the images ship, eager is the default, and the
resident build stays only as the control.

**Measured first:** of the 24 files under `tools/overlay/`, **21 were
byte-identical** between branches; `overlay.h` differed by five lines,
`mkoverlay.sh` by six, and only eager had `mkbundle.py`. The difference
was a loader (60 lines lazy, 250 eager) behind three calls. Each branch
had its own commit *"The image build could go stale three ways, and did
in two"*. A fix written twice will be forgotten once.

**The seam:** `mac/ovl_shim.c` dispatch, `mac/ovl_reloc.c` relocation and
cache flush, `mac/ovl_load_eager.c` / `mac/ovl_load_lazy.c` behind
`ovl_image()`, `ovl_preload()`, `ovl_release_if_unwanted()`; no-ops are
real functions, not `#ifdef`s.

### Three things the merge decided, each with a reason worth keeping

- **The switch is a BOOLEAN, `UNC_OVL_LAZY`**, because every harness
  passes `-D NAME` as `1`; a lifetime spelled as a VALUE could not be
  driven from `run.py`, `interactive.py` or `os9.py`. **A configuration
  your instruments cannot express is one you cannot test.**
- **`ci.sh` builds both lifetimes** (variants 4b and 4c).
- **The resident build survives as an instrument**: the 84–103 KB is a
  difference against it.

### The ratchets had to be re-based, and one of them had stopped meaning what it said

`tools/build_mac.sh`'s one ceiling, 153,804 B, was the resident build's;
the shipped build's resident code is **54,028 B**, which could have
TRIPLED unnoticed. One ceiling per configuration now, each shown to fire.
`tools/check_app_size.py` opened "Every byte of this application is
RESIDENT" — untrue now (bundle 146,176 B, mostly released before the
budget); its figure moved 185,472 → 65,792 B. **A check's rationale ages
faster than its number.**

### And the lazy lifetime had never flushed the instruction cache

The lazy loader writes relocations and executes them too, with no flush;
no runnable tier could show it (*the flush nobody wrote*, above). Now in
`mac/ovl_reloc.c`, called by both. **Two implementations of one mechanism
do not inherit each other's fixes; one implementation with two behaviours
does.**

## 2026-09-25 (the disk images that found another home) — DART leaves, NDIF and UDIF never arrive

**Claim: expanding a compressed disk image is not this program's job.**
The maintainer's call, before a release. DART (in since 2026-09-09, *the
disk image that is expanded and not opened*) goes out, and the `ndif-udif`
branch with it — deleted from `origin` at **`7269acd`** (recorded because
a deleted ref is recoverable only from the object).

**The argument that brought it in takes it out**: what comes out is
another disk image, and the only thing a user does with it is MOUNT it,
which is MacMount's.

**Gives back** 2,220 B resident `CODE` and 164 B A5 on the resident build;
696 B and 136 B on the shipped overlay build; the download falls 3,456 B.
Every ratchet LOWERED in the same commit. `unc_lzah.c` loses its DART mode
(LZHUF over a zero window); `UNC_ERR_NOTCOMPRESSED` goes and its number
is retired, not reused.

### The transferable part: scope is a question about the WHOLE task, not about the file

The scope question is not "can this engine read it?" but **"after this
program has done its part, is the user finished?"** For a disk image it
never was. **A sibling project is a reason to move a feature, not keep
it**: MacMount already had its own LZHUF (`src/mm_lzhuf.c`, benchmarked
here 2026-09-19).


## 2026-09-26 (the guard that was on the other side) — every cipher gains a fuzz seed, and PackIt's zero was seventeen

**The item.** Three of eight ciphers had no encrypted seed (Compact Pro,
traditional zip, WinZip AES); PackIt's two were recorded at 0 of 30
*"because a flipped bit fails its header CRC before a key is derived"*.

**The seed is not the oracle.** A fuzzer's seed must be the same bytes on
every machine and run; Info-ZIP seeds its encryption header from the
clock and 7-Zip picks a random salt. So the three zip seeds (traditional,
AES at both key lengths) are written in `synth_crypt.py` and handed BACK
to `unar` and `7z t`, which caught a planted flipped bit in each. No
Python AES exists here (`cryptography`, `pycryptodome` absent), so
`synth_crypt.py` gained a ~60-line encryption-only AES, S box computed
from FIPS-197, checked against the standard's two known-answer vectors.

**Compact Pro cost nothing**: `tools/synth_cpt.py` has written encrypted
archives since 2026-08-23. *Before building a generator, look for the one
that exists.*

### PackIt's zero, and the guard that was on the other side

Same instrument and mutation: `sit-des` (19) and `sit5-rc4` (21) reproduce
**exactly**; both PackIt schemes come back **17 of 30**. **PackIt
encrypts the entry HEADER with the payload** (`build_packit` encrypts a
whole `PMa4` stream), so `src/fmt_packit.c` keys the cipher before the
CRC comparison: the checksum is BEHIND the cipher. The real guard is the
first entry, deliberately in the clear: a flip at offset 20 or 60 never
reaches the key, one at 200 does — 100 bytes of 890.

**What the wrong cause cost** was its attached remedy, *"a mutation that
repairs the header CRC afterwards"*, which would have been built against a
nonexistent problem. A figure gets re-measured; the story beside it gets
implemented.

### The ranges, which are worth having anyway

`synth_crypt.py --ranges` reports per shape the byte ranges handed to a
cipher; half the flips land inside. Every shape improved — `cpt` 20 → 29,
`sit-des` 19 → 26, AES past the two-byte verifier into
`aes_encrypt_block` 26 → 29. The other half still flips anywhere.

### The instrument, and its control

`tools/fuzz_reach.py` makes the 2026-09-23 method re-runnable: an
out-of-bounds store planted in one cipher's key setup, rebuild, count
sanitizer trips. It runs the **unmutated** seed first and requires the
fault to fire, and keeps `--untargeted` so before and after come from ONE
instrument — which is why the PackIt contradiction counts: the same run
agrees to the case about StuffIt.

### The ninth seed, and the entry that was refused without being tried

The item's arithmetic counted seven ciphers; **ARC's garble was missing.**
Its password is XORed over compressed bytes with no record, so
`src/fmt_arc.c` detects it by decode failure and retries. The retry
condition, `est != UNC_ERR_CRC && est != UNC_ERR_CORRUPT` written twice,
**refused an entry whose ungarbled stream ran SHORT without trying the
password**: garbled RLE90 over 200 A's, three 0x90s and 120 B's decodes to
a truncation; `unar -p` read it, this engine said *"file is truncated"*.
`src/fmt_packit.c`'s `pit_retryable()` (since M3) includes
`UNC_ERR_TRUNCATED`; the fix is `arc_retryable()`, that predicate plus
ARC's CRC. **When two formats ask one question, copy the one with a name
for it.**

**Why it survived**: `run_crypt.py`'s garbled-ARC cases need Debian's
`arc`, and every `./ci.sh` printed *"no `arc` ... garbled ARC skipped"*
(BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn claims*, the mechanism list). The synthetic
seed closes it: three methods, graded by `unar -p`, failing two ways
against the old engine. `tools/get_arc.sh` worked first try and the three
real garbled fixtures pass (45 cases to 48) — but `ci.sh`'s `make clean`
deletes `build/arc` every run, while `build/deark` and `build/mpack` are
rebuilt on demand. *A skip whose remedy has to be re-run after every clean
is a permanent skip with a helpful message*; hence the synthetic seed.

### What it found in the engine: nothing else

3,000 crypt-only and 2,000 mixed cases, clean. Four never-fuzzed ciphers
now are, and no MUTANT found anything; what was found was found building
the seeds. The coverage is what makes "the paths are clean" mean
something.

**Two counts over lists, both stale.** BLOCKERS.md said *"Ten mechanisms"*
over a list of **thirty** (CLAUDE.md said ten too); FORMATS.md's
*Encryption* said *"Seven ciphers across five formats"* over **eight rows
across six** (TESTING.md repeated it). Corrected in place, dated. **A count
written above a list is the cheapest claim to check and the least likely
to be checked.**


## 2026-09-26 (the numbers DART left behind) — the ratchet was lowered and the prose quoting it was not, and the control nothing built went 4 B over

**What was wrong.** FORMATS.md's *Overlays* gave the shipped build as
54,028 B resident `CODE`, 19,124 B A5, a 214,784 B download and a
146,176 B bundle of fifteen images — all from BEFORE DART left on
2026-09-25. Measured: 53,332 / 18,988 / 211,328, a 143,616 B bundle,
**fourteen** images.

**The tool was right.** DART's commit lowered all three ratchets in
`tools/build_mac.sh` (*"eager 54,028 -> 53,332, lazy 52,600 -> 51,956,
resident 153,804 -> 151,584"*), the file that ENFORCES the number; the
prose was not touched and could not complain. **When a commit lowers a
limit, grep for the number it lowered from**: here FORMATS.md twice (one
updated, one not, 60 lines apart), `check_app_size.py`'s docstring, and
an image count in six files including CLAUDE.md.

### The launch read: two numbers that were written as one

The section said the launch read grows by *"26,368 B, which is the
download delta and not a second term"*. Measured: the read grows by
**24,960 B** (183,552 B control against 64,896 + 143,616 = 208,512 B),
the download by **24,448 B** (211,328 against 186,880). *"X, which is
also Y"* is two claims, and the second was never measured.

**Corrected later the same day: the bundle is 143,072 B, not 143,616 B**,
so the read grows by 24,416 B and the deltas are 32 B apart (*the fork
that was mistaken for its contents*, below). The 512 B left unaccounted
was the whole of the error.

### A control that is not built is not a control

Building the resident configuration by hand came out **4 B over its own
ratchet** while `ci.sh` was green: `arc_retryable()` (*the guard that was
on the other side*) lives in an OVERLAY in both shipped lifetimes, so only
the all-linked build pays. `ci.sh` compiled variants 4, 4b, 4c and left
out the control, while TESTING.md said all were built. The ratchet rises
4 B with its reason, the A5 ratchet falls 4 B, and `ci.sh` gains
**variant 4d**. Of three configurations, the one a suite skips is the
unshipped one — exactly the fixed reference. **A control earns its name
by being rebuilt.**

## 2026-09-26 (the feature that was parked, and is now out) — choosing entries in the Macintosh application leaves the brief

**Decision, the maintainer's, 2026-09-26: the application will not offer a
list of entries to tick.** Selective extraction stays in the CLI's
`--only` (M39, on `l`, `x` and `t`), and the engine keeps both halves a
host needs: `UncOptions.list_only` and the skip a
`begin_entry` returning >0 performs (`include/macextract.h`, *Sink*). **Nothing is removed.**

**Rests on:** every run pays for a picker, and the shell is the thin part
by design (CLAUDE.md, *Mission*). **Does NOT rest on the branch's price**:
`selective-extract`'s `BRANCH_NOTES.md` figures predate the overlays and
DART's removal (2026-09-25, *the parked decision that outlived its
numbers*), and none is quoted. **A stale number is not evidence, and a
scope answer that needed a byte count would be a different answer.**

**Transferable.** "Genuinely open" (2026-09-23) was carried three days as
a status while its only number went stale. *An open decision decays the
same way a claim does.* The cheap move was to ask what the decision turned
on, find it was not the price, and take it.

**Consequence.** OPEN_ITEMS.md's Part 2 section deleted; one Part 1 row
(*Out by the brief*). BRANCHES.md keeps the branch as parked-by-decision.
`tools/run_only.py` grades the CLI half.

## 2026-09-26 (the loader that could be run after all) — the overlay images were never Retro68's to hold

**Claim: "no obvious Linux-side loader test" was not a property of the
Macintosh.** OPEN_ITEMS.md's reasons (m68k images, a loader only in the
Mac build, `qemu-m68k` without a Resource Manager) were each true; the
conclusion did not follow, and cost three defects found by hand
(DECISIONS.md 2026-09-25, *the flush nobody wrote*).

**What the mechanism needs.** An image is a flat `-mpcrel` blob with a
relocation trailer and no Toolbox. The loader needs eight Memory Manager
calls (`NewHandle`, `DisposeHandle`, `GetHandleSize`, `HLock`, `HUnlock`,
`MoveHHi`, `BlockMoveData`, `MemError`), two Resource Manager calls
(`GetResource`, `ReleaseResource`) and a trap probe — and
`tests/mac_sink_test.c` had run against a mock Toolbox of that shape since
2026-08. So `mkoverlay.sh` gained a toolchain PREFIX, `m68k-linux-gnu-gcc`
builds the identical sources and flags, stub `Memory.h`/`Resources.h`/
`OSUtils.h` let all four loader files compile **unmodified**, and
`qemu-m68k` runs them. One macro seam in shipping code (ROM85's ADDRESS);
identical codegen in every shipped build.

**First run:** 17 fixtures through real m68k images, byte-exact against
the oracle manifests, both lifetimes, about a second each; eager reads one
resource and never re-reads, lazy once per image, and **every relocation
in every image is checked against the raw trailer at the address the image
runs at**, including a kept copy relocated twice.

**Two deliberate differences from a Macintosh**: every unlocked block
moves on every allocation (a forgotten lock fails every time), and every
block's last byte abuts a guard page (the class `off + 4 > table` guards).

**Made to fail, six ways, permanently** (`--mutate`, in `ci.sh`): delta
dropped, trailer mislocated, kept copy relocated by its own address,
bundle fixup not flushing, lazy loader not locking, codecs image not
kept. The first attempt reported a mutation UNCAUGHT that was never
applied (`sed` matched nothing, exit 0); `tests/ovlbox/mutate.py` fails on
an absent pattern.

**The shipped images too.** `--shipped-only` (variant 3d) loads `dist/`'s
images: **30 relocations across six images**, all correct (the
m68k-linux build emits 15 in one image). They cannot be CALLED here — a
Retro68 image entered from an m68k-linux binary segfaults, measured on
`synth-sit-rle90.sit`. LOADED here, RUN only on the emulator.

**Still not reachable:** an instruction cache (the flush is counted), any
Retro68 image executing off the Macintosh, a Resource Manager,
fragmentation, the interface; and the control lane's oracle is our own
output, blind to a decoder wrong in both configurations (the 932 fixtures'
job). OPEN_ITEMS.md, *The overlay loader*.

**Transferable.** *A negative built out of true clauses is still a
hypothesis.* The question was not "how could this be tested?" but **"what
does this code actually require?"**, asked of the code, not the platform.

## 2026-09-26 (the fork that was mistaken for its contents) — one instrument mismatch, three wrong numbers, and the 512 B nobody could place

**Claim: the `'OVLY'` bundle is 143,072 B, not 143,616 B.** The larger is
`build/mac/ovl_bundle.r.rsrc.bin`, the Rez'd RESOURCE FORK (map and
header included), where every other figure in the paragraph was resource
DATA or the download: 544 B of fork overhead.

**Three numbers fell with it** (FORMATS.md, *Overlays*):

- the index cost, **724 B**, is **180 B**: a 4-byte header, 12 bytes of
  directory per image (`tools/overlay/mkbundle.py`), 8 bytes padding;
  172 + 8 = 180;
- the launch read, 208,512 B / **+24,960 B**, is 207,968 B / **+24,416 B**;
- the **512 B** gap of DECISIONS.md 2026-09-25 (*the overlay launch read
  was counted as a cost twice*) is **32 B**, inside MacBinary's 128 B
  per-fork quantum.

**Findable because** adding `--bin` to `mkbundle.py`, so
`tests/run_overlay_host.sh` could hand the shipped bundle to the real
loader, was the first time anything read the bundle's bytes. The figure
had been quoted in four places, including `tools/check_app_size.py`'s
header, and produced by no tool.

**Transferable.** *An unexplained residue is an unread instrument*: ask
which file each number came from. **A figure nothing measures is a figure
nobody can correct** — the build writes the bundle size now and the host
lane reads it every run.

## 2026-09-26 (the reproduction that had stopped reproducing) — a recipe whose mechanism was a size, and which never said to check the size

**Claim: a 2-byte field in `UncEntryInfo` makes two DiskDoubler
self-extracting fixtures ~20× slower on the Macintosh** (filed 2026-09-25,
*unexplained, reproducible and load-bearing*, labelled hypothesis). **It
does not reproduce: six runs, all PASS in 5.1 s** (BLOCKERS.md,
*Withdrawn claims*, has the grid).

**The recipe's flaw.** *"add `uint8_t encrypted;` … anywhere in the
struct"* — before `method_data` it lands in padding and `sizeof` stays
**300**, and the first two runs here did exactly that and passed,
meaninglessly. The entry's own clue was the SIZE (`uint32_t` +4 passes,
`uint8_t`/`uint16_t` +2 hang). **A reproduction whose mechanism is a
number has to assert that number**: `sizeof` 302, checked by
`m68k-linux-gnu-gcc -Iinclude` on a four-line probe under `qemu-m68k`.

**With 302** both fixtures pass at 1 MB and 4 MB, shipped and resident;
the field was in the binary (autotest `CODE` 114,544 B with, 114,428 B
without).

**Not claimed:** that the timeouts were imagined (observed twice; a
size-neutral placement can only produce a spurious pass). Since then the
tree lost DART, gained default overlays and moved ~8 KB, and the effect
pointed at block placement. Gone from this tree, cause never established.
*A reproduction is a measurement with a date, not a property of the code.*

**Claim: `tools/run_tiers.py` modelled one budget per tier — the
control's, since 2026-09-25.** With a budget per tier PER FORMAT it

## 2026-09-26 (the AES that was never Gladman's) — the standard was one fetch away, and the code was already written from it

**The claim that failed.** `src/unc_crypt.c`'s AES said "Source: FIPS-197
as implemented in `reference/XADMaster/Crypto/aeskey.c` and `aescrypt.c`"
since `895fb64` (2026-08-23). FIPS 197 was not in `reference/`.

**One fetch:** `csrc.nist.gov` serves FIPS 197 (26 November 2001);
`tools/fetch_references.sh` takes it now.

**The code was already the standard's.** Against §5.2 Fig. 11,
`aes_setkey` is the pseudo-code line for line (`temp = w[i-1]`,
`SubWord(RotWord(temp)) xor Rcon[i/Nk]`, the `Nk > 6 and i mod Nk == 4`
branch, bound `Nb(Nr+1)`, `Nr = Nk + 6` from Fig. 4); the round is §5.1
Fig. 5, state index §3.4's `4c + r`, `xtime` §4.2.1, SubBytes folded into
ShiftRows §5.3.5. Nothing changed.

**Disproved by shape.** Gladman's `aeskey.c` is a 32-bit word machine:
per-key-size functions, `ke4`/`ke6`/`ke8` macros, Rcon from a TABLE
(`t_use(r,c)`), a running `ss[]`; `aescrypt.c` routes through `aesopt.h`
to `aestab.c`'s round tables. This file has one function for all key
sizes, Rcon doubled in GF(2^8), a 256-byte S box.

**Priced at nothing executable**: the crypt `OVLY` image byte-identical at
9,800 B; resident `CODE` 53,332 B and A5 18,988 B unchanged; bundle
byte-identical at 143,072 B; `src/crypt_tables.h` regenerates
identically. **The tick probe was not run**: byte equality already says
more than a tick-resolution probe could (the tick-probe rule is for
changes that alter code).

**Grading:** `ci.sh` runs AES-128, 192, 256 and a stored AES-256 entry
through `tools/run_crypt.py` on **7-Zip** archives; `tools/synth_crypt.py`
asserts appendix C's AES-128 and AES-256 vectors. AES-192 (`Nk = 6`) is
graded only by 7-Zip.

**Transferable.** *A citation to a document not on the machine cannot be
held against the code — it is a promise.* It stood 34 days through two
re-citation passes (2026-09-19, 2026-09-23) that read it as sourced; and
`tools/synth_crypt.py`'s `Aes` (`0472a81`, that day) already said
"FIPS-197 section 5.2" for the same algorithm.

## 2026-09-26 (the inventory that listed the decoders) — the licence was tracked against a table assembled from the format list, and ten files were never in it

**The claim.** OPEN_ITEMS.md, *What is still XADMaster's*: a twelve-file
table, "the licence changes only when the last row is gone".

**Disproved in one command:**

    grep -rlE 'Source:.*(XAD|macutils)' src/*.c src/*.h

Fifteen files, **eight with no row**: `unc_util.c` and `unc_internal.h`
(three CRC tables, the MSB-first bit reader), `fmt_binhex.c`, `fmt_uu.c`,
`fmt_mime.c` (macutils' `hexbin`), `fmt_foreign.c`, `fmt_sit_probe.c`,
`fmt_packit_probe.c`. **Two more the grep cannot see** (`unc_lzah.c`'s
window preload, `unc_encinfo.c`'s second-hand citation), with `Source:`
and the name on different lines. Ten. Every existing row was a format:
**the decoder list with a provenance column, read as an inventory of the
repository.**

**Why.** Each shedding pass asked "what does THIS decoder owe?"; shared
primitives are owed by eleven decoders and attributed by none. *An
inventory assembled by walking the subjects is complete only for the
dimension you walked.* The capability search here was `Source:`, never
run.

**Two documents already contradicted the source.** NOTICE said BinHex left
XADMaster on 2026-09-19 while `fmt_binhex.c` cites `hexbin` for two
rules; NOTICE said `unc_lzah.c`'s preloads were this project's, while the
file says the -lh1-/StuffIt method 5 preload is `resetLZSSHandle`'s. That
pattern is published — LHa for UNIX's `larc.c` `decode_start_lz5`, **for
LArc's -lz5-, not -lh1-** — and lhasa fills -lh1- with spaces; what is
XADMaster's is its application to this method.

**Fixed rather than filed**, each verified against the document:

| line | said | says |
|---|---|---|
| `unc_internal.h`, the bit-serialized tree | `XADStuffItHuffmanHandle.m` (parseTree), macutils `de_huffman.c` | `docs/formats/serialized-huffman-tree.md`, which NOTICE and `unc_huffman.c` have named since 2026-09-20 |
| `unc_internal.h`, the canonical codes | `XADPrefixCode.m`, macutils `cpt.c` | RFC 1951 §3.2.2 and `puff.c`, named since 2026-09-19 |
| `unc_encinfo.c`, Compact Pro's index | fmt_cpt.c's comment, "itself from" XADMaster and macutils | `docs/formats/compact-pro.md`, which is what that comment says now |
| `fmt_cpt.c`, `CPT_WINDOW` | "macutils CIRCSIZE" | `1 << 13`, the offset width in compact-pro.md's correction 3 |

Comments only, **measured**: the built application's payload sha256
equals `dist/`'s (`2f20f588…`, 211,328 B, `tail -c +129` past the
MacBinary header) — `ci.sh`'s stale-`dist` comparison, hence no `dist/`
rebuild — and the `tools/build_mac.sh` ratchets agree in all four
configurations. The rest are rows, priced or explicitly unpriced; a row
closes by a graded rewrite.

**The CRC row was next, by precedent**: `unc_util.c`'s tables are
described as "generated mechanically from the polynomials", check values
asserted in `tests/unit_main.c` and `tests/unit_formats.c` (not the
never-existing `tests/unit_util.c` the comment named); polynomials in
`reference/notes/binhex40_lewis.txt` and `zip_appnote.txt` (`0xdebb20e3`
residue); deark and lhasa BUILD the 0xA001 table.

CLAUDE.md's session-start reading was corrected that morning from 7.5k to
14k tokens with *re-measured 2026-09-26* — while the next figure,
*"BLOCKERS' withdrawn-claims archive is another 15k"*, was 2026-08-26's.
The archive was 164,442 characters, **~41k tokens** (four characters per

a sentence leaves the sentence looking measured, and the new date stops
the next reader asking about the rest.**

The smells count was wrong for the third time (thirty-three over a list of

## 2026-09-26 (the magic in somebody else's index) — two files this project had given up on, and the search that was never by name

OPEN_ITEMS.md's *"Waiting on a file this machine does not have"* held two
items. Both are gone, with no emulator.

### What the searches had all been

Twenty emulator runs on making SpaceSaver compress, seven on making
Aladdin's software read a package written here, both filed as *nothing
here can produce one*. Nobody searched anybody else's disks, because
**neither format is labelled**: SpaceSaver renames nothing, and `.pkg`
means InstallShield, Newton, OS/2, BeOS and five others first.

One query against the BYTES worked. Discmaster indexes ~1.7 billion files
from CD-ROMs and disk images, with `file`'s output full-text searchable. A
SpaceSaver file begins `SIT!DFD3`, which `file` prints as **`StuffIt
Archive (data) : T!DFD3`**: `detection=DFD3` returned 296 files, 142
genuine after parsing the 84-byte header, both header versions, methods 0
to 4. **Ask of any corpus: what is it indexed BY?** Now a smell in
BLOCKERS.md.

### The originals, which are what make them worth having

The codecs were already graded against Aladdin's modules under
`qemu-m68k`; a specimen buys the CONTAINER, if the original is beside it.
It is: publishers pressed a title from a SpaceSaver machine and, earlier,
from one without. `MPW Script Tips 1.1.1/Sample Scripts/SmallWindow` is
**1,024 bytes** compressed on Tool Chest discs from November 1993 and
**665 bytes of plain text** on twelve discs March 1992 – March 1993; 665
is the compressed header's data-fork length. (leaf name, decoded length)
gave 50 candidate pairs; 46 byte-exact, four provably different files.

**40 of the 142 leaf names contain *small*** — SpaceSaver's name rule
firing on somebody else's Macintosh; not the only trigger (`MAD.h`,
`Rates`, `cdev.π`), and BLOCKERS.md's record that it never fired under
Mini vMac stands.

### What a real package turned out to be

`ALink.PKG` and `Read First.PKG` ship beside AppleLink 6.1 on fifteen
Apple Developer CDs. **534 of the 539 fixtures `fixtures/SOURCES.md`
fetches over HTTP come from `www.nic.funet.fi` or
`raw.githubusercontent.com`** — name-indexed; none ever came from a CD
image. The packages are **binary containers** (two lengths, type, creator,
Finder flags, Pascal name, two dates at fixed offsets, then data). The
2026-08-23 *transfer manifest* hypothesis is withdrawn, and the shipped
`.pkg` probe — Aladdin's recogniser, correctly transcribed, 0 false
positives over 928 fixtures — **rejects both real packages**, one being
claimed by the Compact Pro segment probe. *A false-positive rate measured
over a corpus with no specimen of the format is a fact about the corpus.*

### Two instruments that were not instruments

`tools/run_spacesaver.py` looked for the decoded file with `.ss` removed,
where the CLI keeps the whole basename (SpaceSaver adds no extension):
46 of 46 failed the first time it had input. Fixed, and a specimen
without an original must now decode rather than be skipped. **A harness
written for files that have not arrived is green because it is empty.**

MANUAL_TESTS.md's section asking a stranger to compress and mail a file
is the second of that file withdrawn after the machine could answer it.
**Asking somebody outside this machine is the last resort, not the
second.**

## 2026-09-26 (the bargain that was finally paid) — a probe admitted it was weak, and a real file from another format collected

`unc_cptseg_probe` accepted byte 0 = 1 with a zero longword at 4, a bargain
its comment called deliberate. `Read First.PKG` (`01 01 00 00`, zero
index) was sniffed as a set's first segment.

**The probe was not using bytes 2–3, the set identity.** A segment
carrying no index must now carry a non-zero one. Measured: of **82 raw
Compact Pro files — 75 distinct identities, including the real sets
`edu3` (`0xab78`, four parts) and `biplane5` (`0xdac4`, five) — none is
0**; `tools/synth_cptsplit.py`'s `identity()` already ended `return h or
1`. The final segment is untouched (`unc_cpt_probe` walks its CRC).

**Transferable.** The field was already parsed, documented two paragraphs
above the admission of weakness, and reported by `unc_cptseg_describe`.
*A probe that calls itself weak is worth re-reading against its own format
notes* — "nothing else to check" was about the payload.

`tests/unit_formats.c` gains `test_cptseg_probe`, the probe's first unit
test (the package header negative, both real sets positive), confirmed to
fail with the check removed.

## 2026-09-27 (the prediction that was run) — a model said 66/71 before any machine had, and the machine agreed fixture for fixture

`tools/run_tiers.py`'s shipped lane PREDICTED System 6.0.8 on a 512 KB
512Ke at 66/71 against the resident 64/71, naming five refusals and two
fixtures a per-format budget would clear; FORMATS.md carried it as a
hypothesis.

**The machine returned 66/71, refusing those five and no others**;
`derived-Troi-ClipSave-Plug-in1.1.sit` and `derived-Expand_Now_1.0.1.sea`
passed as modelled. Asserted by name from today, confirmed to fail with
one name misspelled. Reproducing a measured number cannot tell a model
from a lookup table. *A model validated only against the runs it was built
from is a record of those runs.*

### The residue did not reproduce, and that is labelled

The same boot with `-D UNC_AT_BUDGET` granted an LZH 753,382 B at the
1 MB floor against a computed 750,456 B (2,926 B, against a 1,138 B
residue). **Hypothesis**: the 648,250 B base was taken on the v0.33.0
binary, and the probe build is not the modelled build. A number taken from
two binaries is not a residue, it is two numbers. (Settled next:
*the residue that was two numbers*, below.)

### And the harness beside it was lying about which machine ran

`run.py` printed `N/M PASS at {args.mem}`, so `--emu mv-512Ke` reported
**"66/71 PASS at 4M"**; `sys30.py` has guarded against exactly this, with
a comment naming the consequence. The JSON was right. Fixed as sys30.py
does it. Second instance of *a harness that ends its runs differently from
the harness beside it* (2026-08-22); method added: **grep for the COMMENT,
not for the bug.**

## 2026-09-27 (the residue that was two numbers) — a base and a grant from one binary, and a constant that was drift

Taken from ONE tree and ONE probe pair (`run.py --mem 1M -D
UNC_AT_BUDGET` with and without `-D UNC_OVL_RESIDENT`), the 2,926 B
decomposes exactly:

    base, re-taken       652,996 B   was 648,250      +4,746
    residue, re-taken       -714 B   was  +1,138      -1,852 (-1,820 net of
                                                       OVL_SAVED's 32 B)
    2,926 B accounted for to the byte

**The model was never pessimistic; it was arithmetic on a stale base** —
the floor-budget mistake again (*the fold, on a Macintosh*). **A
difference of two measurements is a measurement only if both come from the
same binary.**

### The constant that fit three formats was a property of the build

`OVL_RESIDUE` is **−714 B** on this tree, opposite sign. The three-row fit
established only that the PER-FORMAT arithmetic (images kept, 8 B block
header each) is right; the term is per-build slack and must be re-taken
with the tier budgets. Ten keep sets now from one pair, all leaving the
same constant to the byte (the envelope row LOSES 26,706 B). 368 B
attributed: `-D UNC_AT_BUDGET` costs eager 400 B of `CODE` + A5 against
the control's 320 B, so a probe pair saves 116,720 B where the shipped
pair saves 117,088 B. Unattributed: 346 B.

### Two smells, both already on the list, both paying out again

**Cross-file contradiction.** `OVL_SAVED` was 117,056 B under a comment
naming FORMATS.md's *Three configurations, one tree* as "the only place to
correct them", which read 117,088 B. `run_tiers.py --check-saved` now
grades it against the build artefacts, in `ci.sh` after the resident
control. **A comment saying where a number lives is not a check.**

**A number quoted for the wrong question.** The open item blamed "this
tree's application is ~24 B smaller" (what v0.34.0's segment check cost);
the base had moved 4,746 B. A 24 B difference cannot produce a 2,926 B
discrepancy; it was quoted because it was the only size number in reach.

### What it cost, and the one number that was free

Two 1 MB boots to settle, nine to widen to ten keep sets, three tier
re-takes — and all again after the AppleLink probe left the same day
(*the recogniser that was a command line*), which moved every budget
536 B and every per-format GAIN not at all; the 346 B surviving a 496 B
application change is a figure, not noise. All three tier budgets rose
4,746 B and no tally moved. The third tier was PREDICTED at 224,108 B
before the boot, and is.

## 2026-09-27 (the recogniser that was a command line) — a routine copied correctly out of the right file, answering a different question

`unc_applelink_probe` (since 2026-08-23) named a file an AppleLink package
when its first token was `Decode` and its third `to`/`into` — `PKG Expand
Translator`'s @0x2952, transcribed accurately and witnessed
(`tools/vmac/spacesaver.py --pkg`). It named neither real package.

**The right routine for a question nobody asked it.** The five other
translators on the disk carry the SAME routine:

| translator | `STR# 129` items 1–4 | its recogniser |
|---|---|---|
| PKG Expand | `Decode`, ` Folder`, `.pkg`, `to` | @0x2952 |
| CompactPro | `Decode`, ` Folder`, `.cpt`, `to` | @0x2bc8 — instruction for instruction the same |
| UnZip | `Decode`, ` Folder`, `.zip`, `to` | same shape, same three item tests |
| BinHex4, UUCode, Unix Compress | `Decode`, `Encode`, `replace`, … `to` | same shape |

Input is a Handle at `param+4`, answer at `param+8`, selector at
`param+12` (PARSE bit 1, RUN bit 2): `Decode "X" to "Y"` is the StuffIt
translator API's command language. The CompactPro copy would reject all
108 Compact Pro fixtures. File recognition is by EXTENSION (`STR# 129`
item 3, stripped for ` Folder` @0x2e5c); the dialog lists only
directories; expansion is `GetResource('Eng ', 2)` in `StuffIt Engine™`
(@0x334c).

**The probe is removed.** The unit test asserts the four lines it accepted
are `UNC_FORMAT_UNKNOWN`.

### The lesson, and it is a new smell

Rule #1 (magic from a reference, with `/* Source: */`) was obeyed; it does
not say **check which question the cited routine answers**. Running a
sibling's copy against its own format's 108 fixtures would have answered
on the day. It also explains the seven boots of 2026-09-01 that could not
hand Aladdin's expander a package (DECISIONS.md 2026-09-01): read as an
obstacle, it was evidence about the routine.

**Cost: 35 days of a format counted as named that named no file**, a
supporting measurement that could not fail ("0 false positives across 928
fixtures"), and those seven boots. Settled with no boot: five resources on
an image installed since August.


## 2026-09-27 (the signatures that were already on the disk) — a row said its replacements were not on this machine, and eight of the ten were compiled by ci.sh every run

**Superseded 2026-10-18** for `src/fmt_foreign.c` and StuffIt X's probe
(*the formats it only named*): that code is gone. PackIt's recogniser is
unaffected.

The XADMaster inventory row for `src/fmt_foreign.c`, `src/fmt_sit_probe.c`
and `src/fmt_packit_probe.c` said: *deark for Zoo, already cited; the rest
are in each format's own published description, none of which is on this
disk.* **That asked about descriptions and answered for implementations.**
deark, compiled by `tools/build_deark.sh` every `ci.sh` run, states eight
of the ten:

| signature | where deark states it |
|---|---|
| ARJ `60 ea`, the 30..2600 header bounds, the basic-header CRC-32 | `modules/arj.c` — `g_arj_hdr_id`, `de_identify_arj`, `arj_read_member` |
| RAR 5.x, 1.5–4.x, and "RE~^" | `modules/rar.c`, `rar_get_fmtver` |
| Cabinet `MSCF` | `modules/cab.c` |
| Zoo, four bytes at 0x14 | `modules/zoo.c` (already cited) |
| bzip2 `BZh` + the block header | `modules/unsupported.c`, `get_fmt` |
| 7-Zip, xz | the same function |
| PackIt's recogniser | `modules/packit.c`, `de_identify_packit` |

wiki page `fmt_sit.c` already uses (`0x724c6175` at offset 10; `SIT!`,

digit) is XADMaster's in origin, kept as this project's: `rLau` must match
too, and all 336 corpus archives with `rLau` at offset 10 carry `SIT!`.
ARJ's lower bound moved from XADMaster's 32 to deark's 30 (length guard 40
to 38), deark citing the ARJ TECHNOTE; no fixture exercises ARJ.

**Lesson already on BLOCKERS' list: an oracle that was never asked.**
Method 6 cost four weeks of "macutils is the only reference" while deark
implemented it; this row cost five. Ask *"does anything here READ this
format?"*

## 2026-09-27 (half a citation) — one of the two facts behind DiskDoubler method 8 was measured away and the other turned out to be unfalsifiable on this corpus, which is a better answer than unmeasured

`src/unc_internal.h`'s `Source: XADDiskDoublerParser.m case 8` covered two
facts: method 8 IS Compact Pro's two decode stages, and its Huffman block
is 0xfff0 (Compact Pro's own is 0x1fff0).

**The first is measured**: `tools/derive_dd8.py` decodes every method-8
fork in reach with `tools/derive_cpt.py`'s published-pages reader and
matches an independent oracle's sha256 **7 of 7**.

**The second cannot be, and the grid says so.** Swept DOWN as well as up:
a size above any stream's reach never flushes and pins nothing, one below
fails. **Every size ≥ 0x1000 reads all 7; the largest failing anywhere is
0x400.** So 0xfff0 is unfalsifiable here; the specimen needed is a
method-8 fork whose coder output crosses 0xfff0 cost units (2 per literal,
3 per match). The biggest in reach is 44,549 B, compressing to 1,230.
(settled: DECISIONS.md 2026-10-06, *the other half of that citation*.)

**Two harness errors**: the stages are FUSED in the published reading
(`lzh` sinks through an `Rle`), so calling both decoded twice; and a
method-8 fork opens with **sixteen bytes whose sum selects the path**,
the container's. Four stored forks in the same archive hashing exactly
proved the offsets first. **Grade the harness on a case whose answer is
known before reading anything into a failure.**

reference/XADMaster/<file>` comment"*). Six carriers lacked it

the event.* Ask: **what does the source look like immediately before and

|---|---|---|
| HFS+ | HFS+ | the alert |
| HFS+ | HFS | the alert |
| **HFS** | HFS+ | the alert |
| **HFS** | HFS | the alert |

## 2026-09-27 (the fuzzer that could only reach what the corpus had) — the ciphers' reach question asked of the decoders, and one whole file had never been fuzzed

The 2026-09-23 reach question had never been asked of the decoders — and
the one decoder heap overflow found (`now_next_block`) came from a crafted
archive, not a mutant.

**Instrument: coverage.** `tools/fuzz_cover.py` builds `--coverage`, runs
`fuzz.py`, reports per family.

**3,000 cases, seed 11**: `src/unc_lzdyn.c` 16 of 16 functions never
entered (all of `-lh2-`/`-lh3-`); also never entered DiskDoubler methods
3, 4 and 7, ARC's Crush, three Arsenic index helpers, six of Now
Compress's thirteen.

**One cause: three of four generators mutate a corpus fixture, so the
fuzzer's reach is the corpus's coverage.** Every method graded by
GENERATING a file (`run_lzh.py`, `ddencode.py`, ARC's encoder) is fuzzed
not at all. Remedy: a deterministic in-repo seed per method, as
`synth_crypt.py` did. **Now Compress is the exception**: its archives are
in the corpus, but a 32-bit sum gates the block table — the gate the
overflow sat behind; a checksum-repairing generator is what reaches it.

**Process notes.** A 400-case run's zeros were mostly sampling. The first
analysis credited `pit_synth`/`cpt_synth`/`sit_synth` (in `tests/`) as
decoders: `gcov -f` prints functions BEFORE their `File` line, so splitting
on `File '` misassigns every one; filtered per gcov invocation now. **An
instrument's first output is a draft.**


## 2026-09-27 (the rule both references already followed) — a decision put to the maintainer dissolved on reading what lhasa yields rather than what it stores

`src/fmt_lzh.c` truncates a level 0/1 name at an embedded NUL; filed as
its last XADMaster-only rule and put to the maintainer as a DECISION
(*"lhasa takes the whole field"*).

**There was no decision.** XADMaster stops at the NUL and keeps the rest
as `XADCommentKey`; lhasa's `process_level0_path()` copies the whole field,
but every consumer treats it as a C string (`strrchr` in
`split_header_filename`, `strdup`, `strlen`/`sprintf` in
`lha_file_header_full_path`). Same name; they differ only on surfacing the
tail as a comment, which this engine drops. lhasa's level-0 comment support
is in the extended AREA (`process_level0_extended_area`, for PMarc).

**Consequence: `fmt_lzh.c` leaves the provenance inventory**, cited to
lhasa (ISC); its base-header citation went too (section A of the document
states every field).

**Lesson.** "lhasa takes the whole field" was read off what lhasa STORES.
**A claim that two implementations disagree is a claim about their
output.** Cost: five days in the inventory and a decision offered three
times that was not one.

`fuzz.py`'s fifth generator flips bits in a Now Compress block payload and
calls `tools/mutate_now.py`'s `fix_trailer` (corrupt what the CODER reads,
fix what the WALK checks). **Now Compress goes from 6 never-entered
functions to 1** (`now_find_delta`), at seeds 11 and 12.

**The rest was a draw.** At a sixth of the cases the total never-entered
count rose 132 → 149 and StuffIt classic 0 → 7, written up as starvation.
