seed 12 on an identical build gives StuffIt classic 1 vs 6, ARC 10 vs 6,
Compact Pro 1 vs 4. Changing a generator changes the RNG sequence, so rare
formats are hit by luck.

**A measurement with no noise floor cannot support a delta.** One extra
six-minute run set the floor at ±5 functions per family and retired a
causal sentence already committed to `fuzz.py`'s comments. Supported:
whole-family figures (`lzd_*` at zero at every seed; 6 → 1 at both); the
rest is labelled noisy.


## 2026-09-27 (the encoder that only wrote literals) — chasing a coverage number found that a decoder's whole LZSS half had never been graded by anything

The `-lh3-` seed run UNMUTATED through the coverage build showed
**`lzs_decode_p` at zero there too**: `lh3_stream()` emitted nothing above
255, and the corpus has no `-lh3-`. **The whole LZSS half was graded by
nothing** while `run_lzh.py` reported six cases agreeing with LHa.

**Writing the encoder was the fix; LHa adjudicated** (it extracts each
generated archive first) and caught two encoder errors:

- **The block size counts SYMBOLS, not bytes** (both decoders decrement
  per code); a literals-only stream cannot tell.
- **The longest match is 31, not 32.** Both decoders read `c - (256 -
  3)`, making symbol 285 a 32-match, and both refuse it (LHa a CRC error,
  this engine truncation) while 3..31 round-trip at every distance. **Why
  285 is not a length-32 code is not established**; the ceiling is
  measured and labelled.

**Seeds split**: in a ten-entry archive a mutant breaks an earlier entry
first. One archive per case: `unc_lzst0_decode` 100 %, `lzs_decode_p`
88.9 %, `lzs_read_tree_p` 64.3 %.

**A function at zero is a question about every suite**; tell them apart by
running the instrument on input that is supposed to work.


## 2026-09-27 (the tree that never had to be rebuilt) — the same question put to -lh2-, and the subject that answers it had to satisfy two conditions at once

The graded suite under coverage: `-lh2-` is written by a real encoder
(the patched LHa), so `unc_lzdyn_decode` and `lzd_decode_p` are at 100 %
— the `-lh3-` hole came from our own encoder.

**`lzd_reconst` was at zero**: the adaptive tree rebuilds when the root
count reaches 0x8000 (32,768 codes); `-lh1-`'s `lzah_reconst` is at 100 %
from long corpus archives, but `-lh2-` has none. Choosing a subject took
three attempts:

- **48 KB incompressible**: LHa stored it `-lh0-` — visible only because
  the printed entry COUNT did not move;
- **80 KB of digits**: stayed `-lh2-` but ran at about a quarter of the
  bytes in codes;
- **50 KB over a 64-symbol alphabet**: Huffman shrinks it and repeats are
  rare, so codes track length.

`lzd_reconst` and `lzd_update_c` at 100 %, GRADED (LHa reads each archive
first). **A path guarded by a threshold is reached by input size, not
shape**; suites of small subjects never reach them. `lzd_update_p` (32,768
MATCHES) is recorded, not chased.

| all zeros | 932/933 |

## 2026-09-28 (the six bytes Aladdin's own Get Info pane reads) — a field filed as needing an emulator session was in a program already on this disk, and the answer turned a message into a correctness fix

**Claim.** Where a StuffIt 2.x archive records which add-on module a fork
needs was filed *"not known here"*, closed only by an emulator specimen. It
is six bytes of the entry header, and the writer had been extracted onto
this disk an hour earlier.

**Evidence.** StuffIt Deluxe 2.0.1's Get Info pane calls its module
manager per fork with the method byte and three id bytes; a module matches
when its `COMP`/`DCMP` resource ID is `class << 8 | id`. Offsets:
FORMATS.md, *Where an archive names the module*.

**Consequence.** `src/fmt_sit.c` refuses an optimized or externally
compressed fork per entry (`UNC_ERR_MODULE`) and names the module.

**A missing specimen and a missing implementation are different gaps.**
The blocked question was *where is the field*, and the WRITER answers it
— one file, on archive.org, listable by `macextract`. **Before filing "we
need a file this format wrote", ask whether the program that writes it is
reachable**: it is a reference implementation under rule #1.

**A disassembly is a reading only if something pins the base.** The
manager gets a pointer into a 112-byte buffer at `A5-2844`; the same call
passes longs from `A5-2760` and `A5-2752` for the compression percentage,
and 84 and 92 are where the header keeps a fork's lengths. Three of four
fields then land on bytes XADMaster labelled "unknown".

**Anchor a field's meaning to the flag that switches it on.** In 2,512
forks of 1,256 entries in 227 archives, bytes 46/47 are nonzero in **91**,
but no entry has method nibble 7 (StuffIt 1.x wrote buffer garbage); the
earlier "zero in 1,251 of 1,256 entries" for 104..109 measured the
feature's absence.

**A correctness bug, not a message.** An Optimizer preprocesses before the
compressor, so a bit-`0x40` fork decodes perfectly to the optimized bytes
(resources deleted, spaces to tabs) under the original's name, CRC
agreeing, exit 0. The unit test extracts it with the refusal removed.
**An unread header field is not inert when it says the bytes mean
something else.** `unar` 1.10.8 writes all three optimized entries'
preprocessed bytes and reports success, so `run_diff.py`'s excuse
mechanism would have pressed a future session to copy it; TESTING.md
records why this decline is not eligible. **Ask first what the tool you
grade yourself by does with a field nobody had read.**

## 2026-09-28 (the two walls between here and one archive) — went after the specimen and met a licence and a submenu, and the run disproved what the harness beside it was thought to be driving

**Claim.** The optimized specimen, filed as one session away, is not
reachable from this machine: six boots, and something else disproved.
(Withdrawn next entry: *the page the codes were not on*.)

**Evidence.** `tools/vmac/sitopt.py`: StuffIt Deluxe 2.0.1 installs by
copying the payload and launches on System 6, then wants a name, a
**signature drawn in a box**, and a **serial number it checks** (*"You must
type in and sign your name"*; *"The serial number you have entered is
invalid"* for every code tried). Magic Menu runs without one; its
`StuffIt Options ▸` submenu holds method and Leave/Delete Originals, not an
Optimizer.

**"Installs" is not "runs"**: when the plan is to drive somebody's
application, first ask whether it will start; the same wall was recorded
for 3.5.1 and 4.0 next door.

**`sitcrypt.py` does not drive StuffIt Deluxe 3.5.1**: every dialog in
its runs is **Magic Menu's** over a Finder menu bar. "Nothing in this
project has ever launched a StuffIt Deluxe application" — WITHDRAWN
2026-10-10: those attempts were ⌘O, and a double-click launched it that
day (BLOCKERS.md). **A description of how a WORKING harness works is the
least-read sentence in any file**; the menu bar had been photographed
twenty times.

**Run the control before the interesting explanation**: "3.5.1 will not
launch with a 2.0 Optimizer installed" — the image without them did not
launch either.

**A trap narrower than its wording**: README said submenu items *"never
highlight and cannot be selected"*; under System 6 with Magic Menu 2.0 the
parent highlights and the submenu draws. The failure is System 7's
Translate menu. **A trap written from one measurement should name what it
was measured on.**

## 2026-09-28 (the page the codes were not on) — one question from the maintainer turned a registration wall back into a boot, and the archive that came out corrected the reading it was meant to confirm

**Claim.** StuffIt Deluxe 2.0.1's serial was reachable; the six codes came
from the wrong version's page.

**Evidence.** `macintoshgarden.org/apps/stuffit-deluxe-2` (not
`/apps/stuffit-deluxe`, where `spacesaver.py` gets 3.0.7's and 5.x's
codes): *"Requires a name and serial activation: A nnnnn (where 'n' = any
number, for example: A 12345)"*, plus a *"pre-registered"* build. `A 12345`
was accepted first try.

**Consequence.** Three archives written by 2.0.1 with `Text 1` enabled,
graded by `tools/run_sitopt.py` against 2.0.1's own unstuffer.

**A provenance line is a claim about a URL, and the only test is to open
it.** The codes carried a citation to a page that does not host this file;
the false sentence *"every code published on the page the software comes
from"* reached five files and a commit message. **The cheapest disproof of
a citation is `curl`**; an inherited PROVENANCE is *a limitation you
inherited from the reference rather than measured*.

**"It refused six codes" measures the codes, not the software.**

**The archive corrected the reading.** Byte 106 was read as the module id;
`Text 1` is module 5 and the byte reads **255** — an Optimizer that cannot
be undone (`Text 1` has no `DCMP`, the Get Info pane special-cases 255,
2.0.1's unstuffer returns the optimized bytes). The engine now DECODES
those and refuses only ids a module could restore. A reading tells you
where to look; only the writer tells you what it wrote.

## 2026-09-28 (nothing here is one, and nothing here can make one are different sentences) — a manual test was filed for a file the emulator could draw, and drawing it confirmed the half of the reading that was still open

**Claim.** The reversible half (byte 106 holds the module id when the
module has a `DCMP`) needed a MacPaint document, and MacPaint is here.

**Evidence.** `MacPaint 1` keys on type `PNTG`; the 933-fixture corpus has
six `sfil` sounds and no paint document. MacPaint 2.0 (a `.sea.hqx`
`macextract` unwraps) runs on the System 6 image and drew one in a single
boot; stuffed with the Optimizer, bytes 106 and 108 record **4** —
`MacPaint 1`'s resource id.

**Consequence.** MANUAL_TESTS.md §8 deleted four minutes after it was
written; `tools/run_sitopt.py` grades both branches.

**"Nothing here IS one" and "nothing here can MAKE one" are different
sentences.** Ask before filing anything manual: *do we have something that
emits it?* **Where a format's own software is reachable, it answers
questions about that format better than any reasoning** — including about
a second format it writes.

## 2026-09-28 (the module said what it wanted, twice, and the second time it was right about our own resource forks) — three Optimizers declined every subject until their acceptance tests were read, and one of the refusals was a bug in this harness

**Claim.** All five 2.0 Optimizers write their own module id into byte
106, except the one that cannot be undone.

**Evidence.** `Sound 1` → 1, `Photoshop 1` → 2, `Photoshop/JPEG Lossy` →
3, `MacPaint 1` → 4, `Text 1` → 255 (FORMATS.md, *What Aladdin's own
output says*). `tools/run_sitopt.py` grades eight archives.

**Consequence.** The reading is closed; no `DCMP` had yet been executed
here.

**"It declined" is a question the module can answer.** A corpus sound
suitcase and an ImageMagick Photoshop document were refused twice each.
Forty instructions of each `COMP` settled it: `Sound 1` tests for type
**`FSSD`** (Sound Designer II); `Photoshop 1` for **`8BIM`** (Photoshop
1.0's type, not modern `8BPS`). **Two failed guesses cost more than the
reading would have.**

**A negative in a program's own words**: the first run printed *"* * *
Optimizer Not Found: Sound 1"* into the status file (`--install` had
copied two of five modules) — visible only because every script begins
with `Write Status To`.

**The 255 sentinel survived the test that could have killed it.** `JPEG
Lossy` is lossy, and 255 is what Get Info prints as *" lossy"*; it writes
**3**. So 255 means *nothing can undo this*, and only `Text 1`, with no
`DCMP`, writes it. **Test first the case that would make you wrong.**

**The last refusal was ours.** The harness's resource map lacked the
two-byte attributes field, so `typeListOffset` sat two bytes early and
`Get1Resource` returned NULL. **A generator whose output nothing parses
is not a generator**: `spacesaver.resources()` now parses what
`one_resource()` writes before an emulator sees it.

## 2026-09-28 (the right answer with the wrong reason, again) — asked the application to undo an Optimizer and it did not, which withdrew the justification for a refusal the header had been justifying all along

**Claim.** The engine refused a `DCMP`-able Optimizer entry because *"the
module would restore the original and we do not have it"*. The module does
not restore the original; the refusal is right for a reason in the header.

**Evidence.** StuffIt Deluxe 2.0.1 with `MacPaint 1`, unstuffing its own
archive by script with the original deleted: artwork byte-identical from
offset 512, the 512-byte header differs in 486 bytes, the 501-byte
resource fork is gone. Run twice (once alone).

**Consequence.** FORMATS.md, *What a module gives back*; the engine
comment cites the lengths.

**The declared lengths were the answer.** A `Text 1` entry declares 0/594
where its control declares 338/732 — the header describes the OPTIMIZED
file. Every `DCMP`-module entry declares its control's lengths exactly
(501/2945, 342/8192) and stores a remnant (`MacPaint 1`'s resource fork
is two compressed bytes for a declared 501). Four bytes of arithmetic per
entry, and it makes 255 obvious. **Compare the control's bytes to the
specimen's before running anything.**

**Third right answer with a wrong reason** (after `checkdisk.py`'s `hls
-a` and the `HOpen` attribution). Here the sentence came from Aladdin's
alert *"Please use StuffIt Deluxe instead"*, which says only that the
application can open it. **A quotation is evidence for what it says, not
for what it implies.**

## 2026-09-29 (the record was a CInfoPBRec, and the header it writes is a stack frame) — drove both halves of an Optimizer and the round trip came out byte-identical everywhere it can be

**Claim.** `MacPaint 1`'s `COMP` makes the remnant and its `DCMP` rebuilds
the document from it, run on an emulated Mac Plus with nothing invented in
between.

**Evidence.** `tools/vmac/sitopt.py --dcmpdata`. The remnant is 2,437
bytes: a 4-byte length, then the 2,945-byte document from offset 512, byte
for byte. The rebuilt file is 2,945 bytes, no resource fork, artwork from
512 identical to the document AND to 2.0.1's unstuffer. FORMATS.md, *What
the data path does*.

**Consequence.** OPEN_ITEMS.md's Optimizer item keeps one question: an
optimized entry declares the ORIGINAL lengths, so producing the remnant
looked to need a decode-until-input-exhausted mode (withdrawn next entry).

**The record is a `CInfoPBRec`, proved by TWO fields**: `DCMP` reads the
parent directory at +48, `COMP` at +100 — `ioDirID` and `ioFlParID`.
**When an offset could be anything, find the second that could only be one
thing.**

**The 512 bytes a `DCMP` writes are the CALLER's uninitialised stack** (a
670-byte frame). Three runs write the same 512 bytes; a differently built
probe 135 different; 2.0.1 421 different. So **an optimized MacPaint entry
has no byte-exact answer not tied to one caller**. Repeating says
"deterministic"; only CHANGING the caller says what it is a function of.

**Both bugs were mine.** One `FSRead` for 2,437 bytes returned 2,048 (the
first extent), and the buffer's uninitialised tail became the document's
last 389 bytes — right LENGTH, wrong content. And `_FlushVol` returning 0
is not Shut Down. **A short read is legal**; Aladdin's transform loops
over `_Read` for exactly this.

**The way OUT was the module**: the temp file a `COMP` holds cannot be
opened (-49, `opWrErr`), but `*selector > 0` on a `COMP` reads it into the
caller's buffer and returns the count.

## 2026-09-29 (a question, not a run, disproved this) — "every decoder would need a new mode" was true of the loops and false of the problem

**Claim.** Getting an optimized entry's remnant out does NOT need a new
decode mode in the eight methods; it needs the right output length, and
the remnant carries it.

**Evidence.** Every method in `src/fmt_sit.c` decodes to a requested
length and stops (stated as an invariant), so a caller may ask for four
bytes; `MacPaint 1`'s `DCMP` reads the remnant's length from the first
four bytes. `unar` 1.10.8 on the 2.0.1 archive produces **2,437 bytes
identical to what the `COMP` made on the Mac**. Two-pass decoding is a
**hypothesis**; the rest measured.

**Consequence.** OPEN_ITEMS.md's item shrinks; the withdrawal is in
BLOCKERS.md.

**Disproved by somebody asking why** (*"why do you need to touch other
decoders to add the 512 missing bytes"*), which required opening
`unc_sit_decode_fork`. **An estimate is a claim, checked against the code
it is about.** "The loop condition is wrong" became "the loop must change"
with no step between; **ask what else knows the right value before
deciding who has to be rewritten.** And FORMATS.md had said since
2026-09-28 that *"`unar` … is right about one of them"* (data fork exact,
resource fork 82 bytes of nothing). **A tool named as wrong about a case
is still evidence about the case.**

## 2026-09-29 (the smallest module was the biggest gain) — three of the four reversible Optimizers are undone in the engine, and two of them are exact

**Claim.** `src/fmt_sit.c` extracts Optimizer-touched entries: `Sound 1`
and `Photoshop 1` byte for byte with the archive's CRC agreeing; `MacPaint
1` as a valid painting that is not the user's file, reported as such;
`JPEG Lossy` still refused by name.

**Evidence.** `tools/run_sitopt.py` over the eight 2.0.1 archives:
`Sound 1`'s 8,192-byte and `Photoshop 1`'s 115,320-byte subjects identical
in both forks; `MacPaint 1`'s painting identical from 512 on, no resource
fork. Negative controls — delta disabled, header length wrong by twelve,
length prefix left in — give 2, 1 and 1 problems, the last as
`UNC_ERR_CORRUPT`.

**Consequence.** FORMATS.md, *What an Optimizer did to the fork*;
OPEN_ITEMS.md keeps only `JPEG Lossy`.

**The 264-byte module was worth more than the 3,010-byte one.** A day on
`MacPaint 1` bought a blank header; `Sound 1`'s **264-byte** `'DCMP'` took
ten minutes — a byte-wise cumulative sum, exact, and `Photoshop 1`'s is
the same code. **Survey the set before committing to a member of it.**

**The CRC field said which entries were restorable**: a `Sound 1` entry
carries the ORIGINAL's CRC-16; `MacPaint 1` and `JPEG Lossy` entries carry
**`ffff` in both fields** — missed twice (the 2026-09-28 reading counted
104..109, never printed 100..103). **A constant in a field that should
vary is the smell, in headers too.**

**The filter went in `unc_fork_flush`**, which takes the checksum, so the
CRC is over RESTORED bytes and no decoder changed — `unc_fork_put` would
have been bypassed by method 2, which writes straight into the staging
buffer.

**The guard earns its place**: `MacPaint 1`'s remnant states its length,
compared with the header's implied length — the defence against the
right-size-wrong-389-bytes failure seen twice.

## 2026-09-29 (the third time the corpus was mistaken for the machine) — Photoshop 1.0.7 runs on an emulated Mac Plus, and its own Optimizer round-trips what it writes

**Claim.** `Photoshop/JPEG Lossy` is not broken: `--makemods`'s subject was
not a Photoshop 1.0 document, and it round-trips one that is.

**Evidence.** `sitopt.py --add-photoshop`, `--psdoc`, `--psjpeg`.
Photoshop 1.0.7 runs under Mini vMac on the Plus and saves **196,608 bytes
of raw pixels, 256x256x3, no header**, geometry in a ten-byte `8BIM` 1000
resource. Stuffed and unstuffed in one boot: same size, **10.1 % of pixel
bytes changed**, 58 distinct values where it had 2.

**Consequence.** The refusal stands on new grounds: there is an oracle and
a subject; what stops it is a JPEG decoder on a 1 MB floor.

**Third time the corpus was mistaken for the machine**: *"the corpus has
no type-`8BIM` document"* was published as *"no oracle and no subject"*,
with the application a 441 KB download away. **A rule written down is not
learned; the tell is "this machine has none" reading as a conclusion
rather than "can it make one?".** And the page's *"Macintosh SE or newer"*
was wrong: **a stated minimum is a support claim, not a measurement**
(four-minute boot).

**The previous failure was in the archive's first sixteen bytes**: the
module's container records channels, height, width — **0, 0, 0** on the
synthetic subject, **3, 256, 256** on the real one — dumped the day before
and not decoded. **A structure worth dumping is worth parsing.**

## 2026-09-29 (the spike that found the work already done) — `JPEG Lossy` carries its own tables, and the codec has a name on it

**Claim.** The payload is a self-describing TIFF with its quantisation and
Huffman tables, and the module wraps a licensed C-Cube JPEG engine.

**Evidence.** The 14,047 bytes after the 80-byte header begin `MM\0*`: a
22-entry IFD, 256x256, 3x8 bits, YCbCr, compression **32865** (C-Cube's
private JPEG), quantisation at tag 33606 (Annex K zigzag, halved), DC/AC
Huffman at 33607/33608 byte-identical to the module's `DATA` 1001, quality
25 at 33604 matching `Pref` 128. The module file holds **`C3a` 1, 31,952
bytes, "C-Cube V1.0"**.

**Consequence.** Refusal unchanged; the estimate behind it withdrawn
(BLOCKERS.md).

**A spike should be allowed to invalidate its question**: look at the
artefact before executing the plan (listing the module file's resources,
never run). **When a dump answers "no", read it again for what it does
say** — `MM\0*` was on screen the day before. **Read the labels before the
instructions.**

## 2026-09-29 (a measured zero, declined — then reversed) — `JPEG Lossy` was put out of scope and put back the same day

**Decision.** StuffIt 2.0's `Photoshop/JPEG Lossy` Optimizer (module 3) is
out of scope for v1; entries named and refused per entry. OPEN_ITEMS.md,
Part 1.

**Not decided on difficulty or budget**: a 5,166-byte blob compiled into
`src/fmt_sit.c` moved resident `CODE` and A5 by **0 and 0**, landed in
`ovl_stuffit.bin`, moved no tally. **The price was zero and the answer is
still no.**

**Decided on**: **lossy by construction** (10.1 % of pixel bytes change in
Aladdin's own round trip); nobody has seen such an archive this project
did not write; and naming the module and skipping is already the right
answer.

**Two offered premises fail**: forging TIFF `Compression` 32865 → 6 gets
it past `libtiff`, which returns a **solid black 256x256 frame**; and an
upscaler cannot read a format. A decision can be right on other grounds —
first case where the wrong reason was corrected before being written.

**Reversed the same day.** The maintainer put it back once the premises
were shown not to hold: it will land as `module_restored = 2`, named and
flagged like `MacPaint 1`, because the format is described and costs the
shipped build nothing. Both halves kept as a record of how the arguments
moved. **Cost is a veto, not a reason.**

## 2026-10-01 (a page comment found what 947 fixtures could not) — zip's Macintosh extra fields are unread, and the corpus had no subject to say so with

**Found, not decided.** A Macintosh zip carries type, creator, Finder
flags and Mac dates in an extra field; `zip_extra_scan` knew Zip64 and
WinZip AES and passed the six Macintosh ids as unknown. Filed in
OPEN_ITEMS.md Part 2, *Zip's Macintosh extra fields*. (Implemented next
entry: *the field that was published all along*.)

**Evidence from a user's download page**: Macintosh Garden's Rex Nebular
entry has a 2022 comment that the disk images lose type and creator. On
`rexnebular_1_0_0.zip` data forks are perfect (21 of 21 identical to
`unzip`, ten disk images matching the archive's `checksum.md5`), `l` prints
empty type/creator for all 22 entries, `lsar` reads them. The page's `.sit`
gives all four metadata, 15 of 15 forks identical to `unar`.

**Why no suite caught it**: the differential suite grades type/creator
wherever `lsar` reads them, but none of the seven zips among 947 fixtures
carries a Macintosh extra field (`derived-MUSFMT10.ZIP`: host 0x07, no
extra fields). **A property the suite DOES grade is still ungraded if no
fixture exhibits it**: ask **"which fixture would fail if it broke?"**

**A corpus inherits its blind spots from the query that built it**: Mac
indexes hold `.sit`, `.cpt`, `.hqx`, `.bin`; the zips came from PC indexes
and a generator.

## 2026-10-01 (the field that was published all along) — zip's Macintosh extra fields cost 2,000 B of overlay and no licence

**Decision.** Read them. Info-ZIP's `0x334d` and ZipIt's `0x2705`/`0x2805`
give type, creator, Finder flags and dates; a ZipIt `0x2605` entry's data
is a MacBinary stream yielding both forks. **+2,000 B, all in
`ovl_exo`**; resident `CODE` +0, A5 +0, peak RAM +0, no tally moved
(FORMATS.md, *Zip's Macintosh extra fields*).

**The price nearly paid was the licence.** The first implementation cited
`reference/XADMaster/XADZipParser.m`; `tools/check_provenance.py` failed
it (`fmt_exo.c` is HISTORICAL). APPNOTE.TXT 4.6.4–4.6.6 specifies all
three ZipIt fields including `0x2605` (*"This block MUST be present if the
file is stored MacBinary-encoded"*), already in `reference/notes/`;
`0x334d` is specified in full in Info-ZIP's `proginfo/extrafld.txt`, one
`curl`. **The entire licence cost was an unfetched document.**

**The spec changed the code.** `FlCrDat` is "original Mac FileTime values
(local time!)" and the consumer `ioFlCrDat` is local, so dates are taken
unadjusted. **XADMaster adds `CrGMTOffs` and deark subtracts it, and both
label the result UTC** — neither is an oracle for that field. Every
`rexnebular_1_0_0.zip` entry carries −18000, so this engine's dates stand
5 h from `lsar`'s.

- **"The reference implementation on disk" is not "the source"**: a
  reader describes the format plus its author's purpose.
- **When two implementations disagree, the disagreement is the finding**,
  and it retires an oracle for one field only (dates ungradeable against
  `lsar`, type/creator gradeable).
- **A hardcoded budget does not fall when the build grows**:
  `run_tiers.py`'s resident `TIERS` were read at budgets not reduced by
  the control's +2,024 B and reported unmoved before that was measured.
  They hold at 651,508 / 222,620 / 127,220.

## 2026-10-02 (a 1990 approximation, reproduced on purpose) — C-Cube's JPEG is in the engine, byte-exact, and it cost the shipped build nothing

**`src/sit_ccube.c` decodes the `JPEG Lossy` payload, and the restored
data fork is byte-identical to what StuffIt Deluxe 2.0.1 hands back** —
196,608 bytes, zero differing — while the RESOURCE fork matches the
original document's (2.0.1's own output does not). FORMATS.md, *What an
Optimizer did to the fork*.

**The target was Aladdin's output, not the picture.** A float IDCT came
0.96 % away and jpeg-6b's `jpeg_idct_islow` 1.065 % — *worse*. The only
reachable answer is the 1990 decoder's, error included: read the
arithmetic out of the module.

**Half was published and unfetched**: the entropy layer is ITU-T T.81's
(Annex F tables, category codes, `FF 00` stuffing, Figure A.6 zig-zag),
now `reference/notes/itu-t81.pdf` via `tools/fetch_references.sh`;
`src/sit_ccube.c` cites what T.81 states and what only `CCOD` does
separately.

**Reading beat guessing**: a sweep over families and precisions (8–16
bits of cosine, every descale split) bottomed at 4.48 % on the inked
blocks; `tools/ccube/m68ktrace.py`, a symbolic interpreter over one
straight-line region, had the 1-D network out of `CCOD`+0x2f3c in about an
hour. **A search over plausible implementations is unbounded; reading the
implementation is bounded by the size of the function.**

**Cost**: all in the StuffIt overlay (18,582 → 23,174 B); resident `CODE`
and A5 unchanged to the byte; all six tallies unmoved. Peak heap 31.7 KB
for 256x256, growing with the stored fork and PADDED width: one MCU row of
three components, the stream decoded once per output plane (14 KB stream
against a 64 KB plane).

**UB only a sanitizer could find**: `blk[i] <<= 3` on a negative
dequantised coefficient is undefined (C99 6.5.7p4); UBSan caught it on the
first full `ci.sh` (coefficient −25). Now `blk[i] *= 8`. **A transform can
be bit-for-bit correct on every specimen and still be undefined.**

**Left measured and unexplained**: `CCOD`+0x3826's apparent
round-toward-zero after `(x + 16) >> 5`; output is exact only WITHOUT it
(with it, 709 of 65,536 luma samples miss by one). (settled: DECISIONS.md
2026-10-02, *the measurement that was waiting for a second input*.)

**"Somebody else's archive" was the wrong bar.** An archive **we
synthesised** differs from one **the original application wrote for us**:
all nine specimens are 2.0.1's own output, so the reading is graded
against authentic bytes. What a stranger's archive would add is an unasked
combination (another quality, method, an Optimizer over an encrypted
entry) — boots of `sitopt.py`, so the item moved from *"find one"* to
*"ask for them"* (OPEN_ITEMS.md). Only a SUBJECT needing absent software
remains: Sound Designer II.

- **The provenance that matters is the WRITER's, not the owner's.**
- **"More correct" is not a direction when the oracle is old software**:
  the better IDCT scoring worse was the settling measurement.
- **The cost question and the scope question are different**: a decoder in
  its format's overlay measured the shipped build identical. Price the
  axis the user pays on first.

## 2026-10-02 (the measurement that was waiting for a second input) — `CCOD`+0x3826 does not round toward zero, and one drawing was too easy to say so

**The C-Cube entry's one unexplained item is settled** (FORMATS.md, *What
an Optimizer did to the fork*); the claim is withdrawn (BLOCKERS.md).

**Two readings that cannot both be true** — "the trace of that tail is
wrong" and "the image never takes that branch". Re-reading the disassembly
is circular for the first; an input that takes the branch separates them.

**A subject drawn for the arithmetic**: `sitopt.py --psdoc --drawing grid`
crosses a 6-pixel comb with a 12-pixel one (an edge in nearly every 8x8
block); Photoshop 1.0.7 saved it, 2.0.1 stuffed and unstuffed it. Stored
22,097 B against 14,127, 21.0 % of pixel bytes changed against 10.1 %. The
correction got **9,645** bytes wrong against 2,127, and the decoder was
byte-exact on both: the branch is taken, the correction is not the
module's.

- **"Unexplained" has an expiry date, retired usually by an input, not an
  insight**: ask *what input would make the two explanations disagree*.
  Two boots.
- **A test passing on an easy subject is not evidence it is
  load-bearing**: a tolerance would have swallowed the easy subject's
  2,127 bytes; grade an approximation by equality when available.

## 2026-10-02 (three defaults that were being read as format) — what StuffIt Deluxe 2.0.1 will actually be asked for, and what it refuses to be asked by script

**Every optimized specimen was one subject, default quality, one method.**
Six boots made it a range, and three "format properties" were the
defaults'.

**The quantisation tables are not "halved"**: that is Q=25; at Q=50 they
are Annex K **unscaled**, so the rule is Annex K x Q/50. The decoder reads
the tables from the file and was never at risk.

**The quality is a user setting**: the Optimizers dialog is an activation
list, but clicking a module's row opens **the module's own dialog**
(quantization level, recommends 20 to 30) — found by a failed run whose
screenshot showed a filename swallowed into its Q field. **A probe that
fails usefully beats one that passes blindly**, given a photograph after
every click.

**The method matrix closed a comment.** `src/fmt_sit.c` refused a `JPEG
Lossy` fork with method nibble ≠ 0 *"the only shape seen"*. Asked for
`fast`, `faster`, `better`, `optimal`, 2.0.1 stores the optimized fork
identically every time; the refusal is now measured across every method.

**Not closed**: arming `PassLock` from Options ▸ Custom Encryption… ticks
the item, but a scripted `Stuff` writes a plain archive silently. The
script's security vocabulary is `newde` and `des` (STR# 257), so **menu
state does not reach scripted stuffing**.

- **A default observed once is indistinguishable from a constant**; ask
  the writer for a second value.
- **When a tool will not be driven, find out which half refuses**: menus
  configure interactive Stuff, scripts carry their own arguments.

## 2026-10-02 (the question that was about the user, not the format) — `PassLock` protects nothing, so the engine stops refusing

**"But what if the user has the password?"** The engine had just been
taught to refuse `PassLock` with *"no password will open it"*. The module
appends sixteen bytes of key material and the method's padding and
**leaves every compressed byte of both forks exactly as an unprotected
archive has them** — measured on two subjects, FORMATS.md, *Encryption*.
Refusing withheld bytes in the clear.

**The specimen's plaintext was already known** (default quality, a payload
already held byte for byte), so one XOR compared them: identical, not
something a cipher produces. **A specimen whose plaintext is already known
is worth more than one merely valid.**

**Investigated properly**: the entry's CRC-16 passes over the engine's
output; the `DCMP` data path **pushes the buffer pointer and calls a
routine that sets a flag and returns, never dereferencing it**, and `COMP`
is the same; the About box says *"PassLock provides simple password
protection for files"*. Its resource id **514** (`(kind-1) << 8 | id`,
kind 3, id 2) confirms the header byte.

**Then made SILENT.** A per-entry line gives a user nothing to act on;
lines are earned by entries whose bytes differ from what went in (`MacPaint
1`, `JPEG Lossy`). The fact lives in FORMATS.md.

**The field went with the message.** `UncEntryInfo.encryptor_nominal` took
the struct from 302 to 304 bytes on the 68000 (fields 292..300 packed,
`name_full_len` then needs a pad); removed, it is 302 again.
`check_docs.py` failed on the stated size in both directions, naming all
three places.

- **A refusal is a claim**: *"No password will open it"* was about the
  format and false; the true statement was about us. Test: would somebody
  with the right software or password get a different answer?
- **Measure a security property before assuming it either way**: one XOR.
- **A true fact is not automatically worth printing**: a warning that fires
  every time and cannot be acted on is noise.

## 2026-10-02 (the verifier that said where NOT to look) — all five of StuffIt 2.x's ciphers, decrypted

**Five schemes, three ciphers, one key derivation**: `DES`/`DESex` are
standard DES in CBC; `NewDE™`/`NewDEx` StuffItDES in CBC; 3.5's built-in
StuffItDES through an 8-byte feedback XOR; `PassLock` enciphers nothing
(FORMATS.md, *The three ways 2.0.1 encrypts*).

**The engine's own verifier located the problem.** `unc_crypt_sit`
decrypts `'MKey'` under the derived key and checks it — and on a 2.0.1
`DES` archive with the right password **it passed**, so only the fork
transform could be wrong. **A verifier is a bisection point.**

**The sweep**: 32 file-key variants × 8 transforms, scored on 286 known
plaintext bytes; 286 of 286 on the first run including STANDARD DES
(already here for PackIt) — possible because a plain control was made in
the same boot.

**Implementation**: both primitives existed (`des_crypt` with IP/FP for
PackIt, `sitdes_crypt` without for StuffIt); CBC is four lines.

- **A refusal that names what the WORLD cannot do is a bug** — second
  that day; smell: "nothing", "never", "cannot be" about something outside
  the program.
- **Ask the format's own check before asking the format**: a verifier is a
  free measurement of your own code.

## 2026-10-02 (the bar somebody else set) — "everything StuffIt 2 can make BY DEFAULT", and why that is the right line

**"Are we good now?" needed a bar**: the format lets a fork go to an
external COMPRESSOR module, which anybody could have written. The
maintainer's line: **everything the application writes by default**, with
what Aladdin sold in the box; a third party's plug-in waits for somebody's
file.

**Finite, and its inside closed**: Aladdin's two disks carry five
Optimizers, three encryptors, nine translators, **not one compressor**. On
2026-10-02 every Optimizer, cipher, script compression word including
`guess`, a 1.5.1-compatible archive and a folder were asked of 2.0.1 and
read back (FORMATS.md).

**The comparison table's row** says what StuffIt Deluxe 2.0 wrote; the two
later Deluxes' cells say *not tested here*; the 🔴 is 2.0's own Engine
refusing its Optimizers' entries.

**A completeness claim needs a bar somebody can check**: what the SHIPPED
software produces is finite and is what users have; "what the format
permits" is an argument.

## 2026-10-03 (method 14) — the hole that needed no file, and the four places the transcription departs

**"The only open items need files we don't have" was wrong about one
row.** StuffIt 5 method 14 needed only a decoder: two specimens (Aladdin's
5.5 and 7.0.3 installer payloads), `unar`, and
`reference/XADMaster/XADStuffItOldHandles.m`. The engine refused 80 of
7.0.3's 258 entries; it extracts all 258 now.

**The method**: LZSS over a 256 KB window, both alphabets canonically
Huffman-coded per block, plus an alphabet for the code lengths. deark names
it "installer" with a NULL decompressor, so the citation is permanent
(NOTICE; OPEN_ITEMS.md Part 1).

**Four measured departures:**

- **Two recursions removed**: the code-length quicksort runs from an
  explicit range stack (same permutation), the nested tree read is a
  branch.
- **A nested tree that nests again is refused**: the reference aliases one
  array as scratch and result; 797 nested reads across both payloads, all
  depth 1.
- **The byte boundary discards its bits** (`xadIOByteBoundary` leaves up
  to seven bits for the next refill to OR over): **3,326 boundaries, not
  one nonzero pad**.
- **The block length clamps instead of wrapping** past zero.

**17 KB of tables omitted**: `SIT_14` builds `var6[1024]` and
`var8[0x4000]` and never reads them (a compressor's inverse mapping) — 17
KB of a 283 KB working set.

**Grading needed an ENCODER**: the specimens are uncommittable installers,
so `tools/synth_sit14.py` writes 1,859 B, four entries, one shape each,
adjudicated by `unar`. Its first version omitted an escape before a repeat
count, and the decoder said so.

**Fuzzing**: 1,500 `fuzz.py` cases entered no method-14 function (seed
drawn from 946 fixtures); 2,000 targeted mutants reached 95.5 % of lines
and found two faults — a signed left shift in canonical code assignment on
a corrupt tree, and a pre-existing leak in `cli/main.c` on the path where
an archive fails after a name was shortened (which also suppressed the
notice saying where those files went). **"0 failures" from a run whose
reach is unmeasured is the emptiest green.**

**Cost**: 2,613 B of text, all in `ovl_stuffit` (23,670 → 26,278 B);
shipped `CODE` and A5 unmoved; control +2,624 B. Peak heap 276 KB on a
real fork, 65 KB on the synthetic (window sized to the fork,
`sit13_winsize`). No tally moves.

## 2026-10-04 (the tolerance that had to be written down first) — a real MacZip in the corpus, and the column that had been eating the names

**The fixture lands.** `rexnebular_1_0_0.zip` — 29.7 MB, 22 entries, Zip
2.3, host 0x07 (the 2026-10-01 Macintosh Garden comment's archive) — is
corpus fixture 935, the first Macintosh-written zip there. OPEN_ITEMS.md's
row is closed and gone.

**Graded**: names, folders, both forks, type/creator and Finder flags,
22/22 against `lsar`, 21 data forks byte-identical to `unar`, every
`ci.sh` run. **Not graded: the three Macintosh DATES** — XADMaster does
`create += readInt32LE`, deark `de_mac_time_to_timestamp(mt_raw -
mt_offset)`, both labelled UTC (re-read in `XADZipParser.m` and
`modules/zip.c`); every entry carries −18000, so our unadjusted dates
stand 5 h from `lsar`'s on all 22.

**The exclusion is declared, not inherited.** The manifest carries
`"ungraded": {"dates": "..."}` with the reasoning; `run_diff.py` refuses
any other field under the key or an empty reason, and prints the
declaration every run; `make_manifests.py` carries it across `--force`.

**The fixture found a hole.** Type/creator came from `macextract l`'s
`%4s/%-4s` columns, so a code holding a SPACE shifted the name: `PDF
/CARO` parsed as type `PDF` and name `/CARO docs/mac_package.pdf`, matched
no manifest entry, and **the comparison did not happen**. 200 of the
corpus's 5,539 codes hold a space; a NUL truncates the row. `l --finder`
now prints type, creator and flags as hex, and an unparsable row fails.
All 935 fixtures pass the exact comparison: the silence hid agreement, and
cost the ability to notice.

**Finder flags graded where the oracle has them**: 22 entries today
(no older manifest carries the key). Corpus-wide 3,195 would be gradeable;
`unar`'s AppleDouble `fdFlags` and `lsar`'s `XADFinderFlags` agree on all
423 where both exist, and the engine agrees with `lsar` on all 3,195.
Recording them means rebuilding 934 manifests, a separate change.

**Cost, measured first**: 0.51 s a diff run, 2.8 s a robustness run, ~11 s
of `ci.sh` across eight lanes; slowest robustness variant 0.51 s against a
30 s timeout; `fixtures/` grows 41 % (TESTING.md, *The Finder metadata,
and the one field no oracle settles*). **Not measured** as a whole-suite
difference: 489 s with against 511 s without, the diff suite moving 24.7 →
38.4 s between identical runs. **A difference measurement needs the
difference to be bigger than the instrument.**

**Transferable.** *A comparison that cannot run is indistinguishable from
one that passes*; `run_diff.py` printed "fixtures ok" through both holes.
The suite now COUNTS what it compares (it prints how many Finder flags it
checked).

## 2026-10-04 (the archive that carried its own extractor) — nine real ZipIt archives, and the premise that was only APPNOTE's word

OPEN_ITEMS.md said ZipIt's three Mac extra fields were graded only on
archives written here, because **ZipIt's output is a plain `.zip`,
invisible to a search by name** — true and incomplete.

### What was indexed, and what was not

**By content, for the self-extractors**: dexvert (Discmaster's identifier)
files a ZipIt SEA's stub as `zipIt`. `format=zipIt` returns 69 files, 67
ZipIt's own distribution (59 copies of one 1.4 self-extractor) and **two
somebody else made**, an EV Nova plug-in and its installer.

**Not at all, for the plain ones**: `detection=ZPIT` returns one unrelated
file, `q=ZPIT` none. So: `format=zip` over the 40 Discmaster items
`tools/fetch_specimens.py` cites gives **3,029 zips**; an HTTP `Range`
request for each first local header — **512 bytes per archive, 1.5 MB for
the sweep** against 7.3 GB — finds **seven carrying a ZipIt field**, four
distinct. `tools/scan_discmaster_zips.py` keeps the sweep. **Trap**:
Discmaster's `pageNum` is 0-based and `pageNum=1` on a single-page result
returns an empty array, so a sweep from page 1 reports "0 zips" for an item
holding 35. **A crawler asked for a page that does not exist gets an empty
answer, not an error**; test against a known hit.

### The premise, measured in both directions

APPNOTE.TXT 4.6.4: the long field "MUST be present if the file is stored
MacBinary-encoded and SHOULD NOT be used if the file is not". Over **119
entries**: all **16 file entries with a reachable `0x2605` payload decode
to MacBinary**, none of the **86 carrying `0x2705`** does; the field's
`FileType`/`Creator` equal the MacBinary header's in all 16, so reading
the header (2026-10-01) loses nothing.

**One exception, ZipIt 1.x's**: the LONG field on three DIRECTORY entries
(1.4 and the Japanese 1.x), where APPNOTE assigns `0x2805`. Zero bytes, so
the claim is false; `zip_mb_peek` refuses under 128 bytes and probes the
header — **the engine verifies the claim instead of trusting the flag**.
ZipIt 2.2.2 uses `0x2805`.

### The three shapes a real writer uses

`0x2705` at **12 bytes** (type and creator, ZipIt 1.x), **14** (plus
`fdFlags`) and **16** (plus the trailing word); `0x2805` always 8. Both
length guards do something, and the 12-byte form has a subject.

### The name, which neither implementation reads

`0x2605`'s "full Macintosh filename" is ignored by this engine. Over 20 real
`0x2605` entries the zip's name, the field's and the MacBinary header's
agree 16 times. The four that differ split evenly:

- ZipIt 2.2.2's `Drop files here to zip (OS X)` is 29 characters in zip and
  field, 22 in the MacBinary header; XADMaster takes the header's and
  **loses `(OS X)`**; this engine keeps the zip's.
- One archive's names went in MS-DOS form (`PSYCHO!`, `README`, `SAMPLE`)
  with `Psycho!`, `READ ME`, `Sample` in the field; XADMaster recovers
  them, **this engine writes the PC-safe name**. (Written as a habit of
  ZipIt 1.x; corrected 2026-10-05 — a per-archive PREFERENCE, see *a leaf
  is not a path, and a version is not a preference*.)

Nothing changed: **every entry this build can extract is in the agreeing
16**. `tools/run_zipit.py`'s tolerance is "ZipIt's own field is one of the
two names", which can fail.

### And the premise that fell with it

`Psycho!v1.0ß1.zip` — a White Knight script set, February 1994, written by
ZipIt, MacBinary payloads with resource forks — has **every entry in method
6, Implode.** Part 1's remaining ground for keeping Implode out, *"not a
Macintosh method"*, **is now false, measured**. The CLI's refusal asks for a
specimen and one has arrived; the decision stays the maintainer's. Adding
Implode would also need the `0x2605` name: these are the three entries
whose names this engine gets wrong.

### What went into the suite, and why not all of it

Two became corpus fixtures, plain zips the sniffer reads:
`MrTs_Paint_Folder.zip` (`0x2705`, `0x2805`, no forks) and
`NPWritersKit.zip` (a `0x2605` entry, 150,016 B data fork, 323 B resource
fork), graded by `run_diff.py` against a committed manifest with **no
oracle at run time**. The other seven are specimens because **a ZipIt SEA
was not recognised**: the head is code, though the walker reads all five
with `-f Zip`. `tools/run_zipit.py` forces the format for those five and
asserts the other four are sniffed. (Recognised from 2026-10-05: *the scan
that was already being paid for*.)

### The instrument, and what it cannot see

Made to fail first: rewriting every `0x2605` id to `0x2805` in one specimen
gives 4 failures; moving the `0x2705` flag read two bytes in
`src/fmt_exo.c` gives 66. It asserts per-specimen tallies (entries, count
per field id, MacBinary payloads) so a parse that stopped would not pass
on zeros. It compares no fork of an out-of-scope method (declared every
run) and adjudicates no date (`lsar` reports the MS-DOS stamp where the
MacBinary header carries two Mac ones).

### The tool that was eating the documentation

`harvest.py --probe` rewrote `fixtures/SOURCES.md` whole from its own
`HEADER` constant, so **registering a fixture deleted twelve lines of
prose** (the paragraph naming non-archive fixtures that must not have
manifests); noticed only from `git diff`'s `1 insertion, 13 deletions`.
`save_sources` keeps everything above the table marker verbatim and
round-trips byte-exact. **A generator that regenerates a file it does not
own all of throws away the part it does not know about.**

## 2026-10-04 (the installation nobody installed) — StuffIt 5.5 and 7.0.3 over Info-ZIP's `0x334d`, and three ways a keystroke lies

**The question.** FORMATS.md said StuffIt does not read `0x334d`: 3.5.2
RUN over an archive, 5.5 and 7.0.3 READ (labelled). Now measured: both run
on 2026-10-04 and agree (FORMATS.md, *What Aladdin's own software does with
the same bytes*).

**Why it got cheap.** 5.5 wants a 68020, 7.0.3 a PowerPC: the Mac OS 9
guest (~40 s a pointer move, menus unusable). But method 14 (2026-10-03)
extracts both installer PAYLOADS, and `hfsboot.img` (2026-09-27) is
writable by hfsutils, so the installation is **assembled on Linux** —
engine, translators and application `hcopy -m`'d into a System Folder; the
only pointer work is two licence buttons. **Closed by a decoder and a disk
image, neither written for it.**

**Where the pieces go is read**: the 5.5 engine's `STR# 999` (`Extensions`,
`Aladdin`, `Extensions:Aladdin`), `STR# 1004` (`:Extensions`, `StuffIt
Engine™`), `fld# 999` (`Translators`); the installer's *What was installed
(and where)* `PICT`s agree.

**Select by type and creator, never by name**: an InstallerMaker payload
carries zero-length `STde`/`STin` directives (one is `! Zip Translator`);
matching `*Translator` selected empty files. Picking by `SITo`/`SIT!` and
asserting the documented count (seventeen) fails instead.

**Three keystrokes that lie, identical from outside:**

- **A Return in the Finder renames.** `os9.py`'s `Cmd-Q, Return` quits the
  HFS+ master's Setup Assistant; `hfsboot.img` has none, so the Return
  renamed the boot volume `HFSBoot` to `sit` and the run reported every
  step healthy. **A step borrowed from another harness carries its
  assumptions about what is on screen.**
- **A chord the application does not have is ignored**: 5.5's Expand is ⌘E,
  7.0.3's ⌘O (`MENU` 129); under ⌘E 7.0.3 sat 127 s and carried on.
- **Return does not reach a non-default button**: `Disagree`/`Agree` have
  identical frames (six presses moved neither); in 7.0.3's Navigation
  Services dialog `Open` is enabled for FOLDERS, so Return navigated into
  the boot volume and reported "expansion started".

**Caught by reading the verdict off the disk and looking at the
screenshots.**

**The CarbonLib gate.** 7.0.3's Expander names the CarbonLib version it
refuses; Apple's 1.6 update is NDIF (out of scope, OPEN_ITEMS.md Part 1),
so the guest mounts and installs it, and the pass condition is the
extension's `vers` read back with hfsutils.

**Result.** No StuffIt reads the field across nine years and three
generations; all three lose `MSWD` three times of three. 7.0.3 stopped
rewriting text (3.5.2 and 5.5 convert CRLF to CR; 7.0.3 returns all four
forks byte-identical) and stopped GUESSING (`checksum.md5` gets type and
creator zero, not `TEXT/ttxt`). **The last classic StuffIt fixed the data
and dropped the metadata.**


## 2026-10-05 (the sample that was read as the table) — two of fourteen call sites, and the id they named belonged to another format

The 2026-09-27 reading said the decoding was behind `GetResource('Eng ',
2)` @0x334c, and the brief became **read the 26,362-byte `'Eng ' 2`.**

**It is the StuffIt/PackIt unstuffer.** There are **fourteen** `'Eng '`
literals, a 7 × 2 table of thunks for ids 0–6, reached from a seven-way
chain at @0x30c0, and **none tests `.pkg`**:

| recogniser | test | → |
|---|---|---|
| @0x37ac | extension `.HQX` | `'Eng ' 0` |
| @0x37f0 | type `PACT` or creator `EXTR` | `'Eng ' 1` |
| @0x3834 | type `HBSF` | `'Eng ' 2` |
| @0x386a | `.ZIP`, `.GZ`, `.TGZ` | `'Eng ' 3` |
| @0x38dc | `.ARC` | `'Eng ' 4` |
| @0x3920 | `.Z` | `'Eng ' 5` |
| @0x3962 | `.UU`, `.UUE` | `'Eng ' 6` |

Three are confirmed by contents (`'Eng ' 0` BinHex's table, `'Eng ' 3` the
gzip magic, `'Eng ' 5` `1f 9d`). `'Eng ' 1` is **Compact Pro**: its header
parser matches `src/fmt_cpt.c` field for field, and its `STR# 211` item 15
(*"this is a segmented archive"*) is `UNC_ERR_SEGMENTED`'s condition.

**The resource names say where the code came from**: `PKG Expand
Translator`'s `'Othe' 0` is *named* `CompactPro`, `Unix Compress
Translator`'s code `UUCode` — copied siblings with a new `STR# 129`.

### Where the reference implementation actually was

**StuffIt Deluxe 3.0.7 ships `AppleLink Package Translator` 3.0.3,
"Copyright © 1990-1992 Aladdin Systems, Inc."** — not a predecessor of
`PKG Expand` but a different program: `'Othe' 1`, 33,300 bytes, **148
MacsBug symbols**, `'ALinkFont'`, an `'INT ' 6000` *"line speed, bps"*.
Its `'HBSF' 0` is `SQUEEZEPLAY 1.0`; routines `RdSQPDirectory`,
`WrSQPDirectory`, `InitSqp`, `unpackFile`, `Decompress`, `GetCode`. The
format is **SqueezePlay**.

No emulator: the 3.0.7 installer's two StuffIt segments (`ac d9 00 01` /
`00 02`) each carry a 100-byte header, and `seg1[100:] + seg2[100:]` is
**exactly** the `0x14dd14` the `SIT!` header declares; then `macextract`
extracts it, CRCs passing. Layout, codec and grading: FORMATS.md
(*AppleLink packages*); `tools/derive_sqp.py`, thirteen witnesses. **4 of
4** members of both real packages expand to their declared length.

### The lessons

**Count the call sites before believing the one you read** — one step on
from *check which question the cited routine answers*: fourteen hits in
the same 16,482 bytes, seven consecutive ids, is a dispatch table. **A
resource's NAME is evidence about where its code came from.** And the 3.0.7
installer had been in `~/.cache/macextract/stuffit307/` since 2026-09-28,
fetched to count translators — the fourth time: **before filing a route
that needs new evidence, look for what a PAST question produced.**

### One thing this session got wrong in its own tool, and it is the smell in CLAUDE.md

The first `derive_sqp.py` passed `rec["dlen"]` as a ceiling and asserted
the output was `dlen` long: **it reported OK on a package with a byte
flipped mid-stream.** Without the ceiling the corrupted file reports 1,960
bytes against a declared 1,954 and exits non-zero. Each member's sha256 is
recorded in the script, because a package has no per-member checksum.


## 2026-10-05 (the file the item asked for was already in ci.sh) — the offset-delta search fuzzed, and a `--check` that compared nothing

`now_find_delta` was the last unfuzzed Now Compress function; OPEN_ITEMS.md
wanted *"an archive whose block table carries a delta"*. **This project has
written one since M12** (`synth_now.py`'s `synth-now-delta`,
`synth-now-delta-small`, graded three ways against `unar` by `run_now.py`).
`fuzz.py`'s repair generator drew only from `corpus()`. **When an item
names what it wants, grep for it**: eight days.

**The file alone would have done nothing**: `now_repair` finds payloads via
`mutate_now.blocks` → `derive_now.member_blocks`, which had no offset-delta
search, so a delta archive fell out of `now_seeds()` silently. The Python
side got the engine's search, transcribed from
`-findFileHeaderDeltaWithHeaderOffset:firstOffset:`
(`reference/XADMaster/XADNowCompressHandle.m`), same order.

**`tools/mutate_now.py --check` compared nothing**: on every `--delta` run
since 2026-09-21 it zipped two empty lists, printed `0 block(s) read the
same, 0 changed` and exited 0. No downstream cost (the delta ladder's
verdicts came from the Macintosh, 2026-09-21; the engine is graded by
`unar`), but it is why this took eight days. **A comparator that iterates
over what it parsed reports success when parsing failed.** Compared-nothing
fails now; planting a `table_delta` returning 0 turns it red.

**One archive had to be written, with the sign on it**: existing deltas
were +134 and +8. `synth-now-delta-neg` is off by **-64**, read by `unar`,
this engine and `derive_now`, and **gated on the sign**: forcing
`now_find_delta` positive refuses it and leaves the other three, 1 of 4.

**Re-measured**: `fuzz_cover.py` at 3,000 cases, **Now Compress 13
functions, 0 never entered, at seeds 11 and 12**. Other families moved both
ways in those runs — **ARC 0 at seed 11 against 13 at seed 12**, StuffIt
classic 9 against 2 — **more than the five functions the noise floor
claimed**; corrected to thirteen in all three places. Read only whether a
family is WHOLLY at zero, at more than one seed.

**Wart**: `fuzz_cover.py` opened with `make clean` and no `BUILD=`, i.e.
`rm -rf build`, deleting `build/san` and every oracle (deark, lha, mpack,
50 MB of clone-and-compile). It now empties only its own directory.

## 2026-10-05 (the seed nobody drew) — method 14 fuzzed by naming a seed and targeting its streams, and the two rows of the instrument that could not report

**The row was half wrong.** *"method 14's decoder is never entered by
`fuzz.py`"* was measured at 1,500 cases; at 3,000, **ten of eleven
functions are entered** at seeds 11 and 12 (the seed is 1 of ~958, ~2.3
draws). Written without its case count (BLOCKERS.md) — while the tool's
own docstring said small-run zeros may be sampling.

**What a bigger run cannot buy**: `sit14_lengths_coded` is at 0 % at every
seed and count (entry 4's shape; mutants die first). Fix as for the
ciphers (2026-09-26): name the seed and confine edits to decoder bytes.
`synth_sit14.py --ranges` gives the four method-14 streams, 1,345 B of
1,859.

**The decomposition is not the obvious one.** Naming the seed is most of
the gain: 120 whole-file-mutated cases reach all eleven functions and
95.5 % of the entry function's lines; targeting adds 98.5 % and
`sit14_tree` 94.4 → 100. **A per-case probability is not a reach figure.**

**The twelve existing seeds had the same disease.** `method_seeds()`
(`-lh2-`, `-lh3-`, DiskDoubler 3/4/5, since 2026-09-27) entered the pool at
fixture weight: `-lh2-`'s `lzd_*` read 2 never entered at seed 12 and
**16 of 16, the whole file, one reshuffle later.** Named seeds now take one
case in 32; `-lh2-` reads 1 at seeds 11, 12 and 13.

**1/32 over 1/16, measured**: same family counts at three seeds; total
never-entered LOWER at 1/32 at all three (147/137/150 against
174/163/156). ARC reads 7, 11, 18 at 1/32 against 15, 15, 13 at 1/16 — **a
family whose specimens are one archive each is a lottery however the
draws are weighted**, so the share was chosen on the one number that moved
one way at every seed.

**Two instrument rows could not report.** `^sit\d*_` put method 14's eleven
functions in a "StuffIt classic" of 34, which can never read wholly zero.
The BinHex regex named `hqx_`/`binhex_` where functions are `bh_`: zero
matches, skipped silently, twelve functions absent rather than unmeasured.
**An aggregate that names its subjects by pattern has to be asked whether
the pattern matched anything.** Empty rows now print, and unmatched
functions are counted: 381 of 581 (containers and envelopes).

**Would it have found the motivating defect?** `sit14_build`'s counter
planted signed again (2026-10-03) is caught by **11 of 400 `--stream-only`
cases and by none of 3,000 under the old instrument**. Entered is not
exercised. `ci.sh`'s 150-case smoke misses it too (11 stream cases, 2.75 %
hit rate), in TESTING.md so nobody reads the green as coverage.

**What the mode cannot see**: the window-wrap half of `sit14_flush` (needs
a fork past 256 KB; this seed's largest is 17,799 B) — **withdrawn
2026-10-06, 458 B of stream decode to 278,896 B and a second named seed
wraps it** (BLOCKERS.md; 2026-10-06, *the fork that was cheaper than the
file*); the `goto out` after a failed flush (a sink write error); any
container but a bare `.sit`. A mutant is graded by nothing; the seed is,
by `run_diff` against `unar`.

## 2026-10-05 (the deviation that was the reference) — AppleLink packages extract, and the codec needed no parameter

The brief: **SqueezePlay sets the next free code to 256 after a clear where
`compress` sets 257, so `src/unc_lzw.c` cannot be reused unchanged —
choose a parameter or a separate path on measured m68k size.**

**Neither: the premise is wrong.** `reference/macutils/macunpack/
de_compress.c`, Unix `compress`'s own decompressor, at the clear code:

    clear_flg = 1;
    free_ent = FIRST - 1;

`FIRST` is 257, so `compress` sets **256**, as the expander does at
@0x2ae0. **deark**'s rendering (`delzw_clear`, `free_code_search_start =
first_dynamic_code`) sets 257, and `src/unc_lzw.c` was transcribed from
deark. A fact about our own source, promoted to a fact about `compress`.
Withdrawn (BLOCKERS.md). The renderings differ only in an unobservable
write to slot 256 (consumed as the clear code before any lookup).

**0 bytes of either**: `unc_lzw_init(&z, al, in, 13, 1, clen)`, ARC method
9's configuration, graded by 10 ARC fixtures every run.

### What made that safe to believe, and it is not the argument above

**A SqueezePlay fork is a `.Z` file without its header**: prepend `1f 9d`
and 13 | 0x80 and `gzip -dc` decodes it. All four real members and all 18
LZW forks of six synthesised packages match the engine, including a
36,000-byte stream filling the 8,192-entry table twice (two clears). A
**second implementation found by asking what the codec IS** — nothing reads
`.pkg` (`unar`, deark, macunpack: zero hits for "applelink" or
"squeezeplay"). In `ci.sh` now (TESTING.md, *AppleLink packages:
SqueezePlay*).

### Three things the reading had wrong, all from routines nobody had read

`tools/derive_sqp.py` graded 4/4 with three fields wrong:

- **Record +4 and +16 are the resource fork's compressed length and
  absolute offset** (mirroring +8/+12), filed as unread because zero in all
  four members; `DoWork` @0x714 tests +4, @0x816 writes +16.
- **The stored flag is bit 1 of the BYTE at +84**, not a `u16` (bit 1 vs
  bit 9); all four hold `0x8000`. Evidence: `btst #1,%a3@(96)` on memory is
  a byte operation.
- **The resource fork has its own stored bit**, bit 2 (`DoWork` @0x96e).

New: the header's count is the **SQP** directory's (capped at 50, skipping
folders and compressed types), the **item** count the second header's; a
version-1 HFS directory carries a `u16` level and folder flag per record —
a folder TREE, which the engine extracts.

**A folder's type and creator are a rectangle**: `AddItems` @0x2378 copies
16 bytes of Finder info whatever `PBGetCatInfo` left, so a folder carries a
`DInfo` whose first eight bytes are its window rect. Flags and dates
survive; type/creator are left unknown for folders.
`synth-sqp-folder.pkg`'s `TEXT`/`ttxt` were the generator's. **A generator
that shares the decoder's reading agrees with it about its mistakes.**

**A reading that passes is not a reading that is complete**: every one of
the five fields was zero or constant in both specimens; reading the WRITER
(`DoSqForward`, `DoItemsForward`, `AddItems`) found them.

### The probe, which had to be a file test

`src/fmt_sqp_probe.c`: item count, version byte, eight zero bytes, a
directory tiling the file to its last byte, plus every name within a
`Str31` and every level between 1 and one deeper than the previous.

**666 B of 68000 text, resident** (the sniffer calls it for every file);
with the release switch case, shim and table row, **788 B off every
extraction's budget on a 1 MB Mac Plus**, the largest single shipped
addition since the overlays. Two cheaper shapes measured **6 B worse**
each (a field-offset table; one zero-run helper). Aladdin's reader matched
the extension; this one recognises CONTENT.

### Its own image, and the count goes back to fifteen

`ovl_sqp` is **1,972 B**, the smallest of fifteen. An image costs 12 B of
bundle directory and 8 B of block header — 20 B against making every
`.pkg` carry PackIt's 2,648 B and every `.pit` SqueezePlay's 1,972. A
package gets the **largest per-format grant any format has**, +119,534 B
against the control (FORMATS.md, *What each format is granted*).

### What the generator is for, and what it is not

`tools/synth_sqp.py` writes a package per unreached path (resource fork,
stored fork, two clears, version 0, folder tree), an ENCODER read from the
same binary: `Compress` @0x27de and `PutCode` @0x28fe (`compress()` and
`output()` without `cl_block`). Stored members are incompressible bytes
(the writer's rule at @0x4e2). **Three of five paths are graded against
our own reading** (no second container reader exists), stated in
FORMATS.md; `gzip` settles the clear code and 13-bit width. What would close
the rest: hand a synthesised package to `AppleLink Package Translator`
3.0.3 under Mini vMac — a different program from the 3.5 translator whose
dialog failed (seven boots, 2026-09-01), worth one attempt.

## 2026-10-05 (the scan that was already being paid for) — a zip behind a stub, and the segment claim that rested on four bytes

The brief: decide, measured, whether to recognise ZipIt self-extractors.
OPEN_ITEMS.md priced it as **not free** ("a backward scan for every file
the sniffer rejects"). **The scan was already running on every one of
those files, finding the record, and throwing it away**: `unc_zipseg_probe`,
just before `unc_zip_probe`, scans the last 64 KB for the end record and
returned `UNC_FORMAT_UNKNOWN` on "disk 0"; the next probe read four bytes
of code.

### The number that settled it

`tools/sniff_io_probe.c` counts `UncIO.read` calls and bytes for
`unc_sniff` alone (each a `SetFPos` + `FSRead` on a floppy). With the scan
disabled as control it is **50.0 % of every read a sniff of the 955-file
corpus makes and 71.4 % of the bytes** (44.8 reads and 45,271 bytes per
BinHex fixture, 204 of them). Recognising the archive behind the stub adds
**one four-byte read** where the record corroborates and **+0 reads, +0
bytes to all 7,601 files a sweep of 8,364 non-archives has the sniffer
reject** (FORMATS.md, *What the zip pair claims, and what it costs*).

Actual cost: **316 B of resident `CODE` and 4 B of A5, in all three
configurations** — 320 B off every 1 MB extraction budget; it cannot go in
an `'OVLY'` (called for every file, like the 666-byte AppleLink probe,
2026-10-05, *the probe that had to be a file test*). Instructions: 0.003 %
of an extraction, no tick probe (four orders of magnitude is not a close
call).

### Why self-extracting LZH's reasoning does not transfer

Self-extracting LZH stays out (OPEN_ITEMS.md Part 1) because an LZH is a
chain from its first header and nothing says where that is. **A zip is the
opposite**: every offset is absolute from the file start and the record is
found from the END, so the stub is never read — why `-f Zip` already read
all five ZipIt specimens. A DOS self-extracting zip being claimed is a gain
(one built with `zip -A` extracts correctly). Four of the five ZipIt
specimens are MacBinary over a PEF container with a zip behind it.

### What the measurement found that was not asked about

The 8,364-file sweep found **five the engine already claimed** as
`UNC_FORMAT_ZIPSEG` (four Python `.pyc`, one deark object file): the
segment half required only `PK\5\6` by backwards scan and a nonzero disk
number, which a `.pyc` carries about once in 1,700 files. **The strong
test was being withheld and the weak one was already in the binary.** Both
halves now go through `zs_cd_is_there` (BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn claims*).

### The test that was proposed, the test that shipped, and why they differ

Proposed: the directory starts with `PK\1\2` and holds the declared count.
The first half ships. The second does not: APPNOTE.TXT 4.3.13 allows a
digital-signature record inside the directory, and walking a 74-entry
specimen is ~74 reads against the sniff's 4. Shipped instead, a **lower
bound**: a central header is 46 bytes before its name (4.3.12), so `total`
entries need ≥ 46 × total, and the `here` entries on this part lie in
front of the record (4.3.6). Zero reads. Each of the five tests is observed
to reject something (FORMATS.md table).

### The first draft refused a set Info-ZIP writes

**`zip -s` splits the central directory** once it outgrows a part:
measured at 1,200 entries and 64 KB parts — disk 7 of 8, directory starting
on **disk 6**, 132,048 bytes declared, 238 of 1,201 entries in the
26,312-byte final file, the declared offset landing mid-filename. The first
draft refused that set ("format not recognized"). Found by running the
generator at an untried size; `tools/synth_zipsplit.py` gains `zspancd`.
The five zip cases in `run_segments.py` all passed the broken draft.

### A fixture that declared 43,521 entries

The `total` test failed nine checks, and the engine was right:
`zs_build_tail` in `tests/unit_formats.c` wrote both two-byte counts **one
byte at a time**; the caller that fills with 0xAA had declared 43,521
entries in a 47-byte directory since written. Its property (a signature
straddling the scan window edge) never depended on it. Corrected.

---

## 2026-10-05 (a leaf is not a path, and a version is not a preference) — the `0x2605` FileName measured before it was read, and the tolerance that could only fail one way

The brief: extract under ZipIt's `0x2605` FileName (`READ ME` comes out as
`README`). Gate first: **is it observable on anything this build decodes?**
No.

**Measured.** All `0x2605` fields on this disk (the nine specimens' 22 and
`NPWritersKit.zip`'s) are **23**: three on directories, three method 6,
seventeen MacBinary. The FileName differs from the leaf on **3**, all
method 6 in `zipit-Psycho_1.0b1.zip`, refused per entry. **0 of the 23
divergences sit on a method this build reads** (FORMATS.md, *ZipIt's own
archives*). The row stays in OPEN_ITEMS.md, coupled to the Implode
decision.

### A version was a preference

"ZipIt 1.x upper-cased the names" — three 1.x writers here, one did:
`macextract l` on 1.4's own distribution zip and the Japanese 1.x's prints
`Read me`, `Mac SEA`, `Drop files here to zip`. ZipIt 1.4's resource fork
has a `DOSN` boolean "dosify filenames" (*"Convert filenames to MS-DOS
compatible format (8.3, uppercase)"*). **Both halves of the disproof were
in one archive the suite already extracts byte-exact** (BLOCKERS.md,
*Withdrawn claims*). As a checkbox the population is unbounded.

### A leaf is not a path

The field carries one component. `Psycho!v1.0ß1.zip`'s entries live under
`PSYCHO!/` with **no entry and no field for that folder**, so leaf
substitution gives `PSYCHO!/Psycho!`, `PSYCHO!/READ ME`, `PSYCHO!/Sample`
— still one component wrong, unfixable from the archive. "The right name
in all 20" was true of the field, not the path.

### The tolerance that could only fail one way

Committed: `grade_name_coupling` in `tools/run_zipit.py` sweeps the nine
specimens and corpus zips and fails if a FileName divergence lands on
method 0 or 8 — no `unar`, no engine; shown to fail on a `zipit-1.4` copy
with one name dosified.

That copy also showed `alias_of` (the existing tolerance) fails on a
dosified MacBinary entry, two rows, but on an entry with **no reachable
MacBinary payload** takes the field's name as `unar`'s alias and passes —
the three Implode entries' shape (measured: green, all three names wrong)
and a stored non-MacBinary `0x2605` entry's (hypothesis; none here). **The
tolerance could fail on the case the engine gets right and not on the case
it gets wrong.** Ask which direction a tolerance can fail in.


## 2026-10-05 (the reference implementation was the fixture's payload) — PackIt's two ciphers read out of PackIt III 1.3, and then RUN out of it

**The claim that moved.** OPEN_ITEMS.md's licence table said
`fmt_packit.c`'s resync and both ciphers wanted "a second implementation
of `PMa5`/`PMa6`", for three reasons: deark's `packit.c` errors on both,
macutils' `pit.c` skips the block, and the unPACKIT manual's appendix B
lists "PMa5" twice so cannot name the fourth word. **The third is false**:
the manual's (L)ist section gives all four words and attributes both
encrypted forms to PackIt III; only appendix B's table duplicates one
(BLOCKERS.md). No document describes either cipher. But
`fixtures/packit.pit_.bin` contains **`Packit III 1.3`**, APPL/`'PIT '`,
dated 6/14/87 by its own `'PIT '` resource — the generation that wrote
every `PMa5` and `PMa6` block. `tools/derive_packit.py` had been grading
the container against an archive carrying the writer of the part it could
not cite.

**Four rows now.** The usable form: **a format's own application is a
reference implementation, and for a 1980s Macintosh format the application
is a file somebody archived.** Ask what the corpus contains, not only what
it exercises.

**Read, then executed.** `tools/derive_pitcrypt.py` checks 32 byte
patterns each AT its claimed offset (17 occur more than once; `--witness`
prints the count). `CODE` 1 has exactly one Toolbox trap in the cipher's
call graph (`_BlockMove`, A02E), so `tools/pitcrypt/pit_run.c` sets up an
A5 world, maps `CODE` 1, copies `CODE` 256 to A5-19150, and calls `SetKey`
@0x334a and the cipher @0x3390 under `qemu-m68k` (the trap via
`tools/sdmodule/`'s SIGILL handling). `--make` has the original cipher
encrypt two entries in a `tools/synth_pit.py` container, and this engine
reads them back: 890 B, 890 B and 302 B, every fork byte-exact, and
`PMa6`'s output identical to `openssl enc -des-ecb`.

**New smell.** "Our use is graded — `unar -p` reads both ciphers back"
was worth nothing: `unar` IS XADMaster, the transcription's source. **A
differential test whose oracle is the implementation the code was copied
from grades the transcription and not the format.** Four of eight ciphers
now have an archive the original software produced; the others are ARC
(Debian's `arc`), zip (Info-ZIP), WinZip AES (7-Zip) and `PassLock`.

**What the application settled.** The fourth magic byte is `'0' +
4·compressed + mode` (@0x109a..0x10c4), which is why an outside document
lists one twice. Both encryption items force compression on (@0x0c7e,
@0x0c9a) and compression goes inert while mode ≠ 0 (@0x0c50), **so `PMa1`
and `PMa2` cannot exist** — the four-word check is complete. The `PMa5` key
is seven bytes because PC-1 selects 56 bits (@0x3386). The key is set once
per ENTRY, magic in the clear (@0x12c0, @0x12ec): no salt, no chaining.

**The one behaviour change.** The resync after an undecryptable entry was
macutils' byte-wise scan. PackIt rounds its last flush with `addq.l #7` /
`and.l #-8` whenever mode ≠ 0 (@0x1942), so the next magic lies on the
eight-byte grid; the engine scans the grid. `fmt_packit.c` 2,142 -> 2,160 B
of m68k text at `-Os` for the grid, but factoring the twice-written magic
test into one predicate made **`ovl_packit` fall 4 B**; the resident
control's code rose 20 B with A5 falling 20, so `OVL_SAVED` is unchanged.
`run_tiers.py --check-images` refused the moved image twice and
`build_mac.sh` the control at 32 B over (the first draft cost 26 B). It
can fail: the third specimen's ciphertext carries a false `'PMag'` five
bytes in, off the grid, and the old scan loses the entry after it with
either key.

**The citation it replaces had a second error**: "cannot name the fourth
word" sat in `fmt_packit.c`, `derive_packit.py` and OPEN_ITEMS.md since
2026-09-21. **A document is not one claim**: the part read is the part the
last task needed. Everything is measured on **1.3**; for earlier III
releases it is a hypothesis, stated where the figures are.

**No wild archive can grade either cipher, measured.** Discmaster's
first-16-bytes index has 0 rows for `504d6135*`/`504d6136*`, so
`tools/scan_discmaster.py`'s `pit` probe walks the chain decoding every
`PMa4`: **182 wild archives, 1,107 blocks, zero encrypted** (plus 6 from a
partial `.pit` sweep). Blind spot (TESTING.md): MacBinary-wrapped archives.

**Harness trap**: `pit_run` returned a different exit status each run
while writing correct ciphertext — `SetKey` saves no registers and uses
A2, the dispatcher writes D2, D3 and A2 — so the clobber list had to name
D2-D5 and A2-A4.


## 2026-10-05 (the negative that was about one rule) — a line-ending citation shed to a file the same header already cited

**The claim that moved.** `src/fmt_uu.c` and `src/unc_internal.h` cited
macutils' `hexbin/readline.c` for CR, LF and CRLF each ending a line and an
unterminated last line counting. Stuck because *"mpack is LF-only"* (true:
`part_gets` breaks on `'\n'`).

**deark was not asked for this cell**, though the 2026-09-27 sweep read it
for the row's other cells. `dbuf_find_line` in `src/deark-dbuf.c` (MIT):
CR, LF and CR+LF each end a line (`eol_size` 2 for the pair), an
unterminated last line is a line (`eol_size` 0), nothing is not;
`modules/xfer.c`'s uudecode skips a leading CR/LF as *"a multi-byte EOL
sequence, or blank line"*, exactly `fmt_uu.c`'s choice. **`unc_internal.h`
already cited `deark-dbuf.c` four lines below.**

**Transferable.** A negative is about the pair (reference, fact). **When a
row gives a different blocker per item, check each names every reference**
— and a file's existing citations are candidates one grep away.

**Closes / does not.** Three of six rules gone (two to mpack, this to
deark); `unc_internal.h` is off the row except the LZAH preload. Three
remain, re-verified: the whole-line garbage skip (deark errors, mpack keeps
the prefix), the second-document rescan (deark's binhex reads one document,
banner search bounded to 8,192 bytes), and UUTool's MU layout. No behaviour
changed; `tools/run_uu.py`'s gapped sets and the multi-part fixtures grade
as before. (The last two later shed: *the alphabet nothing here had seen*
and *the separator that was in the alphabet*, below.)


## 2026-10-06 (the lesson that was written down and then not applied) — six real AppleLink packages, out of the same index that held the first two, found by the technique the entry beside them already named

OPEN_ITEMS.md's *three container paths no real package has*, filed
2026-10-05, closed 2026-10-06 by the question DECISIONS.md 2026-09-26 had
already written down.

### The search that was by name, in the entry that says not to search by name

2026-09-26 found SpaceSaver files by magic in Discmaster's *detections*
index, and wrote the lesson — but its AppleLink packages came from a
**path** (`AppleLink 6.1` on fifteen CDs). **`detection=` is also
full-text over the first 16 bytes of every file** (its `searchHelp.html`),
with `*` and `?`. A version-1 package's first 16 bytes are the item count,
`01`, eight zero bytes and a zero long — a hex token `??01` plus fourteen
zeros. Fifty tokens, one per item count: **1,443 files, 36 packages**.
`extension=.pkg&family=unknown` (2,641 files) adds 13 more, including every
version-0 one (whose token matches 1.1 million files of padding). **49 real
packages**, where the project had two.

**Neither key subsumes the other**: 20 of the 49 are not called `.pkg`
(`SPAudit10`, `Roland`, `MCNCode`, `Houston, TX Map picture`, `Iconf
Display`), and the hex key is blind to a version. *Run the search by
content beside the search by name; they are blind in different
directions.*

### What six of them were worth

Six are specimens (FORMATS.md, *What the eight real packages exercise*):
a **resource fork** (30 members, up to 352,407 B), the **stored** bit on
each fork separately, **version 0**, and **folders** (14, nested four
deep). `MPW Shell 3.2.2.pkg` carries **29 clear codes** and fills the
8,192-entry table (the old two reached 12 bits and 2,260 entries).
`tools/derive_sqp.py`'s unexercised line now reads **"UNEXERCISED by these
packages — nothing"**.

### Three readers and a fourth number, because a package has no checksum

`tools/run_sqp.py` lane 1 holds **67 forks of 8 packages** against four
things: the engine, `derive_sqp.py`, `gzip` through a `.Z` header on all 59
LZW streams, and **each record's declared expanded length**. All four agree
on all 67. Failed first by accident (a tuple returned where bytes were
expected made gzip "disagree" with 60 forks of matching length — a
disagreement with no difference is a harness bug) and then deliberately
(one flipped byte in `Read First.PKG`, four complaints).

### The two members that want one file

`Iconf Display` holds `bullseye π` (empty data fork) and **`bullseye
π.rsrc`**; under `-nr` the first's resource fork and the second's data fork
are one path. The engine refuses the second and names it — M9's overwrite
refusal reached by a real archive first time; `--forks hidden` writes all
six. **No synthesiser here would have written it.**

### What it cost

Built while the second search was not run: `tools/synth_sqp.py`, an
encoder for five paths four real packages reach; **seven Mini vMac boots on
2026-09-01**; a MANUAL_TESTS.md request; and a day of the folder
type/creator bug (2026-10-05) that a real folder package would have caught
