  5.3.4 decode. Short-circuiting would turn a *truncated* report into a
  checksum failure, which `run_truncation.py` and `run_robustness.py`
  grade; and a corrupt first entry does not lock the archive into the
  wrong reading, as deark's shape does.

**`PKZ101.EXE` is a fixture** (pinned URL, sha256, six identical
Discmaster copies, `tools/specimens/implode.tsv`), graded on every
`ci.sh`. **It catches what the generator cannot**: a probe that only asks
whether the decode finished passes `run_implode.py` and fails this
fixture, because `README.DOC` under 5.3.4 has the right LENGTH and wrong
bytes. Two details: **deark identifies it as a DOS EXE**, so
`make_manifests.py` names `-m zip` in a `DEARK_MODULE` table —
deliberately not a fallback, which would silently re-identify any
fixture whose names failed to match; and **`lsar` names the STUB**, so
`run_diff.py`'s `IMPLEMENTED` maps `"Self-extracting Zip": "Zip"`.

**8 K/2-tree under the bug is still the generator's alone**, and
FORMATS.md says so: all three authentic bug entries are 4 K/three trees.
For that half, `tools/synth_implode.py` is graded by deark reading it back
and `unar` required to REFUSE it. **One archive per shape** — a
correction: the verdict is per archive, so a second entry rode on the
first's answer, and the order decided which bend escaped.

**The bend nothing caught was the cost axis.** Of five bends, four fail a
suite; the predicate WIDENED to every Implode entry changes no output,
and **no lane counted a decode pass**: the "+0" for unambiguous entries
rested on callgrind `Ir` and `strace` `read`+`lseek` (the Mac's
`SetFPos`+`FSRead` axis). **Corrected 2026-10-09: both the widening and
the inverted order are caught now** by `run_implode.py`'s fifth lane,
counting passes through the CLI's allocation trace.

**Not done: an ENCRYPTED ambiguous entry** (the probe runs before
`unc_password`; re-keying per pass) — decoded under 5.3.4 as before,
named in the source, no file in reach. Likewise `zip_mb_peek` reads under
5.3.4; a PKZIP 1.01 entry with a ZipIt field cannot exist.

**Two stale figures, one cause.** `tools/check_app_size.py`'s
`EXPECT_BUNDLE` was still 156,068 from before `ovl_exo` grew 1,924 B,
inside its WARN tolerance, so nothing went red for a day; FORMATS.md's
launch-read paragraph quoted 25,860 B (222,468 − 196,608, pre-growth).
The single difference is now removed rather than corrected; the two terms
are quoted. *A constant that three places quote and one place checks, with
a tolerance wide enough to absorb the change.*


## 2026-10-08 (the writer a zip is allowed to have twice) — a scope that assumed one writer per archive, bounded to the entry it can be wrong about

The minimum-match-length verdict is settled once per ARCHIVE (*the second
attempt that had nowhere to go*), which ASSUMES one writer per zip — and
that was written into four files as the reason.

**It is wider than the measurement.** The sweeps establish that none of
1,537 archives mixes the readings (all 29,799 entries classified
individually); they cannot establish that a zip has one writer. A zip is
appendable, PKZIP 1.1 also wrote Implode, and deark settling per archive
is one implementation's choice (three implementations agreeing was
withdrawn as corroboration once already, `UNC_PATH_MAXDEPTH`).

**Measured, on a three-entry archive our encoder wrote — bug-written entry
first, two conforming after, all at one ambiguous combination:**

| build | what came out |
|---|---|
| 2026-10-08 morning | entry 1; entries 2 and 3 BOTH refused, both *"file is truncated"* |
| before the reading existed | entries 2 and 3; entry 1 refused, *"checksum mismatch"* |
| this | entries 1 and 3; entry 2 refused, *"checksum mismatch"* |

The assumption cost the archive's whole remainder, and the diagnosis was
wrong: a stream decoded under the other reading desynchronises and runs
out of input.

**The bound: one probe, paid only on an entry that has already failed.**
An entry that INHERITED the verdict and failed is decoded once more with
no output under the other reading; if that reproduces the CRC-32, report
a checksum failure and reset the archive to UNSETTLED. It cannot fire on a
one-writer archive or on the entry that settled the verdict, and cannot
turn a failure into a success (the bytes reached the sink). **It does not
rescue that entry**: buffering is out on 32-bit `usize`, a restartable
sink is an unrequested API change, and a per-*version made by* verdict
was tested the same day (*the key that survives and has nothing to
separate*). One entry of a mixed archive is the price.

**Transferable.** A scope decision's sentence ("a zip has one writer") is
wider than its measurement ("no archive of 1,537 mixes"). Ask what the
FORMAT allows, and whether the damage is bounded if the assumption is
wrong; here "more than assumed" and "no", and bounding cost one probe on
a path already failing.


## 2026-10-08 (the key that survives and has nothing to separate) — a per-writer verdict, tested on PKZIP itself under DOSBox, and not built

**The hypothesis.** The entry *the writer a zip is allowed to have twice*
still loses could be kept by settling the verdict per *version made by*:
PKZIP 1.01/1.02 stamp 0x000a, 1.10 stamps 0x000b — valid only if 1.10
keeps the stamps of records it did not write. Our encoder cannot answer
that, so the three `PKZIP.EXE` binaries were run headless under DOSBox;
`tools/pkzip_writers.py` re-runs it in about 30 s.

**The stamps survive. Measured.** 1.10 adding (`-a`), updating (`-u`) or
freshening (`-f`) a 1.02 archive leaves every 1.02 record 0x000a, and the
reverse; 1.10 adding to `PKZ101.EXE` keeps all thirteen of 1.01's records
0x000a.

**And there is nothing for it to separate. Measured.** None of the three
writers ever writes a disagreeing combination: dictionary size follows
tree count (8 K/three, 4 K/two). Over 50 inputs each version wrote 31
entries at 4 K/two trees, 15 at 8 K/three and 4 stored; about 170 more by
hand (`PKNO386`, `-ex`, 350–500 KB taken by `loadfix`) moved nothing.
`PKZ101.EXE`'s own three 4 K/three-tree entries, and `CPUTEST.ZIP`'s
(Simtel, 1989; spec-1.1 MS-DOS, 8 K/two and 4 K/three) both come back at
4 K/two trees. So 1.10 entries appended to a 1.0x archive are
unambiguous, and the current build extracts the one real such archive
(`PKZ101.EXE` + 1.10 `-a`, 15 entries) byte for byte. **A lane on it
cannot fail on the current build, so the change was not built.** It
reopens only for a mixed archive where BOTH writers wrote disagreeing
combinations — e.g. an Info-ZIP-era writer (0x030a, 28,896 of the 29,799
bug-capable entries in the 2026-10-08 sweep) appending to 1.0x. None is on
this disk.

**The rule is now measured on the READERS.** PKUNZIP 1.01 and 1.02 fail
both `CPUTEST.ZIP` entries on CRC and pass all of `PKZ101.EXE`; PKUNZIP
1.10 passes `CPUTEST.ZIP` and fails exactly `README.DOC`, `ORDER.DOC` and
`OMBUDSMN.ASP`. What wrote those three is none of the shipped writers;
*hypothesis:* an internal build, untestable here.

**Filed, not chased:** PKUNZIP 1.01/1.02 refused every
`tools/synth_implode.py` stream; reduced on 2026-10-09 (*the run PKZIP
never codes at distance one*).

**Transferable.** A key that exists is half a fix; the writer's output
histogram says whether there is a case for it. Fifteen seconds of DOSBox
beat reasoning, and **the writer's own reader is an oracle for the
writer's own rule.**

## 2026-10-08 (the method a Macintosh wrote once) — Shrink comes into scope, Reduce goes out, and the count that split them was the writer, not the shelf

**Claim.** Zip method 1, Shrink, is implemented; methods 2–5, Reduce, are
out by the brief (OPEN_ITEMS.md, Part 1). Both had been refused per entry
with "not supported yet" and named in neither part of OPEN_ITEMS.
(Reduce: reversed by DECISIONS.md 2026-10-11, *Reduce comes in*.)

**The question was who WROTE them.** 96,193 files open with a shrunk
entry (FORMATS.md, *Shrink*); 141 distinct ones sit where a Mac user would
meet them. 139 say MS-DOS or Unix in *version made by*, one is truncated,
contents are `.EXE`/`.COM`/`.DLL` — a shelf is not a writer (*the stub is
the writer's signature*). The host byte found **one** Macintosh-written
archive, `BBA.zip`, ZipIt 3.2. Reduce: 5 on Mac media, 0 from a Mac
writer. The split follows Implode's criterion; one archive is thin, but
it is the brief's case, and the 141 DOS zips on Mac CDs are what users
would open.

**The oracle was the wrong source, and the stored CRC said so.**
XADMaster's `XADZipShrinkHandle.m` makes code 256,2 a FULL clear; PKZIP's
partial clear keeps every parent code, so `unar` fails 270 of 2,246 wild
entries. A transcription of it would have agreed with `unar` everywhere
and failed one entry in eight. deark's `fmtutil-lzw.c` matches 2,246 of
2,246 (2,247 until 2026-10-09 — *the three entries that were the
harness's*), so it is the source. **Grade a reference against the
archives' own checksums before transcribing it**; a second implementation
with the same gap tells you nothing.

**Two rules that read as defensive are load-bearing**: a code naming a
free slot is the string about to be defined (1,799 entries); a walk
reaching a freed slot uses the previous string's first byte (1 entry,
`MM.COM`). Each has a fixture that fails when bent (FORMATS.md, *Shrink*,
*What grades it*).

**Placement was decided by the 68000.** Beside Implode in
`src/fmt_exo.c`, `ovl_exo` stopped linking: `-mpcrel` reaches data by
16-bit offsets and the image passed 32 KB, a ceiling nothing had
recorded. It moved to `src/unc_lzw.c` (codecs image): a codecs-only
format's grant +36 B, a zip's −64. `ovl_exo` has about 730 B left.

**Three bytes a slot because the fourth was measured**: a kind byte took
`dream`'s peak to 47,286 B; packing the flags into the 13-bit parent word
gives 39,094 B. The table is sized from the compressed length and kept as
one fixed allocation, since it IS the allocation.

**The CLI stops asking for what it will not use**: a Reduce entry says it
is out of scope and names deark; the specimen request is only for
methods merely missing.

## 2026-10-09 (the specimen was one search away, and the installer was an archive) — Private File reads, and its payload turned out to be another format

**Claim.** Aladdin Private File (`.pf`) extracts, graded byte-exact on
three files Private File 2.0 wrote under Mini vMac (FORMATS.md, *Private
File*). The 2026-10-07 hypothesis — RC4 keyed by MD5 of the password — is
now a finding.

**The leg filed "unfinished, not negative" had it**: Macintosh Garden
answered over plain `http://` on the first retry (`private_file_2.0.sit`,
`old.mac.gdn` mirror, browser user agent).

**No installer was walked.** The InstallerMaker application's data fork
is a StuffIt archive, so `PF Encrypt™` came out on Linux in one command;
its cipher is in its own `CODE` 4, pre-registered, launched from `Startup
Items` on System 7.0.1. **Before driving an installer, ask whether its
payload is a format already read here.**

**Read before run; the run graded the reading.** `CODE` 4 kept its
MacsBug names: an 18-byte clear header, a 308-byte record under one RC4
stream, both forks under a second, a clear 12-byte footer with two
CRC-32s. The first emulator file matched to the byte (header
`CSIT 0002 0001 0001 0005 0000 00000000`). Only the run could say:

- **The key is five bytes**: `GetEncryptionKeySize` reads `'KSiz'` 128,
  falls back to 5, and the application has none.
- **The payload is never the file**: PF Encrypt Stuffs the subject first.
  So Private File is an ENVELOPE, unwrapped by `x` like MacBinary, its
  reader in the StuffIt `'OVLY'` image.
- **The writer refuses passwords under six characters.**

**Placement, measured**: resident, **+1,652 B of `CODE`**; split, **+368
B of `CODE` and +32 of A5**. Two host-vector slots reach the cipher; the
key setup is `unc_crypt_pf` in the crypt image beside MD5. No tier tally
moves.

**The probe was the outlier** (222 B, more than StuffIt classic's): its
fields went through `unc_get_u16be`, which on a 68000 rebuilds each field
to compare with 0, 1 or 2. Comparing bytes made it 186 B, total 400 B.
**A field the code only compares with small constants should be compared
as bytes.**

**The reader, priced before changing it.** `tools/m68kprof.py` over a
256 KB file: **RC4 at 65 % and CRC-32 at 32 %** of 8.5 M instructions
(8.0 M after the first change, which FORMATS.md quotes); reads ~2 %, MD5
0.05 %, so a second MD5 is not worth a host-vector slot. Taken:

- **RC4's indices in locals** (`buf` may alias the struct): 21 → 19
  instructions a byte, the four lost being `d16(An)` accesses — **roughly
  15 % off RC4 by the timing table, an ESTIMATE** (the tick probe cannot
  supply a password). StuffIt 5 shares the loop.
- **The record decrypted in place**, re-read per wrong password: peak
  5,696 → **5,392 B**; the lane gained a retry case that fails without
  the re-read.

Both in images (`ovl_stuffit` −12, `ovl_crypt` −4). Left alone: two
`andi.l #255` per byte, assembly-only.

**The Mac run's "failure" was the harness**: bytes 48..125 of the resource
fork held the file's name, in system-reserved bytes 16..127 every on-Mac
harness has masked since M10 except the new one. **A new harness inherits
the old ones' masks or rediscovers them.**

**Not supported, by decision:** derivation 0 and cipher 0 (PFEngine
accepts them, no writer here produces them), refused per entry.

## 2026-10-09 (what GCC will not do with an index) — RC4 in 68000 assembly is estimated at ~40 % fewer cycles, and is filed rather than written

**Claim (an ESTIMATE, from the MC68000 timing table; nothing timed):**
RC4's keystream loop is ~178 cycles a byte compiled, ~104 hand-written:
with an index register's upper byte cleared once, `add.b` wraps at 256
for free and `(d8,An,Dn.w)` addresses the table; GCC zero-extends with
`andi.l #255` (16 cycles, twice a byte) and reloads through `lea`.

**C cannot be coaxed into it, measured**: 16-bit indices with `& 0xff`
and a pointer walk compiled to 25 instructions a byte against 19.

**Filed, not written, by the maintainer's call**: it would be the
engine's first 68000-only path, ungradable on x86 CI. Collected in
OPEN_ITEMS.md (*Hand-written 68000 assembly*).


## 2026-10-09 (the writer's own output was the population the flags excluded) — PKZIP 1.0x's fingerprint, swept, never writes the 8 K/two-tree half, and its OS/2 twin narrows who did write PKZ101.EXE

**Claim, measured.** No real archive written with the 1.01/1.02 rule at
0x0002 (8 K, two trees) exists in reach: **151,924 Implode entries in
19,278 zips whose directory says MS-DOS + spec 1.0**, each fetched whole,
are all at 0x0000 or 0x0006. The 0x0002 half stays graded by
`tools/synth_implode.py` and deark (FORMATS.md, *Which half is graded by a
real file*; sweeps: TESTING.md, *Searching somebody else's index by
content*).

**The 2026-10-08 flag keys excluded that population by construction**:
they name archives whose first entry is already at a disagreeing
combination, which no shipped PKZIP writes (10 of 3,821 said
MS-DOS/1.0). *Version needed* 1.0 plus a first member dated 1988–1989
gets **19,299 of 48,948** (39 %). **A key that names the answer can only
find writers who give it**: select on the writer, count the shapes.

**PKZIP 1.01 for OS/2 narrows the hypothesis.** `PKZ101_2.ZIP` and
`PKZ101-S.EXE` (1989-07-21) carry the same `ORDER.DOC` (4,607 B) and
`OMBUDSMN.ASP` (595 B) at **0x0000**, where `PKZ101.EXE` has 0x0004: the
bug writer wrote ONLY the DOS distribution. *Hypothesis, unreduced:* a
pre-release build (a 1989-05-29 CompuServe message, `pkz100.txt`, quotes
Katz testing *"PKZIP 1.0 Alpha"* — fits, does not establish). Inside
`PKZ101.EXE` it used 4 K up to 4,607 B, 8 K/three trees only for the three
texts of 8,959 B and over, and 4 K/two for five program files up to
31,342 B; if that is its rule it may never have written 0x0002 either —
resting on one archive.


## 2026-10-09 (the read nothing sent short) — a contract half of which no host exercises is a contract nothing tests

**Claim, measured.** Private File's reader read its 12-byte footer with
one bare `io->read`, so a valid file extracted in full was then reported
*file is truncated* under a short read, which `UncIO` allows
(`include/macextract.h`); reproduced by a review with a 7-byte cap. Fixed
with `unc_read_full`: `ovl_stuffit` −24 B, shipped pair unmoved.

**Neither host ever returns a short read**, so half the I/O contract had
never been exercised. The CLI's `UNC_SHORT_READ` and
`tools/run_shortread.py` now send them: **959 fixtures at 1 B per read,
and the decryption and Private File suites whole, agree with uncapped** —
this was the only one (TESTING.md, *Short reads*).

**The first green run graded nothing**: a sanitizer build linked before
the hook matched itself 959 times. The CLI announces the cap and the lane
refuses a binary that does not. **A harness that sets an environment hook
has to see it was read.**


## 2026-10-09 (the run PKZIP never codes at distance one) — the generator's streams cut down until PKUNZIP 1.01 read them, and two things 1.0x read differently from 5.3

**Claim, measured.** PKUNZIP 1.01 and 1.02 refused every
`tools/synth_implode.py` stream (*the key that survives and has nothing to
separate*). Cut down token by token under DOSBox, that was **two
features, not one**, both now avoided: each of the six shapes is read by
the PKUNZIP whose rule it was written to (1.01/1.02 read both `-mmlbug`
shapes and refuse the 5.3.4 shapes at the disagreeing combinations; 1.10
the reverse). So the 1.01/1.02 rule is graded by 1.01/1.02 itself, by
hand, for the 8 K/two-tree half too. `tools/pkzip_writers.py` asserts
each minimal case's pass or failure and its control since 2026-10-09; the
bytes PKUNZIP wrote, the per-value sweep and the two 9-bit trees were
observed by hand and are not re-checkable from the repository.

**1. A match at distance operand 0.** Eight literals and one length-2
match at operand 0: 1.01 and 1.02 fail on CRC, 1.10 reads it; operand 1
is read by all three. 1.01 turns `abcdefgh` + (0, 6) into `abcdefghh` and
five zeros; over stale data, the first byte right then each stale byte
twice (`c s0 s0 s2 s2 …`). *Hypothesis, unreduced:* a forward copy two
bytes at a time. **No PKZIP writer emits operand 0**: 105,658–105,962
matches over 51 inputs, none at 0 (1.01 codes zero runs as length-320
matches at operand 319). The generator's one-byte fill is now two
literals and a match at operand 1.

**2. A literal tree that gives a high byte a short code.** One literal
0x80 under a flat 8-bit tree: 1.01 writes 0x00 and loses sync, 1.02 and
1.10 read it; 0xFF comes out 0x00 from **all three**, sync kept; under
PKZIP's own tree all three read it. Per value, 1.01 fails every byte 0x80
and up whose code is ≤ 8 bits, under three trees. *Hypothesis,
unreduced:* an 8-bit-indexed decode table holding the symbol in a signed
byte, negative meaning "longer code".

**Why no PKZIP file shows it: PKZIP stores one literal tree.** Every
three-tree entry the three writers made, 15 of 15 each, stores the same
99 bytes whatever the input (text with é one byte in six still gave é
12 bits and 'v' 8); every byte 0x80 and up has 12 or 13 bits. Only
`PKZ101.EXE`'s entries carry trees of their own. The generator now stores
that table (`PKZIP_LITERAL_TREE`), its first eight 12-bit codes re-split
into a chain 10…16, 16 so a 256-value tree still states a 16-bit code;
all three PKUNZIPs read every byte value under it.

**Consequence.** These are a third and fourth difference from 5.3, both
in the READER, and no PKZIP-written file reaches them, so nothing in
`src/` changes: such a stream in a stranger's zip meant 5.3. **Found and
not reduced:** two hand-built trees with 128 bytes at 9 bits are misread
by all three PKUNZIPs on many values; unar and deark read them; the
generator's trees are unaffected (measured per value).

**Transferable.** A reader refusing a whole stream says nothing about
which rule it disagrees with; cutting it down does (under two seconds a
DOSBox run). The second feature appeared only once the first was fixed:
**a reduction ends when every reader agrees, not at the first
difference.** A table a writer always emits is a fact about the writer,
invisible to every question about its flags.

## 2026-10-09 (the base nobody re-took) — the shipped tier model was 16,888 B generous for a week, and the machine was the only thing that could say so

**What happened.** With `shrink-wild-titanic.zip` added, four tiers
re-run: System 6.0.8 on a 512Ke came back 66/72 where `run_tiers.py
--shipped` said 67 — `a2ps.V4.3.tar.Z`'s compress layer granted 81,938 B,
needing 86,080.

**Why the model missed it.** A shipped budget is `TIERS` (control build's
budget, read off the machine) + `OVL_SAVED` (control less shipped `CODE` +
A5) − what the format keeps. When the control grows G and the shipped
build S, `TIERS` must fall G and `OVL_SAVED` rise G−S. `--check-saved`
re-checked `OVL_SAVED` every run; `TIERS` was lowered once (2,024 B,
2026-10-01) and then left, so from 2026-10-02 every printed budget rose by
what should have come off. The `-D UNC_OVL_RESIDENT -D UNC_AT_BUDGET`
probe in three boots: all three bases 16,888 B lower, identical across
both systems and RAM sizes — the signature of application size. At those
bases the model puts `a2ps` 4,070 B short against the machine's 4,142.

**Why nothing else caught it.** Every tier argument from 2026-09-26
compared a cost with "the narrowest margin, 16,490 B" — from the same
model, so it moved with the error. *A tolerance measured by the
instrument it protects is our own output again* (CLAUDE.md).

**What changed.** `TIERS_CONTROL` pins the control build's `CODE` + A5
the bases were read against, and `--check-saved` fails when it moves. The
resident `EXPECT` tallies (72, 68, 63) were re-pinned from the model and
the same evening confirmed on all three machines, refusing exactly the
named fixtures; `EXPECT` asserts the names. The bases had fallen the
256 B the control grew in between, to the byte.

**Transferable.** For a derived figure, list its inputs and ask which
something re-takes. The cheap input (a difference of two builds) got
automated; the one needing an emulator did not — the usual direction of
this failure.

## 2026-10-09 (the three entries that were the harness's) — a gap between two decoders was two harnesses counting different entries, and a slow path the review read was priced before it was fixed

**Claim.** The Shrink row's "2,247 against 2,244, 3 UNEXPLAINED" was never
the decoder's: transcription and engine agree on all 2,246 distinct
entries of the 2026-10-08 sweep, entry by entry, and on 1,953 of a fresh
346-archive draw (FORMATS.md, *Shrink*, *What grades it*).

**Two totals are comparable only if they count the same things.** The
transcription could not parse `Thief35.zip` (12 entries skipped); Python's
`zipfile`, used by the C comparison, refuses two RISC OS zips over Acorn's
`0x4341` field (15). 2,247 − 15 + 12 = 2,244; both also counted one
re-drawn archive twice. **A difference between two decoders' totals is
first a question about the denominators**; per-entry verdicts keyed by
archive and name settle it.

**"Was not kept" was a claim about a directory nobody had looked in**: the
working set was in `/tmp` all along. `scan_discmaster.py --probe keep`
now writes files and a manifest under the cache.

**A slow path found by reading is priced before it is fixed.** The partial
clear is O(table) per 18 bits of input, so a crafted 100 KB stream holds a
Mac Plus for hours — an ESTIMATE from 68000 instruction counts at ~0.5 M
a second, and instructions are not cycles (FORMATS.md, *What a crafted
stream costs*). That cost is the format's (deark pays it too); a fix can
buy a working Cancel: ticks came only from the reader, ~17 minutes apart,
and a tick per clear (+76 B, codecs image) makes it ~0.3 s, same
estimate. The peek's double decode (up to 8 KB per ZipIt Shrink entry, 0
such entries exist) was left; its no-progress pass was fixed (+20 B).
Lowering the walk bound gives ~3× against an adaptive attacker, not a
bound, and was not built.


## 2026-10-09 (the bar that counted the peek) — a dry pass has to tick and must not count, and the first check that compared `done` with `total` found 66 more

**Claim, measured.** Zip's two dry passes (the 128-byte MacBinary peek on
a ZipIt entry, the minimum-match-length probe) read through `c->ps`, so
the decode proper counted their input again: 152 % on a ZipIt unit-test
archive. Both now restore `done`: they tick, only the decode counts.

**The missing thing was the check.** `tools/run_ticks.py` had graded
since 2026-08-28 that every archive ticks and no gap passes 32 KB, never
that `done` stays under `total`. Asked, it named **75 layers**: these two
zips and 73 rows (66 distinct layers) of DiskDoubler, MacLHA's peek and
uuencode, months older (a 5,193 B DDn archive reported 96 KB). They went
into a `KNOWN_OVERRUN` ratchet and were closed the same day (*DiskDoubler
read every block six times*), measured separately rather than handed this
fix. **An aggregate never compared with its bound is not checked by the
lane that collects it.**

## 2026-10-09 (DiskDoubler read every block six times) — the 66 overruns closed in three formats, and neither engine-wide option was needed

**Claim, measured.** All 66 `KNOWN_OVERRUN` layers now finish at or under
the archive's size; the table is empty. Three causes, each traced to its
line under gdb first:

- **MacLHA** (`fmt_lzh.c`): the MacBinary peek counted through `c->ps`
  (11,157 B on 7,094 B); `done` saved and restored, as `zip_mb_peek`.
- **uuencode** (`fmt_uu.c`): `uu_scan_doc` reads the document to size the
  forks, then the writing pass re-reads it, and the next-`begin` search
  re-reads the buffered tail. Progress is pinned per pass (`base + pos`
  before the search, `base + d.start` before writing).
- **DiskDoubler** (`fmt_dd.c`) was **two causes**; the open item named
  one. `ddtf-dd377ad.dd` has no DDn fork and still counted 43.6 KB on
  16,848 B: no fork's `UncBufIn` had a `limit`, so refills read into the
  next fork. DDn added six reseeks per block, each discarding a buffer
  that nearly always held the target. Each reader is now limited to its
  compressed length, and `ddn_seek` moves within or just past the buffer.

**The two engine-wide options, priced as asked; neither needed.** Shipped
(eager) 68000 build; callgrind over every file in `fixtures/` (972 on that
run; 959 with a manifest; base 10,233,708,156 Ir):

| | resident CODE / A5 | 'OVLY' images | callgrind Ir | tick lane |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: count consumed (the old buffer, at refill) | +12 / +20 | +0 | −27,363 | **FAILS**: 64 of 66 clear, uuencode untouched, and 77 fewer archives tick (1,134 → 1,057), two of them 259 KB (`MacburgerHelper.sit`), over the lane's 64 KB floor: Cancel out of reach |
| B: high-water mark (one `tell` per `unc_bufin_init`, not per refill) | +128 / +0 | +0 | +528,682 (`ftell`) | passes, all 66 clear |
| C: in the formats (chosen) | **+0 / +0** | `ovl_cptdd` +144, `ovl_lzh` +18, `ovl_text` +8 | +50,754 | passes, all 66 clear |

A also loses partly-consumed buffers when a reader is abandoned. B costs
resident code, leaves DiskDoubler's reads untouched, and hides the fault
the lane exists for (a second pass sits at 100 %). C's `ovl_cptdd` +144 is
`ddn_seek` +72 and `dd_fork` +74 per function, +146; the 2 B difference is
not attributed (CORRECTED 2026-10-10: this called it +146 B in
`ovl_cptdd`).

**x86 callgrind is the wrong instrument for C.** Its +50,754 Ir is
`dd_fork` +741k against libc's read path −600k or more, plus x86 outlining
moving the hot loop; `inline` on `ddn_seek` fixes x86 and leaves the
68000 overlay **byte-identical**, so it is kept. On the Mac (`run.py --emu
mv-4M-1x -D UNC_AT_TIMING`, `ddtf-ddpro411dd1.dd`, System 6, each run
twice, identical to the tick):

| | total | FSRead | FSWrite | rest of the File Manager | remainder (engine) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 707 | 15 | 7 | 36 | 649 |
| C | 698 | 2 | 1 | 39 | 656 |

The remainder's +7 is within the per-call rounding of 113 reads; the
robust figure is the total: **−9 ticks, −1.3 %**.

**No wider window was needed**: it would have widened a discarded buffer.
`strace` (`t -nr ddtf-ddpro411dd1.dd`): **113 reads, 179,695 B and 65
seeks before; 3 reads, 6,025 B and 29 seeks after**, on a 5,193 B file.

**Accepted:** 36 small DiskDoubler layers no longer tick (1,134 ticking →
1,098); all under 8 KB (largest 7,153 B), below the pump's step; they
ticked only by double counting.

**Transferable:** an open item's diagnosis is a hypothesis about the
population as well as the cause; "DDn reseeks" was true of its one
archive, and the AD-only rows in the same table disproved it as the
whole story.


## 2026-10-09 (the key is folded at decrypt time, not at launch) — the Shortcut updater's archive key is recoverable from a decrypt-time RAM dump by an 8-byte oracle, but its install UI never reached decrypt here

**Status: WITHDRAWN 2026-10-10.** The 45 dumps were taken while the
installer had no target; once it accepts one, the key is in memory before
any file is written (2026-10-10, *the installer's own key*; BLOCKERS.md).

**The question.** `sit_scheme()` read bytes 107/109 as encryptor ids, and
on two forks of Aladdin's *Shortcut 1.5.3 Update* (5/3 and 6/5 at 106/109,
empty data forks) routed one to `NewDEx` and refused the other, while the
other eleven forks (method 13, id 0) asked for a built-in-scheme password
(FORMATS.md, *Where an archive names the module*). Hypothesis: the bytes
are installer-private and all thirteen share one password the installer
carries.

**The oracle needs no password guess.** An encrypted StuffIt classic
archive's eight-byte `'MKey'` verifies the key before any fork (that every
scheme shares the archive key is not established; the self-test grades
the 3.5.1 built-in scheme on three Aladdin archives since 2026-10-10). It
decides a candidate eight-byte **archive key**, so recovery is a
fixed-width search: slide an 8-byte window over anything.
`tools/sit_mkey_oracle.py` is the self-testing oracle; the C hot loop,
committed 2026-10-10 as `tools/sit_akscan.c`, scans a 12 MB dump in a few
seconds (Python ~1 ms a window). The updater's MKey is
`4d87bcb0c49abe53`.

**Where the key is not.** Under Mini vMac (boot-shell build, `mkboot.py
--app-name`) the updater shows the InstallerMaker 1.0.3 splash, a license,
and an SFGetFile picker; **45 dumps** of `/proc/<pid>/mem` across them
held **nothing**, nor did the uncompressed resources (the engine is in
`ADCR` resources nothing here decodes). **The reading drawn, WITHDRAWN the
next day**: that the key is computed lazily at extraction. The picker was
Standard File asking for the installed Shortcut.

**Transferable.** A verifier of the derived key rather than the password
lets a memory image answer, and it held. The inference from 45 empty
dumps did not: an absence said the program had not reached the key, not
WHEN it would — the shape of a timeout read as a measurement (BLOCKERS.md,
*Withdrawn claims*).

## 2026-10-10 (the header that checks its own CRC) — a search of unread bytes is a count only when the thing searched for can fail a checksum

**Claim (measured).** The 112 StuffIt walks the 2026-10-09 sweep left
short were two stops: 88 at a header `plausible()` rejects, 24 at a
header past the end of the indexed file (short fetches, a third kind,
were none of them on re-run). Searching the first kind's unread bytes by
plausibility gave **2,571 "flagged headers"** with ids spread evenly over
0..255 — the signature of compressed data.

**What made it a count.** `src/fmt_sit.c` refuses an entry whose header
CRC-16 at +110 fails. All 2,835 headers in `fixtures/` and 2.0.1's
specimens pass it, and the same unread bytes held 12,255 headers that
check, none flagged (TESTING.md, the 2026-10-10 row). **Plausibility says
where to look; only a test the bytes can fail says nothing is there.**

**Consequence.** The two StuffIt 2.0 rows in OPEN_ITEMS.md have no
population left in reach; closing them needs somebody's file.

## 2026-10-10 (the installer's own key) — the Shortcut updater wanted the product it updates, not a destination; with a stand-in it extracted, its key came off its memory, and the two stray ids were InstallerMaker's

**Claim (measured).** Bytes 106..109 of a method-13 fork are not module
ids when InstallerMaker 1.0.3 wrote them. All thirteen forks of
*Shortcut 1.5.3 Update* decrypt under the built-in scheme and password
`PeekAB00`; twelve pass their CRC (the Addendum is damaged in the
archive). Under the standard resource-header mask the six files compared
are byte for byte what the installer wrote to an emulated disk, the two
stray-id forks included (FORMATS.md, *Where an archive names the
module*). `sit_scheme()` no longer reads the id on a method-13 fork.

**What stood in the way was a question.** The "destination picker" was
Standard File filtering on `cdev`/`Cut!`. Its pre-flight hook (`IBeg`,
`ADCR`-compressed on disk) is plain 68000 in the RAM dumps: `FindFolder
('ctrl')`, look for `Shortcut™`, fall back to creator, accept a non-empty
first `cdev` (`GetHandleSize`). A 373-byte stand-in with a `vers` and a
16-byte `cdev` in System 7.0.1's Control Panels is found without a dialog,
and installation proceeds. (6.0.8 with this stand-in not tried; the
earlier stand-in with no `cdev` made it quit silently on both.)

**When the key exists.** A launcher staying alive as Mini vMac's parent
dumped memory from Install to the end (Yama `ptrace_scope` 1 lets only an
ancestor read `/proc/<pid>/mem`; a detached dumper got `EACCES`). All 30
dumps from the restart alert and save dialog and all 120 during
extraction hold `78a51a6ffd3a3ea4` at two offsets, verified by `--ak`; 16
dumps from the rejected-stand-in run hold none. The key exists once the
installer has a target, before any file is written (BLOCKERS.md).

**The password came back with the key.** StuffIt classic folds the
password under one schedule keyed by `0123456789abcdef`; for ≤ 8
characters that is one DES encryption, so `D(key) ^ 0123456789abcdef` is
the password (`unfold()` in `tools/sit_mkey_oracle.py`, which also grades
`tools/sit_akscan.c`).

**Transferable.** An empty Standard File list is a filter, and the filter
is readable code — already in dumps taken for something else. And the
installer that carries the key also extracts, grading the engine against
Aladdin's own decoder for free.

## 2026-10-10 (the six repairs that were a 16-bit check) — a CRC-16 cannot adjudicate a search of 592,576 candidates; the stream's own end symbol and the fork's own map could

**Claim (measured).** The Shortcut updater's Addendum is damaged in its
compressed stream and no single flipped bit explains it (FORMATS.md,
*Where an archive names the module*); three decoders, Aladdin's included,
agree byte for byte.

**The search said otherwise six times.** Every bit of the 74,072-byte fork
flipped in turn: `macextract t` passed six (a positive control found a
planted flip, and only it). A 16-bit CRC passes one in 65,536, and 592,576
candidates predict about nine. None of the six ended at the end symbol
`0x140`, and none gave a resource map that parses.

**Transferable.** A checksum grades a search only while the search is
smaller than its range. Structure the format already carries decided it:
method 13 ends every healthy fork with `0x140` at the declared length (12
of 12 here), and a resource map points at itself — the header-CRC entry's
lesson from the other side. No engine change: the CRC already refuses the
entry.

## 2026-10-10 (the application that was asked) — 3.5.1 cannot use an Encryptor module, measured by asking it for one; it had been launchable for twelve days

**Claim (measured).** StuffIt Deluxe 3.5.1 writes encryptor id 4 beside
method 13 whatever it is asked for, and has no route to a 2.x module, so
`sit_enc_id` ignoring 107/109 on a method-13 fork costs nothing on
anything 3.5.1 wrote (FORMATS.md, *Where an archive names the module*).

**Evidence.** `tools/vmac/sitenc351.py`, with 2.0's three Encryptors in
both candidate folders: the script words `des`, `newde` and `encrypt` each
wrote 4 / 4; `Set encryptor` and `Enable Optimizer` answered *"No longer
supported"*; both dialogs offer a checkbox only. The static read (3.5.1's
folder list has no `Encryptors`) was the cheap half; the run could have
come out the other way.

**Transferable.**
- **What a program writes is settled by asking the program, not by
  counting its absence in the wild**: 166,970 walked headers said nothing
  about what 3.5.1 *could* write; two runs did.
- **"Does not launch" has to record how it was launched.** The 2026-09-28
  write-up omitted that all three attempts were ⌘O; the double-click that
  worked went into a code comment, and every status file was wrong for
  twelve days (BLOCKERS.md, withdrawn claims).
- **No engine change**; the lane asserts the 4, so a 3.x archive saying
  otherwise fails there first.

## 2026-10-10 (the clock that was timing its own check) — the 1x wall-clock table was mostly the harness's bit-at-a-time CRC; a table took the two copies from 52 s and 46 s to 9 and 15, and the tick probe now bills the read-back

**Claim (measured).** On the 7 MHz tier the autotest build's read-back
was 92 % and 83 % of the two copy-only fixtures' extract wall, so
FORMATS.md's "the extract column is the archive alone" was wrong for
every row (FORMATS.md, *Measured on a 7 MHz Mac Plus*).

**Evidence.** `run.py --emu mv-4M-1x --poll 3 -D UNC_AT_TIMING`, a new
`gTkBack` bracket around the read-back in grid slot 7:

| fixture | `gTkRun` | read-back, bit at a time | read-back, table | extract wall, before → after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kermitut9test.bin` | 90 ticks (1.5 s) | 2,860 ticks (47.7 s) | 341 ticks (5.7 s) | 52 s → 9 s |
| `derived-PCCTS.tar` | 459 ticks (7.7 s) | 2,286 ticks (38.1 s) | 325 ticks (5.4 s) | 46 s → 15 s |

`at_crc32_update` is now table-driven (built on first use, separate from
`unc_crc32`). Graded 72/72 at 4 MB and at 1 MB on System 6.0.8, all
fifteen `timing.txt` rows byte-exact at 1x; one table entry XORed by 1
(`tab[0x5A]`) failed both fixtures on the CRC slot only. Autotest build
only; `dist/` unchanged. DECISIONS.md 2026-09-20 (*the window that was
already the staging buffer*) had already said so.

**Transferable.**
- **A clock that stops on a painted result times everything before the
  paint.** "Boot is split off" was read as "the rest is the archive"; the
  tick probe's bracket had the answer since 2026-08-30.
- **A harness's cost is proportional to what it checks**, so it distorts
  comparisons as well as totals (Compact Pro and DiskDoubler halved,
  `derived-Export.sit` did not move).
- **An independent clock agreed once the harness was out**: the
  interactive application reads 56 s for `derived-EmpireBuilderDemo.sit`;
  the autotest 61 s now, 119 s before.

## 2026-10-10 (the double-click that goes by the application's creator) — a Desktop-file entry launches MacExtract for a SIT! archive but hands it nothing; retagging the application's own creator hands it the file, with no Desktop edit at all

Question: a companion that makes double-clicked archives open in
MacExtract on System 6 and earlier by writing MacExtract into the
`Desktop` file under other creators.

**Claim (measured, System 6.0.8; one case on System 3.0).** The Finder
hands a double-clicked document to the launched application only when the
document's creator is the APPLICATION FILE's own creator. Which
application launches is the `Desktop` file's business; whether it gets
the document is not.

**Evidence.** `tools/vmac/deskclaim.py`, one boot each, a `SIT!/SIT!`
archive double-clicked, graded on the dialog the application opened:

| `Desktop` file | application file's creator | result |
|---|---|---|
| stock | `MExt` | the Finder refuses: *"could not be opened/printed (the application is busy or missing)"* |
| + `APPL` entry `SIT!` → MacExtract | `MExt` | MacExtract launches, **no document** — its Open dialog |
| + that entry and a bundle filed under `SIT!` | `MExt` | the same |
| stock, archive's creator `MExt` | `MExt` | handed over — the first System 6 double-click of a MacExtract document ever measured |
| + the `SIT!` entry | `SIT!` | handed over |
| **stock** | **`SIT!`** | **handed over**, and on System 3.0 the same |

The Finder registered the retagged application under `SIT!` itself; its
`BNDL` still names `MExt`, so it draws the generic icon.

**Consequence.** The companion need not write the `Desktop` file; one
application FILE per claimed creator is needed — whole copies (~230 KB
each) or a small relaunching stub (untested). Open: which application
wins with StuffIt on the same volume; the `APPL` list allows duplicates
(`MACS` three times), so "the last one seen" is a hypothesis. System 7's
`Desktop DB` was not written.
(Followed by DECISIONS.md 2026-10-11, *the stub that hands it on*, and
2026-10-12, *the stub beside StuffIt*.)

**Transferable.** The first probe graded on the volume and passed a run
that handed over nothing (the harness's own Return opened the archive from
the Open dialog). A launch and a handover end in the same files.

## 2026-10-11 (where the stubs can live) — a visible folder beside MacExtract, provided the companion writes each stub's Desktop entry and each stub carries a bundle under its own creator

Where the per-creator stubs (2026-10-10, *the double-click that goes by
the application's creator*) can sit. **Decided: visible, in one folder
next to MacExtract** (the maintainer wants no invisible files; the
invisible rows are measured, not used).

**Claim (measured, System 6.0.8).** A stand-in stub (a copy of MacExtract
with creator `SIT!`) is handed a double-clicked `SIT!` archive from a
never-opened folder, and after a desktop rebuild, if the companion writes
its `APPL` entry and the stub's `BNDL` and signature are filed under the
creator it claims. A stub on the startup disk serves floppy archives.

**Evidence.** `tools/vmac/deskclaim.py`, one boot each; *refused* is the
Finder's alert, identified positively:

| stub | `Desktop` file | result |
|---|---|---|
| startup disk's root; archive on a second floppy | stock, startup window opened first | handed, entries on the floppy |
| `MacExtract Helpers:`, never opened | stock | refused |
| the same | + `APPL` entry `SIT!`, dirID of the folder | handed |
| the same, creator retagged only | deleted, rebuilt at boot | refused |
| the same, with `--stub-bundle` | deleted, rebuilt at boot | handed |
| root, invisible | stock, window opened | refused |
| root, invisible | + `APPL` entry | handed |
| root, invisible, with `--stub-bundle` | deleted, rebuilt at boot | handed |
| `MacExtract Helpers:`, `--stub-bundle --doc-icon 'SIT!'` | deleted, rebuilt at boot | handed, and **the archive drawn with the stub's icon** |

**Consequence.** Per creator, a visible stub in a folder beside
MacExtract, bundle under that creator, `APPL` entry written; a rebuild
finds them by their bundles. **A stub can also give the archives their
icon**: an `FREF` for type `SIT!` and its own `ICN#` drew the archive with
it (the inherited `'****'` `FREF` gives none); a drawn icon re-run settled
that the inverted frame was not a selection. **The icon** is
`tools/icon/make_archive_icon.py`'s: Apple's blank document (System
3.0/6.0.8 `ICN#` 132, System 7.0.1 `ics#` -4000, reproduced pixel for
pixel) carrying MacExtract's 16x16 at 32x32 and a reduced carton, block
and folded document at 16x16, colour members taking `make_icon.py`'s
colours by name; the maintainer's choice over four alternatives. Drawn by
the System 6.0.8 Finder (`--doc-icn`, `--doc-ics`); the colour members
have been seen in no Finder. Icons are per TYPE. Open then: StuffIt on
the same disk, and the handover (no stub existed yet).

**Transferable.** Two runs were invalid and one passed: moving the
application moved the archive's icon, the double-click hit empty space,
and the control read "no MacExtract dialog" as the expected refusal. **A
control that expects nothing to happen passes when nothing is clicked**;
the grade now has to SEE the alert.


## 2026-10-11 (the cells that were run) — three StuffIts over 2.0's archives, encrypted Compact Pro and mail sets; each box graded by its own Expander

**Six README.md comparison cells rested on documentation or nothing.**
Four were measured on 2026-10-11 (the three StuffIt columns of the
StuffIt 2.0 row; 5.5.1's and 7.0.3's encrypted Compact Pro); the
disk-image cell came from 4.0.2's own files, the mail row from running
all three. Results: FORMATS.md, *Run over the hard cases*.

**A box is graded by its own Expander**, which is what it hands an archive
to and which installs from Linux (`sitzip.py`); 5.5's Deluxe will not
start on an assembled installation. Not measured: an application with its
own modules could differ for the 2.0 Optimizers.

**The mail row went back to "several mail messages"**, cells qualified
"BinHex postings only, not MIME": two StuffIts read the BinHex posting,
the newest does not, none joins a MIME set (6f140b9 had narrowed it).

**Transferable.** Each StuffIt fails differently, and none is an older
one plus additions: 4.0.2 refuses what 5.5.1 decrypts; 5.5.1 hands back
damaged files where the others refuse; 7.0.3 alone loses a multipart
BinHex posting. "A later version does everything the earlier one did"
would have been wrong in both rows.

## 2026-10-11 (the string that said reduced) — 5.5.1 decodes zip Reduce and 7.0.3 writes it wrong, though both binaries name it

README.md's zip row ticked all three StuffIts and qualified only
MacExtract for Reduce. Run on two wild Reduce archives (FORMATS.md, *Zip
methods in the three boxes*): 5.5.1 decodes Reduce byte for byte; 7.0.3
writes wrong bytes and then crashes. **The README gained a Reduce row**
rather than "except Reduce" in two columns.

**Transferable.** Both binaries name the method — 7.0.3 a
`reduce_decompressor` class, 5.5.1 an error message listing what it
supports, which omits Implode, which 5.5.1 decodes. **A capability string
in a binary is a claim, like a Read Me**, and it failed in both
directions; hence 4.0.2's cell says "not tested", though its translator
carries 5.5.1's sentence.

## 2026-10-11 (Reduce comes in) — the maintainer reversed the scope call; the source was graded against 2,379 stored CRCs, and the first version was redone: placed where only zip pays, twice as fast, and following the specification where its oracle does not

**Claim.** Zip methods 2 to 5, Reduce, decode (FORMATS.md, *Reduce*).
Out since 2026-10-08 (*the method a Macintosh wrote once*) on a census
that found no Macintosh writer; **the census stands, the maintainer moved
the line**: a Mac user with a DOS CD meets these files, and 5.5.1 reads
them (*the string that said reduced*).

**Graded before transcribed.** APPNOTE.TXT 5.2 states the method; deark's
`foreign/ozunreduce.h` is the one implementation in `reference/`
(XADMaster has no decoder; Info-ZIP UnZip 6.00 refuses). A Python
transcription over every Reduce entry in reach — the Shrink sweep's 346
files, all 105 + 92 + 13 distinct method 2–4 zips, 150 method-5 zips drawn
with `--seed 20261011`: **2,371 of 2,379 entries reproduce the CRC-32 the
archive stored**, and deark fails all 8 others (three PHP test stubs, two
in archives cut before their directory, three CRC-bad in deark too,
damage a HYPOTHESIS). The C decoder agreed with it file by file, before
and after the rewrite.

**Asked what I would have done differently, the maintainer asked for all
of it; four things, measured:**

- **Where it lives.** The first commit put Reduce in `ovl_codecs` beside
  Shrink, which every format keeps: 2,275 B for methods only zip has.
  Both now live in a sixteenth image, `ovl_zipold`, kept for zip alone.
  Against the tree before Reduce, every non-zip format has **1,128 B
  more** heap, tar 1,052, zip 1,622 less. Resident: 80 B of code and 16 of
  A5 (first 108 and 36; one shared patch routine).
- **Speed**, never measured: tick probe on a Mac Plus **75.6 s** for
  549 KB of output; `m68kprof` put 43 % in the bit reader's out-of-line
  calls. Bits in two locals and B(N) from a table: **35.6 s**, −53 %.
- **A copy longer than its distance**: first refused, as `ozur` does, and
  called a rule the CRCs needed; they did not (no good entry has one; the
  3 that do fail either way). **APPNOTE.TXT 5.2.5 permits it**, so this
  follows the specification and deark refuses a legal stream; the unit
  test checks the repeated run.
- **An index past a follower set's count**: `ozur` gives 0; 5.2.4 defines
  S(j)[I] only for I < N(j), so this refuses. No wild entry has one.

**Withdrawn from the first entry**: the zero window is not "from a calloc
rather than from a comment" — **5.2.5 states it**, and 1,480 entries
confirm it. And `synth-dd-m5.dd`'s 512Ke "short by at least 854 B" was
read as a fixture Shrink and Reduce cost; that is only the first refused
allocation, and **the entry needs 401,408 B**, 180 KB more than granted.
**"Short by at least" is a floor; binary-search the budget before calling
a fixture close.**

**An encoder, because nothing here writes Reduce.** `tools/synth_reduce.py`
from 5.2 alone, graded by deark byte-exact on its four entries; the fifth
fixture and the fuzz seed that took `unc_reduce_decode` to 100 % of lines
in 3,000 cases. Its first draft never reached before the output start;
counting each rule over its own output caught it.

**The fixed 8,448 B table was questioned** (CLAUDE.md's smell): follower
sets use a median 359 of 8,192 slots, so sizing from the stream saves up
to ~8 KB; not done, because the whole Reduce peak, 21.8 KB, is under
deflate's and Shrink's in the same reader.

**The CLI loses a mechanism**: `method_out_of_scope` and its deark
paragraph existed for Reduce alone and are deleted.

## 2026-10-11 (the bytes paid for the speed) — a second speed round on zip's two old methods, every change priced on five axes, and the one that saved space bought the one that cost it

**Claim.** Reduce is 3.9 % and 2.1 % faster on two wild archives and
Shrink 13.3 % and 13.2 % on two fixtures, on the tick probe, and their
image is 8 B SMALLER (FORMATS.md, *Reduce*, *Speed*; *Shrink*). Resident
code, A5, heap and every tier tally unmoved; Reduce's frame grew 4 B on a
chain that is not the deepest.

**Each change measured alone, size first, ticks second; two of six not
taken.** Fewer live values was smaller and 4 ticks slower, twice; a mask
table was 37 B larger and no faster (a register shift of ≤ 5 beats an
indexed load). Both were plausible from the listing.

**The space came from the cold path.** The follower-set header, read once
per entry, carried two inlined copies of the window top-up: 92 B for no
measurable time. That paid for the copy loop's cursors (+4 B, −62 ticks)
and Shrink's inline bit fast path (+82 B, −474 ticks). **Before calling a
speed change a trade, look for the bytes in the same image's cold code.**

**For Shrink the narrower change was faster.** The fully local bit reader
that made Reduce fast was −268 ticks for +112 B in Shrink, whose decoder
had no registers to spare; inlining only the fast path through `UncBitIn`
was −474 for +82. **The same fix does not always work twice** (CLAUDE.md).

**What is left is register pressure**: Reduce's copy destination moves
data→address register every byte (a rewrite bought 63 ticks for 34 B);
Shrink's double string walk, a few percent, estimated. Both in FORMATS.md,
not done.

## 2026-10-11 (the digest our own oracle could not compute) — `message/partial`'s two wrong anchors: `Content-MD5` catches both once mpack computes MD5, and the check was declined for its size

**The check the item named would have refused every good set.**
`Content-MD5` disagreed on the RIGHT anchor too: `9wUjvhRTvxJ5PathZdghuA==`
is not the MD5 of `MacROT13.cpt` (`dO2NH00wvu2hojPgtDVU+w==`). mpack's
`md5.h` declares `UINT4` as `unsigned long`, 64 bits here, so
`build/mpack/mpack` wrote `eZncdejaZIxnJ+E3xbd4Aw==` for `abc` where RFC
1321 gives `kAFQmDzST7DWlj99KOF/cg==`, and munpack, built alike, agreed —
the oracle pair could not fail on a digest. The 68000 port is right
(`tools/vmac/macmime.py` asserts it since 2026-08-29).
`tools/build_mpack.sh` now edits that line and rebuilds any mpack whose
`abc` is wrong.

**The mechanism was the format's**: fixed munpack writes the same 929 B
on the concatenated anchor, and warns; part 1's body runs to the end of
its file, as OPEN_ITEMS hypothesised. No joiner defect.

**Built, priced, declined.** On base64 parts it failed both anchors per
entry and passed the good set, `run_mime.py` and the unit tests on x86 and
`qemu-m68k`. It needed its own MD5 in `ovl_text`: **+1,446 B**, resident
+0 shipped, +784 in the control (costing that lane `derived-DD_Expand.sea`
at 512 KB), for a header seen nowhere but mpack's output. The maintainer's
call: too many bytes. Numbers: FORMATS.md (*`message/partial`*); decision:
OPEN_ITEMS.md (*Out by the brief*).

**Transferable.** Two programs from one source agreeing is one
measurement when they share a bug. And a check's population is a number
to take before building it: the size was measured to the byte, the use
never.

## 2026-10-11 (the constant was a square) — asking 2.0.1 for every combination instead of searching for a stranger's

OPEN_ITEMS.md held `Photoshop 1`, `JPEG Lossy` and the five ciphers as
*"graded only on archives this project made"*, closable by *"a file from
somebody who has one"* — argued against on 2026-10-02 (*the Optimizer
that was in somebody else's corpus*): a stranger's archive could add only
a COMBINATION, and the writer is on the emulator image. So the
combinations were asked for: 22 boots, 121 archives, each set unstuffed by
2.0.1 in its own boot (`tools/vmac/sitcombo.py`; FORMATS.md, *Every other
document 2.0.1 will optimize*).

**Everything but `JPEG Lossy` was already right** (`Photoshop 1` under
every method, a second `MacPaint 1` painting, every Optimizer under each
cipher, the plug-ins, cipher edges, four Optimizers over a folder, a dozen
stale ids in 104..109). `JPEG Lossy` was right on 2 of 33 new documents
(the two its module declined) and **wrote garbage with exit 0 on 5**.

**The constant was a square, twice.** `src/sit_ccube.c` decoded 7 restart
segments per MCU row because both subjects were 256 pixels wide, and
FORMATS.md called *"a tile row is 7 segments = 21 MCUs"* the format. The
rule, `(w + 39) / 40`, was at C3a+0x4366, read in ten minutes once a
second width existed. Width and height were also swapped in `decode.py`
until a 400x300 document failed.

**Grey content hid the colour path.** Pencil on white has chroma 128
everywhere, so replicating and interpolating chroma agree, and so do the
old `>> 14` and CCOD+0xd98's 16-bit conversion. Twenty-one coloured
documents (`cdocs/`) were 56 % wrong at 256x256; the third model —
interpolation at full precision, last column repeated — is exact on every
width 1 to 512. CCOD+0x5b9a's byte-domain upsampler, found first, is NOT
what runs (31 bytes off on a 7x5 document).

**The search would have found nothing**: none of 196,139 classic StuffIt
archives carries either module. **Ask what the original software will do
before asking who else used it**; a reachable writer is a loop, not a
search.

**Same root, smaller.** `cli/main.c` told a forkless DES archive's owner
DES was unimplemented (it fired only on a missing `'MKey'`); an Optimizer
refusal printed *"method 64"* (the bit included); and `run_crypt.py`'s
*"unimplemented encryptor"* case bent id 3 (`NewDEx`, implemented since
2026-10-02) and passed because its copy had no resource fork. With the
fork and id 5 it fails if the id check goes (id 3 gives *"truncated"*,
expected *"encrypted"*).

**Costs, measured.** StuffIt overlay 27,938 -> 28,614 B (+676), resident
`CODE` and A5 unchanged; peak RAM unchanged at 256x256, 51.9 KB at
400x300 (FORMATS.md, the `JPEG Lossy` table).

**Transferable.**
- **A specimen set samples a format's PARAMETERS, not only its bytes.**
  List what the writer lets a user vary — size, mode, colour, quality — and
  check each has more than one value.
- **Content can hide a whole stage**: a stage with constant input cannot
  fail — the pipeline passed vacuously, not the test.

## 2026-10-11 (the zip that was a set of one) — every plain `.zip` opened on a Macintosh failed as "more parts", for two months, and the first real machine found it in one session

**Claim.** From 2026-08-14 to this fix the application refused every
ordinary `*.zip` with *"This archive has more parts. Find them and try
again."* Measured on the maintainer's LC475 under System 7.6.1 (`08
Reduce.zip`, `09 Shrink.zip`, repeatably), reduced: `run.py --as
archive.zip` gives `ret = -11` (`UNC_ERR_SEGMENTED`) on System 7.0.1, and
PASS under the harness's old name. Fixed; `interactive.py --named zip`
still joins a real spanned set.

**Mechanism.** The shell decides by NAME first that a file is in a family
(`ZipFamPartOf`, 2026-08-10); `.zip` is a spanned set's LAST part, so
every `.zip` went to `SegDescribeLast`, and an ordinary zip's "disk 0" is
not-a-set, reported as a missing part. The CLI decides by sniffed format.
A `.zip` is now a set member only if its own record says so; a `.zNN` is
still placed by name.

**Why nothing caught it.** Every Mac tier opened fixtures as `archive.sit`
(`run.py`'s `ARCHIVE_NAME`; `compat9.py` names zips `z1`, `z2`). `run.py
--as NAME` now chooses the name. **What the tiers still cannot see:**
every other extension the shell dispatches on by name (`.NNN`, `.zNN`,
the gzip/.Z fallback name) unless a run asks with `--as`.

**Transferable.** A harness that renames its input to one constant removes
a dimension of the input space: 964 fixtures, one distinct name.

## 2026-10-11 (one archive per launch) — the eager overlay lifetime cannot open a second format, so the application quits after an archive instead of offering one

**Claim.** On the LC475 a `.sit` opened after a `.cpt` in one launch
failed: `ovl_release_if_unwanted` gives back every image the first
format cannot want and never reloads (`mac/ovl_load_eager.c`), yet the
loop returned to Standard File.

**Decision, the maintainer's.** Quit rather than reload — a reload is the
floppy swap the eager lifetime exists to avoid. `ovl_spent()` reports a
release and the loop stops; an archive that never reached one still
returns to Standard File; lazy and resident builds keep looping.
**Cost:** of several archives dropped at once, only the first is
extracted.
(Superseded: DECISIONS.md 2026-10-12, *the reload that the list needs*.)

## 2026-10-11 (the folder that is already there) — a top-level folder already on the disk is numbered, not merged into

**Claim.** Extracting `derived-Library_ISBN_Barcoder.sit` twice into one
folder on the LC475 put 34 `name~1` files through the first run's tree —
by the 2026-09-03 decision to descend into an existing folder "rather than
sprout a `~1` beside it".

**Decision, the maintainer's, reversing that.** At the TOP of the
extraction an existing folder is numbered `~1` like a file; below the top
nothing can be there that this run did not make. Top folders a run made
are kept in `gTopMade` (16 ids), because `gDirMemo` can fill and a
forgotten top folder would be split in two; when full, the top merges as
before. Measured with `-D UNC_AT_TWICE` on System 7.0.1:
`derived-Jobs_Quote.sit` gives `Jobs Quote` and `Jobs Quote~1`, four files
each under their own names.

## 2026-10-11 (the icon that did not darken) — the 8-bit icons used colours the Finder does not darken, and the generator had stopped being the source

**Claim.** Selected on the LC 475, the colour icon darkened only its
white. Documented cause: *"only the 34 colors shown in Figure 8-23 get
darkened when a color icon is selected"* (Macintosh Human Interface
Guidelines, ch. 8, *Selection mechanism for color icons*); five of the
nine `icl8` indices were outside the 34 (240 of 1,024 pixels in the box's
mid-tone alone). Values from Kreative Korp's MoCCP
(`gpl/AppleIconColors.gpl`), whose `MacOS8Bit.gpl` also confirmed the
generator's palette on all 256 entries — the 2026-08-24 "reconstructed,
not transcribed" caveat is withdrawn, now checked.

**Change.** `make_icon.py` takes every 8-bit tone from the 34 via
`icon8()`, which asserts membership: cyan 153/255/255, 0/153/255 and
102/102/204, orange 255/204/153, 255/102/51 and 221/0/0 (the dark cyan
moved to Apple's periwinkle to keep three tones).

**Seen selected.** Under Mini vMac as a Macintosh II, System 7.5.5
(`tools/vmac/colouricon.py`): at 256 colours the old icon darkens only its
sheet, the new one all over, as SimpleText
(`docs/screens/0c-icon-selected-256.png`). **At 16 colours there was
nothing to fix** — every selected icon is flat grey
(`0d-icon-selected-16.png`); the "16 colours" in the item was a misreading,
never measured. **On silicon 2026-10-12** (LC 475, 7.6.1): darkened only
its white until a desktop rebuild — the Finder kept v0.39.0's `icl8` — so
the download notes say to rebuild.

**The generator had stopped being the source.** `macextract_icons.r` ("edit
the script, not the hex") had gained a `'****'` FREF, its BNDL entry and
both `'vers'` by hand; a whole regeneration lost 102 lines, caught in the
diff. **"Generated, do not edit" decays the first time somebody edits it
anyway; diff a regeneration before trusting it.**

## 2026-10-11 (the stub that hands it on) — a 7 KB application per claimed creator launches MacExtract with the Finder's document list intact, so MacExtract is not changed at all

**Claim (measured, System 6.0.8 under the Finder and under MultiFinder,
and System 3.0).** A `SIT!` stub in `MacExtract Helpers` beside an
UNCHANGED MacExtract is launched for a double-clicked `SIT!` archive and
starts MacExtract, which is handed the archive and extracts it: the
Segment Loader keeps `AppParmHandle` across the stub's `_Launch`.

**Evidence.** `tools/vmac/deskclaim.py --stub`, the stub from
`companion/make_stub.py`, one boot each:

| system | stub registered by | result |
|---|---|---|
| 6.0.8, Finder | a desktop rebuild, from the stub's own bundle | handed, entries on the volume |
| 6.0.8, Finder — control, the stub claiming `ZZZZ` | a rebuild | refused (the Finder's alert) |
| 6.0.8, MultiFinder (its icon in the menu bar) | a rebuild | handed |
| 3.0 | the companion's `Desktop` entry | handed |

**How it works.** `companion/stub/stub.c`: the folder above its own (from
`GetAppParms`, `PBGetFCBInfo`, `PBGetCatInfo`); MacExtract found by type
`APPL` and creator `MExt`, not name; that folder made default with
`PBOpenWD` and `SetVol`; the original `_Launch` form (name pointer and
configuration word, `launchBlockID` 0), leaving `AppParmHandle` alone; an
alert if MacExtract is missing. 7,424 bytes as MacBinary, mostly Retro68's
runtime (the "1-2 KB" estimate was wrong). `make_stub.py` sets the creator,
`hasBundle`, and writes a `BNDL`, signature, `FREF`s and both icon
families.

**Two wrong first attempts, both caught by a frame**: built
`onlyBackground` (faceless) from a misread of the `SIZE` bytes; and
MultiFinder started by writing the boot blocks' shell field, which stopped
the boot — the stock blocks already name it at 0x5A, and copying back
`MultiFinder`, `DA Handler`, `Backgrounder` and `Finder Startup` starts it.

**Consequence.** No change to MacExtract. Open then: System 7, StuffIt on
the same disk, several archives at once (measured next: DECISIONS.md
2026-10-12, *the stub beside StuffIt* and *the reload that the list
needs*).

## 2026-10-12 (the application nobody could leave) — a menu bar and a titled progress window let System 7 switch out of an extraction; the same code on every System, and the `SIZE` flags left alone

**Claim (measured, System 7.0.1 under Mini vMac, from the Finder;
`interactive.py --switch`).** During an extraction the user can click a
Finder window or choose from the Application menu; the Finder comes to
the front at once and the extraction finishes behind it. One ending in the
background shows its alert or report only when MacExtract is brought back.
About opens mid-extraction, which waits behind it.

**What it took** — Toolbox calls a Mac Plus has under System 3.0, no OS
test (the maintainer's ask: one behaviour everywhere):

- A menu bar: Apple (About MacExtract…) and File (Quit, which is
  Cancel). **The Apple menu is what makes it work**: with File alone,
  System 7.0.1 drew neither Help nor Application menu.
- The progress dialog becomes `noGrowDocProc` instead of `dBoxProc`; the
  pump uses `FindWindow`, then `MenuSelect`. (`dBoxProc` with a menu bar
  never tried.)
- One event path, `SystemTask` + `GetNextEvent`; `WaitNextEvent` and its
  trap test are gone (the autotest keeps them for `at_idle`).

**Withdrawn before it shipped.** Clearing `acceptSuspendResumeEvents` and
setting `needsActivateOnFGSwitch` made System 7.0.1 hold the switch until
the extraction ended (Finder's menu bar over a minute late); the old
flags switch at once. Same build, same archive. **Cost: one emulator run.**

**Price: 16 B given BACK** (eager −8 B code, −8 A5; partly `.data`
alignment). The first commit was **+192 B**; priced by removing each piece:
Cmd-Q (`MenuKey`) 32 B, dragging 32, a quit flag 48, NULL checks on our
own `MENU`s 32, About's number from `'vers'` 1 64. The last three went
(`check_docs.py` holds the DITL's number to `UNC_VERSION`); Cmd-Q and
dragging were the maintainer's call. Stack probe (`-D UNC_AT_STACK`):
sp=4,068, paint 7,706 of 12,190 B, with and without About, on the first
commit's build.

**Two harness traps, a run each.** A diagonal pointer across the menu bar
opens every menu it crosses (it released on File > Quit, then on "About
Balloon Help…"); `pick()` moves straight down, then across. A press is
seen only at the next progress callback, so the harness holds the button.

**Consequence.** Closes the LC 475's System 7 item. Open: real hardware
(MANUAL_TESTS.md §2), and how long the button must be held on the slowest
decoder (OPEN_ITEMS.md).

## 2026-10-12 (the stub beside StuffIt) — opening the helpers folder once registers a stub, on System 6 and 7; with StuffIt Deluxe on the same disk the archive still opens — on System 6 in whichever the Finder registered last, on System 7 in whichever file is newer — and the icons stay with whichever was registered first

**Claim (measured, System 6.0.8; System 7.0.1 for the first row).** A stub
in a never-opened `MacExtract Helpers` folder is registered by opening the
folder once — no rebuild, no `Desktop` entry written. With StuffIt Deluxe
2.0.1 (`SIT!`) on the same disk, a double-clicked `SIT!` archive opens in
both install orders, in the application registered LAST (the `APPL` list
holds both, newest first); the bundle kept under `SIT!` is the one
registered FIRST, so the other application wears its icons.

**Evidence.** `tools/vmac/deskclaim.py --stub`, MacExtract as committed
(`HEAD:dist/MacExtract.bin`), one boot each:

| system | setup | result |
|---|---|---|
| 6.0.8 | helpers folder opened once (`--open`) | handed |
| 6.0.8 | not opened — control | refused |
| 7.0.1 | helpers folder opened once | handed |
| 7.0.1 | not opened — control | refused (System 7's alert) |
| 6.0.8 | Deluxe's folder opened, then the helpers' | handed to MacExtract; the stub drawn with Deluxe's icon |
| 6.0.8 | the helpers' folder, then Deluxe's | Deluxe opens it in its archive window; Deluxe drawn with MacExtract's icon |
| 6.0.8 | desktop rebuilt, `MacExtract Helpers` sorting first | Deluxe opens it; the archive drawn with the stub's archive icon |
| 6.0.8 | desktop rebuilt, Deluxe in `A StuffIt Folder`, sorting first | handed to MacExtract; the archive drawn with Deluxe's |
| 7.0.1, Deluxe 3.5.1 dated 2026-08-22, stub 2026-10-11 | Deluxe's folder opened, then the helpers' | handed to MacExtract; the stub drawn with Deluxe's icon |
| 7.0.1, the same | the helpers', then Deluxe's | handed to MacExtract; Deluxe drawn with MacExtract's icon |
| 7.0.1, Deluxe re-dated 2026-11-11 | Deluxe's, then the helpers' | Deluxe opens it in its archive window |
| 7.0.1, the same | the helpers', then Deluxe's | Deluxe opens it in its archive window |
| 7.0.1, stub newer | `Desktop DB`/`DF` deleted, rebuilt at boot, either folder sorting first (2 runs) | handed to MacExtract; the archive drawn with the stub's archive icon |
| 7.0.1, Deluxe newer | rebuilt, either folder sorting first (2 runs) | Deluxe opens it; the archive drawn with Deluxe's |

The Deluxe copy from `sitopt.hfv` had Finder flags `0x0100` (no
`hasBundle`), so the Finder registered nothing and **the first two Deluxe
runs tested no competitor and said "handed" anyway**.

**System 7 chooses by date, not order**: only the MacBinary modification
date (offsets 91 and 95) was changed between rows (which of creation or
modification it compares is not separated). Opened folders give icons by
System 6's first-bundle rule; after a REBUILD icons follow the date too.
The stub registering in rebuild runs where the stock `Desktop DB` refused
it is what shows the rebuild happened. A rebuild registers in catalog
order (alphabetical): last-sorting opens, first-sorting gives icons
(System 6).

**Consequence.** No installer: copy the folder beside MacExtract and open
it once. A StuffIt on the disk does not stop archives opening; the icon
crossover is the Finder's (one bundle per creator) and unavoidable without
giving up the bundle a rebuild needs (2026-10-11, *where the stubs can
live*).

**Grader**: Deluxe 3.5.1's window border at y 82 matched one-row as
MacExtract's Open dialog; dialogs are now matched on all three frame rows.
System 7 positioning is by type-select (`--open NAME`, `--archive-at
NAME`).

**Transferable.** A competitor the system never registered is no
competitor: check the second application is in the list before reading
"the first one won".

## 2026-10-12 (the reload that the list needs) — several archives opened at once are all extracted: the eager build reads its decoders again between archives of one Finder list, with the bundle reserved low so the next archive gets a launch's heap

**Claim (measured).** The Finder hands a launch a LIST of documents on
every system, and since 2026-10-11 the shipped build extracted the first
and silently quit (*one archive per launch*, whose cost line this
reverses). It now disposes the decoders it kept, re-reads the bundle and
continues with the next; one chosen in Standard File still quits after
it. `tools/vmac/relaunch.py`, a `.cpt` and a `.sit` together, graded on
both destination dialogs and every entry: **both extracted on System 6.0.8
at 4 MB and on a 512Ke, System 3.0 on a 512Ke, System 6.0.8 under
MultiFinder and System 7.0.1**, where the build before extracts the first
only.

**Rejected: relaunching itself** (`_Launch` with the list left in
`AppParmHandle`, as the stub does): worked on System 3.0 at 512 KB and 6.0.8
under the Finder, returned without launching under MultiFinder and System
7. A mechanism needing the system told apart was not wanted.

**The reload broke the heap up (measured).** The first version refused
`derived-a2basic.dmg.sit` (one 205 KB block) second on the System 3.0
512Ke: *"Memory is too broken up"*. `-D UNC_AT_HEAPLOG` (free total,
largest block, every unmovable block; its sum agreed with `FreeMem()`;
the 24-bit block header layout is from memory of Inside Macintosh II,
*Memory Manager*, not a source here) showed the 164,272 B bundle landing
locked at 239,626, mid-heap: largest free block **317,692 B at the first
archive, 175,478 B at the second.**

**The fix: reserve the bundle low.** `ovl_reload` gets the handle without
loading, takes `GetResourceSizeOnDisk` (A9A5, `SizeRsrc`) and `ReserveMem`s
it (A040, `ResrvMem`, lowest place it can — from memory of Inside Macintosh
II, confirmed by the log) before reading. The bundle lands at 62,896, as at
launch, and the next largest block is **295,422 B against 295,572 B after
a fresh launch for `a2basic`, 317,594 against 318,530 B for a `.cpt`**.
`Cool_Tools__.sit` then `a2basic.dmg.sit` extract one after the other. If
the bundle cannot be re-read, ALRT 135 says so (a string literal would be
72 B of A5).

**Cost, all five axes.** `CODE` +192 B, A5 +0 shipped (`ovl_reload` 114,
`main` +62, 16 alignment); control +24/+8; lazy +80/+16 (by symbol,
tools/build_mac.sh). Heap: nothing during an archive. Stack: called from
`main`. **Extractions lost: none** (`run_tiers.py --check`, both lanes,
all three tiers; a shipped grant 192 B lower, `OVL_SAVED` −160, TIERS −32).
One disk access between archives of a list — a possible swap, paid only
when the user asked for several.

**The list is read by POSITION now**: `AppParmHandle` is relocatable and is
now read after an extraction. HYPOTHESIS that it ever moved: not observed;
the pointer was latent only.

**Met on the way.** Writing `Heap Log` mid-extraction hung the 512Ke at 0 %
with Retro68 Multiversal's `HCreate`/`HOpen`/`FSWrite` glue; through
`PBHCreateSync`/`PBHOpenSync`/`PBWriteSync` it works (bisected: no walk, no
write; HYPOTHESIS that the glue is at fault, not read).
(See DECISIONS.md 2026-10-13, *the bug was the footnote*.) System
7's Finder put `In`'s neighbours off the window edge, so the harness
type-selects there.

## 2026-10-12 (the second bundle that only paints) — an application's BNDL for another creator gives that creator's documents icons on System 7 and opens none of them; the creators come from the programs, and TCDB only says where to look

**Claim (measured).** StuffIt Expander 4.0.2 (`SITx`) carries a second
`BNDL` owned by `SIT!` declaring `SITD` and `SIT!`, as do DropStuff and
later Expanders. With Expander alone, a double-clicked `SIT!` archive is
REFUSED on System 6.0.8 and 7.0.1, window opened or rebuilt; System 7's
rebuild draws it with StuffIt's icon and still refuses
(`tools/vmac/deskclaim.py --extra`). The 2026-10-10 rule stands: **a
bundle for another creator decorates and does not open.** MacExtract
cannot claim creators by bundles; the stubs stay.

**Where the creators come from.** `companion/app-bundles.tsv`: 42 creators
read off the applications — the BinHex family (`BNHQ` 4.0, `BnHq` 5.0,
`HQXr`, `HQX `, `PnLh` DeHQX), StuffIt's (`SIT!`, `SITx`, `DStf`, `SITC`),
Compact Pro's (`CPCT`, `EXTC`), DiskDoubler's, Now Compress's (`NCdc`,
`NCar`, `NCcm`), `LARC`, `LHAx`, `arc*`, `MARC`, `UPIT`, `LZIV`, `Gzip`,
`ZIP `, `TAR `, `MB2P`, `GJBU`, the uu and base64 decoders, and more.
Copies from Discmaster (`/file/` originals arrive as MacBinary), two per
program from different discs, one request every 3 seconds
(`companion/harvest/`), plus cached disk images; copies agree.

**TCDB was the list of names only.** Where compared (BinHex 4.0 and 5.0,
HQXer, HQXing, DeHQX) it agreed; its licence forbids redistributing a
table built from its rows (MacStamp's DECISIONS.md, *TCDB's data is
licensed*), so a stub's claim cites the program.

**Macintosh Repository was not the source** (guests download once per 10
minutes); its 190 category pages were read for what the programs are
(OPEN_ITEMS.md, *Formats classic Mac programs wrote that nothing here
opens*).

## 2026-10-12 (the flush the LC 475 did not need) — a build without the instruction-cache flush ran six decoders byte-exact on a 68LC040, and the flush stays

**Claim, measured once.** `-D UNC_OVL_NOFLUSH` (bare `ovl_flush_code`) on
the maintainer's LC 475 (68LC040, System 7.6.1, caches at default, not
checked) extracted `08 BinHqx.cpt`, `10 DD Expand.sea`, `12 PackIt.pit`,
`14 LhA.lha`, `16 ARCDOS.arc` and `23 Troi.sit`, dropped together (so the
bundle was relocated, released and READ AGAIN): all 28 files byte-exact in
both forks against the Linux CLI.

**What it does not show.** A clean run proves only this machine, this
time, did not stale an instruction; other traps may flush, and a copyback
cache is a race this run may have won. **The flush stays**: Inside
Macintosh requires it (*Stale Instructions*), it is 104 B. The item is
closed: hardware was asked, and the answer is "not here".

**Transferable.** Run the probe that can fail before the one that can
only pass.

## 2026-10-12 (the block nobody could cancel) — StuffIt 5 went four minutes without looking at the event queue; Arsenic now reports while it decodes a block and builds either inverse

**Claim (measured, Mini vMac 1x, System 6.0.8, `-D UNC_AT_TICKGAP`).** The
longest gap between progress callbacks — the longest Cancel, Cmd-. and the
menu bar go unanswered, since the shell pumps nowhere else — was **254 s**
of `derived-a2basic.dmg.sit`'s 281 s at 4 MB, and 140 s of the
Barcoder's. Arsenic reported only from its output walk; the block decode
and the inverse called nothing. The 2026-08-07 output tick was timed under
the 1 MB sampled index, where the WALK is slow.

| fixture, 1x | before | after | extraction |
|---|---|---|---|
| a2basic, 4 MB | 254 s | **0.8 s** | 281 → 281 s |
| Barcoder, 4 MB | 140 s | **1.1 s** | 462 → 462 s |
| KeyGraphics, 4 MB | 9.4 s | **0.3 s** | — |
| a2basic, 1 MB | 18.3 s after the block fix | **0.6 s** | 341 → 342 s |
| Barcoder, 1 MB | 24.1 s after the block fix | **1.9 s**, inside the walk | 745 → 742 s |

All byte-exact; other formats: FORMATS.md (*How long a click waits*).

**What it took.** Three ticks reporting the walk's last position (bar
still, pump runs): per 256 bytes appended to the block (a threshold — a
low-byte mask cost KeyGraphics a third of its reports, since zero runs step
over multiples), and per 8 KB chunk of each inverse pass. Both inverses
lost a 1 KB array (counts reused in place): frames 2,060 and 2,348 →
1,072 and 1,328 B.

**Price.** `ovl_stuffit` **+312 B** (28,614 → 28,926; shipped resident
unmoved); control `CODE` +328, A5 −8, `TIERS` −320 by derivation; +4 B of
heap; no tier tally moved. Host instructions −0.3 % (table), +0.05 to
+0.17 % (sampled). Autotest stack: 3,044 → 4,088 B at 4 MB, **5,372 →
4,356 B** at 1 MB, so the deepest point fell. The interactive build's
Toolbox under the pump was not measured (*hypothesis*: ~1 KB deeper on the
table path, against a 12,144 B stack). Handing the index to `a->index`
before its second pass lets a Cancel free it on the way out (−12 B).

**Cancel path.** Aborting at each of KeyGraphics' 236 callbacks under ASan,
default and `UNC_ARS_FORCE_SAMPLED`: 236 clean aborts each; the negative
control (index handed over late) leaked 70 KB at four points.

**Transferable.** `run_ticks.py` bounds the gap in input BYTES, so a
decoder whose expensive work reads no input passes at any duration. **A
bound in the wrong unit cannot fail on the case that matters.**

## 2026-10-13 (the mail that counted itself three times) — MIME's bar is the input its writing passes consumed, and a Cancel in its walk is no longer taken for the end of the message

**Claim (measured, host).** A MIME message reads most bytes three times
(walk, then per entry a sizing and a writing pass) and counted all of them:
a 405,753 B message with a 300 KB attachment counted 1,236,327 B, the bar
full a third of the way in. The corpus's one 1,248 B message never ticked
at 8 KB; a 4 KB step surfaced it.

**What it took.** The readers count into a private `UncProgressState`
whose callback, a relay in `fmt_mime.c`, reports the input the writing
passes consumed: still a tick every 8 KB of any pass, the bar moving only
during writes, never back, ending at 95–99 % on three generated messages
(against 300 %+). The maintainer chose this over spreading the bar across
three passes (more code). The Mac never sets `test_only`.
