**A second fault, from the abort sweep.** The header reader and boundary
scan took any failed read for the end of the message, dropping a Cancel:
aborting at each of `big.mim`'s 149 callbacks gave 98 aborts, **49
successes with entries missing** and 2 "not a MIME message". Both now pass
anything but a clean end up: 353 of 353 callbacks across three messages
abort, once or sticky, under ASan, nothing left allocated.

**Price.** `ovl_text` **+240 B** (11,510 → 11,750: +158 progress, +52
Cancel); resident unmoved; control `CODE` +228, A5 −4, `OVL_SAVED` +224,
`TIERS` −224, no tally moved. `MimeCtx` 2,428 → 2,464 B; a 16 B relay frame.
A first design ticking from MIME's own loops cost +368 B.

**The test can fail**: `run_mime.py`'s new cases fail the build before
(836,211 and 638,931 B past the end); at a 4 KB step `run_ticks.py` passes
all 1,399 archives, where it had failed `synth-os9-mime.mim`.

## 2026-10-13 (the disk that was still in the drive) — a split set's next part is asked for after the floppy the last one came from is ejected

**Claim (measured, emulated).** The "Part N has not been found" alert came
up with part N−1's floppy still in, so a one-drive user had to eject it
first (Cmd-Shift-1).

**Decision, the maintainer's.** Before the alert, part N−1's disk is
ejected and the alert says so: *"Part N of "X" is not on that disk, so it
was ejected. Insert the disk it is on."*, Find… kept. Ejected only if the
drive queue calls it ejectable (byte 1 of the flags before the `DrvQEl` is
1 or 2, Inside Macintosh: Files, *Drive queue*) and it holds neither the
application nor the System. **The destination is deliberately not
checked** (the maintainer declined it: extracting a split set onto one of
its parts is the user's mistake).

**Not done: a too-small-destination warning** — the extracted total is
unknown until the last part, and part 1 knows only the joined size for
StuffIt segments. **Maintainer: no warning**; the disk-full error suffices.

**Price.** Shipped `CODE` **+256 B**, A5 **−48 B**: **208 B off every
extraction's budget** (`SegAskUser` +156, `SegDriveOfFile` 82 new, 18
alignment). Both sentences are DITL text (131, 136); as strings they cost
+352 and +80. Control +192, `OVL_SAVED` −16, `TIERS` −192, no tally moved.
`SegAskUser`'s frame 660 → 728 B; `SegDriveOfFile`'s 188 B returns before
the alert.

**The test can fail.** `interactive.py --diskeject`: part 1 alone on
Floppy A, output to the boot volume; asserts Floppy A's image is closed
while the alert is up (Mini vMac `fclose`s on eject), the boot image open,
the contents landing after Floppy B with nothing clicked. Passes on System
3.0, 6.0.8 and 7.0.1; the build before fails on 6.0.8 (*"floppy A ...
STILL IN THE DRIVE"*). `--segments` and `--diskswap` still pass.

**Found on the way.** `--diskswap` fails on the old build too when its
fixture is an ARCHIVE (it compares the joined file, which the application
unpacks) — the trap `--segments` hit on 2026-08-31; documented in
`tools/vmac/README.md`, not fixed.

## 2026-10-13 (the bug was the footnote) — Retro68's `paramErr` is Apple's documented contract; the uninitialised `ioMisc` the report called latent is written through, and is what broke M10

Re-verifying `tools/retro68-hopen-repro/ISSUE.md` before the maintainer
posts it. Retro68 master `d8b891a` pins a multiversal whose
`custom/glue.c` is byte-identical to the one measured. The tracker, never
searched: **#53 (2018)** is this exact `HOpenDF` `paramErr` on System 6,
closed by a fallback in `libretro/syscalls.c`, and Technote FL 1041
(*Inside Macintosh: Files* errata) says the caller retries with `HOpen`.
The headline would have been closed as a duplicate of documented
behaviour.

The same technote: "ioMisc must be initialized to zero before calling
PBHOpenDF, PBHOpenRF, or PBHOpen. Failure to initialize ioMisc to zero on
some Macintosh models will cause the system to crash." The report called
it latent because a poisoned `0xA3A3A3A2` opened fine — on a 24-bit Mac
Plus that is not RAM. `iomisc_repro.c` points `ioMisc` at a 1 KB decoy
and counts what changes:

| case | System 6.0.8 | System 7.0.1 |
|---|---|---|
| `PBHOpenSync`, `ioMisc = NULL` | 0 longs | 0 |
| `PBHOpenSync`, `ioMisc = &decoy` | 131 (524 B, one access path buffer) | 3 |
| `HOpen`, `&decoy` left on the stack | 131 | 3 |

The disassembly agrees: `HOPEN` reserves 124 bytes, writes four fields,
never pb+28. Case 3 first read 0 because GCC inlined the poisoning
function into `main`'s frame; `noinline` fixed it — showing the case can
fail.

A bare `open()`/`write()`/`close()` probe on System 6.0.8 hung in
`close()`, the same with the stack zeroed (two runs, probe not kept), so
`ioMisc` does not explain it; *Retro68's newlib cannot open a file* saw
mpack stop in `open()`. Unexplained.

**It is what broke M10**, measured: a worktree at `014ed25` built six ways,
switching only what `MyOpenFork`/`MyHCreate` call, run through that
commit's `tools/vmac/run.py` on four fixtures
(`tools/retro68-hopen-repro/m10-variants.patch`):

| variant | result |
|---|---|
| 0 zeroed param blocks, as committed | 4/4 |
| 1 Retro68's `HOpen`/`HOpenRF`/`HCreate` (the pre-fix code) | hangs, still extracting at 300 s |
| 2 Retro68's `HOpen`/`HOpenRF`, zeroed create | 0/4, all hang |
| 3 verbatim copy of the glue's `HOpen`/`HOpenRF` | 0/4: 0 files, or never paints |
| 4 that copy plus `ioMisc = NULL` | **4/4** |
| 5 that copy plus `ioVersNum = 0` | 0/4 |

3 and 4 differ by one line; the symptom moves with stack layout (hang,
zero files, a bomb, in 2026-07 a garbage refNum).

**Transferable:** a junk-value probe proves only that value harmless; ask
what the field is *for* and give it a value that would be used. Search
the upstream tracker before writing an upstream report.

## 2026-10-13 (the grey that cost no code) — two 'dlgx' resources give the progress and password dialogs Mac OS 8/9's background, paid for with the icons' resource names

**Claim (measured, Mac OS 9.2, `os9.py --cancel` and `--encrypted`).** A
`'dlgx'` beside `DLOG` 128 and 132, theme-background bit only, draws both
dialogs in the theme's grey, as Mac OS 9 draws every alert; text, bar,
edit field and refusal message draw cleanly. Code and A5 unchanged
(55,300 / 19,052 B); Systems before Appearance 1.0 never ask for the type.

**The layout is measured**: Apple documents the flag bits (*Dialog Feature
Flag Constants*) and the layout only as a figure; all 100 `'dlgx'` on the
Mac OS 9.2 disk are 6 bytes: version word 0, then 32-bit flags.

**The download stayed 235,776 B by paying for itself.** Each `'dlgx'` is
22 B of fork (30 for the first, adding the type) and the last MacBinary
block had 21 B left; the six icon members dropped their unread name
`"MacExtract"`: 66 B, net −14 B. The `.dsk` is a fixed 800K image.

**Not taken:** **Standard File** (-4000, -3999) — a `'dlgx'` in our file
changes nothing, theirs are the System's; owning copies via
`SFPGetFile`/`SFPPutFile` costs code past the ceiling (maintainer: white
Standard File is fine). **The report dialog** (133) — `RepListDraw` erases
with the port's background. **A blue bar** — +12 B, over the ceiling.

**Transferable.** A resource-only change can still cross a 128-byte
MacBinary block, and the code ceiling refused 12 B the `.bin` would have
absorbed: measure the fork and the code.

## 2026-10-14 (the icon the eject left behind) — the floppy a split set's last part came from is unmounted as well as ejected

**Claim (measured, silicon then emulated).** On the LC 475 the 2026-10-13
eject left a dimmed floppy icon: `Eject` "flushes the specified volume,
places it offline, and then ejects" it, and does not unmount (Inside
Macintosh: Files, *Eject*). Reproduced under System 7.0.1; System 6 shows
none either way.

**Change.** `UnmountVol` then `Eject`, by drive number. `UnmountVol` fails
with `fBsyErr` while a file on the volume is open (destination on that
floppy), and the eject proceeds as before. Parts remembered on that drive
are forgotten first (their refNums die with the volume).

**Price.** `CODE` +80, A5 +16 (alignment), shipped and control: **96 B off
every grant**, `TIERS` −96, no tally moved.

**The test can fail.** `interactive.py --diskeject` on System 7 reads the
desktop after quit: 0 px off the pattern now, **636 px** (a dimmed Floppy
A) on the build before. Passes on System 3.0, 6.0.8 and 7.0.1.

## 2026-10-14 (the disk the dialogs were on) — every dialog and alert is preloaded, so a one-drive Mac is not asked for the application's floppy mid-extraction

**Claim (measured, one-drive Mini vMac, System 7.0.1).** With MacExtract
and the archive on two floppies, the extraction after Save asked for ME,
C, ME, C: the progress window's `DLOG`/`DITL`/`'dlgx'` and the closing
alert's `ALRT`/`DITL` were purgeable resources read on first use. Every
dialog, alert and `'dlgx'` is now `preload` as well as purgeable, and the
walk asks for nothing.

**Why it costs nothing.** The budget is taken with `PurgeSpace`, which
counts purgeable blocks as free: `-D UNC_AT_BUDGET`, System 6.0.8 / 512
KB, 196,184 B against 196,186 B (−2 B; other tiers not re-run). `CODE`
and A5 unmoved. Under memory pressure they are purged and the old
behaviour returns.

**How it was found.** The LC 475 took eleven swaps before the first
dialog (OPEN_ITEMS.md, *What the LC 475 found*), and Mini vMac gives every
disk a drive. `NumDrives` 2 makes the System ask for disks by name: build
`mv-4M-1d`, walk `tools/vmac/onedrive.py`. It did not reproduce the drop
(7.0.1's Finder copies files dropped on an alias of an app on an ejected
disk), and showed launching from the floppy costs ME, C, ME, the Finder's.
**Confirmed on the LC 475, 2026-10-14**: no swap after Save; the previous
day's copy gives ME, C, ME.

**The test can fail.** `onedrive.py --app` on the build before: *"asked
for after Save: ME, C, ME, C"*, exit 1; this one: nothing, exit 0.

## 2026-10-14 (the swaps that are the System's) — the swaps before the first dialog happen before MacExtract's main() runs, and a stock application takes as many

**Claim (measured, one-drive Mini vMac, System 7.0.1).** Two archives on
floppy C opened together with MacExtract on ME take ME, C, ME, C, ME, C,
ME, C before *"Extract into"*; the LC 475 took eleven on 7.6.1.

**MacExtract cannot change it.**
- A probe painting a mark at each step of `main()` shows **no mark in any
  ME prompt** and all six in the next frame: every ME is before `main()`.
- Preloading everything but the bundle, the lazy build, a copy without
  colour and small icons: the same eight.
- **SimpleText** from 7.0.1 on ME with two text files on C: **ten**.

**After Save.** The reload's ME between archives is by design. One more
inside the second *"Extraction complete."* **is the Finder's**, measured:
with the alert's resources in memory (checked with `SetResLoad(false)`),
no icon, no sound, every segment preloaded, still asked; no alert and 20 s
of `GetNextEvent`, not asked; no alert and 20 s of `WaitNextEvent` at sleep
30 (a modal dialog's idle), asked. Another comes after quit. An alert has
to wait.

**Kept.** `onedrive.py --drop` prints the sequence; it fails only if it
never reaches *"Extract into"* twice.

## 2026-10-14 (the floppy a USB drive can write) — a 1.44 MB HFS image joins the download, and why it is not a self-extracting archive

**Claim.** A USB floppy drive writes MFM only (720K, 1.44 MB), not the
800K GCR `MacExtract.dsk`, and a `.bin` copied to a PC disk arrives still
MacBinary. `dist/MacExtract-1440K.img`, the same HFS volume at 1,474,560
B written raw, is a disk a SuperDrive Mac mounts (*hypothesis* until
MANUAL_TESTS.md §9: it is the format a Mac formats 1.44 MB in, and hfsutils
reads it back byte-exact).

**Why not a self-extracting archive**: a `.sea` is an application with its
code in the resource fork, so every channel that loses MacExtract's fork
loses the `.sea`'s. Size was not the obstacle; the channel is, and a raw
image carries the whole volume.

**Left out.** The Plus, 512Ke and original SE read GCR only, so this does
nothing for the floor target. No 720K image until a SuperDrive is seen
mounting one. `make_dist.sh` now requires hfsutils.

## 2026-10-14 (the BinHex before 4.0) — `.hex` and `.hcx` extract, graded against what BinHex 2.0 itself wrote

**Claim (measured).** **BinHex 2.0 (Yves Lempereur, 1984) writes both**
pre-4.0 encodings — `.hcx` with File ▸ *Compressed* checked (default),
`.hex` without; `***COMPRESSED`, `***CRC:` and `***CHECKSUM:` are strings
in its `CODE` (`tools/vmac/binhex2.py`). The version labels were never
evidence (macutils' README asks "Is it BinHex 2.0?"/"3.0?";
`reference/notes/BinHex.md` gives `.hcx` to 2.0).

**`src/fmt_hecx.c` transcribes hexbin's `hecx.c`, the only reader**, and is
graded by four files BinHex 2.0 wrote on System 6.0.8 from a known
two-fork subject (`.hcx`, `.hex`, `.hex` with line feeds, that `.hcx`
inside a `.hex`), each byte for byte, plus three `.hcx` files from the 1985
*mactosh* archive whose 16-bit sums verify. `unar` reads neither.

**Settled by the writer:** the `.hcx` sum adds bytes **unsigned** (`hecx.c`
passes a plain `char`; the 131 high bytes of BinHex 2.0's own `.hcx` and
2,037 to 13,697 in the 1985 files agree with no signed sum); the `.hcx`
sum fixes the fork order (it rotates; resource fork first); the `.hex`
8-bit add does not.

**Two departures from hexbin, each a file it loses**: hexbin waits for the
"(This file" banner before the `#TYPECREA$FFFF` line, and two 1985 files
have none (`tools/run_hecx.py` asserts hexbin fails them); and it reads a
`.hcx` line's count BEFORE restoring mailer-stripped spaces, so a
one-character line reads its count 2 too high — seven lines of BinHex
2.0's own `.hcx` are such, once stripped.

**The probe**: a `#TYPECREA$FFFF` line (four hex digits, always written,
not required by `hecx.c`) followed by a `***` marker; after a banner, the
first non-header line settles BinHex 4, so all 204 `.hqx` sniff as before
(`run_diff.py`).

**Price, shipped (CODE + A5): +352 B off every grant** (probe +222, +76 of
it a shared header test; table row and name 36; switch case and
alignment); `ovl_binhex` 2,590 → 4,994 B; control +2,480; no tally moves.
(CORRECTED the same day from +416: both encodings now enter through
`unc_binhex_extract` via a new `UncCtx.fmt` — −64 B shipped. Reusing
`UncForkOut` for output staging was +54 B of overlay for nothing, left
out.)

**Not graded.** Only BinHex 2.0 has been run; BinHex 1.0 and the BASIC
BinHexes wrote `.hex` too (`BinHex.md`), output not found. SUMacC's `.dl`
was then a lead (since extracted: DECISIONS.md 2026-10-24, *the format
before BinHex*).

## 2026-10-14 (the layer that had its envelope's name) — an unwrapped entry no longer lands on the envelope being read, and is no longer deleted with it

**Claim (measured).** A nameless layer is named after its file minus an
extension, so with no extension the entry and the envelope are ONE path.
The CLI exempted that path from its clobber check, opened it `wb` while
the engine read it, then deleted "the envelope" — by then the entry:
**exit 0 and nothing on disk.** Found on BinHex 2.0's `.hcx` inside a
`.hex` (`YN.hex` → `YN` → `YN`); two nameless gzip layers in `Same` lose it
the same way.

**Change.** An entry whose path is the envelope's is written as
`NAME.unwrap~` and renamed onto it after the deletion; a second entry for
that path still meets the clobber check.

**The test can fail**: `tools/run_unwrap.py`'s gzip pair gives an empty
directory on the build before. The Mac shell's own sink was not affected.

## 2026-10-14 (the file the disk was too full for) — a fork of 2 GB or more is refused as one entry, not reported as a full disk

**Claim (measured).** On Mac OS 9.2.2, HFS+, 110 GB free, a zip holding one
2,300,000,000-byte file ended on *"The disk is full."*: the shell's
`SetEOF(ref, (long)want)` overflows a signed `long`, and the classic File
Manager's offsets are signed 32-bit, so no ≥ 2 GB file can be written
here. The engine is not the limit (the CLI decodes it, CRC checked).

**Change.** Before the file is made, an entry with a fork ≥ 2 GB (not
`UNC_SIZE_UNKNOWN`) fails alone: *"Big.bin is over 2 GB, too large here"*,
and the run goes on. Mini vMac, System 6.0.8: that line and *"Extraction
finished."*; the build before, *"The disk is full"*. Confirmed on Mac OS
9.2.2 the same day.

**Not done.** An unknown-size entry (streamed gzip) growing past 2 GB still
ends the run with the File Manager's error.

**Price.** Shipped `CODE` +60, A5 +36: **96 B off every grant**; control
+64, `OVL_SAVED` −32, `TIERS` −64, no tally moved. A first version calling
`RepEntryFailed` from its own check cost +144 (a third call stopped the
inlining of a 78 B function).


## 2026-10-15 (the rest of the block) — the shell moves to Retro68's File Manager glue only once the glue sets every input field

**Decision (the maintainer's).** After Retro68 fixed #320 on 2026-10-14
(BLOCKERS.md), the shell's own zeroed blocks (`MyOpenFork`, `MyHDelete`)
are to give way to the standard glue — code every Retro68 program uses is
preferred to a private copy, even at no gain. `MyHCreate` stays (corrected
the same day: `HCreate` also reads and rewrites the Finder info, two more
traps per entry that `sink_end`'s stamp makes redundant). Not yet: #320
fixed one field and nobody had checked the rest.

**Measured.** Every File Manager function in multiversal `4c78d24`'s
`custom/glue.c` read against Inside Macintosh: Files, ch. 2, then the
suspects run (`tools/retro68-hopen-repro/`, *glue_audit*): four more, on
Systems 3.0, 6.0.8 and 7.0.1. The one that would hit this application is
`HOpen`'s unset `ioFVersNum`: harmless on HFS, `fnfErr` on MFS — the 400K
disks of the floor System. Switching would have swapped our fixed bug for
theirs, where nobody would look.

**What made it believable.** Each glue row has a zeroed-stack control, a
no-glue row exercising the field alone, and a `-DGLUE_FIXED` build applying
only the proposed patch, after which every row matches its control.

**Consequence.** The switch waits for that patch upstream (OPEN_ITEMS.md,
*The shell's own File Manager blocks, until multiversal's glue is inline*);
the issue is for the maintainer to post (MANUAL_TESTS.md §7).

## 2026-10-15 (the File Manager a 64K ROM has) — extracting onto an MFS disk is out of scope, and so is a 64K ROM without HFS

**Decision (the maintainer's).** On a Macintosh 512K with no Hard Disk 20,
branch `rom64k` opens Standard File, then bombs `ID = 12` at its first HFS
call (measured, BRANCH_NOTES.md on that branch). Writing there is not
taken.

**Why.** Without HFS an HFS trap does not exist, so it bombs rather than
returning an error; the shell cannot try and fall back, only test first
and run a second path — the per-machine behaviour the maintainer rules
out. Pre-HFS calls everywhere cannot create folders. The second path was
estimated, not built, at 1.5–3 KB of `CODE`.

**MFS destinations, on every Macintosh**: the same decision — MFS has no
folders, so it needs that second path even where HFS is present. Out of
scope; what a user gets is deliberately not documented; no harness writes
to one.

**Consequence.** The Hard Disk 20, whose driver file supplies HFS, is the
only route for a 64K ROM (MANUAL_TESTS.md §6).

## 2026-10-15 (the words in one file) — every string the application shows is in mac/macextract_strings.h

**Decision (the maintainer's).** Every menu, dialog, alert, report line
and Standard File prompt moved out of `macextract_mac.c` and
`macextract.r` into one header both include, as `#define`d literals.

**Cost: nothing, measured** — the MacBinary payload (offset 128 on) is
byte-identical; an edit to a code string and to a DITL string both
reached the binary incrementally. Retro68's `add_application` makes each
`.r` depend on itself alone, so `mac/CMakeLists.txt` appends the header to
the rule. Rez and C differ on escapes (`\0xC9` vs `\xC9`), so no string is
shared between the halves.

**Not moved.** Format names and `unc_strerror` (`src/unc_engine.c`, shared
with the CLI); the `'vers'` strings (`macextract_icons.r`).

## 2026-10-15 (the height nothing needed) — a `JPEG Lossy` image is capped in width only, and a tall one StuffIt restores now extracts

**Claim (measured).** `src/sit_ccube.c` refused a `JPEG Lossy` image over
8,192 pixels in EITHER dimension, with no recorded reason for the height.
StuffIt Deluxe 2.0.1 optimized and restored a 16 x 8,208 RGB document;
this engine refused it ("past this engine's 32-bit reach", at 394 KB) and,
with the height cap lifted, matches the restore byte for byte in the data
fork (resource fork differs only in reserved bytes 16-255, as on the
256 x 256 control).

**The width cap stays**: it keeps `w * h * channels == outlen` in 32 bits
(8,192 x 65,535 x 4 fits, so no TIFF-short height overflows) and the row
buffers grow with width. An 8,208-pixel WIDTH crashed the emulated Mac
once, leaving no archive (hypothesis: the COMP keeps width x 4 and width
x rows in 16-bit words), so the cap refuses nothing known to exist.

**The documents.** Photoshop 1.0's file is raw pixels plus a 10-byte
`'8BIM'` 1000 resource (channels, rows, columns, depth, mode);
`sitopt.py --pssynth` writes one, and a 256 x 256 control is
byte-identical to `psdoc2`. The first attempt packed six words, so the
mode read as 8 and the module declined silently — a run that measured the
construction, not the size.

**Consequence.** `run_sitcombo.py` grades the tall archive (set `settall`,
optional) and fails on the capped engine; FORMATS.md, *Size limits*.

## 2026-10-15 (the purge MaxApplZone never did) — one launch path for every ROM, and the four bytes it is not neutral by

**Claim: `MaxApplZone` is replaced on every machine by three calls the 64K
ROM has, and the zone ends where it did.** `GrowApplZone()` issues
`_MaxMem` (largest free block in D0, growth in A0; Inside Macintosh
II-38), `NewPtr`s their sum, which can only be met by growing the zone
(II-13), and frees it. System 6.0.8 at 1 MB: the zone ends at `ApplLimit`
in both builds. The `Has128KROM()` guard was two behaviours.

**Not budget-neutral, and not because of the code.** The budget came out
+4, +4 and +6 B against `main` on the three tiers, with `CODE` + A5 summing
to the same 212,368 B. **Same-size hybrids** (one trap word swapped:
`_MaxApplZone` for `_MaxMem`, then a register clear for `_NewPtr`)
settled it: with no `NewPtr` the budget is `main`'s to the byte; with a
failing, purging `NewPtr` (II-13), `main`'s +4 on System 6 and +14 on
System 3.0. **A same-size hybrid splits layout from behaviour in two
runs.**

**On System 6 the +4 is the purge; on System 3.0 the +6 is not
attributed.** (CORRECTED the same day: first given as the purge on both.)
`_MaxMem` purges every purgeable block (II-38), `MaxApplZone` none
(II-30); the blocks are back by budget time. A non-purging candidate still
reads +14 B on System 3.0 against its own hybrid, so a whole-zone
`NewPtr` leaves more behind there regardless; the split is not measured.

**The purge can be avoided, and was not.** `HeapEnd` is documented (II-51;
Memory, 1992, 2-104) and `CompactMem(maxSize)` compacts without purging
(2-71): `NewPtr(CompactMem(0x800000) + ApplLimit − HeapEnd)` worked on
System 6.0.8 at 1 MB, `FreeMem` within 36 B of `main`'s. Budget −32, −32
and −18 B against `main` (on System 6 exactly its +32 B of `CODE` + A5); +24
B of `CODE` against `_MaxMem`'s +12; `HeapEnd` never checked on System 7
or Mac OS 9. The maintainer kept `_MaxMem`; the alternative is here if the
purge's reload at launch, never timed, matters.

**`_MaxMem` is inline asm, the first in `mac/`**: two register outputs, and
Multiverse's Pascal glue costs +44 B against +12. autc04/multiversal pull
request 20 (open, 2026-10-15) generates such inline code; it would also
inline `PurgeSpace` (hand-inlined: `CODE` −80 B in all three
configurations, CODE + A5 −64 B shipped, −96 B lazy and control). Not
taken; the toolchain here is unpatched. (Superseded: DECISIONS.md
2026-10-19, *the toolchain that inlined PurgeSpace*.)

**Merged into `main` 2026-10-16**, after the LC 475 (7.6.1) ran it; built
on branch `rom64k` (`BRANCH_NOTES.md`). Re-measured on `main`: on the
emulated 512K under MFS System 3.0 it opens Standard File, where the prior
`dist/` bombs `ID = 03`; no tally moves.

**Price** (BRANCH_NOTES.md): `CODE` +12 B in `main()` everywhere; A5 −12 B
shipped, +20 B elsewhere, `.data` padding; stack 0; no extraction lost on
any Mini vMac tier or Mac OS 9.2.

**Decision (the maintainer's).** Extracted, refused, not an archive, could

## 2026-10-16 (the installer that was a layer) — a chain of layers stops at an application: an installer is run, not extracted

**Found by the maintainer**: `stuffit_expander_55.bin` (MacBinary of
*Aladdin Expander™ 5.5 Installer*, `APPL`/`STi0`, data fork a StuffIt
archive) was unwrapped, its data fork extracted and the installer deleted
as a layer. What an installer installs is not its data fork.

**Decision.** A layer that leaves one `APPL` file ends the chain, in the
application and the CLI. An application opened directly is still
extracted (the user's choice). `unar` already stopped there.

**Measured.** The CLI writes the installer alone, as `unar` (before: its
contents and two output errors); Mini vMac System 6.0.8, the same and
"Extraction complete." Over the corpus, 69 fixtures now stop one layer
earlier and 65 of their `unar` manifests already listed the application
alone; the differential suite stays 971/971. Five suites now open the
application as a second step: `run_segments.py`, `run_sdmodule.py`,
`run_crypt.py`, `run_sitopt.py`, `run_zipit.py` (one ZipIt MacBinary
records no type, so still goes through). Stopping at a `.sea` is accepted
(the maintainer, 2026-10-16).

**Price.** Shipped CODE +32, A5 0; with the `gDropLeft` change the day
nets +16 B against 2026-10-15.

## 2026-10-16 (the estimate that went back up) — the time left is taken from the byte counts, not the percentage, and timed per layer

**Seen by the maintainer** on a StuffIt 5 archive: the time left went
back up by one. **Not specific to StuffIt 5** (measured): the estimate was
`elapsed * (100 - pct) / pct` from the WHOLE percentage, so it climbs
within each percent. Replayed at the engine's real cadence (8 KB steps,
read at most every 6 ticks) on a constant rate, it rose 211 times in an
hour on a 3 MB archive, by up to 16 minutes, and by up to 65 minutes in
four hours. That this is what the maintainer saw is a hypothesis.

**The engine was ruled out first** (measured): over 759 fixtures `done`
never goes down within one total (`uu-wild-terrainman.uu`'s exception is
the CLI's second pass).

**Decision.** `ProgressReading` uses `done` and `total`, shifted until
`total` fits 16 bits, with `elapsed * (t - d) / d` as `elapsed / d * (t -
d)` + `elapsed % d * (t - d) / d`: 32-bit unsigned, no 64-bit division. No
rise over 2 s up to 400 MB and four hours; 2 s is TickCount's resolution
(1.65 s at 1%), and a rounded minute can still turn over once in the
400 MB case. Above 512 MB the 16-bit `d` is coarser than 8 KB and the
climb returns in smaller steps.

**Each layer is timed from its own start** (`startTicks` was per file, so
`X.sit.hqx`'s inner rate included BinHex's time). Read from the code, not
observed.

**Test.** `mac_sink_test --eta` replays through the real function,
natively and on qemu-m68k; the old formula fails 12 of 16 cases. It cannot
see a rate that really changes.

**Price.** Shipped CODE +20, A5 +12 (`.data` padding): 32 B off every
budget; control CODE +20, A5 −20, `OVL_SAVED` −32. No tally change at the
three asserted tiers (74/74, 72/74, 68/74, the same names).

## 2026-10-16 (the empty password) — OK on an empty password field is a wrong password, and a refusal is added under the request

**Found by the maintainer** on the LC 475: OK on an empty field skipped
every encrypted entry — `MacAskPassword` treated it as Cancel.

**Decision (the maintainer's).** An empty OK is an empty password, refused
like any wrong one, the dialog returning with *Incorrect password.*;
Cancel alone declines. CORRECTED the same day: the first version ignored
an empty OK, which looked unresponsive.

**Measured.** `interactive.py --password` presses OK on the empty field
first (*pw-3b-empty-ok*): the refusal appears and every entry decrypts;
the build before fails the walk.

**Wording, the same day (the maintainer's).** Every ask shows *Enter the
password for "X".*; after a refusal *Incorrect password.* is added as its
own item (DITL 132, item 5), so a wrapped name cannot push it off.
Photographed in the same walk.

**Price.** With the first version: CODE +8, A5 −8, 0 B of budget; the final
version is priced with *the folders that lost their icons*.

## 2026-10-16 (the folders that lost their icons) — a folder's Finder flags and dates are set as a file's are, so a custom folder icon survives

**Found by the maintainer**: `NorbikNudleys_Icons.sit` (StuffIt 5)
extracted as plain folders. Each icon is a folder with flag `0x0400` ("has
custom icon") holding an invisible `Icon` + CR; the engine delivered both
(`lsar -t` verifies all 316 entries), but the shell stamped files only.

**Decision.** A folder gets the same `StampCat`: flags (inited cleared) and
creation and modification dates (`HFileInfo` and `DirInfo` share those
offsets; type and creator left alone). Not on a merged folder; the
modification date is then overwritten by writes inside (fixed:
DECISIONS.md 2026-10-17, *the metadata, carried to the disk*).

**Measured.** `run.py --keep-disks`, catalog read with `hfs_peek.py`
(MacMount's): `0x04c0` on the icon folders (the archive's `0x05c0` less
inited) against `0x0000`; System 7.0.1's Finder shows `animals`'s thirty
icons. The top folder stays plain correctly: its 2008 `Icon` holds only an
`icns`.

**Not settled: why StuffIt 5.5 calls the archive damaged.** Both decoders
here agree on every entry; the 2008 top-level icon being the cause is a
hypothesis (no StuffIt 5.5 runs here).

**Price.** CODE +92, A5 +4, shipped and control, with the empty password's
test removed: 96 B off every budget, `TIERS` −96, no tally moves.

## 2026-10-17 (the metadata, carried to the disk) — every Finder field, the backup date, the lock and the Get Info comment travel from engine to disk, and a folder keeps its date

**The brief, the maintainer's:** every file and folder comes back as it
was — whole Finder info, extended Finder info, Get Info comment, three
dates, the lock; a foreign read-only permission becomes locked.

**Decision.** `UncEntryInfo` carries `finder_info[32]` (FInfo/DInfo then
FXInfo/DXInfo, raw, as AppleSingle entry 9 and the catalog hold them),
`backup_date`, `comment`/`comment_len` (valid until `end_entry` returns),
`locked` (0 not stated, 1 no, 2 yes), and a `meta` byte saying which of
the first three the archive stated (zero is a value each can hold). The
shell writes everything stated in `StampCat`: the 32 bytes, backup date,
comment via the Desktop Manager, lock last, files only. First readers:
AppleSingle/AppleDouble (entries 4, 8, 9, 10, 12; RFC 1740) and AppleLink
packages (cited to the translator's `AddItems`); the rest followed
(DECISIONS.md 2026-10-17, *the envelopes' own Finder info*, *the archives'
own Finder info*).

**Two writes are not verbatim.** (Corrected the same day by *the bit that
kept the position*: inited is KEPT unless the file has a bundle, and
fdPutAway, frPutAway and frOpenChain are cleared too.)
- **Finder flag 0x0100 (inited) is cleared.**
- **FXInfo/DXInfo +10, fdComment/frComment, is cleared.** Measured on
  System 3.0's disk (`tools/vmac/hfscat.py --fcmt DeskTop`): it is the id
  of the `FCMT` resource in the Finder's `DeskTop` file (Font/DA Mover's
  0x5389 is `FCMT` 21385; the Finder's 0x6727 is 26407), meaningless on
  another volume. *Hypothesis, not run:* a System 6 Finder would show or
  overwrite the wrong comment. The text travels as `comment`.

**Comments and the one-behaviour rule.** mpack's calls
(`reference/mpack/macfile.c`): `PBDTGetPath`, `PBDTSetComment`,
`PBDTFlush`. Measured (`tools/vmac/metarun.py`):

| volume | PBHGetVolParms | vMAttrib | PBDTGetPath | comment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| System 3.0, 1,440 KB floppy | −50 | — | −50 | not written |
| System 6.0.8, 1,440 KB floppy | −50 | — | −50 | not written |
| System 7.0.1, 1,440 KB floppy | 0 | 0xE0 | −123 | not written |
| System 7.0.1, 8 MB volume | 0 | 0x10E0 (bit 12) | 0 | **read back exact** with `PBDTGetComment` |

`PBDTGetPath` alone refuses every volume without a Desktop Manager, so
mpack's prior `PBHGetVolParms` was dropped (−60 B). **System 6 and earlier
cannot get a comment by the System 7 path**; their Finder's own `Desktop`
file would be a second path, which the rule forbids, so it is **not
written, and nothing says so** (a line some Systems print is itself
per-machine behaviour). **Settled by the maintainer 2026-10-17: a
limitation** (OPEN_ITEMS.md, part 1). A System 7 floppy loses it the same
way.

**A folder's date.** Creating or deleting an item resets its folder's
modification date. A memo per folder was refused (`gDirMemo` 200 rows: a
date each is **+800 B of A5**); `DirMd` reads the date before each create
or delete and restores it after: three catalog calls per item (replaced
the same day by a one-entry cache, *the date held once per folder*, after
+10.6 % and +13.5 % at 1x). Not the destination folder. Measured: the mock
catalog's no-restore control fails; on the emulator `Placed` reads
0xA0000002 after two writes inside.

**End to end** — `tools/vmac/metarun.py`, `synth-as-meta.as` and
`synth-sqp-meta.pkg`, read off the catalog with `tools/vmac/hfscat.py`
(libhfs's layout; *the window StuffIt kept in the name*):

| tier | values as the archive states |
|---|---|
| System 3.0, 4 MB | **18/18** |
| System 6.0.8, 4 MB | **18/18** |
| System 7.0.1, 4 MB, 8 MB output | **17/18**, the comment included |
| control: `main`'s build, System 7.0.1 | 7/17 — the 10 new values all missing, the folder's date the run's own |

**Not settled: System 7.0.1's `fdXFlags`.** FXInfo +9 reads 0x70 where
0x00 was written, on 7.0.1 only, and stays 0x00 with `main`'s build (which
leaves `fdScript` 0). That System 7 rewrites it when `fdScript` (+8) is
0x81 is a hypothesis; `metarun.py` keeps failing on it rather than
tolerating an unexplained byte.

**Two harness facts.** The report reached `in.dsk` only with an eject
first (Mini vMac writes buffered changes on eject; three runs spent). And a
resource fork not shaped like one is masked on the Mac's read-back but not
the host's.

**The CLI** writes none of this to Linux (the `._NAME` sidecar is the raw
resource fork, as `unar -k hidden`); it lists it: `l --meta`, graded by
`tools/run_meta.py` against `lsar` and the synthesizers.

**A cut AppleSingle was called complete**: `run_truncation.py` failed five
cuts of the corpus's first AppleSingle archives (an entry past EOF skipped
as "corrupt"). Such an entry now marks the file cut and ends
`UNC_ERR_TRUNCATED`, what is there still streaming (+60 B CODE, 4 A5 of the
total below; the five cuts exit 0 on the build before).

**Price.** Shipped CODE +820, A5 +12, **832 B off every extraction's
budget on a 1 MB Mac Plus**; lazy CODE +820, A5 −20; control CODE +864, A5
0. `ovl_sqp` +40, `ovl_text` +8, bundle +48. `OVL_SAVED` +32, `TIERS` −864
DERIVED. Stack: `UncEntryInfo` 302 → 346 B, every reader's frame +44,
deepest chain 3,310 → 3,354 B; the shell's chain under `sink_begin` 592 →
636 B (`StampCat` 176 → 208, `DirMd` 156). **The first cut was +1,032 B of
CODE and `StampCat` 476 B of frame.**

## 2026-10-17 (the bit that kept the position) — the archive's inited bit is kept unless the file has a bundle, the source volume's directory IDs are cleared, and a folder's date is priced in time

**The reviewer's hypothesis, confirmed.** Clearing Finder flag 0x0100
(inited) everywhere discarded restored positions. `tools/vmac/finderpos.py`
extracts a package holding a folder `Spread` (a window rectangle), three
files at unusual positions and MacExtract itself, opens the windows, shuts
down and reads the catalog back:

| System, volume | inited | the three files | `Spread`'s window | application's position | bundle registered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7.0.1, blank | cleared | moved to a row: (0,0) (0,64) (0,128) | default place | moved to (0,0) | yes, own icon |
| 7.0.1, blank | kept | **where the archive put them** | **at its rectangle** | kept | yes, own icon |
| 6.0.8, blank | cleared | (folder not opened) | rectangle rewritten | moved to (0,64) | yes |
| 6.0.8, blank | kept | kept | kept | kept | yes |
| 7.0.1, **desktop already there** | kept | kept | kept | kept | **no: generic icon, `MExt` 0 times in `Desktop DB`** |
| 7.0.1, desktop already there | cleared | moved | — | moved | yes, 14 times |
| 6.0.8, desktop already there | kept | kept | kept | kept | yes (`APPL`, `BNDL`, signature) |

Frames `fp-1-volume.png`, `fp-2-spread.png`, `fp-4-volume-app.png`
(regenerated by `finderpos.py`). "Desktop already there" is `--seeded`,
the case of a user's own disk.

**Decision.** Keep inited where the archive stated FInfo whole
(`UNC_META_FINFO`) **and the file has no bundle** (0x2000); otherwise
clear it — on System 7.0.1 a kept-inited application on a user's disk
shows a generic icon until a rebuild. Measured both ways on both seeded
volumes. **Superseded 2026-10-18** (*the icon Expander registers*): inited
is kept on a bundle too, and the shell registers the bundle itself.

**The source volume's directory IDs are cleared**, as fdComment is:
fdPutAway and frPutAway (+12) and frOpenChain (+4) (libhfs `apple.h`); a
file's +4..7, fdUnused, are kept. Not shown harmful by measurement.

**What a folder's date costs** (superseded the same day by *the date held
once per folder*): `-D UNC_AT_TICKGAP`, 1x, System 6.0.8, to a floppy,
repeatable to the tick: **+218 t (3.6 s, +10.6 %)** on
`derived-CursorAnimator.sit` (86 files) and **+106 t (1.8 s, +13.5 %)** on
100 files in one folder; `DirMd` disabled leaves 2–4 t (FORMATS.md, *What
keeping a folder's date costs*). 18–42 ms per file created in a folder.

**Controls** (`mac_sink_test --meta`, one rule reverted each): inited always
cleared, and inited kept on a bundle, fail the FInfo check; only fdComment
cleared fails FXInfo.

**Harness lessons.** `interactive.Mac` gives keyboard focus only at its
first coordinate lookup (the first type-select went to the X root); and
`Mac.shot()` parks the pointer, so a held menu was released off-screen,
Shut Down never happened, and `hfscat.py` refused the torn image.

**Price**, the review's part: CODE +40 everywhere, A5 −8 shipped, +24
control: **864 B off every budget in all**; `OVL_SAVED` 138,608, `TIERS`
−928 in all, derived.

## 2026-10-17 (the date held once per folder) — a folder's date is held in a one-entry cache, three catalog calls per change of folder instead of per item

**The second review refused the per-item hold** (+10.6 % and +13.5 % at
1x). **Decision, the reviewer's:** a one-entry cache (`heldDir`, `heldMd`).
Before a create or delete in folder X (files in `sink_begin`, folders in
`EnsureDir`, a failed entry's delete in `sink_end`), if X is not held the
held folder gets its date back and X's is held (`DirHold`); never the
destination. `RunExtract` restores it when the engine returns
(`DirFlush`), before `ExtractOne`'s layer delete. When `StampCat` stamps
the held folder itself (a zip's folder entry after its files), the held
date becomes the archive's.

**Not only the cache.** `EnsureDir` CREATED every path component first and
read `dupFNErr` as "already there", which would have thrashed the cache;
it now looks up first: one call where two were.

**Measured** (FORMATS.md, *What keeping a folder's date costs*): **2,063 t
and 761 t against `main`'s 2,058 and 779** on the two subjects;
preservation's share 59 t (+2.9 %) and 1 t.

**Shown to survive**, each with a failing control:

| case | mock (`mac_sink_test --dirdates`) | emulator (`metarun.py`, real File Manager) |
|---|---|---|
| A/x, A/B/y, A/z | A and A/B keep theirs | A and A:B read back on 3.0, 6.0.8 and 7.0.1 |
| a folder entry after its files | Z keeps its | not run: no committed writer orders a folder after its files |
| a failed entry's delete | F keeps its | not run |
| control | no restore in `DirFlush`: A, A/B, F wrong; no flush on a switch: A, A/B, F wrong; no held-date update in `StampCat`: Z wrong | preservation disabled: `Placed`, A, A:B read the run's own time |

**Stack.** Two live parameter blocks in `EnsureDir` cost +96 B of
`sink_begin`'s frame; a union put it back to 416 B. The chain under
`sink_begin` is 624 B, +32 over `main`, all `StampCat`.

**Price**: CODE +16, A5 −16 shipped, +12/−12 control: 0 B. **864 B off
every budget in all**, unmoved from *the bit that kept the position*.

**Seen in passing:** the mock sink cannot write
`derived-CursorAnimator.sit`'s two names holding a `/` (not in its lane;
passes on the emulator).

## 2026-10-17 (the window StuffIt kept in the name) — where five formats keep the Finder info, measured against each format's own expander

**Why.** The brief is a file and folder back exactly as they went in; no
reference says where StuffIt classic keeps a position or window, and four
other formats have unassigned bytes. Measurement only; `src/` unchanged.

**Method.** Each format's own expander runs under emulation and every
catalog record it wrote is read back (`tools/vmac/hfscat.py`, libhfs's
`apple.h` offsets, shown able to fail against `hls`). The **corpus** says
what writers put in the bytes; a **sentinel** archive (each unassigned byte
naming its own offset) says which bytes the expander READS, one suspected
gate switched per archive (the first set confounded the version byte with
the name CRC). Tables: FORMATS.md, *Finder info in the archive*; re-run:
`tools/vmac/README.md`, *Finder info, read back*.

**StuffIt classic, Expander 4.0.2 — measured.** 225 corpus archives (1,719
entries), three sentinel boots (21 archives). Every rule agrees with every
entry; `--report --control` (rules without gates and masks) disagrees on
806.

- **The name field is 31 bytes and @34 is its CRC** (CRC-16/ARC over bytes
  2..33; XADMaster's `SITFH_FNAME_CRC` comment had it, the INVENTORY's
  63-byte reading did not). Writers that do not compute it (every
  version-1 archive bar two; StuffIt Deluxe 2.0.1) leave name leftovers
  in @34..65, and **Expander restores position, rectangle, scroll or lock
  only when that CRC holds** — the validity flag is the CRC.
- **Two more gates**: a folder's flags and view need version ≥ 2; the
  0x0986 at @36 gates nothing.
- **Folder scroll is @100..103, h then v**; @104..107 is not restored (being
  frOpenChain is a hypothesis).
- **The lock is bit 15 of @36** (three corpus exceptions, five sentinel
  variants).
- **Expander walks by link**: first child @62 (folder), next @54 (file).
- **Expander never restores** `fdFldr`, `FXInfo`, `DXInfo` past the scroll,
  backup dates or `dirFlags`; **writes garbage as it stands**; gives the
  top folder it creates (−1,−1).

**The other four.**
- **DiskDoubler 3.7 — measured**: writes `fdLocation` at +42, which its
  own Expand does not restore; +82 is a CRC-16/XMODEM over 0..81 (70 of 70)
  that 3.7 enforces; +58..77 zero.
- **Now QuickFiler 5.0.1 — measured**: +38..53 is FInfo/DInfo whole, +62
  the **backup** date (XADMaster says access), +66..81 a folder's `DXInfo`;
  a file's `fdFldr` and `FXInfo` not restored.
- **SuperDisk! — measured, one self-extractor**: file +18..21 is
  `fdLocation`; a folder's 20 bytes are `DInfo` then `frScroll`.
- **StuffIt 5, Expander 5.5 — measured on one archive**: second block
  b+4..19 FInfo/DInfo, b+20..35 FXInfo/DXInfo (INVENTORY hypothesis
  confirmed); b+2 is a block CRC (272 of 272), found after four sentinel
  boots got *"-12043"* — the unmodified control extracting is what kept it
  from being filed as "Expander 5.5 rejects these values". The script byte
  comes back 0x80; two files below the first folder level lost their
  position in both runs, explained only by hypothesis.

**Limits.** One reader per format; comments not measured (Desktop file);
the destination folder's location not attributed; DiskDoubler's
`DDAR`/`DDA2`, SuperDisk!'s other reader and Now Utilities 6.0 not run.

**Consequence.** Every field marked restored has a measured home. A field
NO expander restores (StuffIt classic's `FXInfo`, backup date, `fdFldr`) is
not shown absent from the format — 3.5.1's script path was the next writer
(run: *the window Expander puts back*).

**For readers where a format restores part of `FInfo`**: state all 16
bytes, unrestored parts at what the expander writes, so the shell's inited
rule behaves as Expander. For StuffIt classic, on 1,279 matched corpus
files: `fdFldr` 0 and `FXInfo` zero in all; `fdLocation` (0,0) where no
position is restored (551 of 551); inited kept only where the header has
it AND a position is restored (260 kept, 503 cleared, 516 absent in both).
The one remaining difference was a file with a bundle (43 kept it, 39
applications).

**Two header CRCs the expanders enforce and this engine does not**:
DiskDoubler 3.7's +82 and Expander 5.5's StuffIt 5 b+2; `src/fmt_sit5.c`
also reads neither the first block's @32 nor the archive header's @98.
(Corrected 2026-10-17, *the window Expander puts back*: the DiskDoubler
half is withdrawn — the SNIFFER checks +82; the StuffIt 5 half stands.)

**Cost.** Forty-five boots, 23:59 on 2026-10-16 to 03:49, sharing the
machine; one stall from a wait loop grepping `ps aux` for `minivmac` that
matched another session's shell, now a match on process names
(`tools/vmac/README.md`).

## 2026-10-17 (the envelopes' own Finder info) — MacBinary, AppleSingle, MIME, uuencode and base64 deliver every field their standards hold

**Decision.** Each envelope reader states what its standard keeps, cited
in the reader (FORMATS.md, *The envelopes: what each standard holds*):

- **MacBinary**: one header reader, `unc_macbinary_meta`, shared by
  `fmt_macbinary.c`, ZipIt (`fmt_exo.c`) and MacLHA (`fmt_lzh.c`). FInfo
  whole (65..80, flags' low byte from 101); the lock from 81's
  "Protected" bit and, in MacBinary I, 73's bit 7; III's `fdScript` and
  `fdXFlags` as FXInfo +8/+9; in `fmt_macbinary.c` the Get Info comment
  after the resource fork.
- **AppleSingle's fixed records** (8, 9, 10, 12): one function,
  `unc_as_record`, also used by MIME's applefile part. **RFC 1740's
  unknown date, 0x80000000, is left unknown** (it came out 1931-12-13). A
  16-byte entry 9 states its FInfo.
- **uuencode and base64**: a `begin` mode without owner write (0200) is
  locked, with it unlocked — **not in a UUTool document**, whose mode is a
  preference (0700 everywhere, "ignored on the Mac side"); UUTool's
  `.finfo` stated whole.
- **BinHex 4 and before** hold name, type, creator and flags only: no
  change.

**Choices, recorded.**
- **II does not read 73's bit 7 as a lock**: under System 7 a II header
  carries isAlias there (ZipIt 2.2.2's alias, III, 73 = 0x80).
- **The standards tell a downloader to zero `fdLocation` and `fdFldr` and
  clear inited** (macbinary_ii.txt); delivered as held, by the brief.
- **An unreadable comment is dropped, not an error** (`unar`, which grades
  cut files, reads none).

**Not done.** The comment of a MacBinary payload inside ZipIt or MacLHA
(it follows both forks in a compressed stream; needs a second decode or a
comment arriving by `end_entry`); none of 14 readable ZipIt payloads has
one. OPEN_ITEMS.md's. AppleSingle entry 11 (ProDOS access): no reference
states its bits.

**Evidence** (TESTING.md, *The Finder metadata*): `tools/run_meta.py` holds
generated cases (`tools/synth_envelopes.py`) to deark, macunpack, hexbin,
Python's `email` and `lsar`, and sweeps corpus and specimens: **507 fields
of 255 entries** against a second reader (`fractionalwidths.sit` the one
real Protected bit; ZipIt 2.2.2 the real III payloads). Against
`origin/main`'s CLI it fails 522 times. `tests/unit_formats.c`: reverting
the comment read, the MacBinary I lock or the unknown-date rule fails 3
checks each. **Not on the emulator**: the shell's write path is
AppleSingle's, unchanged.

**Price** (shipped/eager): **CODE +464, A5 +16 — 480 B off every
extraction's budget**; lazy +460/+36; control +744/−8. New
`unc_macbinary_meta` 234, `unc_as_record` 290; `unc_macbinary_extract`
+126; `unc_appledouble_extract` −230. `ovl_text` **+404**, `ovl_exo` −36,
`ovl_lzh` −10, bundle +356: a MIME/uu/base64 grant falls 884 B, a zip's 444,
an LZH's 470, others 480. `OVL_SAVED` 138,608 → 138,864, `TIERS` −736,
DERIVED; no tally moves (no tier re-run). Deepest chain, 3,354 B through
DiskDoubler, unmoved.

**At the merge, 2026-10-17 (the reviewer's).** A MacBinary I header's bit 7
of 73 is masked out of the written flags as well as read as the lock (left
in, System 7 made a locked file a broken alias); II and III unchanged; a
unit check holds it. Shipped 0 B; control +32, `OVL_SAVED` +32, `TIERS`
−32. FORMATS.md's grants table re-taken from `run_tiers.gain()`.
fdLocation/fdFldr delivered as held; the ZipIt/MacLHA comment stays in
OPEN_ITEMS.md.
## 2026-10-17 (the window Expander puts back) — StuffIt classic states exactly what Expander 4.0.2 restores, DiskDoubler restores the location its own Expand drops, and its header CRC was already checked

**Decision.** `src/fmt_sit.c`'s `sit_finder` implements FORMATS.md's
*StuffIt classic, read by StuffIt Expander 4.0.2* table row for row, gates,
masks and garbage included: the whole FInfo/DInfo (and a folder's DXInfo)
with unrestored parts at what Expander writes, and the lock, under the
name CRC, as the tri-state; a folder's `finder_flags` are 0 under version
1. `src/fmt_dd.c` states a single-file 84-byte header's FInfo whole
(+32..47, `fdLocation` at +42, `fdFldr` 0).

**DiskDoubler's location is restored although 3.7's Expand drops it**: the
brief is the file before compression, and 3.7 copied it from that file's
catalog record (`ddmeta.py --writer`); the engine's FInfo equals the
subject's pre-compression record, all 16 bytes (`run_meta.py`). Four
headers holding (−1,−1) with inited are restored as they stand. The 1990
48-byte header: not measured.

**DiskDoubler's header CRC: no change, earlier claim withdrawn.** The
sniffer (`unc_diskdoubler_probe`, from macutils and XADMaster) refuses a
nonzero mismatching +82 as "format not recognized" (measured, one flipped
byte), accepting XADMaster's "really old files have 0000", which 3.7 would
refuse. Every 84-byte header in reach has a valid nonzero CRC (69 in
`fixtures/`, 33 specimens, 70 of 70 of 3.7's); dropping the exception would
be a guess against the only source naming it (BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn
claims*).

**StuffIt Deluxe 3.5.1, the next writer, measured** (`sitmeta.py
--writer351`): version 2 WITH the name CRC; lock bit 15 of @36; `fdLocation`
@62, `fdFlags` @74, `frRect` @38, `frFlags` @74, `frView` @68, a nested
folder's `frLocation` @70 and **(−1,−1) at @70 for the top folder**; no
`frScroll`; the planted `FXInfo`, extended `DXInfo` and backup dates in no
byte. So neither classic writer stores what no expander restores
(`fdFldr` not planted). Nothing implemented from it.

**Evidence.**
- `tools/run_meta.py --expander` (in `ci.sh`): `l --meta` against Expander's
  catalog records, 241 archives (225 corpus, 16 sentinel), **6,627 fields,

  17 sentinel): **496 catalog values read back, all as Expander wrote
  them**, 24/24 forks PASS; `origin/main`'s application 112 wrong.
- The one allowed difference (inited cleared on a bundle) is gone since

**The flags the shell writes are the stated ones.** Giving `finder_flags`

is stated (`mac_sink_test --meta`'s `Doc`: raw 0x0101, stated 0x0100).

## 2026-10-17 (the archives' own Finder info) — PackIt, StuffIt 5, Now Compress, SuperDisk!, Private File, ArcMac and ARC, zip, tar, gzip and LZH deliver the Finder info, dates, lock and comment they hold

**The brief, the maintainer's** (*the metadata, carried to the disk*); this
entry is the archive formats' readers (envelopes: *the envelopes' own
Finder info*). Offsets are cited in each reader; tables are FORMATS.md's.

**What each reader now states** — measured where the cell says so, read
from a document otherwise:

| format | fields | from |
|---|---|---|
| PackIt | lock (word @74 non-zero) | the format's own appendix C; graded against macunpack |
| StuffIt 5 | per-entry comment; the archive comment (bit 5); FInfo/DInfo b+4..19 and FXInfo/DXInfo b+20..35, entry version 1 only, folder frFlags less 0x0001 | measured against Expander 5.5 (*the window StuffIt kept in the name*); the comment's place measured on three archives |
| Now Compress | FInfo/DInfo +38..53, backup date +62, FXInfo/DXInfo +66..81 | measured against QuickFiler 5.0.1 |
| SuperDisk! | a file's fdLocation +18..21 (fdFldr stated 0); a folder's DInfo, less 0x0001, and frScroll | measured against its self-extractor |
| Private File | FInfo @260, FXInfo @276 | PF Encrypt's `MakeFileInfo` |
| ArcMac / ARC | the whole FInfo at 34..49; the MS-DOS date (both) | ARCMAC.DOC; deark for ARC's |
| zip | `0x334d` whole: FInfo/DInfo, FXInfo/DXInfo, backup date, Finder comment; the per-file comment; the lock from the external attributes; the MS-DOS date where no Macintosh field gives one | Info-ZIP's Macintosh UnZip (`DecodeMac3ExtraField`, `mapattr`), unix/unix.c `mapattr`, APPNOTE.TXT |
| tar | lock (mode 00200), mtime, a pax `x` header's mtime and comment | POSIX ustar and pax |
| gzip | MTIME, FCOMMENT | RFC 1952 |
| LZH | the base header's time and attribute byte; 0x3f comment, 0x40 MS-DOS attributes, 0x41 Windows times, 0x50 mode, 0x54 mtime; level 0's Unix area | header.doc, LHa for UNIX's `get_header`, lhasa |

**The time zone rule — the maintainer's to confirm.** An MS-DOS date (zip,
ARC, LZH levels 0 and 1) is a zoneless wall clock, like a Macintosh date,
and is carried unchanged. A Unix time or FILETIME (tar, pax, gzip, LZH 2
and 3, 0x54, 0x41) is an instant, made the Macintosh date whose wall clock
reads it in UTC (`src/unc_date.h`). Measured: MacLHA 2.24's level 2
headers hold a Unix time exactly 3,600 s before the MacBinary date in the
same entry (a Mac an hour east of UTC); lhasa's test outputs give level
0/1 dates an hour east of `lsar`'s (its `mktime` in its author's zone).
`0x334d`'s three dates stay local. (Superseded: DECISIONS.md 2026-10-17,
*dates in the Macintosh's own zone*.)

**StuffIt 5's second-block CRC at b+2.** CRC-16/ARC of the block with its
word zeroed holds on **587 of 587 entries of the 53 Aladdin-written StuffIt
5 archives here** (measured 2026-10-17); the five failures are
`synth-sit14.sit`'s, from a synthesizer. **Decision:** the block's
FInfo/FXInfo is stated only where it holds; type, creator, flags and forks
as before. Refusing the entry (Expander's answer) would lose verifying
forks on a metadata-only word, with no Aladdin entry in reach failing it.
`am-sit5-badcrc` in `tools/run_meta.py`; the gate removed fails 20 fields.
**The first block's @32 and the archive header's @98 are still not read.**

**Now Compress: a file's FXInfo is stated though Dearchive does not restore
it** — the goal is the file as archived. That +66..81 is a file's FXInfo
is a hypothesis (layout, and one specimen,
`derived-Expand_Now_1.0.1.sea`: fdPutAway 2, the rest zero); the shell
clears fdPutAway and fdComment anyway.

**Zip host 7 means the MS-DOS byte.** `rexnebular_1_0_0.zip`'s 22 entries
are host 7 with a Unix mode high and the read-only bit low (0x81240001,
0x81b60000); both Info-ZIP UnZips read host 7 by the low byte and MacZip
calls `FSpSetFLock` from it. Unix-mode hosts are Info-ZIP's list (3, 2, 5,
12, 13, 16, 17, 18, 30), falling back to the low byte when the high half is
0. Amiga's bits not read.

**Two rules no reference gives, labelled.** A `0x334d` date within a day of
the wrap is "never" (rexnebular's backup fields read 0 or 0xFFFFAB9F,
−21,601 s, beside BkGMTOffs −18,000 — hypothesis: 0 moved by a zone).
ZipIt's `0x2805` View word is NOT stated (one specimen, value 0, no
document; OPEN_ITEMS.md).

**Comments travel as the archive's bytes** (zip CP437, gzip Latin-1, pax
UTF-8, not converted, as names are not), at most UNC_ENTRY_COMMENT_MAX
(255), buffer allocated on first use.

**Tar left `ovl_exo`.** That image was 32,124 B, 640 B short of a 68000
`-mpcrel` image's ±32 KB, and the metadata came to ~1.9 KB: the link failed
(R_68K_PC16 truncated). Tar calls nothing there, so its reader moved into
`src/fmt_tar.c` and `ovl_zipold` (`OVL_TAR_EXTRACT`). A bare tar's grant
RISES by 26,886 B (it keeps the 5,238 B `ovl_zipold`, not the 32,124 B
`ovl_exo`); a zip pays tar's 2,580 B.

**Graded** (`tools/run_meta.py`, TESTING.md): generated cases per format
(`tools/synth_archmeta.py`), the sentinel archives, macunpack for PackIt,
Info-ZIP's Mac UnZip for rexnebular, the corpus against `lsar` in UTC and
lhasa's header dumps for LZH: 228 generated fields, 655 corpus fields, 0
disagreeing. Where the oracles part, lhasa is followed (XADMaster ignores
level 0's Unix area, prints years past 22700 for 0x41, takes an OS/2 0xff
header's mtime). Controls: 228 tampered rows caught; seven engine rules
undone each fail. `run_diff.py` 974/974.

**Price** (against `origin/main` 6cd0e47): **shipped (eager) and lazy CODE
+0, A5 +0 — 0 B off any budget for the application**; control CODE +4,520,
A5 +72. Images: `ovl_zipold` +2,580 (tar), `ovl_lzh` +1,626, `ovl_stuffit`

**Shipped lanes: no extraction lost**; the resident control's sys6-512K

## 2026-10-17 (the sidecars Mac OS X left beside the file) — a zip's `__MACOSX/…/._name` and a tar's `._name` are put back on their file: resource fork, Finder info, comment, dates and lock

**The problem.** Mac OS X writes a resource fork and Finder info an archive
cannot hold into an AppleDouble `._` + name (reference/notes/copyfile.c,
`copyfile_pack`): the Finder's Compress as `__MACOSX/dir/._name`, bsdtar
inline as the member before
(reference/notes/libarchive_write_set_format_pax.c). Both came out as
files. **No such zip or tar was in the corpus** (measured over `fixtures/`,
`~/.cache/macextract` and `/tmp`).

**Specimens.** One paced Discmaster search gave `Aqua_Candy_Two.zip` (a 2006
Macworld UK disc, Mac OS X 10.4's Finder): 190 files, each with a sidecar,
data forks empty. Finder order: `dir/name`, any unwritten `__MACOSX/…`
folder records, then `__MACOSX/dir/._name` (16 of 190 not adjacent unless
those records are skipped); entries 9 at 50 and 2 at 82. Second:
libarchive's `libarchive-zip-mac-metadata.zip` (ditto, `0x5855`, an ACL,
no Finder info). A third, a 2024 `.dsk.zip` (100 MB), read and not kept:
only `com.apple.macl`/`com.apple.provenance` and 32 zero bytes of Finder
info (XADAppleDouble.m's "only if it is not empty" case).
`tools/synth_macosx.py` writes the rest with Info-ZIP and GNU tar, values
known by construction, including an `-edge` pair (a far sidecar, one naming
nothing, a non-AppleDouble `._` file).

**Decision: a sidecar pairs with the file it names, wherever the directory
puts either.** Names by XADMaster's rule (XADMacArchiveParser.m), sidecar
validity by XADAppleDouble.m's (magic, version 2, entry 2 or 9) plus a
resource fork that fits. Folders under `__MACOSX` are never emitted. A
file's sidecar is the first naming it after it, going round the directory;
a sidecar is taken only if the file's own search finds it, so both answer
alike in either order, and a second sidecar for one file comes out as
itself. A sidecar that pairs with nothing, is not AppleDouble or is
encrypted comes out as itself — **never lost**. A 1,024-bit filter over
the leaves clears unnamed files in one test; the last file is tried first
(Finder order); sidecars all at one end cost a walk per pair. Neither
oracle is followed: XADMaster pairs only neighbours (so `unar` leaves a far
one as an entry); libarchive pairs anywhere but LOSES a sidecar whose file
is absent (`tree_rsrc` read only by lookup). **An adjacency-only version
was built and measured**: 2,262 B against 2,400 — 138 B for every zip whose
sidecars are not adjacent. Kept.

**What the sidecar gives its file**: entries 2, 4, 8, 9, 10 and 12 via
`unc_as_record` (RFC 1740) — resource fork, FInfo/FXInfo (DInfo/DXInfo)
whole, comment, three dates, lock. The first 1,024 bytes are kept
(`UNC_AD_WIN`) and entries inside them read; forks are spans. A zip sidecar
is decoded twice: to the window before its file is offered (the
`zip_mb_peek` pattern, uncounted), and for the fork after the file's data
fork, CRC-32 checked — a failing sidecar fails its file. A tar sidecar is
read in place.

**Not read.** Extended attributes after the Finder info, among them the
Spotlight comment `com.apple.metadata:kMDItemFinderComment` (a bplist;
done 2026-10-18, *the comment Spotlight kept*). The lock as `UF_IMMUTABLE`,
which copyfile does not pack.

**Tar.** bsdtar writes `._name` before `name`; libarchive reads it only
there (`read_mac_metadata_blob`). Here the next member must be the named
file; one AFTER is not paired. Up to two pax headers between are stepped
over, and a sidecar's own pax values are dropped with it (UNEXERCISED: no
case has one). The sidecar code is in `ovl_zipold` beside tar; zip's half
stays in `ovl_exo`.

**Evidence** — each check shown able to fail:
- `tools/run_meta.py` (*the Mac OS X sidecars*): the synthetic archives,
  and every zip with a sidecar against libarchive via ctypes (`zip:mac-ext`);
  no sidecar or `__MACOSX` folder listed; `-edge` forks byte for byte.
  `unc_ad_apply` disabled fails 417 fields (380 on Aqua Candy); pairing
  disabled fails 15 "listed, and must not be".
- `tools/run_diff.py`: `Aqua_Candy_Two.zip`, `synth-macosx.zip` and
  `synth-macosx.tar` against `unar`; `make_manifests.py` learnt a `._dir`
  beside a folder is the folder's. The `-edge` pair is ungradable by
  `unar` manifests.
- `tests/unit_formats.c` (`test_sidecar`), fed a byte at a time and whole.
- emulated (`tools/vmac/metarun.py` with `synth-macosx.zip`): **byte-exact
  both forks on System 3.0, 6.0.8 and 7.0.1** (4 files, 3 resource forks),
  **41 values per tier, all exact on 3.0 and 6.0.8**; Meta's comment read
  back on 7.0.1's 8 MB volume. On 7.0.1 two values wrong, the known
  FXInfo byte (OPEN_ITEMS.md, *System 7.0.1 rewrites one byte of FXInfo*):
  Meta has `fdScript` 0 and still got `fdXFlags` 0x70, Doc did not. **The
  `fdScript` 0x81 hypothesis is withdrawn**; Meta and `Kept Whole` share a
  lock and a comment (hypothesis, not separated). After the rebase onto
  188377b, System 6.0.8 again: 4/4, 41 exact.

**Two grades the specimens met.** The Finder's zip is the corpus's first
with Info-ZIP Unix times (`0x5855`; `0x5455` elsewhere): `lsar` reports the
UTC instant, the engine the MS-DOS wall clock (190 entries an hour and up
to a second apart). Neither grades the other, so such mtimes are left out
of that sweep by condition (`zip_unix_times`). **Whether to take the Unix
time instead is the maintainer's call.** Sidecar-stated fields (8, 10, 12),
which `lsar` does not read, are graded by the sidecar lane
(`sidecar_stated`).

**Harness fact.** `run_segments.py`'s un-buffered zip walk budgets one byte
under the run's peak; `unc_side_zip_open` allocating and freeing before it
knew of a sidecar moved every zip's peak. It now walks the directory once
without allocating.

**Price** (against `main` at 188377b):
- **shipped (eager) `CODE` +0, A5 +32, so 32 B off every extraction's
  budget** (nine host-vector slots); lazy the same; control `CODE` +4,084,
  A5 +12. `OVL_SAVED` +4,064, `TIERS` −4,096, derived.
- **Images**: `ovl_zipold` +3,374 (5,238 → 8,612), `ovl_exo` +972 (31,736 →
  32,708, **60 B under the 32 KB** its PC-relative references reach),
  bundle +4,344, download 240,000 → 244,608 B. A zip's grant **−4,346 B**,
  a tar's **−3,374 B**. `unc_sidecar.c` 2,458 B new; `fmt_exo.c` +774;
  `fmt_tar.c` +798.
- **Heap**: 1,318 B (`UncSideZip`) only for a zip that names a sidecar,
  1,816 B (`TarSide`) only for such a tar; nothing otherwise.
- **Stack**: `zip_side` 184 B against `zip_imp_dry`'s 180 below

- **Extractions lost**: none — shipped 74/74, 72/74, 68/74 and resident

## 2026-10-17 (dates in the Macintosh's own zone) — the engine marks which dates are instants, and the application writes those in the Mac's zone where it can say what that is

**The maintainer's decision, 2026-10-17, an explicit exception to one
behaviour on every System.** An instant is shown in the Macintosh's LOCAL
time when it can say what its zone is, in UTC only when it cannot — so on
System 3.0 (no Gestalt) an instant stays UTC, and from System 6.0.8 with a
zone set it does not; decided, not drift. It supersedes *the archives' own
Finder info*'s time-zone rule for instants only; wall clocks are carried
unchanged.

**The engine, zone-free.** Three `UncEntryInfo.meta` bits,
`UNC_META_CR_UTC`, `_MD_UTC`, `_BK_UTC` (include/macextract.h): set, an
instant written as the Mac date reading it in UTC; clear, a wall clock; 0
is "not stated". Set by tar's ustar and pax mtime; gzip's MTIME; LZH level
2/3 base time, 0x54, 0x41 and level 0's Unix area; AppleSingle/AppleDouble
entry 8 (GMT by RFC 1740, so MIME's `multipart/appledouble` too); zip
`0x334d` where its GMT offsets are present. A MacBinary payload's dates
(MacLHA, ZipIt) replace the container's and clear its mark. MS-DOS and
Macintosh dates are never marked. `l --meta` prints `Z`.

**`0x334d`'s dates CHANGE.** Taken unadjusted the day before; but each
offset is "local … time - UTC" (reference/notes/zip_extrafld_infozip.txt),
so local − offset is the instant, as deark's `ef_infozipmac` and Info-ZIP's
Mac UnZip (unzip60 `mactime.c`, `AdjustForTZmoveMac`) compute; XADMaster
adds it and is the outlier. With offsets, local − offset, marked; without
(flag bit 4), the stored wall clock. All 22 of `rexnebular_1_0_0.zip`'s
entries now state dates 18,000 s later in UTC (offsets −18,000); a Mac in
the same zone would get back what MacZip stored (derived, not run).
BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn claims*.

**AppleSingle: the RFC is followed, its commonest Mac writer is not — the
maintainer's to decide.** mpack's `macfile.c` writes entry 8 as the Mac's
wall clock plus the epoch (`dates.create = fpb->ioFlCrDat + CONVERT_TIME`),
so an mpack AppleDouble lands shifted on a zone-set Mac; a netatalk or Unix
one is GMT. Nothing in the record says which; guessing the writer was not
taken.

**The shell (mac/macextract_mac.c, `ZoneProbe`, `ZoneShift`).** Once per
launch, at the first marked date, mpack's method (`macmpack.c`,
`rfc822_date`), each step guarded and cited: ROM85 > 0; Gestalt
implemented (mpack's `TrapAvailable`, `macninit.c`, with Multiverse's
`GetOSTrapAddress`/`GetToolTrapAddress` inlines); `Gestalt('scri')` as
Universal Interfaces 3.4's inline (`0xA1AD, 0x2288`), noErr and **at least
200, decimal, as mpack compares it** — the brief said 0x200, which no source
in reach gives; `ReadLocation` as UI 3.4's inline (`0x203C 0x000C 0x00E4
0xA051`). gmtDelta is the low 3 bytes at offset 9, sign-extended from bit
23 (Inside Macintosh: Operating System Utilities, *The Geographic Location
Record*, Listing 4-9). The offset is added to every marked date in
`sink_begin`, before StampCat and a folder's held date; out of range, or 0,
stays UTC.

**"Never set" against "set to GMT"**: all twelve bytes zero is unknown
("If the geographic location record has never been set, all fields
contain 0"); both give offset 0, so nothing written differs.

**Daylight saving: gmtDelta whole, dlsDelta not added — hypothesis.** Inside
Macintosh does not say whether gmtDelta includes it; mpack (−4 h with
dlsDelta bit 7 is "EDT"), MacZip (gmtDelta alone) and Mini vMac's disabled
X11 code (`tm_gmtoff`) say it does, none Apple's. Settling it needs the Map
control panel's DST box toggled once (OPEN_ITEMS.md). Only today's offset
is known: a July date extracted in January is an hour out.

**The emulator, and the claim it corrected.** "Mini vMac keeps PRAM in its
own file" is not true of this build: `RTC_Init` (src/RTCEMDEV.c) zeroes
PRAM every launch and writes `CurMacLatitude`, `CurMacLongitude`,
`CurMacDelta` to 0xE4, 0xE8, 0xEC — the 12 bytes ReadLocation reads — 0 on
X11 (`#if 0 && AutoTimeZone`). So the zone is a build: `mv-4M-tz`
(tools/vmac/setup.sh), 5 h west, with a location.

**Measured** (`tools/vmac/tzrun.py`, `synth-exo-tar.tar`, six Unix mtimes,
`hfscat.py`): **System 7.0.1 with the zone, every date −18,000 s; System
7.0.1 without, every date as the engine states it (UTC); System 6.0.8 with
the zone, −18,000 s; System 3.0 with the zone, UTC.** The brief expected UTC
on 6.0.8; "local when possible" is what the measurement makes it (the
Script Manager version was not read out). `derived-MUSFMT10.ZIP`'s 29 MS-DOS
dates on 7.0.1 with the zone: none moved. Each disk graded against the
other shift fails 6 of 6. Re-run on 7.0.1 after the rebase onto 40a5f7f
and Implode's move: unchanged, and `synth-exo-zip-implode.zip` and
`derived-MUSFMT10.ZIP` byte-exact.

**Tests.** `mac_sink_test --zone` (folder held across a write, mixed marks,
−5 h, +1 h and none; two controls fail). `run_meta.py` grades the mark
wherever it grades a date (generated layouts; `rexnebular` recomputed from
`0x334d`; MacLHA's payload unmarked; corpus marks from each format's
document, LZH level 0/1 from a walk of the extension headers,
`lzh_instants`): 119 marked and 245 wall-clock dates graded, 3 ungraded, on
2026-10-17. Controls: 69 of 343 toggle a mark alone, all caught; five
scratch engines each fail (tar 40, AppleSingle 3, `0x334d` 48, LZH 33,
MacBinary clear 3). **`run_diff.py` never compares a date, so cannot see
this change.**

**`ovl_exo` was full, and Implode left it.** On 40a5f7f `ovl_exo` was 32,708
B, 60 under the 32,768 its 16-bit PC-relative references span, and this
branch's +164 did not link ("relocation truncated to fit: R_68K_PC16
against g_ovl_fns"). Implode moved, unchanged but its signature, into
`src/unc_implode.c` and `ovl_zipold`. Priced (measured where built, else
arithmetic from `run_tiers.gain()`):

| option | `ovl_exo` headroom | CODE / A5 | grants | stack | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Implode → `ovl_zipold`** (built) | **1,484 B** | 0 / +4 (one vector slot) | zip −76, tar −1,664, envelopes −76, every other format 0 | +0: the forward is a tail `jmp` (disassembled) | **taken** |
| Unix compress → a new seventeenth image | ~380 B | ~0 / +4, and a 12 B directory entry | zip +482, tar 0, envelopes −12 | +0 | no: little headroom, and "sixteen images" is stated in a dozen places, CLAUDE.md among them |
| gzip and compress out of `ovl_exo` | ~1.3 KB and more, not built | — | zip +1.3 KB | — | no: gzip needs zlib's inflate, which zip needs too, and no image yet calls into `ovl_exo` |
| 0x334d/ZipIt reading → `ovl_zipold` | not measured | — | as Implode | — | no: it inflates the record, the same call back into `ovl_exo` |
| Implode → `ovl_codecs` | 1,588 B | 0 / +4 | every format but tar −1.6 KB | +0 | no: every format keeps that image |

Headroom after it: `ovl_exo` 31,284 B (1,484 under 32,768), `ovl_zipold`

**Price** (against `origin/main` 40a5f7f): shipped (eager) **CODE +356, A5

`ZoneMove`, three calls; `unc_macbinary_meta` +22; `unc_as_record` +16);

## 2026-10-18 (the comment Spotlight kept) — a Mac OS X sidecar's Spotlight comment becomes the file's Get Info comment, as UTF-8 that the shell folds into MacRoman

**The maintainer's call, 2026-10-18: support it.** On Mac OS X 10.5+ the
comment is `com.apple.metadata:kMDItemFinderComment`, a binary property
list, packed by copyfile into entry 9 after the 32 bytes of Finder info.
`src/unc_sidecar.c` (`side_spot`, from `unc_ad_apply`) walks that attribute
block, finds the attribute by name, and keeps the list's top object if it
is a string. Sources: reference/notes/copyfile.c (`attr_header_t`,
`attr_entry_t`, `ATTR_ENTRY_LENGTH`) as XADAppleDouble.m reads it; CF-1153.18
(reference/notes/CFBinaryPList.c, CF_ForFoundationOnly.h): every check of
`__CFBinaryPlistGetTopLevelInfo`, then the `0x5n` ASCII and `0x6n` UTF-16
cases with inline or `0x1n` counts. Refused — the comment unstated, the
file not failed: other top objects, a value over 32 bits or integer wider
than 4 bytes, an ASCII string with a byte over 0x7F, a lone surrogate (both
refused by plistlib too), a list not wholly in the window.

**The encoding.** Names: the engine converts nothing (`name_utf8`), the
shell folds into MacRoman (`Utf8ToMacRoman`); tar's pax `comment`, UTF-8 by
POSIX (reference/notes/posix_ustar.txt), reached the Desktop Manager raw.
So: the engine makes UTF-8 and marks the comment **`UNC_META_CMT_UTF8`**
(0x40, a free `meta` bit, so `UncEntryInfo` does not grow); the shell folds
a marked comment, '_' for missing characters. The pax comment is marked
too, its 255-byte cut backing off a continuation byte. The fold is **in the
engine's buffer** (macextract.h lets a host shorten a marked comment in
place until `end_entry`; `Utf8ToMacRoman` no longer writes a NUL past its
length); the shell's own buffer would be 256 B of stack or A5. `l --meta`
prints `U`.

**Which comment wins.** XADMaster takes Spotlight's "if there is not
already a comment" (reference/XADMaster/XADArchiveParser.m), and so does
this: entry 4, a zip per-file comment, a `0x334d` comment and a pax
`comment` win. XADMaster does not read entry 4, so on a sidecar with both
`lsar` reports Spotlight's — this engine's difference on purpose (entry 4
is the classic Get Info comment).

**Decoded in the 1,024-byte window** (`UNC_AD_WIN`), unread after the apply:
UTF-16 moved to the end, UTF-8 written from entry 9 + 34; an overtaking
write refuses the comment (no writer's layout can for a 255-byte result).
**Heap +0.** A list ending past byte 1,024 is dropped — about 800 ASCII or
400 UTF-16 characters when alone (arithmetic, not measured); hypothesis:
real comments are far shorter.

**What System 7.0.1 keeps.** A 255-byte comment reads back as its first
**199 bytes** through `PBDTGetComment` asked for 255 (measured 2026-10-18
with a digit at byte 200; a space there could not tell cut from trim) —
the Desktop Manager's, true before this change; `metarun.py` expects it.
Six commented, unlocked files kept `fdXFlags` 0x00 on 7.0.1, so the comment
alone does not make 0x70 (OPEN_ITEMS.md, *System 7.0.1 rewrites one byte of
FXInfo*).

**Specimens.** `tools/synth_macosx.py --kind zip-spot` and `tar-spot`
(copyfile's layout, plistlib writing as CF does): ASCII between two
attributes, UTF-16 with é, ü, ©, à and characters MacRoman lacks (CJK, an
emoji pair, €, ≠), 300 ASCII and 130 é (cut at 255 and 254), 900 past the
window, an array, a number, a cut list, a high byte, a lone surrogate, one
with entry 4, a folder's. **No real archive with one was found** in six
Discmaster requests (four 2006–2014 Finder zips carry `TextEncoding`,
`quarantine`, `xcode.*`).

**Graded by.** `tools/run_meta.py`: the generator's values; libarchive's
pairing of every sidecar zip and the `-spot` tar, the blob walked by a
second attribute reader (XADAppleDouble.m's reading) and plistlib; `lsar`
on each case alone in a zip (it stops at the first unparsable list): 9
compared, 1 (`LongU`) listed nothing. Controls: `side_spot` not called 28
failures, mark not set 17, cut not on a character 4. `tests/mac_sink_test.c
--meta` (fold removed: fails). Mini vMac, 7.0.1, 8 MB volume
(`synth-macosx-spot.zip`): every comment read back, 91 values, the two
wrong being the `fdXFlags` item.

**Price** (against `origin/main` e5959ca): shipped **CODE +80, A5 +16 — 96 B
off every extraction's budget** (`Utf8ToMacRoman`, called twice, no longer
inlined; always_inline measured +256; the 16 B of A5 are `.data` head
zeros, lazy moved −20, hypothesis: layout). Lazy +84/−20; control
+1,344/+48. `ovl_zipold` +1,324 to 11,608 B; `ovl_exo` unchanged (31,284);
bundle +1,324. `OVL_SAVED` 148,240 → 149,536, `TIERS_CONTROL` 224,496 →
225,888, `TIERS` −1,392, DERIVED; a grant falls 96 B, a tar's, zip's and
envelope's 1,420. Heap +0. `unc_ad_apply` 56 → 80 B, off every decode
chain; `sink_begin` 416 → 420 B; deepest chain unmoved.

**`tools/run_only.py` moved.** Its every-Nth sweep landed on
`uu-wild-terrainman.uu`, a cut uuencode whose `.sit` the CLI keeps by
design when its inner layer fails; the sweep read that as written outside
the selection (same with `origin/main`'s CLI). The kept layer is now
allowed when the full run kept it and reported a failure.

**Left for the maintainer.** (1) The Desktop Manager's 199 bytes against
the engine's 255. (2) Line endings: presumably LF (hypothesis), not
converted to CR. (3) A standalone `._name` read as AppleDouble
(`fmt_applesingle.c`) does not read the Spotlight comment. (4) A list past
the window.

## 2026-10-18 (the comment the root kept) — a Get Info comment reached the disk only at a volume's root; Find… opens where the parts are; the progress line no longer flickers

**Found by the maintainer** on the LC 475: extracted into a folder,

reaches `StampCat` with directory 0 and `SFPutFile`'s working directory;

anywhere); it now reports the output folder's ID and refuses 0, and the old
line fails `meta [drop none]` (0x10).

part found (`SFSaveDisk`, `CurDirStore` after `PBGetWDInfo`), not the
destination; remembering `SFGetFile`'s folder would be smaller but wrong
for a dropped archive.

**The progress line flickered twice over**: it redrew an unchanged *"about
3 minutes"* every second (now compares the estimate as shown); and
`SetDialogItemText` erases before drawing. It is now drawn over the old
one in `srcCopy`, erasing only what lies right of it; the baseline (item
top plus ascent) was checked by eye on the LC.

**Measured.** Shipped CODE +228, A5 −4 (Find… 108, the line 64): 224 B off
every budget; `TIERS` −224. Find… and the line are seen by no harness; the
