## 2026-10-18 (the icon Expander registers) — an application keeps its inited bit and its position, as StuffIt Expander keeps them, and the shell registers its bundle in the Desktop Database as Expander does

**Why.** *The bit that kept the position* cleared inited on a file with a
bundle, so the Finder placed it. On the LC 475 (7.6.1) and iMac (9.2.2),
Expander 4.0.2 keeps `Ascii Converter FAT`'s flags 0x2100 and its position
and shows its icon; MacExtract's copy moved. The maintainer: the position
is critical. Open question: did those desktops already know the creator?

**Measured, with a creator no desktop here has seen** (`finderpos.py
--seeded --creator zQx7`; Mac OS 9.2 through a one-off driver over
`os9.py`):

| System, volume | inited kept, not registered | Finder actions after | inited kept, registered |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7.0.1, 8 MB, a Desktop DB | **generic icon**, `zQx7` 0 times in `Desktop DB` | launched and quit: still generic, still 0; desktop rebuilt (Command-Option): 14 times | **own icon at (30, 300)**, 14 times; nothing moved |
| 9.2, 32 MB, a Desktop DB | **generic icon** | launched and quit: still generic | **own icon at (30, 300)** |
| 6.0.8, 8 MB, a Desktop file | — (no Desktop Manager) | — | own icon, kept; the Finder put `APPL`, `BNDL` and `zQx7` in `Desktop` itself |
| 7.0.1, 1,440K floppy, a Desktop file | **generic icon**, `zQx7` in no resource of `Desktop` | — | — (no Desktop Manager: nothing to register with) |

Expander 4.0.2 itself on 7.0.1, `Ascii Converter.sit` (`ASci`, never seen
here), read before any Finder ran: onto the boot volume `ASci` 0 → **10
times in `Desktop DB`, written by Expander**, own icon at (0, 33), flags
0x2100; onto a seeded floppy, a **generic icon**, position kept. The real
Macs' result was Expander's registration.

**What Expander does** (its engine, `SEng` 1, 0xd48 on, disassembled):
`PBHGetVolParms` (stop without `bHasDesktopMgr`); `PBGetCatInfo`;
`PBDTGetPath`; `PBDTGetAPPL`, unused; `PBDTAddAPPL`; the resource fork
read-only with `SetResLoad(false)`; per `BNDL`, per `FREF`, the `ICN#`,
`icl4`, `icl8`, `ics#`, `ics4`, `ics8` of its local id via `PBDTAddIcon`
as icon types 1 to 6; other `FREF` types (at most 64) as icon type −1
under `'paul'`, 256 bytes; no `PBDTFlush`.

**Decision.** Keep inited wherever the Finder info was stated whole, a
bundle's included — Expander exactly — and register a bundle as Expander
does, in `StampCat`'s new `DTBundle`, same calls, same order. Departures:
`PBDTGetPath` alone tests the volume (as for the comment); every `BNDL`
read is bounded by its handle and a `FREF` under 6 bytes skipped (the
archive's bytes); one `PBDTFlush` at the end. `-D UNC_AT_NODTREG` builds the
control.

**Same as Expander everywhere measured; the one gap is Expander's too**: a
System 7 floppy has no Desktop Manager. Not measured: System 7.5 to 8.6,
System 3.0's Finder, HFS+, icon families the Finder registers and Expander
does not.

**Tests.** `mac_sink_test --meta`: `Fold/App` carries a `BNDL` and must come
out 0x2100 with its position, registered in Expander's order; dropping the
registration fails it; a `BNDL` overrunning its handle reads nothing else
(without bounds ASan reports the read). `metarun.py --expander` allows no
difference now: 24 archives, **496 values, all as Expander wrote them**,
24/24 forks PASS; a one-byte-shifted control disagrees on 51. `metarun.py`:
91 values on 6.0.8, all as stated; on 7.0.1 the two wrong are the
`fdXFlags` item. `finderpos.py --seeded` (`zQx9`): registered 14 times,
nothing moved.

**Price** (at the merge onto *the format nobody reads*): shipped CODE +760,
A5 +40, **800 B off every extraction's budget** (bounds +48/+16 of it);
lazy CODE +764; control CODE +764, A5 −12, `OVL_SAVED` 149,552 → 149,504,
`TIERS` −752; no tally moves. `StampCat` 200 → 272 B under `sink_begin`
(420), 72 B deeper; the Resource Manager's own calls not measured.

## 2026-10-19 (the clock inside the Mac) — the Mac Plus timings are read off the emulated Ticks from the host at 50 Hz, calibrated against a known wait; the four-archive comparison and the 1 MB table re-measured on it

**The question.** The maintainer asked for ±1 s on README's two speed
tables; the screenshot loop (3 s poll, ~50 ms stolen per `import`, figure
stamped at the first poll AFTER the last change) could not give it.

**Taken: the Mac's own clock, read from the host.** A tick count inside the
Mac cannot time Expander (no hook), and the X framebuffer still times on
a stretchable host clock. Mini vMac keeps emulated RAM in its own address
space in Mac byte order, and the harness is its ancestor (Yama
`ptrace_scope` 1), so the host reads `Ticks` ($16A) and the 21,888-byte
screen buffer at `ScrnBase` ($824) at 50 Hz, ~0.1 ms a poll, nothing
written, the emulator never stopped (`tools/vmac/macclock.py`; addresses
from multiversal's `Multiverse.h`). Start = Ticks just before the key or
click; end = the last buffer change before `--quiet` s of stillness;
duration = ticks ÷ 60.15. Host seconds ride along: Mini vMac drops emulated
time more than 8 ticks behind (`PROGMAIN.c`,
`RunEmulatedTicksToTrueTime`), so a ratio far from 1.00 flags the host.

**Calibration** (`tools/vmac/clockcal/`, `expander.py --calibrate`,
`mv-4M-1x`, other sessions running): 600 ticks asked → 602, 603; 660 →
662, 662; 3,600 → 3,602. **A constant +2–3 ticks of keystroke latency, and
the 60-tick shift of the end mark read as +59 and +60.** Host ÷ Mac
0.9986–1.0001. **Seen to fail first**: `--quiet` 3 s, shorter than the
silent wait, read 2 ticks. **And on a real run**: `--quiet 30` read
`derived-a2basic.dmg.sit` at 1 MB as 0.5 s — the bar sat at "0%" over 30 s
(it redraws when the PERCENTAGE moves), the harness pressed Return into
Cancel, and the empty output flagged it. The two Arsenic fixtures were
re-run at `--quiet 300`; the rest end at a photographed "Extraction
complete." with every file written, at `--quiet 30` (ours) and 60 (against
Expander).

**The comparison** (`--ours dist/MacExtract.bin`, v0.41.0, `--repeat 2`,
`mv-4M-1x`), ours / Expander in ticks, both runs: Export 117,117 /
148,146; EmpireBuilder 3,150,3,150 / 3,274,3,274; FirstClass 4,781,4,781 /
9,333,9,334; macburger 14,788,14,789 / 25,483,25,483. Host ÷ Mac
0.994–1.001 on all sixteen. In seconds 1.9/2.4, 52.4/54.4, 79.5/155.2,
245.9/423.7 — ratios 1.26x, 1.04x, 1.95x, 1.72x. **Expander's unchanged
code reads 0.6–2.3 s under every screenshot figure (3, 56, 156, 426 s)** —
the old instrument's bias, measured, and why "a lower bound" is withdrawn
(BLOCKERS.md, *Corrected figures*). Ours' 56 → 52 s cannot be attributed
between bias and code.

**The 1 MB table is now the shipped application** (`--only ours --emu
mv-1M-1x --quiet 30`, every `timing.txt` fixture twice), not the autotest
build with its read-back. Runs agree to 2 ticks except the two Arsenic
ones, 3 and 5 ticks in 20,550 and 45,066 (FORMATS.md, *The shipped
application on a 1 MB Mac Plus*). README: a few KB is 1.9 s, or 15.7 s for
StuffIt 5's overlay; a few hundred KB 1–103 s (the BinHex chain 246 s);
a2basic 341.6 s (was 341 s), the Barcoder 749.3 s (was 742 s).

**What this cannot see**: emulator fidelity to a real 68000, disk time
(Mini vMac's driver is free), ticks lost to masked interrupts, work that
draws nothing for longer than `--quiet`.

## 2026-10-20 (one place for every probe) — every probe is in its reader's `_probe.c`; the move cost 212 B of resident CODE until its five grown files compared bytes, and lands at −32

**Claim.** Where a probe lived was history: a `_probe.c` existed where a
reader had left the resident link (2026-09-02 on); nine probes sat in
their readers' files, Now Compress's and DiskDoubler's in `fmt_stubs.c`,
tar's in `fmt_exo_probe.c`. Now the probe of `fmt_X.c` is in
`fmt_X_probe.c`, shared code defined there and declared in `fmt_X_priv.h`
(SpaceSaver's shape). `fmt_stubs.c` and `fmt_exo_priv.h` are gone.

**The move alone** (against `main` 7bacda9): eager **+212 B of `CODE` and
+12 of A5**, lazy +208/+16, control +208/+12, no function body changed
(AppleSingle +48, MacBinary +58, the two `fmt_stubs.c` probes +48, spanned
zip +36, DiskDoubler split +20). Cause: `unc_get_u32be` is `static inline`
in `unc_internal.h`, and at `-Os` each translation unit calling it more
than once gets its own 42-byte copy, or an inline expansion
(`unc_applesingle_probe` 0x7e → 0xae, `unc_nowcompress_probe` 0x8e → 0xbe).
224 B off every budget for a move, so it went to a branch
(`probes-one-place`) first.

**Brought to zero by 2026-10-09's lesson** (*the probe was the outlier*):
compare bytes. AppleSingle's magics and versions, MacBinary's 'mBIN',
fork-size and date tests, DiskDoubler's magics and Now Compress's count are
bytes; Now's checksum a word (106 bytes cannot sum past 27,030); the
DiskDoubler-split parse returns the payload length; the spanned zip's scan
wrapper is `static inline` in the private header. Each reader + probe pair
against the old file: AppleSingle +22, MacBinary +6, spanned zip +4,
DiskDoubler split +2, Now + DiskDoubler −34 — **0 in all, and 0 and 0 in
every configuration's link.** StuffIt classic's probe then went to bytes:
−32 in every configuration; `ovl_stuffit` 29,874 → 29,842 B, bundle
178,924 → 178,892; every TIERS budget +32, derived.

**Two refinements.** The lesson applies to a pointer of unknown alignment
(`head`), not a LOCAL buffer: Private File's footer and AppleLink's two
word tests grew by 28 and 8 as bytes, and were put back. And **a file split
is not free on this compiler**: each new translation unit re-pays the
header's inline helpers, so a code move is priced like any change. Compact
Pro's, SuperDisk's and SpaceSaver's helper calls read values used
arithmetically, and were left.

## 2026-10-21 (the probes that left with the bundle) — the sniffer and all twenty-six probes are a seventeenth `'OVLY'` image, run from the bundle before the release and given back with it; 9,284 B of resident CODE and 364 of A5 go, +9,616 B on every budget that keeps images

**Claim.** "The sniff runs before any image is chosen, so a probe cannot
be in an image" does not follow for the eager lifetime: the whole bundle is
in memory at the sniff, and the release follows its answer. `unc_sniff` and
its table are `src/unc_sniff.c`, shipped with every `fmt_*_probe.c` in
`ovl_sniff`, 'OVLY' 144, entered through a one-line shim in
`mac/ovl_shim.c` and in no keep set. The probe files stay resident for
what readers share (`mb_version`, `ddseg_parse`, the MIME header walk);
`-gc-sections` drops the probes, except `unc_macbinary_probe`, reached by
LZH's and zip's self-extractor paths through the host vector, which the
image defines itself (`tools/overlay/mkforwards.py`, `SNIFF`).

**Measured** (against `main` 9be493e): eager **−9,284 B of `CODE` and −364
of A5**, lazy −9,280/−364, control −72/+8. The image is 13,384 B with 30
relocations (the 26 probe pointers). `OVL_SAVED` 149,536 → 159,152. The host
lane extracts its twenty fixtures byte-exact through it in both lifetimes;
no tally moves (FORMATS.md, *Three configurations, one tree*).

**Where it costs.** Every layer whose release keeps images gains 9,616 B.
A layer keeping the bundle WHOLE (an envelope, or a split set joining to a
file, whose inner layer is sniffed from it) pays 3,780 B; no tally moves,
and the archive under it gets the gain.

**Every later sniff still has its probes** (sites read first): open-time
and extraction sniffs precede the release; layer loops under envelopes and
split sets run while the bundle is kept whole; the next archive of a list
is sniffed after `ovl_reload`. A sniff with the bundle gone answers
UNKNOWN and raises the loader's alarm (`gWantedAfterRelease` = 144).

**The host lane caught one.** `tests/mac_sink_test.c` sniffed, released,
then called `unc_extract`, which sniffs AGAIN; the shell dispatches on
what it sniffed (`unc_extract_as`), and now so does the harness. **A
harness mirroring the shell's calls must mirror their NUMBER too.**

**On the machine**, the same day: 74/74 at 1 MB on System 6.0.8, 72/74 on
System 3.0 / 512Ke, 68/74 on System 6.0.8 / 512Ke, the same fixtures by
name as predicted (BLOCKERS.md, *Status*); three host-side emulator exits
in 222 boots, each re-run clean. `synth-dd-m5.dd` "98 B short" (was 9,714)
— a hypothesis, inside what the 666 B residue cannot resolve (corrected:
DECISIONS.md 2026-10-22, *the names in the code*).

**What this cannot see.** The host lane has no instruction cache and no
Resource Manager (TESTING.md, *The overlay loader, off the Macintosh*);
emulated tiers have no cache; only the LC 475 runs it on silicon
(MANUAL_TESTS.md).

## 2026-10-21 (the Desktop Manager System 6 can have) — v0.41.0 bombed "unimplemented trap" under AppleShare's `Desktop Mgr` INIT on System 6.0.8; the bundle's resource fork is opened through a working directory now, and a tier boots the stock System Folder

**The report.** uzTools/MacExtract issue #1, 2026-10-21, two days after
the first public release: Mini vMac Plus, System 6.0.8, v0.41.0, a StuffIt
archive brought over with ImportFl (Cap'n Magneto from Macintosh Garden) —
the extraction starts and bombs *unimplemented trap*. Both archives on that
page (`OriginalCM.sit`, `CM93.sit`, StuffIt 5) pass the System 6.0.8 / 4 MB
tier byte-exact, and the release asset is byte-identical to `dist/` at the
tag (SHA-256): neither engine nor build.

**What differed was the System Folder.** Every harness boots System +
Finder alone (`mkboot.py`, *The System Folder is stripped*), a RAM measure
for the 1 MB floor. The stock `System6.hfv` has twenty-odd INITs and
cdevs, MultiFinder on, among them `Desktop Mgr`, INIT/MACS, 15,886 B, 11
July 1988 — AppleShare's Desktop Manager for System 6. ImportFl types files
`BINA`/`SITx`, which no harness had written.

**Reproduced and bisected** (release binary, `tools/vmac/drive.py`): the
stock folder bombs after the destination dialog, the reporter's frame;
System + Finder + `Desktop Mgr` alone: the same; the stock folder minus that
file: *Extraction complete.*

**The trap.** `DTBundle` (2026-10-18, *the icon Expander registers*) runs
where `PBDTGetPath` answers noErr, and opened the fork with
`_HOpenResFile` (0xA81A), which System 7 added. On a stripped 6.0.8
`PBDTGetPath` is −50 and the call never reached — the measurement "a System
6 volume has no Desktop Manager" rested on (BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn
claims*). The fork is now opened through a working directory: `PBOpenWD`,
`OpenRFPerm`, `PBCloseWD` after closing — 128K ROM calls (Inside Macintosh
IV), the same on every System. **+52 B of resident CODE and +12 of A5**
shipped (A5 `.data` alignment); `StampCat`'s frame 272 → 320 B (FORMATS.md,
*Stack*); the host sink test mocks the three and fails a working directory
left open.

**Verified.** `run.py --keep-inits --expect OriginalCM.sit`, the new lane
booting the System Folder as it is: NOGRID before, PASS after; the
interactive walk on the INIT-only disk completes; `./ci.sh` green. The whole
sample under `--keep-inits`: 74/74 at 4 MB on 6.0.8 (BLOCKERS.md,
*Status*). System 7: both archives onto a floppy; `interactive.py --e2e
--system Sys7.img` onto the Desktop-Database boot volume completes; `os9.py
--hfsplus --launch` on `derived-XferIt_1.5b4.sea` writes all ten files
byte-exact onto Mac OS 9.2's HFS+.

**What this cannot see.** Whether the INIT's database took the bundle,
icons and comment (nothing read it back); whether the reporter's folder has
that INIT (asked in the reply). `PBDTAddAPPL`, `PBDTAddIcon`,
`PBDTSetComment`, `PBDTFlush` are `_HFSDispatch` selectors the INIT serves
or refuses; one application and one archive completed through all.
(Superseded in part: DECISIONS.md 2026-10-22, *the working directory the
bundle closed*.)

**A tier of its own** (the maintainer's call, 2026-10-21): System 6.0.8
with the stock System Folder is ADDITIONAL in BLOCKERS.md's table, at 4 MB
only — at 1 MB the stock folder dies before the application (the System's
stop-sign alert, text undrawn, NOGRID on two fixtures); the strip keeps
its job.

**The lesson is the strip.** A harness simplification written as a cost
measure is also a blind spot: "stripped so the 1 MB floor is measurable"
should have read "and so nothing an INIT adds is ever exercised" (CLAUDE.md,
*When adding a harness, write down what it CANNOT see*).

## 2026-10-21 (the guard that vetoes the Finder info) — GateKeeper 1.3 on System 6.0.8: in veto mode an extracted application loses its type, creator, flags and dates and the run still says "Extraction complete."; in both modes 30 bytes of the fork's reserved header change

**Why.** The maintainer asked after issue #1 whether other INITs could
interfere. Too many INITs and Standard File extenders are the user's
business (decided the same day); resource-fork write guards were tested,
since one could make an extraction look finished. GateKeeper 1.3 (Chris
Johnson, 1993; Discmaster, `Internet Megapac.iso`, kept in
`~/.cache/macextract/gatekeeper/`); Vaccine did not surface in two
searches. Its privilege list grants `File(Other)` BY NAME (StuffIt,
UnStuffIt, Compact Pro, DD Expand…); MacExtract is not on it. Installed as
shipped, stock System Folder.

**Measured, 2026-10-21, `OriginalCM.sit`, v0.42.0, `tools/vmac/drive.py`:**

- *Notify Only* (default): one modal alert ("…violated the File(Other)
  privilege against Cap'n Magneto [PBSetCatInfo(, APPL)]"), then
  *Extraction complete.*; the file `APPL`/`GWCM`, flags 0x2100, dates
  right, data fork exact.
- *Notify & Veto*: the alert says "vetoed", then *Extraction complete.*,
  and the file has **no type, no creator, flags 0, today's dates** (the
  blank `PBHCreate` file; the vetoed `PBSetCatInfo` was everything else);
  resource fork whole. `StampCat` read the result only for the bundle, so
  nothing was said — the one silent loss a guard causes here, in the report,
  not the data (OPEN_ITEMS.md, *A refused PBSetCatInfo is not reported*;
  since reported: DECISIONS.md 2026-10-25, *the two that said nothing*).
- In BOTH modes the resource fork differs in 30 bytes at 66–117, the
  header's system-reserved area (the archive carries name, `APPL`/`GWCM`
  and flags twice; the disk zeros). Every resource and the map identical;
  without GateKeeper byte-exact (`run.py --keep-inits`, 74/74). HOW is a
  hypothesis (its Aid opening the fork, the Resource Manager rewriting the
  area), not reduced.

**What this cannot see.** One guard, version, archive and System;
control panels or INITs as the extracted item; GateKeeper's log.

## 2026-10-22 (the names in the code) — Retro68 ships every function's MacsBug name inside the `CODE` resources and the images; stripped, 4,416 B of resident heap and 12,792 B of bundle go, and the ratchets had never counted them

**Claim.** Retro68's GCC writes each function's name after its `rts` for
MacsBug, and Elf2Mac keeps them unless linked `--mac-strip-macsbug`;
`tools/overlay/overlay.ld` kept them in every image. MEASURED 2026-10-22
off the resource maps: nine `CODE` resources 49,664 → **45,248 B**,
seventeen images 192,066 → 179,276 B, bundle 192,288 → **179,496 B**,
download 254,336 → 237,056 B — all of it heap on every tier.

**Found** answering a reader asking why the application "allocates CODE
resources a bit over 100 kB" (true until 2026-09-25; a FORMATS.md row still
quoted it, corrected that morning, a2decc4): the linker map's
`.text.*.macsbug` sections summed to 4,414 B in `.code00002`.
`tools/code_map.py` groups by object, so had never priced them.

**What the instrument could not see.** Elf2Mac parks the stripped names in
a `NOLOAD` section that keeps `ALLOC`, and `m68k-apple-macos-size` counts it
as text: the first stripped build read 48,314 B against a 48,316 B ceiling
and every ratchet passed while `CODE` had lost 4,416 B.
`tools/build_mac.sh` and `run_tiers.code_and_a5()` subtract that section
by name; every ceiling, `TIERS_CONTROL`, `OVL_SAVED`, `IMAGES`, `BUNDLE` and
`check_app_size.py`'s figures were re-based. **A figure the tool reports is
not the figure the machine pays unless somebody checked which sections it
adds up** (2026-10-06, *the wall the overlays had already moved*, one layer
down).

**Cost.** The name a bomb box or MacsBug shows on hardware; the ELF keeps
its symbols for listings and the stack walk. Not tested: a bomb on hardware
with the stripped build.

**The model.** `OVL_SAVED` 159,120 → 153,360 (control −10,176, shipped
−4,416), every TIERS budget +10,176 (derived), a format's grant +5,076 to
+7,552 B, an envelope's +17,176. Shipped lane: no tally moves; the resident
lane recovers `derived-PuzzleGetter_0.8.sit` at 6.0.8 / 512Ke, 63 → 64/74
(arithmetic; control not booted). **On the machine, shipped build: 74/74 at
1 MB on System 6.0.8, 72/74 on System 3.0 / 512Ke and 68/74 on System 6.0.8
/ 512Ke, the same fixtures by name; two host-side emulator exits, each
re-run clean alone.** `synth-dd-m5.dd` "98 B short" was a lower bound read
as a distance: at a budget 5,928 B larger it reads 378 B short; its peak is
401,408 B against a 235,142 B grant (FORMATS.md, *Overlays*, corrected in
place).

**What is left in the resident 43,900 B.** The Mac shell is 21,192 B with
the names, 143 functions: 12.5 KB extraction driver and sink callbacks,
4.0 KB segmented sets, 2.2 KB report list and bar, 0.7 KB password dialog,
0.6 KB envelope layering, 0.4 KB startup, 0.8 KB helpers — the File
Manager side the engine has no libc for. A Retro68 `CODE` segment could
take out only what nothing calls while the engine holds its budget
(startup, Standard File, About), a few kilobytes, hypothesis; dialogs that
look one-shot run mid-extraction, and a segment reloaded then fails as a
system bomb. Not started.

## 2026-10-22 (the runtime the application did not need) — Elf2Mac's --mac-single and an entry point of our own drop Retro68's multi-segment loader and newlib's exit chain: +4,980 B on every shipped budget, measured on all three tiers

**Claim.** The application had one real code segment and was linked as
multi-segment: Retro68's `MultiSegApp.c` patched `_LoadSeg`, `_UnLoadSeg`,
`_ExitToShell`, `_Launch` and `_Chain`, kept an 816-byte jump table in the
A5 world and six 80-byte stub segments, and copied a `DATA` resource into
A5 at launch; `_start` left through newlib's `exit`, linking
`__call_exitprocs`, the `atexit` table, the stdio file array and
`_impure_data` into an application with no stdio and no constructor.
Elf2Mac's `--mac-single` links one `CODE` 1 (code, data, relocations;
globals in a heap block Retro68's relocator allocates). `mac/mac_start.c`
is the entry (`-Wl,-e,unc_mac_start`): relocates, gives the relocations
back (`SetHandleSize` on `CODE` 1, only when `RecoverHandle` of the image
start names `GetResource`'s handle), calls `main`, leaves through
`ExitToShell`. `tools/build_mac.sh` fails if a constructor, destructor,
`.init` or `.fini` appears — shown to fail on one; an EMPTY static
constructor did not test it (GCC deletes it at `-Os`).

**Measured** (against `main` ce79615): eager **−2,552 B of `CODE` and −1,304
of data + bss**, lazy the same, control −2,504 and −680; `MacExtract.bin`
237,056 → 232,320 B. The budget probe (`-D UNC_AT_BUDGET`,
`derived-PCCTS.tar`) on both builds back to back: **every shipped budget
+4,980 B** on System 6.0.8 at 1 MB, System 3.0 / 512Ke and System 6.0.8 /
512Ke; control +4,204 / +4,186 / +4,204. The difference is the jump table,
stubs and 1,368 B of relocations, resident and never in `code + data + bss`.

**What that also found.** `main`'s own probe read its TIERS 1,288 B below
the derived figures on all three tiers, residue −426 B not −666: the
shipped lane had been ~1 KB generous. Re-taken from this build's boots
(TIERS 201,590 / 106,208 / 630,496, `OVL_RESIDUE` −322); no tally moves.
`TIERS_MACHINE` (budget + its control), which `--check-saved` held constant
because no change inside CODE + A5 can move it, moved here — about 270 B
lower (413,206 / 317,824 / 842,112); the first CI run said so.

**On the machine**: 74/74 at 1 MB on 6.0.8, 72/74 on 3.0 / 512Ke, 68/74 on
6.0.8 / 512Ke, same fixtures by name; 74/74 on 7.0.1 and on 6.0.8 at 4 MB
with the stock INITs — first pass. The quit was graded by `relaunch.py`
(the autotest never returns from `main`): a `.cpt` and a `.sit` from the
Finder on 6.0.8, MultiFinder and 3.0 / 512Ke. On 7.0.1 the second archive
is refused — on `main` too, so filed (OPEN_ITEMS.md, *System 7.0.1: the
second archive of a Finder list is refused*; found: *the working directory
the bundle closed*). The 64K-ROM 512K reaches Standard File on both builds.
Mac OS 9.2 under QEMU (32-bit, 68LC040 emulation): all 22 of
`os9sample.txt` launched, extracted, quit (the last two on re-run, the
sweep having stopped when `./ci.sh` deleted its reference build).

**The lesson: price a link-model change on the machine.** The ratchets'
unit is the ELF's sections; a change to how the application is LAID OUT
moves resident bytes no section holds — here 1.1 KB of 4.98 KB.
`TIERS_CONTROL` moved −3,184 in that unit; deriving TIERS from it would
have under-credited every budget by about a kilobyte.

## 2026-10-22 (the working directory the bundle closed) — v0.42.0's `PBOpenWD` handed back the Finder's own working directory at the top of the output, and its `PBCloseWD` closed it under the rest of the run; no working directory is opened there now

**The symptom.** On System 7.0.1, a `.cpt` and a `.sit` opened together:
the second ends at *"Could not open the archive."* (`relaunch.py --system
Sys7.img --folder-at In`). **The commit**: ba8f2d2 (v0.42.0, *the Desktop
Manager System 6 can have*) — PASS at ba8f2d2^, FAIL at ba8f2d2.

**What it is, measured.** A `-D UNC_AT_HEAPLOG` build logging refNums in
`DTBundle` after `keyAhead` (a bundled INIT at the top of the output): the
Finder's document working directory was −32701 on `In` (dirID 75), the
destination the same, and `PBOpenWD` on (−32701, 75, `'MExt'`) returned
**−32701** — the Finder's. `PBCloseWD` then closed it, failing every later
use: the second document, and within one archive every entry after the
application (reversed, `ScrollbarPattern.sit` first: *"About Scroll Bar
Pattern Editor: could not be created"*). A pair whose first archive has no
bundled file PASSES; one archive at a volume's root PASSES. **The stock
System 6.0.8 folder fails the same way** (`relaunch.py --keep-inits`), so the
regression reached issue #1's own environment with its fix. Why `PBOpenWD`
returns another process's working directory is not established (refNum
seen on 7.0.1 only; on 6.0.8 the frame alone).

**The fix.** At the top of the output (`curDirID` 0) `OpenRFPerm` gets the
destination's refNum and no working directory is opened or closed; below
it, one is opened on a folder this run created, as before. +32 B of
resident CODE shipped.

**Graded.** `relaunch.py` PASS on 7.0.1 (both orders, and `Newer1.1.1.cpt`
first, exercising the folder branch), 6.0.8, MultiFinder, 3.0 / 512Ke, and
the stock 6.0.8 folder (`--keep-inits`, new), where the unfixed build fails.
`run.py --keep-inits --list sample.txt`: 74/74 (one `EMUDIED` re-run). The
host sink test counts working directories and fails one at the top of the
output on ce79615's shell.

**The lesson.** Every `run.py` tier extracts into (a volume, `fsRtDirID`),
the application into (a working directory, dirID 0): the 74/74 that graded
v0.42.0 never ran its users' path. **A harness that reaches the code by
another door grades the door.** Not measured: Mac OS 9 (presumably affected,
hypothesis).

## 2026-10-23 (the format 7.0.3 sniffs) — StuffIt 7.0.3's Expander opens AppleSingle under any type, creator or name, and has no AppleDouble reader: nine subjects on Mac OS 9.2, asked for by MacStamp

**Claim, measured.** StuffIt Expander 7.0.3 Classic recognises AppleSingle
by its magic, needing no type, creator or `.as`; it reads AppleDouble in
none of three shapes.

**Evidence.** Asked by MacStamp (`/home/claude/macstamp`).
`tools/vmac/as703.py` put `fixtures/synth-as-meta.as` (the bytes of the
maintainer's `Comment.as`) on `compat9.py`'s transfer volume nine times
(FORMATS.md, *AppleSingle and AppleDouble in 7.0.3*): six AppleSingle under
`BINA`, `????` and `TEXT`, with and without `.as`, five with creator
`SITx`, one with none — all byte-exact, both forks (the ownerless one via
File ▸ Expand); three AppleDouble shapes (`._name`, `%name`, header alone)
— all Error #17999, leaving a 367-byte stub named by bytes `16 07 00 02 00`
(the header less 128 bytes, named as a MacBinary reader would at offset 1).
The Expander's resources name *"AppleSingle (.as)"* only.

**Consequence.** README.md's 7.0.3 cell says AppleSingle only. For
MacStamp, `SITx` makes a double-click reach it and any type will do. That
AppleDouble was read as MacBinary is a hypothesis from the stub.

**`BINA/TIGR`, the same day.** Mac OS 9's Internet Config gives AppleSingle
that pair; StuffIt ships no `TIGR` stub. The entry names *"Tiger"* and the
Expander as post-processor, and the Expander claims `BINA`, so a
double-click reaches it through the Finder's *"Could not find the
application program"* dialog as the one recommended choice.

**MacExtract in that dialog**: not offered — the list is the Desktop
database's exact-type claims, and `'****'` (DECISIONS.md 2026-08-31,
measured for the DROP) registers none. A `BNDL` with `FREF 'BINA'` is
listed first, above the Expander, and extracts `Kept Whole` byte-exact
(built in scratch, measured, reverted). The wildcard covers the drop, the
claim covers the dialog.

## 2026-10-24 (the two bytes the writer drew) — bytes 0-1 of a StuffIt segment are QuickDraw's _Random, drawn once per set and never seeded; and 96-97, which the probe required to be zero, are the resource fork's running CRC, so every set of a file with one was refused

**Claim, measured, from StuffIt Deluxe 2.0.1's code and four sets it cut
here.** **Bytes 0-1 are `_Random`, drawn once per set** (*the magic StuffIt
never wrote*'s hypothesis): the segmenter stores the date in low-memory
`RndSeed`, which `_Random` does not read, so the k-th set of a LAUNCH gets
the k-th value from `InitGraf`'s seed 1: 41 A7, 3A F1, AC D9. Deluxe 2.0.1's

CRC-16/ARC over the resource fork's bytes, 98-99 over the data fork's.** The
probe required 96-97 zero and the joiner one sum, so every set of a file
with a resource fork was "format not recognized". Both now follow the
writer.

**Evidence.** The application's fork (unpacked by this engine from
`sitopt.py`'s download), 32 `CODE` resources, read with Retro68's `objdump
-b binary -m m68k:68000`, `CODE` 0's jump table resolving calls:
- `_Random` (A861) occurs once: `CODE` 5 +0x3444, in the routine at +0x3204
  typing each part `SegM`/`SIT!` (+0x3a64); result to word 0 (+0x3448)
  after word 1, the part number, is cleared (+0x343e); each part increments
  it (+0x3636) and CRCs bytes 0..93 into 94 (+0x364a). It opens with
  `GetDateTime` stored to `RndSeed`, 0x156 (+0x323a). Nothing writes
  QuickDraw's `randSeed` (every −126 displacement is off the frame
  pointer). `InitGraf` once (`CODE` 3).
- Three launches, two sets each: 41 A7 then 3A F1 every time — `_Random`'s
  first two values from 1, low words of 16,807 and 282,475,249.
- The fork sums: the copy loop (+0x3f5c..+0x40ca) folds resource and data
  bytes into separate accumulators, copied to 96 and 98 (+0x3e32); Join
  compares them (+0x295c, +0x2984), refuses a part whose bytes 0-1 differ
  from part 1's (STR# 269, *"does NOT belong the the file being joined!"*,
  +0x287c) and one out of sequence (+0x28aa).
- Four sets, resource forks of 323, 30,266, 900,211 and 100,211 bytes:
  every part's 96-97 and 98-99 are the two running sums (part 1 of SubjC,
  ending inside its resource fork, stores 0 at 98). **All 42 earlier parts
  were cut from files with no resource fork**, so could not tell the
  readings apart.

tree joins all four byte for byte and refuses SubjC with a flipped resource

**What it does not see.** Other writers' code: Lite 3.0.5's and
InstallerMaker 2.0's 41 A7 fit, unread; Deluxe 5.0's 35 63 and 52 0C,

these sets.

seeks to the document's start, which `.dl` needs.

**A departure from hexbin.** hexbin's `.dl` test is a first line longer than
40, even, of '@'..'O' and '|' only; base64 of zeros is a line of 'A', so a
base64 file of 4,000 zero bytes sniffed as `.dl`. The first line must also
open "@@" (the high byte of a resource fork's data offset, Inside
Macintosh: More Macintosh Toolbox, "Resource File Format", zero under 16
MB); and only the first line is examined (a first version took a later
line, which hexbin never would). A `.dl` whose fork's first byte is not
zero is no longer read here; `tools/run_hecx.py` asserts both halves.

**The sum is compared on 16 bits** (WITHDRAWN 2026-10-25: SUMacC's own
readers compare 32, *the writer that was in 4.3BSD*), as `dl.c`'s
`verify_crc` does.

**The tests can fail.** `run_hecx.py`'s 23 new cases fail 15 times against
HEAD; the base64 case failed the first probe, the later-line case the
second. Sniff over 2,012 fixtures and specimens differs from HEAD only on
`xlispold.dl`; none of 9,251 non-archives sniffs as `.dl`.

**Cost.** Shipped CODE +0, A5 +32 (table row 16 B and name 10 B, by
alignment) — **32 B off every budget**. `ovl_binhex` 4,606 → 5,082 B,
`ovl_sniff` 12,436 → 12,556 B, bundle 180,388 → 180,984. Control +584 and A5
+8, `TIERS_CONTROL` +592, bases −592, `OVL_SAVED` +560 → 156,176 B; grant
rows +560, envelope −36. No tally moves. Heap 9,232 B (the `.hcx`
allocation); stack under the `.hcx` chain (484 + 48 against 524 + 76 + 32).

**What it does not see.** No writer: SUMacC's `dl` tools had not been found
(WITHDRAWN 2026-10-25: they were in 4.3BSD, *the writer that was in
4.3BSD*); one file is all the format's output here.

## 2026-10-25 (the writer that was in 4.3BSD) — SUMacC's tohex and fromhex were in 4.3BSD all along: tohex wrote the wild file, and the format's own readers compare the sum on 32 bits, so this does too

**Claim (measured).** SUMacC's source ships in 4.3BSD's contributed
software, `new.tar.gz` → `sumacc.tar.Z` (June 1986), on TUHS. `cmd/tohex.c`
is the `.dl` writer: on the fork hexbin decodes from
`mactosh/lang/xlispold.dl` it writes that file byte for byte, less the three
blank lines the wild copy ends with. `cmd/fromhex.c` reads the file
("checksum good!") to hexbin's fork; `etc/download.doc` (Bill Croft and Ed
Pattermann, SUMEX) describes the format. "SUMacC's tools have not been
found" was one site's category listing repeated; the first search found
them (BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn claims*).

**The sum is now compared on 32 bits.** `cmd/fromhex.c`, the Mac
`etc/fromhex.c` and the Pascal `etc/fromhex.p` all compare the full 32-bit
value; hexbin's 16 is its `verify_crc`, written for 16-bit CRCs. Refusing a
file hexbin reads is what the format's own readers do.

**What the writer confirms.** `tohex` breaks after every 33rd byte, so its
first line is 66 characters opening "@@": both first-line tests hold for
all it writes. `fromhex` has no line rule (it skips everything outside
'@'..'O'; headers removed by hand) and takes a line break inside the sum
for a digit where hexbin and this skip it; `run_hecx.py` asserts that
difference.

**The tests can fail.** `tools/run_hecx.py` builds `tohex` and `fromhex`
from `reference/sumacc` (`tools/fetch_references.sh`), grades every `.dl`
case against both and hexbin, writes its forks with `tohex` and asserts its
own generator agrees at 66 characters. The 16-bit build fails the
high-half case, which hexbin reads and `fromhex` and this refuse.

**Cost.** Nothing shipped: shipped and lazy CODE and A5 unmoved,
`ovl_binhex` 5,082 B unmoved. `want - sum == size` (−2 at the overlay's
flags, against +4 for `want == size + sum`) lands at the same image size;
the control's `unc_hecx_extract` 2,086 → 2,084, A5 +4, CODE + A5 unmoved.

**What it does not see.** `tohex` compiled here, not on a VAX; its own
`htonl` swaps unconditionally, so writes big-endian only on a little-endian
host (a VAX and this machine both are). No second wild `.dl`: the carousel
disc's 26 `mactosh` directories, the USENIX '87 copy of SUMacC and
Discmaster searches for `fromhex`, `tohex`, `sumacc`, `grow.dl`,
`handson.dl`, `fromhex.dl` gave `xlispold.dl` alone. The Mac `FromHex`
binary (`mactosh/util/fromhex.sit`) was not run.

## 2026-10-25 (the two that said nothing) — a MIME multipart past the walk's depth and a Finder info GateKeeper vetoes are report lines, not silence: UNC_ERR_NESTED, and "name: Finder info refused"

**Claim.** Two silent losses are now reported, each one line naming the
entry.

**A MIME multipart nested past `MIME_MAX_DEPTH` (4)** is still walked as
one leaf (the boundary stack is fixed arrays, ~340 B a level, and real mail
nests two or three deep), but the leaf is now an entry that fails,
`UNC_ERR_NESTED` (-17): "part1: nested too deep to open". Before, a
five-level nest with its only attachment at the bottom exited *not a
recognized archive*. -16 stays retired: its 24-level cap was chosen by
nobody; this one is an array's size, which OPEN_ITEMS.md had called sound.
The Mac shell reuses the engine's sentence. `run_mime.py` adds a four-level
nest that must extract and a five-level one that must fail and say why;
the old CLI fails the second.

**A refused `PBSetCatInfo`** (*the guard that vetoes the Finder info*): now
the report line "name: Finder info refused" and, once a run, after them:
*"Probably virus protection such as Gatekeeper refused these files' type,
creator and dates. Turn it off and extract again."* (the maintainer's
request). "Probably": the File Manager had accepted the file and both
forks, which is what a guard leaves, and GateKeeper is the one measured.
`RepEntry` is shared with the INEXACT line.

**Measured.** System 6.0.8, GateKeeper 1.3 vetoing, `OriginalCM.sit`,
`tools/vmac/drive.py`: the alert, then "Cap'n Magneto: Finder info
refused", the advice, *Extraction complete.* The veto comes back as an
error, not `noErr`, which only this run could show. The sink test fails
both conditions on Linux and checks both lines; the first fails with the
line removed.

**Cost.** Shipped CODE +76, A5 +84 (the sentences and alignment): 160 B off
every budget; control +224, `ovl_text` +92, `OVL_SAVED` +64, `TIERS` −224.
The advice is CODE +44, A5 +100 more, 144 B (a 150-character first wording
measured 176); `TIERS` −144.

**What it cannot see.** GateKeeper only, one System; the error returned is
not recorded; any non-`noErr` result is reported.

## 2026-10-25 (the envelopes that left) — the encryption check joins the sniffer's image and the MacBinary and AppleDouble readers BinHex's: 2,464 B back on every budget but an envelope's

**Claim.** Two resident things now sit in the bundle, which the release
gives back before the budget is taken. Every format but an envelope gains
2,496 B (`OVL_SAVED`); an envelope layer, keeping the whole bundle, loses
232.

**What moved.**
- `unc_archive_encrypted` (`src/unc_encinfo.c`, 576 B) joins the sniffer's
  image: the eager release is its only caller, with the bundle whole;
  without the image the answer is UNKNOWN, which the release treats as yes.
- `unc_macbinary_extract` and `unc_appledouble_extract` join BinHex's image.
  They are reached only through the format table and the shell's envelope
  peek `EnvRun`, which already unwraps BinHex and uuencode through images,
  and whose one caller, `SegScanWrapped`, runs before the release.
- Shared helpers stay resident (the LZH, zip, MIME and sidecar images
  reach them through the host vector): `unc_macbinary_meta` and
  `unc_as_record` move into the probe files, left out of the sniffer's
  forwards file as `unc_macbinary_probe` is; the MacBinary reader calls the
  probe (`mb_version > 0`, already in the vector) — no vector entry added.

**Measured.** Shipped CODE −2,480, A5 +16; lazy −1,908/+20; control
+40/−8. BinHex's image +2,076, the sniffer's +652, bundle 183,804 B. The
engine, CLI and Linux suites are unchanged by construction. On the machine:
`run.py --mem 1M`, System 6.0.8, shipped autotest, five of five byte-exact
(two MacBinary, one a chain to StuffIt; `synth-as-meta.as`; a zip and a
Compact Pro archive, the formats the encryption check decides for).

**What it cannot see.** The full tier sweeps were not re-run; the model
takes the new figures, and the overlay host lane
(`tests/run_overlay_host.sh`) loads the images off the Mac.

**The encryption check's YES, on the machine.** The autotest has no
password, so cannot tell a kept cipher from a released one;
`interactive.py --password --password-kind zip|cpt` (new) boots the shipped
build on System 6.0.8, opens an encrypted zip and Compact Pro archive
(`tools/synth_crypt.py`), answers the real dialog, and reads every entry
back: all decrypted. With the shim forced to NO the zip lost its entries,
so the phase fails when the ciphers are released. Compact Pro's forks came
back with the name at byte 48 (reserved area), compared masked.

## 2026-10-25 (the archive Symantec shipped) — a DDAR record is the stored file's catalog entry: +78 is its resource fork, a creator other than DDAP is stored raw, and +100.. is the Finder's position; read off DD Expand 3.7.7

**Found by asking.** MacStamp's census of commercial CDs found, on the
Info-Mac II CD (May 1993), Symantec's own `DD3.7.7AuxFiles.dd`, a `DDAR`
archive, beside `DD Expand™ 3.7.7` — the oracle OPEN_ITEMS.md's
DiskDoubler-record row named.

**Claim.** A `DDAR` record is the catalog entry of the file Combine stored,
as it sat on the disk.
- **+74 is its data fork length, +78 its resource fork's**, the second
  following the first: the walk is `record + 124 + (+74) + (+78)`.
- **Creator `DDAP` means DiskDoubler-compressed**: the data fork is the
  compressed file, no resource fork (+78 read 0 on all 43 such records);
  it is expanded. Any other creator is stored raw, both forks: here
  Symantec's `APPL/DSEA` self-extractor, +78 at 6,374.
- **+90/+94/+98 are the stored file's type, creator and flags** (the
  compressed file's for `DDAP`), as the 2026-08 reading had it.
- **+100..103 is a file's `fdLocation`**; on a folder record +90..105 is
  `DInfo` whole and +106..109 `DXInfo`'s `frScroll`; +82/+86 the dates.

**Evidence.**
- DD Expand 3.7.7 under System 7 (`diskdoubler.py --ddar`) writes the
  self-extractor back as `APPL/DSEA` with the 78,268-byte data fork +74
  states and the 6,374-byte resource fork +78 states, and expands the seven
  `DDAP` records.
- Every fork it wrote equals ours (resource headers masked), and every
  catalog field: eight file positions, the folder's window, the dates.
- `unar` on each `DDAP` record's carved-out compressed file decodes all
  seven to our bytes.

**Consequence.** This reader and `unar` both walked by +74 alone and
stopped at the raw resource fork (*"file is truncated"* / *"Archive parsing
failed"*, after three of nine entries). The raw branch existed only for
XADMaster's `0x20` flag, which no record sets, and took the inner file for
the entry. It now takes the raw branch for any creator but `DDAP`, steps
over +78, and states each file's FInfo and folder's DInfo/DXInfo. Fixture
`im2-DD3.7.7AuxFiles.dd`, manifest from those two oracles; the differential
suite fails the old CLI and passes 95 of 95 DiskDoubler fixtures after.

The rule rests on the only non-compressed record on this machine: creator
`DDAP` on 43 records of one creator and 1 of another. OPEN_ITEMS.md keeps
the `DDA2` half of the row.

## 2026-10-25 (the review before the release) — the 38 commits since v0.43.0 read before tagging: a DiskDoubler walk that could step backward for ever, and four smaller faults

**Claim (measured).** Read before v0.44.0, the commits since v0.43.0 held
one fault worth a release's delay and four small ones; all five fixed.
- **The DiskDoubler walks could loop for ever.** `DDAR` steps by `start +
  (+74) + (+78)`, `DDA2` by `start + total`, 32-bit words off the record; a
  wrapping sum sends the walk back. A 202-byte `DDAR` file listed one entry
  about two million times in five seconds. dc62805 made it easy to reach
  (every non-`DDAP` record takes the raw branch); the `DDA2` half was in
  v0.43.0. Both now refuse a record not past the last (`UNC_ERR_CORRUPT`).
- **gzip took a failed read after a member for the end of the file** and
  reported the entry whole; only a true end of file is a clean end now.
- **The StuffIt segment probe refused part 1 of a fat installer** whose
  PowerPC tail outweighs its later disks, and a one-part set with trailing
  bytes, both of which the reader takes. Part 1 is exempt from the bound
  (BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn claims*).
- **The advice after "Finder info refused" was said once a layer, and lost
  past 64 refusals** (BLOCKERS.md, *Withdrawn claims*). The refused and
  INEXACT lines are no longer urgent (RepNew reserves urgency for
  failures); the advice is said once, after the envelope chain.

**Evidence.** Each fix has a failing-without regression: three in
`tests/unit_formats.c` (the two walks, gzip), one in `tests/mac_sink_test.c`
(70 refusals leave the reserve). The probe's test holds part 2 to the bound
and part 1 not.

**Cost.** Shipped CODE +20, A5 −20: no budget moves; control +144,
`ovl_cptdd` +72, `ovl_exo` +32, the sniffer's +12; each grant +144 less the
images it keeps (FORMATS.md, *What each format is granted*). Arithmetic, no
emulator booted.

## 2026-10-31 (the helper list Expander asks for) — StuffIt Expander 5.5's installer offers to become Internet Config's helper for downloaded files; it claims no Finder creator, so nothing in it replaces a stub

Question (OPEN_ITEMS.md, *The double-click helpers*): the 5.5 installer
"says it can take ownership of other creators" — does Aladdin have a way to
open other programs' archives by double-click that the stubs should copy?

**Claim (measured, Mac OS 9.2 under QEMU, two installs).** The question the
installer asks, after copying the application, is Internet Config's, not
the Finder's: *"Your Macintosh uses a list of helper applications to help
expand files downloaded from the Internet. StuffIt Expander can be made the
default helper application for expanding all files transferred to your
machine. [...] Click "OK" to set StuffIt Expander as the default helper
application."* (OK / Cancel; `DITL` 4002, text drawn by the installer's
code). OK was clicked; the installer then reported success and showed no
other alert, both times.

**Read off the installer and the application, no emulator.** The installer
(`APPL`/`STi0`, InstallerMaker) carries `STR#` 3000 *Extension*: `.sit .pf
.hqx .bin .uu .uue .zip .gz .tgz .tar .img .smi` — the twelve extensions it
maps — and the alerts *"Internet Preferences is fixed for Stuffit™
Archives"* and *"Could not fix Internet Preferences"* (`DITL` 4000, 4001).
Expander 5.5 exposes the same thing as a preference, `DITL` 3007 *Internet
Config*, *"Use StuffIt Expander for all available types"*. Its bundles are
`SITx` (`APPL ZIP  Bzp2 TARF BINA TEXT ...`) and a second one owned by
`SIT!` (`SITD SIT! SIT5 Seg* SPSV Part`), the 4.0.2 arrangement that
decorates and opens nothing (2026-10-12, *the second bundle that only
paints*). Its own Read Me lists the twelve formats and a "helper"
application lookup for formats it cannot read; the installer's Read Me says
nothing of creators.

**What OK wrote (measured, second install on a writable copy of the boot
volume, shut down from the guest).** `Internet Preferences`' `Mapping`
entry, read with `hfsutils` before and after (`companion/harvest/icmap.py`,
the walk landing exactly on the resource's end): the 14 stock Mac OS 9.2
entries for the twelve extensions were replaced by 22 of Aladdin's. Each
keeps `SITx` as the post-processor, as stock already had it; what changed
is the type and creator a saved download is STAMPED with:

| extension | stock creator | after OK |
|---|---|---|
| `.sit` | `SITD`/`SITx` | `SIT5`, `SITD`, `SIT!` all `SIT!` (StuffIt Deluxe) |
| `.hqx`, `.uu`, `.uue` | `TEXT`/`SITx`; `TEXT`/`R*ch` | `TEXT`/`R*ch` (BBEdit) |
| `.bin` | `BINA`/`SITx` | `BINA`/`????` |
| `.img` | `GKON` (GraphicConverter) | `Wrap`, `ddsk` disk images |
| `.zip`, `.gz`, `.tgz`, `.tar`, `.pf`, `.smi` | `ZIP `, `Gzip`, `S691`, `CSIT`, `sImg` | the same creators |

**Consequence.** No Finder mechanism to copy; the stubs stay. It bears on
*which creators*: on Mac OS 9.2 after that OK, a browser that stamps
downloads from Internet Config (hypothesis — no download was made) saves
a `.sit` as `SIT!`, a `.zip` as `ZIP `, a `.tar` as
`S691` (SunTar, not in `companion/app-bundles.tsv`), and BinHex and uu as
BBEdit's `R*ch`, which no stub can claim without taking BBEdit's text files.
Offering MacExtract as Internet Config's post-processor is a separate
route, reaching only System 7.5+ with Internet Config and only new
downloads (not priced, not proposed).
